<a id="proposition-i2j-tie-sets-of-continuous-and-smooth-score-families"></a>**Proposition I.2j (Tie Sets of Continuous and Smooth Score Families).** Let $I$ be an open interval, let $X$ be a finite set of realizations and let $t\mapsto J_t(x)$ be continuous on $I$ for every $x\in X$.

1. For $x,x'\in X$ the tie set $\{t\in I:J_t(x)=J_t(x')\}$ is relatively closed in $I$. The set of $t\in I$ at which two distinct realizations both maximize $J_t$ is also relatively closed.

2. Conversely, for every relatively closed $F\subset I$ there is a $C^\infty$ function $g\ge0$ on $I$ whose zero set is exactly $F$. The two-element family $J_t(x_0)=0$, $J_t(x_1)=-g(t)$ has tie set $F$: both realizations maximize exactly for $t\in F$, and $x_0$ is the unique maximizer on $I\setminus F$.

Consequently the countable tie structure of Theorem I.2b, item 3, belongs to affine scores. For smooth scores the tie set can be a Cantor set or an interval, and a finite or countable breakpoint census requires additional structure, such as the polynomial scores of Theorems I.2d and I.2i.

*Proof.* Item 1. The difference $J_t(x)-J_t(x')$ is continuous in $t$, so its zero set is relatively closed. The value function $V(t)=\max_{x\in X}J_t(x)$ is a maximum of finitely many continuous functions and is continuous, so each set $\{t:J_t(x)=J_t(x')=V(t)\}$ is relatively closed; the second set of item 1 is their finite union over pairs $x\ne x'$.

Item 2. The set $I\setminus F$ is open in $\mathbb R$. Enumerate the open intervals $(a_j,b_j)$, $j\ge1$, with rational endpoints whose closures lie in $I\setminus F$; they cover $I\setminus F$. Let $\psi_j(t)=\exp\{-1/[(t-a_j)(b_j-t)]\}$ for $a_j<t<b_j$ and $\psi_j(t)=0$ otherwise. Each $\psi_j$ is $C^\infty$, nonnegative, positive exactly on $(a_j,b_j)$ and compactly supported, so every derivative of $\psi_j$ is bounded. Put
$$
c_j=\frac{2^{-j}}{1+\max_{0\le r\le j}\sup_I|\psi_j^{(r)}|},
\qquad
g=\sum_{j\ge1}c_j\psi_j.
\tag{I.2j.1}
$$
For each $r\ge0$ the terms with $j\ge r$ satisfy $\sup_I|c_j\psi_j^{(r)}|\le2^{-j}$, so the series of $r$-th derivatives converges uniformly on $I$. Hence $g\in C^\infty(I)$ and $g\ge0$; $g>0$ on $I\setminus F$ because the intervals cover it, and $g=0$ on $F$ because every $\psi_j$ vanishes there. If $I\setminus F$ is empty, take $g=0$. In the stated family $J_t(x_0)-J_t(x_1)=g(t)$ and $V=0$, which gives the tie set and the uniqueness assertion. ∎

**I.4 Predictive-Information Saturation in Sparse Regimes**

The coordinate $\hat C_{\mathrm{target}}$ is the internal task scale of Definition 21. It represents the complexity of externally exploitable patterns only on a branch with an innovation certificate that compares the coordinate with external records.

*   <a id="hypothesis-i1"></a>**Hypothesis I.1:** On a branch carrying an external innovation certificate for Definition 21, low-density sparse regions have a lower externally measured exploitable-pattern scale than high-density regions, and the certificate identifies this difference with a lower effective $\hat C_{\mathrm{target}}(R)$ within its registered error. Without that certificate, sparsity alone does not determine the internal target coordinate.

<a id="corollary-i2-conditional-target-scale-comparative-statics"></a>**Corollary I.2 (Conditional Target-Scale Comparative Statics).** Write $B(C;\theta)=\Gamma_0\partial_CPP(C,\theta)$ with $\theta=\hat C_{\mathrm{target}}$, and let the marginal-cost function $M(C)$ be common across the compared environments. In addition to Proposition I.2, assume that $\theta_1\le\theta_2$ implies $B(C;\theta_1)\le B(C;\theta_2)$ for every $C$. Then the unique saturation optimizers obey $C^*(\theta_1)\le C^*(\theta_2)$.

*Proof.* First suppose $C^*(\theta_2)=K_0$. Proposition I.2 gives
$$
B(K_0;\theta_2)\le M(K_0).
$$
The monotone-differences hypothesis gives
$$
B(K_0;\theta_1)\le B(K_0;\theta_2)\le M(K_0),
$$
so Proposition I.2 yields $C^*(\theta_1)=K_0=C^*(\theta_2)$.

For the second case, suppose $C^*(\theta_2)>K_0$. Then
$$
B(C^*(\theta_2);\theta_2)=M(C^*(\theta_2)),
$$
and hence
$$
B(C^*(\theta_2);\theta_1)\le M(C^*(\theta_2)).
$$
If $B(K_0;\theta_1)\le M(K_0)$, Proposition I.2 gives $C^*(\theta_1)=K_0<C^*(\theta_2)$. Otherwise Proposition I.2 gives a unique zero of $B(\cdot;\theta_1)-M$; strict decrease and the displayed nonpositive value at $C^*(\theta_2)$ place that zero at or to the left of $C^*(\theta_2)$. Thus $C^*(\theta_1)\le C^*(\theta_2)$ in every case. Without the monotone-differences premise, Hypothesis I.1 and Equation (23) do not order the PCE optimizers. ∎

**I.5 Conditional Parameter-Relaxation Mechanism after Early Saturation**

Assume a registered optimizer map $(\theta\mapsto\delta^*(\theta),p^*(\theta))$ for the complete PCE potential, with $\delta^*$ nonincreasing and $p^*$ nonincreasing in target scale, and assume the selected channel family has actual capacity $C(\mathcal E_p)$ nonincreasing in $p$ on the admitted interval. These are branch data to be proved for a concrete microscopic model; Theorem E.2 supplies an upper bound, not monotonicity of the actual capacity or of the optimizer. Under these assumptions, the lower sparse-region target of Corollary I.2 gives $\delta^*$ and $p^*$ no smaller, and $C(\mathcal E_{p^*})$ no larger. A small-spacing cost may, for example, scale as $1/\delta^2$ or $\ln(\delta_{\mathrm{ref}}/\delta)$ on a declared interval; $\ln\delta$ alone has the opposite monotonicity.

*   **Effective spacing:** $\delta^*$ is nondecreasing as the target scale decreases on the assumed monotone optimizer branch.
*   **Effective channel capacity:** $C(\mathcal E_{p^*})$ is nonincreasing as the target scale decreases under the assumed capacity monotonicity.

When the compared capacities are positive and the packing factor $\eta$ has the same positive value in both environments, these weak inequalities make $\eta(\delta^*)^2/C(\mathcal E_{p^*})$ in Equation (I.1) no smaller at the lower target scale. Strict change requires an additional strict optimizer or capacity inequality.

**I.5.1 Crossover Scale from Information Resolution Limits**

On Proposition I.3's independently registered detector-and-relaxation certificate, equality of the selected Unruh and de Sitter detector temperatures defines an acceleration crossover $a_0$. Resolution limits or MPU status alone do not derive that threshold.

<a id="proposition-i3-detector-calibrated-crossover-threshold"></a>**Proposition I.3 (Detector-Calibrated Crossover Threshold).**

Assume an independently registered detector-and-relaxation certificate which (i) validates the Unruh and de Sitter detector temperatures for the selected operational probes and (ii) defines the relaxation crossover as their equality. Then, in a de Sitter background with $\Lambda>0$, the crossover acceleration is uniquely
$$
a_0=c^2\sqrt{\frac{\Lambda}{3}}.
$$
This is an algebraic threshold calibration; temperature equality alone does not prove gradient indistinguishability or parameter relaxation.

**Physical Setup:**

**1. De Sitter detector temperature:** In a de Sitter background with $\Lambda>0$, the selected detector has the Gibbons--Hawking temperature [Gibbons & Hawking 1977]:
$$
T_{dS} = \frac{\hbar c}{2\pi k_B}\sqrt{\frac{\Lambda}{3}}
\tag{I.3.1}
$$

**2. Registered accelerated probe:** On the detector certificate, the selected uniformly accelerated probe has Unruh temperature [Unruh 1976]:
$$
T_U(a) = \frac{\hbar a}{2\pi c k_B}
\tag{I.3.2}
$$

**The Crossover Criterion on the registered certificate branch:** By definition of that branch, the relaxation threshold is the equality $T_U(a_0) = T_{dS}$:
$$
\frac{\hbar a_0}{2\pi c k_B} = \frac{\hbar c}{2\pi k_B}\sqrt{\frac{\Lambda}{3}}
$$
$$
\boxed{a_0 = c^2\sqrt{\frac{\Lambda}{3}}}
\tag{I.3.3}
$$

*Proof.* By hypothesis, the crossover occurs precisely at the threshold where the local Unruh temperature equals the de Sitter background temperature. Substituting Equations (I.3.1) and (I.3.2) into the threshold condition $T_U(a_0)=T_{dS}$ gives
$$
\frac{\hbar a_0}{2\pi c k_B} = \frac{\hbar c}{2\pi k_B}\sqrt{\frac{\Lambda}{3}}.
$$
Multiplying both sides by $2\pi c k_B/\hbar$ yields
$$
a_0 = c^2\sqrt{\frac{\Lambda}{3}}.
$$
This proves existence of a threshold acceleration with the stated value. For uniqueness, observe that for $a\ge0$ the function $T_U(a)=\hbar a/(2\pi c k_B)$ is strictly increasing in $a$, while $T_{dS}$ is a fixed positive constant when $\Lambda>0$. Therefore the equation $T_U(a)=T_{dS}$ has exactly one nonnegative solution, namely Equation (I.3.3). ∎

**Physical interpretation on that certificate branch:**
- For $a\gg a_0$, the registered detector inequality is $T_U\gg T_{dS}$; the asserted high-fidelity response additionally uses the optimizer certificate.
- For $a\ll a_0$, the registered detector inequality is $T_U\ll T_{dS}$; the asserted channel relaxation and change of effective coupling additionally use the optimizer and gravity-calibration certificates.

**Numerical Estimate:** Using $\Lambda \approx 1.1 \times 10^{-52}$ m$^{-2}$ (Planck Collaboration 2020a):
$$
a_0 \approx 5.4 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m/s}^2
\tag{I.3.4}
$$

**Connection to Empirical Scale:** The relationship to the empirical MOND scale $g_0 \approx 1.2 \times 10^{-10}$ m/s$^2$ involves an efficiency factor $\eta' = 3/(8\sqrt{3}) \approx 0.2165$ on the factor-certified bridge-law class of Appendix H, Definition H.4.2.8a. Within that class the factor is the product of four separately registered terms:
- Active-tangent contraction $a/d_0 = 1/4$, supplied by the active contraction certificate
- Repetition multiplier $w_{\mathrm{cmp}}(2\varepsilon_0)=N_{\mathrm{cmp}}=2$, supplied by the structural bridge convention and the registered two-copy i.i.d. realization
- Spatial-tangent contraction $(D-1)/D = 3/4$, supplied by the spatial contraction certificate
- Generator-amplitude normalization $1/\sqrt{K_0} = 1/\sqrt{3}$, recorded separately from the $1/K_0$ scaling of SLD QFI

<a id="corollary-i3a-cosmological-acceleration-lock-in-the-dark-sector-branch"></a>**Corollary I.3a (Cosmological Acceleration Lock in the Dark-Sector Branch).** On the Appendix H operating-point bridge representative,
$$
g_0
=
\eta' a_0
=
\frac{c^2\sqrt{\Lambda}}{8}.
$$
Define
$$
g_\Lambda:=\frac{c^2\sqrt{\Lambda}}{8}.
$$
Then every galaxy-sector transition written in terms of $g_0$ on this branch is equivalently written in terms of the cosmology-fixed scale $g_\Lambda$. The dimensionless local dark-sector trigger variable is
$$
\chi_b(x)
:=
\frac{|\nabla\Phi_b(x)|}{g_\Lambda}.
$$
No independent MOND-scale fit parameter is present once Definition H.0 and Equation H.4b are adopted.

*Proof.* Proposition I.3 gives $a_0=c^2\sqrt{\Lambda/3}$. Appendix H, Equation H.4b gives $\eta'=3/(8\sqrt3)$. Therefore
$$
g_0=\eta'a_0
=
\frac{3}{8\sqrt3}c^2\frac{\sqrt{\Lambda}}{\sqrt3}
=
\frac{c^2\sqrt{\Lambda}}{8}.
$$
The quantity $\chi_b=|\nabla\Phi_b|/g_\Lambda$ is the canonical direct dimensionless ratio of the local baryonic acceleration to the branch acceleration scale. ∎

<a id="remark-i1"></a>**Remark I.1.** The functional form $a_0 \propto c^2\sqrt{\Lambda}$ follows from equating two well-established temperatures (Unruh and de Sitter). The additional factor $\eta' = 3/(8\sqrt{3})$ is the conditional consequence of the QFI linear-response bridge law adopted in Appendix H, Definition H.0. Once that bridge-law normalization is fixed, no continuously adjustable parameter remains in the galactic-scale prediction; the scale is locked to $\Lambda$ by Corollary I.3a.

<a id="definition-i3b-predictive-focusing-and-susceptibility-datum"></a>**Definition I.3b (Predictive Focusing and Susceptibility Datum).** In this subsection use $c=\hbar=k_B=1$, take $\lambda$ to have length dimension, and measure entropy in nats. On a regular emergent metric/channel-capacity thermodynamic branch, register $G_{\mathrm{op}}>0$ as constant along the affine pencil used below, and let $k^\mu=dx^\mu/d\lambda$ be an affine null generator, let $a(\lambda)$ be the transverse area of one retained horizon pencil, and let $S_{\mathrm{pred}}(\lambda)$ be the retained predictive entropy assigned to that same pencil. Define
$$
\Theta_{\mathrm{PU}}(\lambda)
=
\frac{d}{d\lambda}
\left(
\frac{a(\lambda)}{4G_{\mathrm{op}}}+S_{\mathrm{pred}}(\lambda)
\right).
\tag{I.3b.1}
$$
A metric/channel-capacity susceptibility datum is a linear response function
$$
\chi_g(\omega,\mathbf k)
=
\frac{\delta g_{\mathrm{eff}}(\omega,\mathbf k)}
{\delta T_{\mathrm{bar}}(\omega,\mathbf k)}
\tag{I.3b.2}
$$
for the effective metric response to a retained baryonic stress perturbation, with the response normalization specified by the same operating branch as Definition H.0.

<a id="theorem-i3c-predictive-focusing-and-susceptibility-sum-rule"></a>**Theorem I.3c (Predictive Focusing and Susceptibility Sum Rule).** Suppose the retained horizon pencil satisfies
$$
\frac{1}{4G_{\mathrm{op}}}\frac{d^2a}{d\lambda^2}
=
-2\pi a(\lambda)T^{\mathrm{PU}}_{kk}
-
\mathcal S_{\mathrm{ch}},
\qquad
\mathcal S_{\mathrm{ch}}\ge0,
\tag{I.3c.1}
$$
where $T^{\mathrm{PU}}_{kk}=T^{\mathrm{PU}}_{\mu\nu}k^\mu k^\nu$ and $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{ch}}$ has dimension $L^{-2}$. Suppose also that
$$
\frac{d^2S_{\mathrm{pred}}}{d\lambda^2}
\le
2\pi a(\lambda)T^{\mathrm{PU}}_{kk}.
\tag{I.3c.2}
$$
Then
$$
\frac{d\Theta_{\mathrm{PU}}}{d\lambda}
\le
-\mathcal S_{\mathrm{ch}}
\le0.
\tag{I.3c.3}
$$

For each retained $\mathbf k$, the following explicit sufficient analytic gate implies the dispersion sum rule. Let $h(z)=\chi_g(z,\mathbf k)-\chi_\infty(\mathbf k)$, with $\chi_\infty(\mathbf k)\in\mathbb R$. Assume $h$ is holomorphic in the upper half-plane, continuous on its closure, extends holomorphically to a neighborhood of $0$, satisfies $h(-x)=\overline{h(x)}$ on the real axis, and obeys $|h(z)|\le C|z|^{-\epsilon}$ for all sufficiently large $|z|$ in the closed upper half-plane, with $C<\infty$ and $\epsilon>0$. These conditions imply finite static and high-frequency limits and absolute convergence of the imaginary-part sum rule below. Causality and passivity are separate physical admissibility requirements; they alone do not imply this uniform decay gate. Under this analytic gate,
$$
\boxed{
\chi_g(0,\mathbf k)-\chi_g(\infty,\mathbf k)
=
\frac{2}{\pi}
\int_0^\infty
\frac{\operatorname{Im}\chi_g(\omega,\mathbf k)}{\omega}\,d\omega.
}
\tag{I.3c.4}
$$

*Proof.* Differentiating (I.3b.1), substituting (I.3c.1), and applying (I.3c.2) gives
$$
\frac{d\Theta_{\mathrm{PU}}}{d\lambda}
=
\frac{1}{4G_{\mathrm{op}}}\frac{d^2a}{d\lambda^2}
+
\frac{d^2S_{\mathrm{pred}}}{d\lambda^2}
\le
-2\pi aT^{\mathrm{PU}}_{kk}-\mathcal S_{\mathrm{ch}}
+2\pi aT^{\mathrm{PU}}_{kk}
=-\mathcal S_{\mathrm{ch}}\le0.
$$

On a calibrated branch one may set $G_{\mathrm{op}}=G$; the focusing inequality itself does not perform that calibration.

For the susceptibility, integrate $h(z)/z$ around the upper half-annulus $r<|z|<R$, indenting clockwise around $0$. There are no enclosed poles. Continuity on the boundary permits taking the boundary contour as a limit of contours in the holomorphic region. The large semicircle contributes at most $\pi C R^{-\epsilon}\to0$, and the small clockwise semicircle tends to $-i\pi h(0)$. Thus
$$
\operatorname{PV}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\frac{h(x)}x\,dx=i\pi h(0).
$$
Reality gives $h(0)\in\mathbb R$ and $h(x)-h(-x)=2i\operatorname{Im}h(x)$, so pairing the positive and negative real segments yields
$$
2i\int_0^\infty\frac{\operatorname{Im}h(x)}x\,dx=i\pi h(0).
$$
The integral converges absolutely: holomorphy near $0$ and real $h(0)$ give $\operatorname{Im}h(x)=O(x)$, while uniform decay bounds the tail by $C x^{-1-\epsilon}$. Divide by $i\pi$, use $h(0)=\chi_g(0,\mathbf k)-\chi_\infty(\mathbf k)$ and $\operatorname{Im}h=\operatorname{Im}\chi_g$, and obtain (I.3c.4). This supplies an explicit sufficient branch; response functions failing its decay or boundary conditions require their own subtracted or distributional formulation. ∎

<a id="corollary-i3d-no-replacement-of-the-h-bridge-by-the-sum-rule-alone"></a>**Corollary I.3d (No Replacement of the H-Bridge by the Sum Rule Alone).** The sum rule (I.3c.4) is a consistency and spectral-reconstruction gate for any dark-sector susceptibility model. It does not by itself fix the numerical factor $\eta'=3/(8\sqrt3)$ in Corollary I.3a. That factor remains fixed by Appendix H, Definition H.0 and Equation H.4b unless a separate PU-internal theorem derives the same static normalization from the spectral density $\operatorname{Im}\chi_g$.

*Proof.* Equation (I.3c.4) determines the difference $\chi_g(0,\mathbf k)-\chi_g(\infty,\mathbf k)$ only after the spectral density and high-frequency normalization are fixed. It is therefore a dispersion constraint on an already specified susceptibility datum, not a substitute for the operating-point normalization of Appendix H. ∎

<a id="theorem-i3c5-finite-passive-rational-susceptibility-reconstruction"></a>**Theorem I.3c.5 (Finite Passive Rational-Susceptibility Reconstruction).** Fix distinct rates $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_N>0$ and the passive rational class
$$
\chi(s)=\chi_\infty+\sum_{j=1}^N\frac{a_j}{s+\lambda_j},
\qquad a_j\ge0,
\qquad s>0.
\tag{I.3c.5.1}
$$
If $\chi_\infty$ and $\chi(s_k)$ are supplied at $N$ distinct positive sample points $s_1,\ldots,s_N$, then the residues $a_j$ are unique. They are obtained from the Cauchy system
$$
\chi(s_k)-\chi_\infty
=
\sum_{j=1}^N\frac{a_j}{s_k+\lambda_j},
\tag{I.3c.5.2}
$$
whose determinant is
$$
\det\!\left[\frac1{s_k+\lambda_j}\right]_{k,j=1}^N
=
\pm
\frac{\prod_{k<\ell}(s_\ell-s_k)\prod_{j<\ell}(\lambda_\ell-\lambda_j)}
{\prod_{k,j}(s_k+\lambda_j)}
\ne0.
\tag{I.3c.5.3}
$$
The sampled record belongs to the passive class exactly when the reconstructed residues are nonnegative, and then
$$
\chi(0)=\chi_\infty+\sum_{j=1}^N\frac{a_j}{\lambda_j}
\tag{I.3c.5.4}
$$
is fixed. By contrast, pole locations and a normalized line shape without one absolute-amplitude datum leave the scaling modulus $a\mapsto ca$, $c>0$, and do not fix (I.3c.5.4).

*Proof.* The Cauchy determinant formula gives (I.3c.5.3), so (I.3c.5.2) has exactly one solution. The class definition makes nonnegativity of that solution necessary and sufficient for passivity within the declared finite family. Setting $s=0$ proves (I.3c.5.4). Positive common rescaling preserves pole locations and normalized residue ratios while changing the static susceptibility, proving the final statement. ∎

<a id="theorem-i3c6-unknown-pole-passive-reconstruction-and-nonrational-nonidentifiability"></a>**Theorem I.3c.6 (Unknown-Pole Passive Reconstruction and Nonrational Nonidentifiability).** For an integer $N\ge1$, let $\mathcal P_N$ be the class of functions
$$
\chi(s)=\chi_\infty+\sum_{j=1}^n\frac{a_j}{s+\lambda_j},
\qquad s>0,
\tag{I.3c.6.1}
$$
with $0\le n\le N$, $\chi_\infty\in\mathbb R$, $a_j>0$ and distinct $\lambda_j>0$, the poles being unknown. Let $\mathcal S$ be the passive relaxation class
$$
\chi(s)=\chi_\infty+\int_{(0,\infty)}\frac{d\mu(\lambda)}{s+\lambda},
\qquad
\int_{(0,\infty)}\frac{d\mu(\lambda)}{\lambda}<\infty,
\tag{I.3c.6.2}
$$
with $\mu$ a positive Borel measure. Here $\chi-\chi_\infty$ is the Laplace transform of the completely monotone retarded relaxation kernel $\phi(t)=\int e^{-\lambda t}\,d\mu(\lambda)$, $t>0$, and $\mathcal P_N\subset\mathcal S$. Then:

1. Two members of $\mathcal P_N$ that agree at $2N+1$ distinct points of $(0,\infty)$ coincide, including their pole sets, residues, $\chi_\infty$ and $\chi(0)=\chi_\infty+\sum_ja_j/\lambda_j$. If both carry the same supplied $\chi_\infty$, agreement at $2N$ distinct points suffices.

2. Both counts are sharp. For every $2N-1$ distinct points of $(0,\infty)$ there are two members of $\mathcal P_N$ with $\chi_\infty=0$, each with exactly $N$ poles, that agree at those points and have different values of $\chi(0)$. For every $2N$ distinct points there are two members of $\mathcal P_N$, each with exactly $N$ poles, that agree at those points and have different values of $\chi(0)$.

3. A member of $\mathcal S$ is determined by its values on any subset of $(0,\infty)$ having an accumulation point in $(0,\infty)$: these values fix $\chi$ on $(0,\infty)$, $\chi_\infty=\lim_{s\to\infty}\chi(s)$, $\chi(0)=\lim_{s\downarrow0}\chi(s)=\chi_\infty+\int d\mu/\lambda$, and $\mu$. No finite set of sample values determines $\chi(0)$ on $\mathcal S$. The same two conclusions hold on the causal class of Theorem I.3c sampled at imaginary frequency: if $\chi_g(\cdot,\mathbf k)$ satisfies the analytic gate stated there, its values at $\omega=is$ for $s$ in such a set fix $\chi_\infty(\mathbf k)$ and $\chi_g(\cdot,\mathbf k)$ on the closed upper half-plane, including $\chi_g(0,\mathbf k)$, while no finite set of values at $\omega=is$, $s>0$, determines $\chi_g(0,\mathbf k)$ on that class.

The fixed-pole reconstruction of Theorem I.3c.5 therefore extends to unknown poles at the sharp count $2N+1$, or $2N$ with $\chi_\infty$ supplied, while on the nonrational passive class and on the causal class of Theorem I.3c finite samples never fix the static normalization.

*Proof.* Item 1. Write $Q_i=\prod_j(s+\lambda^{(i)}_j)$, of degree $n_i\le N$, for the two members. Then $\chi_1-\chi_2=P/(Q_1Q_2)$ with
$$
P=(\chi_{\infty,1}-\chi_{\infty,2})Q_1Q_2+Q_2\sum_ja^{(1)}_j\prod_{k\ne j}\bigl(s+\lambda^{(1)}_k\bigr)-Q_1\sum_ja^{(2)}_j\prod_{k\ne j}\bigl(s+\lambda^{(2)}_k\bigr),
$$
a polynomial of degree at most $2N$, and at most $2N-1$ when $\chi_{\infty,1}=\chi_{\infty,2}$. Since $Q_1Q_2>0$ on $(0,\infty)$, agreement at $2N+1$ points, or at $2N$ points in the second case, makes $P$ vanish identically. The two members are then the same rational function, and uniqueness of partial fractions with nonzero residues identifies $\chi_\infty$, the poles $-\lambda_j$ and the residues $a_j$; setting $s=0$ gives $\chi(0)$.

Item 2. Let $0<s_1<\cdots<s_\ell$ be the sample points and choose rates $0<\theta_1<\cdots<\theta_{2N}$. Every square submatrix of $[1/(s_k+\theta_j)]$ with increasing row and column indices has the positive Cauchy determinant $\prod_{k<k'}(s_{k'}-s_k)\prod_{j<j'}(\theta_{j'}-\theta_j)/\prod_{k,j}(s_k+\theta_j)$. Appending a last column of ones keeps every maximal minor positive: multiplying a further last column $1/(s_k+\theta)$ by $\theta$ and letting $\theta\to\infty$, the factors containing $\theta$ in the Cauchy formula combine to $\theta\prod_j(\theta-\theta_j)/\prod_k(s_k+\theta)\to1$, so
$$
\det\Bigl[\frac1{s_k+\theta_j}\Bigm|1\Bigr]
=\frac{\prod_{k<k'}(s_{k'}-s_k)\prod_{j<j'}(\theta_{j'}-\theta_j)}{\prod_{k,j}(s_k+\theta_j)}>0,
$$
the products running over the rows and the retained rates. Let $M$ be the $(2N-1)\times2N$ matrix $[1/(s_k+\theta_j)]$ when $\ell=2N-1$, and the $2N\times(2N+1)$ matrix $[1/(s_k+\theta_j)\mid1]$ when $\ell=2N$. All maximal minors of $M$ are positive, so the vector $c$ with $c_i=(-1)^i\det M^{(i)}$, where $M^{(i)}$ deletes column $i$, satisfies $Mc=0$ by Laplace expansion of a determinant with a repeated row, and its entries alternate strictly in sign. Split the pole terms by the sign of $c_j$: $\chi_\pm(s)=\sum_{\pm c_j>0}|c_j|/(s+\theta_j)$, each with exactly $N$ poles. When $\ell=2N$, the entry $c_{2N+1}$ is negative because $2N+1$ is odd, its magnitude $|c_{2N+1}|$ is the constant $\chi_\infty$ of $\chi_-$, and $\chi_+$ has $\chi_\infty=0$. In both cases $D:=\chi_+-\chi_-$ equals $\sum_{j\le2N}c_j/(s+\theta_j)$, plus $c_{2N+1}$ when $\ell=2N$, so its value at $s_k$ is the $k$th entry of $Mc=0$, and $D=P/\prod_j(s+\theta_j)$ with $P\ne0$ of degree at most $\ell$ vanishing at the $\ell$ sample points. Hence $P=\kappa\prod_k(s-s_k)$ with $\kappa\ne0$, and $D(0)=\kappa\prod_k(-s_k)/\prod_j\theta_j\ne0$.

Item 3. For $\operatorname{Re}s>0$ and $\lambda>0$, one has $|s+\lambda|\ge\lambda$ and $|s+\lambda|^{-2}\le(\lambda\operatorname{Re}s)^{-1}$, so (I.3c.6.2) defines a holomorphic function on the right half-plane by dominated differentiation under the integral. Agreement on a set with an accumulation point in $(0,\infty)$ therefore gives agreement on $(0,\infty)$ by the identity theorem. Dominated convergence with the integrable majorant $1/\lambda$ gives $\chi(s)\to\chi_\infty$ as $s\to\infty$, and monotone convergence gives the limit $\chi(0)$ as $s\downarrow0$. Tonelli's theorem gives $\chi(s)-\chi_\infty=\int_0^\infty e^{-st}\phi(t)\,dt$ with $\phi$ continuous and integrable on $(0,\infty)$, so uniqueness of the Laplace transform fixes $\phi$ and then $\mu$. Finally, given finitely many sample points, adjoin points until their number is even and positive, say $2N$, and apply item 2: two members of $\mathcal P_N\subset\mathcal S$ agree at all of them and have different $\chi(0)$. For the analytic gate of Theorem I.3c, $s\mapsto\chi_g(is,\mathbf k)=\chi_\infty(\mathbf k)+h(is)$ is holomorphic on $\operatorname{Re}s>0$, so the identity theorem fixes it there; the decay bound gives $\chi_\infty(\mathbf k)$ as its limit as $s\to\infty$, and $h$ is then fixed on the open upper half-plane and, by continuity, on its closure, including $h(0)$. Every member of $\mathcal P_N$ gives $h(\omega)=\sum_ja_j/(\lambda_j-i\omega)$, which equals the pole sum of (I.3c.6.1) at $\omega=is$, has its poles in the lower half-plane, is holomorphic near $0$, satisfies $h(-x)=\overline{h(x)}$ and obeys $|h(z)|\le C|z|^{-1}$ for large $|z|$; the countermodels of item 2 therefore lie in that class. ∎

<a id="theorem-i3c7-forward-metric-susceptibility-and-absolute-normalization"></a>**Theorem I.3c.7 (Forward Metric Susceptibility and Absolute Normalization).** The following independently specified material source supplies the forward susceptibility datum of Definition I.3b on its admitted fixed-coupling branch. All clocks, source/stress maps, finite response and approximation domains are retained below.

#### Result and exact scope

A homogeneous, zero-background-stress material field coupled to the fixed-coupling Einstein action has an exactly invariant transverse-traceless (TT) linear-response sector. Its poles and absolute amplitude follow from its local strain energy, inertial density, outgoing reservoir and the independently normalized gravitational action. No response samples or dark-sector observations enter the construction.

The result is on the regular, fixed-coupling metric branch admitted by Definition I.3b and Theorem 12.1a. It is a source realization of one metric susceptibility, not a selection of this material by PCE or a galaxy/cluster prediction. The exact dynamical domain is the quadratic response about the specified stationary background. The matter completion, its zero background stress, its linear conservation identity, the TT projection and the finite-register response realization are supplied below. The zero-input reservoir is distinct from the upstream horizon/KMS state. The H.0 coefficient is implemented on a co-registered acceleration coordinate; it does not rescale the metric kinetic coefficient.

#### 1. Original predicates and imported normalization

Spectral reconstruction of the susceptibility requires the poles or relaxation measure and the absolute normalization. Theorems I.3c.5–I.3c.6 settle reconstruction and identifiability. Its forward physical object is I.3b.2, $\delta g_{\mathrm{eff}}/\delta T_{\mathrm{bar}}$, with normalization on the same operating branch as H.0. The analytic-gate class of Theorem I.3c need not have a positive Stieltjes relaxation measure: damped inertial poles are permitted by I.3c.

Use the fixed-coupling action of Theorem 12.1a. In SI units its TT kinetic density for $h_{xx}=h$, $h_{yy}=-h$ is

$$
L_{\mathrm{EH,TT}}=c^{2}/(32\pi G_{\mathrm{op}})\,[\dot{h}^{2}-c^{2}|\nabla h|^{2}].
\tag{I.3c.7.1}
$$

The coupling is the variational one, $\delta\bar{S}=(1/2)\int\bar{T}^{ij}\,\delta g_{ij}\,dt\,d^3x$. No coefficient of (I.3c.7.1) is fitted to the response.

For the source's capacity record, each register cell consists of three qubits $A,B,R$. The channel $E$ resets $R$ and transports $A,B$ without noise. Its retained label output is supported on a four-dimensional space; four orthogonal messages attain its unassisted regularized HSW capacity $C=\ln 4=2\ln 2$. For $n$ uses the output-label support is $4^n$ dimensional, so the Holevo bound is $n\ln 4$ and the product basis code attains equality, including against inputs entangled across uses. Independent crossing links on the cubic planar-slab geometry of E.5.2 have $\eta=\chi=1$ and proper spacing $\delta$. The geometric census is unchanged when each crossing link is supplied with this two-bit identity channel: the two surface components have one link per proper surface cell of area $\delta^{2}$, and every link carries precisely one four-message alphabet. Uniform four-message states attain entropy $C$ per effective crossing and are additive. Thus the saturated operational coefficient is, directly from E.7/I.1,

$$
G_{\mathrm{op}}=\delta^{2}c^{3}/(8\hbar\ln 2).
\tag{I.3c.7.2}
$$

The horizon-entropy/metric-action identification is the admitted upstream thermodynamic branch, rather than a consequence of writing a register Hamiltonian. Equation (I.3c.7.2) fixes the absolute coupling of this branch in its independently declared length unit $\delta$. An empirical identification with Newton's G would be a separate calibration.

##### 1a. Common carrier and the boundary/bulk distinction

The composite realization has three different, explicitly owned subsystems: spatial boundary communication cells B, the bulk material/reservoir M, and the final probe D. They are coupled to one metric g and one proper-time normalization. The bulk normal-mode registers in section 7 are a finite encoding of M; they are not relabeled as the spatial boundary cells B. Appendix B's variational bulk source and Appendix E's boundary capacity coefficient have different roles in the original branch.

The boundary geometry is the actual proper-area geometry of this $g$. On a flat transverse periodic slab with side lengths integer multiples of $\delta$, one boundary component has precisely $A/\delta^2$ crossing cells; two components have $2A/\delta^2$. For each crossing, four orthogonal retained labels give entropy $\ln 4$ and the identity label channel gives capacity $\ln 4$. A proper-cell subdivision under a changed metric uses the same local normal-coordinate construction and the density certificate already admitted with E.6. Its entropy functional is therefore $S_B(g,\Sigma)=k_B\,C\,A_g(\Sigma)/\delta^2$, with the declared boundary remainder of that certificate. In particular its area and first variation are those of $g$, not of a second metric inferred from a register index. On the TT transverse plane, $dA_g=\sqrt{1-h^2f^2}\,dx\,dy$, so its first-order area variation vanishes, consistently with the constant local coefficient (I.3c.7.2).

The communication link's timing record is its null transport record on this same geometry: for an x-directed link between fixed coordinate endpoints separated by L, its one-way first-order arrival delay is

$$
\delta t_e=(1/(2c))\int_0^Lh(t_{\mathrm{em}}+x/c)\,f(z_e)\,dx.
\tag{I.3c.7.2a}
$$

Here $h(t)\,f(z_e)$ is the metric coefficient in section 3. This follows directly by integrating $ds^2=-c^2dt^2+(1+hf)dx^2=0$ along the unperturbed ray. Internal four-label transport is the identity while this physical arrival-time response changes. The per-use launch time and waveform are fixed and message-independent. At a fixed source perturbation $P$ the extended output is $\Phi_P(\rho)=\Phi_{\mathrm{reset}}(\rho)\otimes\tau_{\mathrm{timing}}(P)$, so the timing factor cancels from every Holevo entropy difference, including at every block length. Its unassisted HSW capacity remains $\ln 4$. Message-controlled timing or waveform alphabets are outside this registered per-use channel. The Appendix E capacity/entropy count is the retained label ledger; the timing record is a source-dependent geometry observable. Thus capacity, proper areas and transport timing refer to the same metric as the source response; an identity label channel is not interpreted as response-null geometry. The reference-field/probe construction keeps these timing records as well as the labels.

The channel entropy states may be carried by degenerate memory Hamiltonians, whose static variational stress is zero. Actual transfer, preparation and reset pulses have their own energy and variational stress and are included in the total source whenever they are present. They are used to calibrate the operating branch and are inactive during the unforced bulk response experiment. The calibration records do not assert that finite-energy signals have zero gravitational back-reaction. Equation (I.3c.7.2) is the fixed upstream normalization consumed by the response experiment; it is not recomputed from a bulk normal-mode basis.

The common dictionary is consequently: boundary $B\to$ ($C$, proper-area density, null timing) $\to$ the accepted Wald-normalized coefficient $G_{\mathrm{op}}$; bulk $M\to$ its metric-variational $T_{m}$ and proper-time generator; baryonic input $\to$ the tensor projection (I.3c.7.7); shared Einstein action $\to h$; $h\to$ proper-length, arrival-time and tidal probe records. Every arrow introduced for the new bulk source is proved below. The horizon/KMS-to-Einstein identification remains the original admitted branch premise, not a newly claimed derivation from the encoding.

#### 2. A common covariant source action with a stationary background

Work with signature $(-,+,+,+)$, $x^0=ct$, and a flat background. All fields below are varied; reference fields are not external spurions. Let $\tau$ be a scalar with timelike gradient, let $u_\mu=-\partial_\mu\tau/\sqrt{-g^{ab}\partial_a\tau\,\partial_b\tau}$, and let $D_t=c\,u^\mu\partial_\mu$. Let $X^I$, $I=1,2,3$, be material-coordinate scalar fields, with dimensions of length. Define

$$
\begin{aligned}
B^{IJ} &= g^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu X^{I}\partial_\nu X^{J}, \\
S^{IJ} &= (B^{IJ}-\delta^{IJ})_{\mathrm{TF}}/2.
\end{aligned}
$$

Here $\mathrm{TF}$ is the traceless part in the fixed internal Euclidean metric. $Q^{IJ}$ is a symmetric traceless internal tensor with dimensions of length. $Y^{IJ}(r,x)$, $r\ge 0$, is an owned continuum of symmetric traceless reservoir coordinates, with $Y(0,x)=Q(x)$. The index $r$ is a reservoir coordinate, not an additional spacetime dimension. Its local chain realization is given in section 7.

The matter action is $S_m=(1/c)\int d^4x\,\sqrt{-g}\,L_m$, with $x^0=ct$ and $L_{m}$ in $\mathrm{J/m^3}$. Its scalar Lagrangian is

$$
\begin{aligned}
L_m &= \rho_X/2 \sum_I (D_t X^I)^2\\
&\quad + \rho/4 \operatorname{tr}[(D_t Q)^2]\\
&\quad - \kappa/4 \operatorname{tr}[(Q-\ell S)^2]\\
&\quad + (1/4) \int_0^\infty\\
&\qquad \{\rho_b \operatorname{tr}[(D_t Y)^2] - \tau_b \operatorname{tr}[(\partial_r Y)^2]\}\, dr.
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.3c.7.3}
$$

All $\rho_X,\rho,\kappa,\rho_b,\tau_b,\ell$ are positive, independently declared source coefficients. Units are $\rho,\rho_X$: $\mathrm{kg/m^3}$; $\kappa$: $\mathrm{kg/(m^3\,s^2)}$; $\rho_b$: $\mathrm{kg/m^4}$; $\tau_b$: $\mathrm{kg/(m^2\,s^2)}$; $\ell$: m. The Hamiltonian of its quadratic material perturbations is nonnegative. The field $\tau$ fixes the material rest foliation and is included in the variational equations. A proper-time clock along $u$ is used throughout.

The background is

$$
g=\eta,\quad \tau=x^{0},\quad X^{I}=x^{I},\quad Q=0,\quad Y=0.
\tag{I.3c.7.4}
$$

Every squared quantity in (I.3c.7.3) vanishes at (I.3c.7.4). Consequently both $L_{m}$ and its first variation with respect to every field and the metric vanish. In particular the complete background material stress is exactly zero. This is not the subtraction of the rest energy of a stretched physical string. The reservoir is a field of internal coordinates with the action displayed in (I.3c.7.3); its background has zero strain, zero kinetic energy and zero stress by direct variation. Minkowski with $\Lambda=0$ is therefore a stationary solution of the common Einstein-matter action before the baryonic perturbation is applied.

For perturbations $X=x+\xi$ and $g_{ij}=\delta_{ij}+h_{ij}$,

$$
\delta S_{ij}=(\partial_i\xi_j+\partial_j\xi_i-h_{ij})_{\mathrm{TF}}/2.
\tag{I.3c.7.5}
$$

The $\rho_{X}$ term supplies positive phonon inertia. At quadratic order the material energy is a sum of positive kinetic terms, the positive strain square and positive reservoir-gradient energy. Zero-energy relabeling/static-relaxation directions are not asserted to be coercive. No nonlinear stability theorem outside this tangent branch is needed or claimed.

The reference-clock sector has an explicit constrained positive kinetic structure. On the background metric its quadratic kinetic term is $\rho_X|\dot{\xi}-c\nabla(\delta\tau)|^2/2$. Writing $p_\xi=\rho_X[\dot{\xi}-c\nabla(\delta\tau)]$, the quadratic Hamiltonian is

$$
\begin{aligned}
H_{m,2} &= \int\bigl\{|p_\xi|^{2}/(2\rho_X) \\
&\qquad +\operatorname{tr}(P_Q^{2})/\rho \\
&\qquad +\kappa\operatorname{tr}[(Q-\ell\,\delta S)^{2}]/4 \\
&\qquad +\int[\operatorname{tr}(P_Y^{2})/\rho_b \\
&\qquad\qquad +\tau_b\operatorname{tr}(Y_r^{2})/4]\,dr \\
&\qquad +c\,p_\xi\cdot\nabla(\delta\tau)\bigr\}\,d^{3}x.
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.3c.7.5a}
$$

The $\tau$ variation imposes $\operatorname{div}(p_\xi)=0$. On periodic boundaries or vanishing boundary flux, the last integral is $-c\int\delta\tau\,\operatorname{div}(p_\xi)=0$. Thus the constrained quadratic matter energy is nonnegative. The shift supplies the corresponding momentum constraint. In the TT sector all $\xi$, $\delta\tau$ and $p_{\xi}$ vanish, and the metric's physical TT kinetic energy is positive by (I.3c.7.1). This proves the needed stable kinetic structure and the exact retained-sector positivity; it does not assert coercivity of the zero modes or a full nonlinear constraint-stability theorem.

The coefficients $\rho_{X}$ and $\rho$ are kinetic coefficients of the displayed reference/material fields. No separate density of massive baryonic carrier hardware is present in (I.3c.7.3). Their vacuum is the field configuration (I.3c.7.4), and its full stress vanishes by variation, rather than only its TT projection. The proper clock is the metric proper time selected by the dynamical unit-gradient foliation; $\tau$ is a constrained reference field, not an uncounted physical timing apparatus. Any additional massive carrier, physical support or finite-temperature bath would add its action and stress and would define another source model. The finite quantum source below gives its own complete nonnegative Hamiltonian with a zero-energy ground, so no oscillator zero-point subtraction is needed for that realization.

Diffeomorphism invariance of (I.3c.7.3), with $\tau$ and X varied, gives the matter Ward identity: the divergence of its variational stress is a sum of its field equations multiplied by their spacetime derivatives. It vanishes on shell. Below the stronger explicit linear TT conservation check is made; the unforced scalar/reference equations are also checked, rather than discarded.

#### 3. Exact invariant tensor sector and genuine baryonic source projection

For a nonzero spatial wave vector $k$ choose the $z$ axis along $k$, and the polarization $e=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,0)$, with $\operatorname{tr}(e^2)=2$. The real Fourier mode $f$ has mean-square normalization $\int f^2\,d^3x=V$. Equivalently these formulas are fiberwise Fourier formulas for finite-energy wave packets in the homogeneous infinite medium; $V$ is a mode-normalization volume and cancels from the measured susceptibility.

Set

$$
\begin{aligned}
&h_{ij}=h(t)e_{ij}f,\quad Q_{ij}=q(t)e_{ij}f,\quad Y_{ij}=y(r,t)e_{ij}f, \\
&\xi=0,\quad \delta\tau=0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.3c.7.6}
$$

Homogeneity makes every Fourier fiber invariant. Since $e_{iz}=0$ and $\operatorname{tr}e=0$, the variation of (I.3c.7.3) with respect to $\xi$ is proportional to the spatial divergence of an $e\,f$ tensor and is zero. The $\tau$ equation has no TT linear forcing: any linear terms in its scalar/reference perturbations vanish at $\xi=\delta\tau=0$, and neither the trace-free transverse strain nor the $Q/Y$ sector produces a linear scalar source. The linear material stress has only TT spatial components; the lapse, shift, scalar and vector field equations are therefore unforced in this sector. Thus (I.3c.7.6) is an invariant linear sector, not an arbitrary Galerkin deletion.

The retained source coordinate is the actual tensor projection

$$
P(t)=(1/(2V))\int e_{ij}f(x)\,\delta\bar{T}^{ij}(t,x)\,d^{3}x.
\tag{I.3c.7.7}
$$

It has units Pa. A pure input component is $\delta\bar{T}^{ij}=P\,e_{ij}f$, $\delta\bar{T}^{0\mu}=0$. It is symmetric, trace-free and conserved to first order: $\partial_i T^{ij}=0$ because the variation is along $z$ and $e_{zj}=0$. Time dependence does not spoil this identity. $P$ is anisotropic stress, not isotropic pressure renamed as a gravitational source. General conserved baryonic perturbations are first TT-projected; only (I.3c.7.7) drives this polarization. Stress perturbations need not individually obey positivity conditions imposed on complete matter states. This is the usual tangent-source domain in I.3b.

The source term from the same variational action is exactly $VPh$. The following positive massive-baryon realization supplies the signed retained perturbation. Take particles of rest mass $m_{b}>0$ with the minimally coupled worldline action $-m_b c\int ds$. Its metric derivative gives $T^{00}=nE$, $T^{0i}=nc\,p_{i}$ and $T^{ij}=nc^2p_ip_j/E$ for a monoenergetic stream, where $E=\sqrt{m_b^2c^4+c^2|p|^2}$ includes the rest energy.

Let $n_0(x)$ be a smooth nonnegative compactly supported total pair-density profile, $N_b=\int n_0<\infty$. In family $A$, half the particles have momentum $(p_{\mathrm{perp}},0,p_z)$ and half $(-p_{\mathrm{perp}},0,p_z)$. In family $B$ use $(0,p_{\mathrm{perp}},p_z)$ and $(0,-p_{\mathrm{perp}},p_z)$. Scale every density by $\epsilon\ge 0$ and propagate each stream by its own free velocity $c^{2}p/E$. For either family $F\in\{A,B\}$, its complete tensor before projection is

$$
\begin{aligned}
T_F^{\mu\nu}(t,x) &= \epsilon/2\sum_\sigma n_0(x-v_{F,\sigma}t) \\
&\qquad [c^{2}p_{F,\sigma}^{\mu}p_{F,\sigma}^{\nu}/E], \\
p_{F,\sigma}^{0} &= E/c.
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.3c.7.7b}
$$

Each summand is conserved because $(\partial_t+v_{F,\sigma}\cdot\nabla)n_0(x-v_{F,\sigma}t)=0$. Both families have finite positive total energy $\epsilon N_bE$, conserved stress at linear order, equal rest-energy records and equal longitudinal momentum records. Their metric corrections to particle trajectories contribute only at second order in $\epsilon$ on the fixed finite observation domain.

For the retained $k=(0,0,k_z)$ use the complex Fourier version of (I.3c.7.7), with the conjugated mode $\exp(-ik_z z)$ in the projection and the same reference-volume convention for both source and response. Define $\hat{n}(k)=V^{-1}\int n_0(x)\exp(-ik_z z)\,d^3x$. In a real orthonormal mode convention $f_{\cos}=\sqrt{2}\cos(k_z z)$, the corresponding row is $P_{\cos}=\sqrt{2}\operatorname{Re}P_{k}$; for $f_{\sin}=\sqrt{2}\sin(k_z z)$, $P_{\sin}=-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{Im}P_{k}$. The susceptibility is the same in each convention because source and response receive the same conversion. Transverse translation does not change this row. Each individual stream has density coefficient $(\epsilon/2)\hat{n}(k)\exp(-ik_z v_z t)$, and each summed pair has coefficient $\epsilon\,\hat{n}(k)\exp(-ik_z v_z t)$, where $v_z=c^2p_z/E$. The difference between the two positive-family right derivatives at $\epsilon=0$ is exactly

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Delta T^{xx}_k &= -\Delta T^{yy}_k \\
&= \hat{n}(k)\,c^{2}p_\perp^{2}/E\,\exp(-ik_zv_zt), \\
\Delta T^{00}_k &= \Delta T^{0i}_k=\Delta T^{zz}_k \\
&= \Delta T^{xy}_k=\Delta T^{xz}_k=\Delta T^{yz}_k=0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.3c.7.7a}
$$

It is precisely the input (I.3c.7.7) in this row. The response is the difference of the two first-order metric responses. No positive stress state with zero energy density is asserted, and no baryonic rest stress is removed by subtraction from an individual source. At $\epsilon=0$ both physical families are vacuum, so the common zero-stress Minkowski background is preserved. Other Fourier rows and non-TT fields are included in the complete beam record and decouple from this retained row by homogeneity. Varying $p_{z}$ gives physical harmonics $|\omega|<c|k|$ with nonzero $p_{\mathrm{perp}}$. The full retarded response to conserved test stresses is derived from the action; these beams establish a genuine baryonic source domain rather than claiming every test waveform is a free-beam waveform.

Substitution of (I.3c.7.6) into (I.3c.7.1) and (I.3c.7.3) gives, exactly at quadratic order,

$$
\begin{aligned}
L &= A/2\,(\dot{h}^{2}-\Omega^{2}h^{2}) \\
&\quad +M/2\,\dot{q}^{2}-K/2\,(q+ah)^{2}+VPh \\
&\quad +1/2\int_0^\infty(\mu\dot{y}^{2}-Ty_r^{2})\,dr,
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.3c.7.8}
$$

where every coefficient is determined from (I.3c.7.1)–(I.3c.7.3):

$$
\begin{aligned}
&A=Vc^{2}/(16\pi G_{\mathrm{op}}),\quad \Omega=c|k|, \\
&M=V\rho,\quad K=V\kappa,\quad a=\ell/2, \\
&\mu=V\rho_b,\quad T=V\tau_b.
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.3c.7.9}
$$

The material tensor source obtained by varying (I.3c.7.3) is

$$
\delta T_{m,ij}=-\kappa a(q+ah)e_{ij}f.
\tag{I.3c.7.10}
$$

It obeys the same explicit linear conservation identity. The metric equation derived from (I.3c.7.8) is therefore also the TT projection of the common Einstein equation with the baryonic source (I.3c.7.7) and material source (I.3c.7.10).

#### 4. Owned reservoir, physical clock and exact forward response

Take zero reservoir perturbation initially and no incoming signal at $r=\infty$. Its wave speed is $v=\sqrt{T/\mu}=\sqrt{\tau_b/\rho_b}$. Choose $v\le c$ as a source causality constraint. The endpoint equation $y(0,t)=q(t)$ has the outgoing solution

$$
y(r,t)=q(t-r/v),\quad\text{with } q(t)=0\text{ for } t<0.
$$

The force on the endpoint is $T\,y_r(0,t)=-Z\dot{q}(t)$, where

$$
Z=\sqrt{T\mu}=V\sqrt{\tau_b\rho_b}.
\tag{I.3c.7.11}
$$

Thus neither a damping rate nor a reservoir spectral measure is inserted into the response. Both follow from the local reservoir action and its outgoing condition. The reservoir energy deposited by time t is exactly

$$
E_b(t)=Z\int_0^t\dot{q}(u)^{2}\,du.
\tag{I.3c.7.12}
$$

It is finite for every finite-duration finite-energy drive. Reservoir records are retained as outgoing memory; a repeated-use reset or replacement must own that energy. This zero-perturbation source state is not identified with a finite-temperature bath.

Equations (I.3c.7.8) are

$$
\begin{aligned}
A(\ddot{h}+\Omega^{2}h)+Ka(q+ah) &= VP, \\
M\ddot{q}+Z\dot{q}+K(q+ah) &= 0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.3c.7.13}
$$

All times and rates use the proper time of (I.3c.7.4), fixed by $g_{tt}=-c^2$. The same clock is the material derivative in (I.3c.7.3), the outgoing bath clock, the Einstein tensor clock and the detector clock. The source does not substitute an entropy count or a freely rescaled PCE iteration for seconds.

For Re $s>0$, the exact retarded susceptibility is

$$
\chi_{hP}(s)=V(Ms^{2}+Zs+K)/D(s),
\tag{I.3c.7.14}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
D(s) &= AMs^{4}+AZs^{3} \\
&\quad +[AK+AM\Omega^{2}+Ka^{2}M]s^{2} \\
&\quad +[AZ\Omega^{2}+Ka^{2}Z]s+AK\Omega^{2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.3c.7.15}
$$

The poles are exactly the four roots of (I.3c.7.15), except for cancellations. With the strictly positive coefficients in (I.3c.7.9) and $a>0$, there are no cancellations: a common zero would have $Ms^2+Zs+K=0$ and $D=-K^2a^2$, a contradiction. The residues at a simple root $s_{j}$ are

$$
\operatorname{Res}_j\chi=V(Ms_j^{2}+Zs_j+K)/D'(s_j).
\tag{I.3c.7.16}
$$

Repeated roots have their uniquely determined higher Laurent coefficients. These are derived source outputs, not fitted coordinates.

#### 5. Stability, passivity, analytic gate and absolute normalization

Let

$$
E=A\dot{h}^{2}/2+M\dot{q}^{2}/2+A\Omega^{2}h^{2}/2+K(q+ah)^{2}/2.
$$

Then (I.3c.7.13) gives

$$
\dot{E}=VP\dot{h}-Z\dot{q}^{2}.
\tag{I.3c.7.17}
$$

The stiffness matrix is positive definite because its determinant is A K $\Omega^{2}>0$. An unforced imaginary-axis mode must have $\dot{q}=0$ by (I.3c.7.17). A nonzero-frequency such mode has $q=0$; the second equation then forces $h=0$. A zero-frequency mode is excluded by positive stiffness. Standard finite-dimensional energy dissipation, or the same eigenvector calculation with Re $s\ge 0$, therefore puts every root of D strictly in Re $s<0$.

For a real frequency $\omega>0$, the cycle-averaged supplied power is $(V\omega/2)\operatorname{Im}\chi_{hP}(\omega)|P|^2$ under the convention $s=-i\omega$. Equation (I.3c.7.17) makes it nonnegative. Thus $\operatorname{Im}\chi_{hP}(\omega)\ge 0$. The rational function is real under conjugation, has no poles on or above the real $\omega$ axis, is holomorphic near zero, and decays as $O(|\omega|^{-2})$ uniformly in the closed upper half-plane. It satisfies exactly I.3c's sufficient analytic gate. Its generally complex poles do not make it a Stieltjes relaxation function, and that stronger claim is not used.

Directly from the source action,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\chi_{hP}(\infty) &= 0, \\
\chi_{hP}(0) &= V/(A\Omega^{2}) \\
&= 16\pi G_{\mathrm{op}}/(c^{4}|k|^{2}) \\
&= 2\pi\delta^{2}/(\hbar c\ln 2\,|k|^{2}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.3c.7.18}
$$

The source's equilibrium $q=-ah$ relaxes its strain. This explains why its static response equals the fixed-$G$ tensor response while its dynamical poles differ. A non-GR static excess is not an extra predicate in I.3b. Equation (I.3c.7.18) and the pole residues satisfy the sum rule I.3c.4; the amplitude follows independently from the capacity-normalized action, rather than being chosen to enforce that integral.

The physical tidal coupling is derived rather than identified with a uniform force by name. The finite probe multiplies it by $F_d(s)$. In (I.3c.7.20) the high-frequency feedthrough is $-\eta'L_dV/(2A)$; the static value is zero. #### 7. Finite three-qubit source Hamiltonians and controlled reservoir refinement

For a spatial Fourier fiber, discretize $r$ by $\epsilon$ and retain $N$ reservoir coordinates $y_j$, $j=1,\dots,N$, with $y_0=q$ and a free far endpoint. The source's quadratic Hamiltonian is

$$
\begin{aligned}
H_N &= p_h^{2}/(2A)+p_q^{2}/(2M)+A\Omega^{2}h^{2}/2+K(q+ah)^{2}/2 \\
&\quad +\sum_jp_j^{2}/(2\mu\epsilon) \\
&\quad +T/(2\epsilon)\sum_{j=1}^{N}(y_j-y_{j-1})^{2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.3c.7.21}
$$

Its mass and stiffness matrices are explicitly positive definite. It contains the same metric-dependent strain interaction and source perturbation $-VPh$. Its proper-time generator is $H_N/\hbar$. No independently chosen mode spectrum appears.

##### 7a. Direct material source coupled to the actual metric

First leave $h$ as the actual Einstein metric variable. Diagonalize only the material $q$ plus $N$ reservoir coordinates at $h=0$. Let $M_{m}$ and $K_{m}$ be their mass/stiffness matrices, obtained by deleting the $h$ row and column of (I.3c.7.21), but retaining $Kq^2/2$. Write $M_m^{-1/2}K_mM_m^{-1/2}=O_m\operatorname{diag}(\nu_j^2)O_m^T$ and $f_j=(e_q^TM_m^{-1/2}O_m)_j\sqrt{\hbar/(2\nu_j)}$. A finite material source is then

$$
\begin{aligned}
H_{M,N}(h) &= \sum_j\hbar\nu_j|1\rangle\langle 1|_j \\
&\quad +Kahq_N+(Ka^{2}/2)h^{2}I, \\
q_N &= \sum_jf_jX_j.
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.3c.7.21a}
$$

The local three-qubit cells attach the two declared controller/memory slots to each response qubit. The coupling in (I.3c.7.21a) is the proper-strain expansion of (I.3c.7.3), not a new gravitational coupling. The source's metric derivative is

$$
T_{m,\mathrm{TT}}=-(Ka/V)[q_N+ahI].
\tag{I.3c.7.21b}
$$

At $h=0$ the product ground has zero energy and zero mean variational stress. The stress operator itself has nonzero ground-to-excitation matrix elements, which generate the Kubo response. Its normalized Schrödinger generator uses the same proper time as (I.3c.7.13). Frequencies, coupling matrix elements and stress rows are all derived from $M_m,K_m$ and the original action.

The finite Hamiltonian is nonnegative for every real $h$. The free-end material stiffness satisfies $e_q^TK_m^{-1}e_q=1/K$, hence $\sum_j f_j^2/(\hbar\nu_j)=1/(2K)$. With $c_j=Kah\,f_{j}$, each two-level operator $\hbar\nu_j|1\rangle\langle 1|+c_jX_j+c_j^2/(\hbar\nu_j)\,I$ is positive semidefinite: its diagonal entries are nonnegative and its determinant is $c_j^4/(\hbar\nu_j)^2$. The sum of the added scalar terms is exactly $Ka^2h^2/2$. This proves the claim for (I.3c.7.21a) without subtracting a metric-dependent zero-point energy.

The ground-state commutator gives exactly the original material resolvent,

$$
\begin{aligned}
R_{qq,N}(s) &= \sum_j[2\nu_jf_j^{2}/\hbar]/(s^{2}+\nu_j^{2}) \\
&= e_q^{\mathsf T}(K_m+s^{2}M_m)^{-1}e_q \\
&= 1/(Ms^{2}+K+sZ_{\epsilon,N}(s)).
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.3c.7.21c}
$$

Consequently $\delta\langle q_N\rangle=-Ka\,R_{qq,N}h$. Substitution of its actual variational stress (I.3c.7.21b) into the Einstein equation gives

$$
\chi_N(s)=V/[A(s^{2}+\Omega^{2})+Ka^{2}-K^{2}a^{2}R_{qq,N}(s)],
\tag{I.3c.7.21d}
$$

which converges to (I.3c.7.14) by (I.3c.7.24)–(I.3c.7.26). Thus the physical output is the Einstein metric itself; it need not be identified with a separately simulated coordinate. The finite source preserves every declared linear material-coordinate and stress-conjugate row on this retained TT sector. This is a response-faithful realization, not a claim that all quadratic stress products or a full quantum vacuum stress tensor equal those of an untruncated oscillator field. The classical continuum action supplies the covariant background and mode closure; the finite models supply its controlled retained material response. The admitted MPU branch supplies qualifying/minimal-cycle status when that name is used; neither dimension eight nor Kubo equality proves a fresh Definition 23 global minimum.

##### 7b. Full coordinate-response check

The following full-system encoding is an additional response-equivalence check of (I.3c.7.21d), rather than the metric interpretation used in 7a.

Let $C_N=M_N^{-1/2}K_NM_N^{-1/2}=O\operatorname{diag}(\nu_j^2)O^T$. For any coordinate row $b$, define

$$
\begin{aligned}
