\tag{I.3c.7.22}
$$

Replace each normal oscillator by a two-level register $R_{j}$ with Hamiltonian $\hbar\nu_j|1\rangle\langle 1|$ and replace $b_j+b_j^\dagger$ by Pauli $X_j$. Attach two data qubits $A_j,B_j$ to each $R_j$; each cell is then exactly eight dimensional. The whole finite source has an explicit finite matrix Hamiltonian, the source operator $h_N=\sum f_{hj}X_j$, the material readout $q_N=\sum f_{qj}X_j$ and all strain readouts from the same coordinate map. Prepare all $R_j$ in $|0\rangle$. The $A_j,B_j$ registers are local controller/memory slots for this bulk encoding. Their two-bit channel has the same elementary type as the boundary channel, but their number and global normal-mode labels do not enter the boundary census. The spatial $B$ subsystem and its proper-area calibration remain those of section 1a at every bulk-reservoir refinement.

The retarded first-order response is exact, not an approximation caused by two-level truncation. Both the oscillator ground state and the register ground state have identical ground-to-one-excitation matrix elements of every coordinate in (I.3c.7.22), and only those matrix elements occur in their Kubo commutator. Consequently

$$
\chi_N(s)=V\,e_h^{\mathsf T}(K_N+s^{2}M_N)^{-1}e_h
\tag{I.3c.7.23}
$$

for both realizations. The finite second-order bulk response is therefore encoded in fixed-size three-qubit carriers with the correct stress-conjugate source, proper clock, energy gaps and retained metric response. Applying (I.3c.7.22) to every local-coordinate row and to every source row proves equality of the entire linear-response matrix, not merely one numerical transfer. Normal-mode encoding is a basis change in that source dictionary; it does not change the spatial support labels of the corresponding original field observables. The continuum retained causal response is that of the local field equations. No claim is made that an arbitrary uncompiled Pauli operation on a normal-mode register is a local operation at a spatial boundary cell. This equality concerns linear response; a finite-register nonlinear approximation is not asserted. At the final readout, binary record and prediction/error labels can be stored in $A_j,B_j$ by a finite instrument; its reset consumes separately recorded pure registers. It does not change the prior response map.

For completeness, the reservoir refinement is quantitative. Put $x=\epsilon s/v$ and

$$
\begin{aligned}
r &= \exp[-2\operatorname{asinh}(x/2)], \\
Z_\epsilon(s) &= Z[\sqrt{1+x^{2}/4}-x/2], \\
Z_{\epsilon,N}(s) &= Z_\epsilon(s)(1-r^{2N})/(1+r^{2N+1}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.3c.7.24}
$$

These follow by solving the chain recurrence and the free-end boundary condition, not by fitting its spectrum. On any compact right-half-plane set $\operatorname{Re}s\ge\sigma>0$, $|s|\le W$, choose $\epsilon W/v\le 1$ and $\epsilon^2W^3/v^2\le\sigma$. Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
|Z_\epsilon/Z-1| &\le \epsilon W/(2v)+(\epsilon W/v)^{2}/4, \\
|r| &\le \exp[-\epsilon\sigma/(2v)], \\
|Z_{\epsilon,N}-Z_\epsilon| \\
&\le |Z_\epsilon|\,2\exp[-N\epsilon\sigma/v] \\
&\qquad /(1-\exp[-(2N+1)\epsilon\sigma/(2v)]).
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.3c.7.25}
$$

The asinh remainder bound $|2\operatorname{asinh}(x/2)-x|\le|x|^3/(6\sqrt{3})$ proves the second inequality. Thus $\epsilon\to 0$ and $N\epsilon\to\infty$ give uniform convergence of the physical impedance on that declared domain.

Let $\Delta_{Z}$ be the right side bounding $|Z_{\epsilon,N}-Z|$. Passivity of both mechanical networks gives $|Ms^2+sZ_*+K|\ge M\sigma^2$ and $|D_{\mathrm{eff},*}|\ge A\sigma^2$ there. Resolvent subtraction then yields the conservative explicit bound

$$
\begin{aligned}
|\chi_N(s)-\chi_{hP}(s)| \\
&\le VK^{2}a^{2}W\Delta_Z/(M^{2}A^{2}\sigma^{8}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.3c.7.26}
$$

The finite-register response therefore converges to (I.3c.7.14) with an owned source, clock and source/metric map. Finite closed reservoirs have recurrences; no uniform real-axis convergence or finite-bath exponential decay is asserted. The continuum/outgoing limit precedes the boundary-frequency limit in the exact susceptibility.

#### 8. A fully evaluated source instance

First choose $\delta$ and positive integers $n_x,n_y,n_z$. Let $L_i=n_i\delta$ and $V=L_xL_yL_z$ be a fiducial mode-normalization cell/slab in the homogeneous noncompact background, and select $|k|=2\pi/L_z$. This normalization cell does not compactify the entire spacetime. Fix $G_{\mathrm{op}}$ by (I.3c.7.2) and $A=Vc^2/(16\pi G_{\mathrm{op}})$. Define the source units $L_*=\delta$, $m_*=A/L_*^2$ and $t_*=2/(\sqrt{5}c|k|)$. Set $M=m_*$, $K=30m_*/t_*^2$, $Z=10m_*/t_*$, $\Omega^2=c^2|k|^2=4/(5t_*^2)$, and $a^2=7L_*^2/50$. The source coefficients are $\rho=M/V$, $\kappa=K/V$ and $\ell=2a$. Any independently chosen $\rho_{X}>0$ and bath speed $0<v\le c$ complete the source through $\mu=Z/v$ and $T=Zv$ and the densities in (I.3c.7.9). Thus geometry and capacity fix the gravitational normalization before the rational material ratios are evaluated; no observed response is used.

With $z=st_*$, equations (I.3c.7.14)–(I.3c.7.15) become

$$
\chi(s)=(Vt_{*}^{2}/A)\,(z^{2}+10z+30)/[(z+1)(z+2)(z+3)(z+4)].
$$

The four physical poles are $-1/t_*,-2/t_*,-3/t_*,-4/t_*$. In the dimensionless transfer the residues are $7/2,-7,9/2,-1$, and the static value is $5/4$. The signed residues show directly that this passive inertial source is not in the positive-relaxation subclass; its exact time kernel nevertheless equals $(1/2)e^{-t}(1-e^{-t})(2e^{-2t}-7e^{-t}+7)$ in unit time and is nonnegative. Its imaginary part is $1260\,\omega/[(1+\omega^2)(4+\omega^2)(9+\omega^2)(16+\omega^2)]$, so passivity and the sum rule can also be checked without a numerical solver.

#### 9. Source inputs and derived outputs

Independent source inputs are $\delta,c,\hbar$; the fixed capacity geometry; $\rho_X,\rho,\kappa,\rho_b,\tau_b,\ell$; the selected nonzero wave vector; and the zero-input outgoing reservoir condition. All are stated before any response evaluation. The action determines $A,M,K,a,Z$; its generator determines $D$ and its poles; the tensor projection determines the Pa input; its metric output is dimensionless $h$; (I.3c.7.18) fixes absolute response units $\mathrm{Pa}^{-1}$. The finite-register construction derives every frequency and source matrix element from that same action. The H.0 coordinate, CPTP contraction maps and physical finite-time phase probe use the same spacing and proper time.

<a id="definition-i3e-rcd-buchert-cheeger-backreaction-datum"></a>**Definition I.3e (RCD-Buchert-Cheeger Backreaction Datum).** On a regular emergent metric/channel-capacity thermodynamic branch, let $D$ be a compact averaging domain in the noncollapsed $\mathrm{RCD}^*(K,4)$ limit of Theorem C.6c, with normalized measure $\langle f\rangle_D$. A backreaction datum consists of:

1. an expansion scalar $\theta\in W^{1,2}(D)$ and shear magnitude $\sigma\in L^2(D)$ for the retained cosmological congruence;

2. the positive Neumann spectral-gap constant
$$
\lambda_1(D)
:=
\inf_{\substack{f\in W^{1,2}(D)\\ \operatorname{Var}_D(f)>0}}
\frac{\mathrm{Ch}_D(f)}{\operatorname{Var}_D(f)} >0,
$$
so that $\operatorname{Var}_D(f)\le\lambda_1(D)^{-1}\mathrm{Ch}_D(f)$ by definition;

3. the Buchert-type kinematical backreaction
$$
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{PU}}
=
\frac23
\left(
\langle\theta^2\rangle_D-\langle\theta\rangle_D^2
\right)
-
2\langle\sigma^2\rangle_D;
\tag{I.3e.1}
$$

4. an elliptic source-control estimate supplied by the emergent metric/channel-capacity thermodynamic field equation on the retained branch:
$$
\frac{2}{3\lambda_1(D)}\mathrm{Ch}_D(\theta)
+
2\langle\sigma^2\rangle_D
\le
B_D[
\operatorname{Var}_D(T_{\mathrm{pred}}),
\dot\rho_{\mathrm{src}},
\mathfrak B_D,
\mathfrak H_D
],
\tag{I.3e.2}
$$
where $T_{\mathrm{pred}}$ is the retained predictive stress tensor, $\dot\rho_{\mathrm{src}}$ is the source-energy rate density when present, and $\mathfrak B_D,\mathfrak H_D$ are the finite Bakry-Émery and horizon-transfer defect budgets on the branch.

<a id="theorem-i3f-rcd-buchert-cheeger-backreaction-bound"></a>**Theorem I.3f (RCD-Buchert-Cheeger Backreaction Bound).** On any branch carrying the datum of Definition I.3e,
$$
|\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{PU}}|
\le
\frac{2}{3\lambda_1(D)}\mathrm{Ch}_D(\theta)
+
2\langle\sigma^2\rangle_D
\tag{I.3f.1}
$$
and therefore
$$
|\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{PU}}|
\le
B_D[
\operatorname{Var}_D(T_{\mathrm{pred}}),
\dot\rho_{\mathrm{src}},
\mathfrak B_D,
\mathfrak H_D
].
\tag{I.3f.2}
$$

*Proof.* By definition,
$$
|\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{PU}}|
\le
\frac23\operatorname{Var}_D(\theta)
+
2\langle\sigma^2\rangle_D.
$$
The RCD/Poincaré inequality with first nonzero Neumann spectral gap gives
$$
\operatorname{Var}_D(\theta)
\le
\lambda_1(D)^{-1}\mathrm{Ch}_D(\theta).
$$
Substituting gives (I.3f.1). The source-control estimate (I.3e.2), which is the elliptic regularity form of the emergent metric/channel-capacity thermodynamic field equation on the retained branch, gives (I.3f.2). ∎

<a id="corollary-i3g-backreaction-status-boundary"></a>**Corollary I.3g (Backreaction Status Boundary).** On a branch carrying Definition I.3e, cosmological backreaction is bounded by Cheeger energy, shear, predictive stress variance, source-energy rate density, and the retained finite-defect budgets. If that datum is not supplied for a cosmological domain, Theorem I.3f supplies no estimate for the domain, and Appendix I states no independent theorem-level backreaction estimate there.

*Proof.* The first sentence is Theorem I.3f. When Definition I.3e is unavailable, the theorem's hypothesis is not satisfied, so its conclusion cannot be invoked. The final clause records the absence of any separate backreaction theorem in this appendix; it is not a contrapositive inference. ∎

<a id="definition-i3h-rcd-elliptic-scale-bridge-datum"></a>**Definition I.3h (RCD Elliptic Scale-Bridge Datum).** Let $(X_n,d_n,m_n,\mathcal E_n)$ be the finite MPU metric-measure networks on a regular operational-continuum branch. The branch carries an RCD elliptic scale-bridge datum when:

1. the finite networks have a uniform Bakry-Émery lower bound $K$ in the sense of the discrete curvature form used in Theorem C.6c;

2. the channel-capacity volume bounds are noncollapsed:
$$
v_- r^4\le m_n(B_r(x))\le v_+r^4
\tag{I.3h.1}
$$
for fixed $v_-,v_+>0$ on retained local scales;

3. the finite networks have uniform local doubling and $(1,2)$-Poincaré constants;

4. $(X_n,d_n,m_n)$ converge in the measured Gromov-Hausdorff sense to $(X,d,m)$;

5. the Dirichlet forms $\mathcal E_n$ converge to the limit Cheeger energy in the Mosco sense;

6. on each retained cosmological averaging domain $D$ with spectral gap $\lambda_1(D)>0$, the emergent metric/channel-capacity field equation admits an elliptic gauge and a source-control certificate of dimension $L^{-2}$
$$
\frac{1}{\lambda_1(D)}\mathrm{Ch}_D(\theta)
+
\langle\sigma^2\rangle_D
\le
\mathcal B_D^{\mathrm{ell}}
\left[
\operatorname{Var}_D(T_{\mathrm{pred}}),
\dot\rho_{\mathrm{src}},
\mathfrak B_D,
\mathfrak H_D
\right],
\tag{I.3h.2}
$$
where $\mathcal B_D^{\mathrm{ell}}$ is a finite bound of dimension $L^{-2}$ in the declared physical-length normalization.

<a id="theorem-i3i-rcd-elliptic-scale-bridge-completion"></a>**Theorem I.3i (RCD Elliptic Scale-Bridge Completion).** Let a branch carry the datum of Definition I.3h and, for every retained averaging domain $D$ used below, items 1--3 of Definition I.3e. Assume, in addition, a discrete-to-continuum stability certificate proving that its measured Gromov-Hausdorff limit satisfies $\mathrm{RCD}^*(K,4)$ and that the Mosco limit of $\mathcal E_n$ is the Cheeger energy of $(X,d,m)$. Then the limit Cheeger energy is quadratic and
$$
|\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{PU}}|
\le
2\mathcal B_D^{\mathrm{ell}}
\left[
\operatorname{Var}_D(T_{\mathrm{pred}}),
\dot\rho_{\mathrm{src}},
\mathfrak B_D,
\mathfrak H_D
\right].
\tag{I.3i.1}
$$

*Proof.* The stability certificate identifies $(X,d,m)$ as an $\mathrm{RCD}^*(K,4)$ space and identifies the Mosco limit with its Cheeger energy. Infinitesimal Hilbertianity in the definition of an $\mathrm{RCD}$ space makes that Cheeger energy quadratic. Theorem I.3f gives
$$
|\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{PU}}|
\le
\frac{2}{3\lambda_1(D)}\mathrm{Ch}_D(\theta)
+
2\langle\sigma^2\rangle_D.
$$
Since both terms are nonnegative and $2/3\le2$,
$$
|\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{PU}}|
\le
2\left(
\frac{1}{\lambda_1(D)}\mathrm{Ch}_D(\theta)
+
\langle\sigma^2\rangle_D
\right).
$$
Applying the source-control certificate (I.3h.2) proves (I.3i.1). ∎

<a id="corollary-i3j-scale-bridge-scope"></a>**Corollary I.3j (Scale-Bridge Scope).** The predictive-stress backreaction estimate (I.3i.1) is established only on branches satisfying Definition I.3h, items 1--3 of Definition I.3e for every retained averaging domain, and the discrete-to-continuum stability certificate of Theorem I.3i. If that package is unavailable, the local estimate (I.3f.1) remains available only on domains carrying items 1--3 of Definition I.3e, including the stated positive spectral gap. No estimate in terms of predictive stress and defect budgets follows without the elliptic source-control estimate.

*Proof.* Theorem I.3i requires its entire branch package to derive (I.3i.1). Independently, the proof of Theorem I.3f derives (I.3f.1) from the definition of $\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{PU}}$ and the spectral-gap inequality; it derives (I.3f.2) only after applying (I.3e.2). Therefore the local bound has exactly the scope stated here, and the predictive-stress bound additionally requires elliptic source control. ∎

<a id="theorem-i3j1-exact-finite-graph-elliptic-source-and-covariance"></a>**Theorem I.3j.1 (Exact Finite Graph Elliptic Source and Covariance).** Let $L$ be the symmetric Laplacian of a finite connected graph with at least two vertices and positive weights on its retained edges, let $\mathbf1^\perp$ be the mean-zero subspace, and let $s\in\mathbf1^\perp$. The mean-zero equation
$$
L\phi=s,
\qquad \phi\perp\mathbf1,
\tag{I.3j.1.1}
$$
has the unique solution $\phi=L^+s$, with exact energy and spectral-gap bounds
$$
\phi^{\mathsf T}L\phi=s^{\mathsf T}L^+s,
\qquad
\|\phi\|_2\le\frac{\|s\|_2}{\lambda_2(L)}.
\tag{I.3j.1.2}
$$
If $s$ is a random source taking values in $\mathbf1^\perp$ with finite second moment and covariance $\Sigma_s$, then
$$
\operatorname{Cov}(\phi)=L^+\Sigma_sL^+,
\qquad
\operatorname{tr}\operatorname{Cov}(\phi)
\le
\frac{\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_s}{\lambda_2(L)^2}.
\tag{I.3j.1.3}
$$
These identities give the elliptic source-control and fluctuation record for the supplied finite graph. Rational $L$, $s$ and $\Sigma_s$ admit exact linear algebra and an exact algebraic representation of the positive eigenvalue $\lambda_2(L)$; another numerical representation requires its own terminating arithmetic and comparison procedures. Passing these quantities uniformly to an RCD limit still requires the convergence and source-identification entries of Definition I.3h.

*Proof.* Connectedness gives $\ker L=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}$ and makes $L$ positive definite on $\mathbf1^\perp$. Spectral inversion there gives $L^+$, uniqueness, the energy identity, and $\|L^+\|_{\mathbf1^\perp}=1/\lambda_2(L)$. Linearity gives the covariance identity. Diagonalizing $L$ on $\mathbf1^\perp$ and using $0\preceq(L^+)^2\preceq\lambda_2(L)^{-2}I$ proves the trace bound. ∎

<a id="lemma-i3j2-positive-covariance-blocks-and-trace-tails"></a>**Lemma I.3j.2 (Positive Covariance Blocks and Trace Tails).** Let $F_j$ increase strongly to the identity through finite-rank orthogonal projections on a separable Hilbert space $H$, and let $C_n$ be positive trace-class operators. The sequence $C_n$ converges in trace norm if and only if every compression $F_jC_nF_j$ converges and
$$
\lim_{j\to\infty}\limsup_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{tr}((I-F_j)C_n)=0.
\tag{I.3j.2.1}
$$
The limiting compressions determine the positive trace-class limit uniquely. For every positive trace-class $B$ and orthogonal projection $F$, setting $t=\operatorname{tr}((I-F)B)$ and $b=\operatorname{tr}B$ gives
$$
\|B-FBF\|_1\le t+2\sqrt{bt}.
\tag{I.3j.2.2}
$$

*Proof.* Factor $FB(I-F)=(FB^{1/2})(B^{1/2}(I-F))$. The trace norm of this product is at most the product of its Hilbert–Schmidt norms, hence at most $\sqrt{\operatorname{tr}(FB)t}\le\sqrt{bt}$. The other cross block is its adjoint; the remaining positive block has trace norm $t$. This proves (I.3j.2.2).

If $C_n\to C$ in trace norm, compression is contractive and
$$
\left|\operatorname{tr}((I-F_j)(C_n-C))\right|\le\|C_n-C\|_1.
$$
Since $\operatorname{tr}((I-F_j)C)\to0$, the two conditions follow. Conversely, one fixed cutoff with eventual tail below one, together with convergence of its compressed trace, bounds all sufficiently late $\operatorname{tr}C_n$ by a common $M$. For such $n,l$, writing $t_{n,j}=\operatorname{tr}((I-F_j)C_n)$, (I.3j.2.2) gives
$$
\|C_n-C_l\|_1\le\|F_j(C_n-C_l)F_j\|_1+t_{n,j}+t_{l,j}
+2\sqrt{Mt_{n,j}}+2\sqrt{Mt_{l,j}}.
$$
Choose $j$ to make the limiting tails small and then $n,l$ to control both tails and the finite block. This proves that $C_n$ is Cauchy in trace norm. Its limit is positive. Equality of all finite compressions fixes every matrix element on a dense subspace, hence fixes the limit uniquely. ∎

<a id="theorem-i3j3-compact-mosco-elliptic-covariance-passage"></a>**Theorem I.3j.3 (Compact-Mosco Elliptic Covariance Passage).** Let finite-dimensional mean-zero graph spaces $H_n$ be isometrically embedded in a separable Hilbert space $H$, with projections $P_n\to I$ strongly. Let $A_n$ and $A$ be positive self-adjoint operators on $H_n$ and $H$, respectively. Assume a common gap $A_n\ge gI$, $A\ge gI$, $g>0$, and Mosco convergence of the forms $\frac12\|A_n^{1/2}u\|^2$, extended by $+\infty$ outside their domains, to $\frac12\|A^{1/2}u\|^2$. Assume also that $A$ has compact resolvent and
$$
B_n:=(I+A_n)^{-1}P_n\longrightarrow B:=(I+A)^{-1}
\quad\text{in operator norm}.
\tag{I.3j.3.1}
$$
Mosco convergence together with collective compactness of these embedded resolvents supplies (I.3j.3.1).

For $R>g$ outside $\operatorname{spec}(A)$, put $E_R=\mathbf1_{[g,R]}(A)$ and $E_{n,R}=\mathbf1_{[g,R]}(A_n)P_n$. Eventually their finite ranks agree, and
$$
V_{n,R}=E_{n,R}E_R(E_RE_{n,R}E_R)^{-1/2}:E_RH\longrightarrow E_{n,R}H
$$
is an onto isometry satisfying $V_{n,R}\to E_R$ in norm. Let $Q_n$ be any positive covariance on $H_n$ and $p\in\{1,2\}$. Then
$$
C_{n,p}:=A_n^{-p/2}Q_nA_n^{-p/2}
$$
converges in trace norm after embedding if and only if both of the following hold:

1. $V_{n,R}^*Q_nV_{n,R}$ converges as a finite matrix for every such $R$;
2. the weighted source tails satisfy
$$
\lim_{R\to\infty}\limsup_{n\to\infty}
\sum_{\lambda_{n,j}>R}\lambda_{n,j}^{-p}
\langle e_{n,j},Q_ne_{n,j}\rangle=0,
\tag{I.3j.3.2}
$$
where $(\lambda_{n,j},e_{n,j})$ is any orthonormal eigensystem of $A_n$ and $R$ avoids the limit spectrum.

No commutation between $Q_n$ and $A_n$ is assumed. The case $p=2$ is the covariance of the elliptic solution $A_n^{-1}s_n$; $p=1$ is its energy-coordinate covariance.

*Proof.* Multiplication of the forms by two preserves Mosco convergence. The form-resolvent equivalence of Kuwae–Shioya (2003), Theorem 2.4, then gives strong convergence $B_n\to B$. To verify the stated sufficient condition for norm convergence, suppose bounded $x_n$ violated $\|(B_n-B)x_n\|\to0$. Pass to $x_n\rightharpoonup x$ and, by collective compactness, to $B_nx_n\to y$. Self-adjointness gives
$$
\langle y,z\rangle=\lim_n\langle x_n,B_nz\rangle=\langle x,Bz\rangle=\langle Bx,z\rangle.
$$
Compactness of $B$ also gives $Bx_n\to Bx$, a contradiction.

The finite spectral cluster of $B$ above $(1+R)^{-1}$ is separated from the remaining spectrum. Norm convergence preserves a smaller open gap: the resolvent Neumann series applies wherever the distance to the spectrum of $B$ exceeds $\|B_n-B\|$. A continuous function equal to the cluster indicator on the two separated spectral sets therefore gives $E_{n,R}\to E_R$ by continuous functional calculus. Projections at norm distance less than one inject into each other's ranges, so their finite ranks agree. The formula for $V_{n,R}$ is the polar isometry of $E_{n,R}E_R$; its positive factor tends to the identity on $E_RH$, proving the asserted convergence and surjectivity.

Write $A_{n,R}=V_{n,R}^*A_nV_{n,R}$. The compressed resolvents converge, so
$$
A_{n,R}=(V_{n,R}^*B_nV_{n,R})^{-1}-I\longrightarrow A|_{E_RH}.
$$
All powers used below consequently converge on this fixed finite space, and
$$
V_{n,R}^*C_{n,p}V_{n,R}
=A_{n,R}^{-p/2}(V_{n,R}^*Q_nV_{n,R})A_{n,R}^{-p/2}.
$$
Convergence of either compressed covariance is equivalent to convergence of the other, multiplying by the convergent positive powers for the reverse implication. The sum in (I.3j.3.2) equals $\operatorname{tr}((I-E_{n,R})C_{n,p})$, since the spectral projection commutes with the inverse power. Positivity supplies this diagonal trace identity without requiring $Q_n$ to commute.

For sufficiency, one low block and its tail bound the total traces eventually. Inequality (I.3j.2.2), now with $E_{n,R}$, and convergence of the embedded finite blocks make $C_{n,p}$ Cauchy in trace norm. For necessity, trace convergence bounds the total traces. Multiplication by $E_{n,R}\to E_R$ in norm then gives convergence of the moving blocks and their traces. Each fixed-cutoff tail tends to $\operatorname{tr}((I-E_R)C_p)$, which vanishes as $R\to\infty$. ∎

On the same gap/Mosco branch, trace-norm convergence of the embedded sources $Q_n\to Q$ already implies $C_{n,p}\to A^{-p/2}QA^{-p/2}$ without (I.3j.3.1). Inverse powers converge strongly and have the common bound $g^{-p/2}$; approximation of $Q$ by finite-rank operators proves the assertion. Compact spectral identification permits the weaker source-block and weighted-tail criterion.

<a id="theorem-i3j4-four-dimensional-source-covariance-and-energy-classification"></a>**Theorem I.3j.4 (Four-Dimensional Source Covariance and Energy Classification).** Fix the sequence of Theorem C.6c.4, writing $\eta\in(0,1)$ for its fixed stencil parameter, and put $A_n=-L_n$, $A=-\Delta$. Use its normalized graph Hilbert spaces and Fourier isometries into $H=L^2_0(\mathbb T^4)$. Write
$$
K_n=\{-(n-1)/2,\ldots,(n-1)/2\}^4,\quad e_k(x)=e^{2\pi i k\cdot x},\quad
\lambda(k)=4\pi^2|k|^2.
$$
Constants are excluded. For every graph source $s_n\in H_n$ with finite second moment, let $\bar s_n=\mathbb E s_n$, $Q_n=\operatorname{Cov}(s_n)$, and $q_n(k,l)=\langle e_k,Q_ne_l\rangle$ in the embedded Fourier representation, setting entries outside $K_n$ to zero. These are Hilbert-space covariances. In vertex coordinates $\langle u,v\rangle_{\mu_n}=n^{-4}\sum_x\overline{u_x}v_x$, so an ordinary coordinate covariance matrix $\Sigma_n$ represents the Hilbert covariance as $Q_n=n^{-4}\Sigma_n$ and $\operatorname{tr}Q_n=n^{-4}\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_n$.

For $p\in\{1,2\}$, the operators $C_{n,p}=A_n^{-p/2}Q_nA_n^{-p/2}$ converge in trace norm exactly when
$$
q_n(k,l)\to q(k,l)\quad\text{for every fixed }k,l\ne0,
\qquad
\lim_{R\to\infty}\limsup_n
\sum_{\substack{k\in K_n\\|k|>R}}\frac{q_n(k,k)}{\lambda_n(k)^p}=0.
\tag{I.3j.4.1}
$$
The resulting covariance is uniquely given by
$$
\langle e_k,C_pe_l\rangle
=\frac{q(k,l)}{\lambda(k)^{p/2}\lambda(l)^{p/2}}.
\tag{I.3j.4.2}
$$
The matrix $q$ can define a generalized source through its quadratic form on finite Fourier sums. Equations (I.3j.4.1)–(I.3j.4.2) construct its trace-class response covariance.

The $p=1$ condition is equivalent to joint solution-and-energy covariance convergence, and gives $C_2=A^{-1/2}C_1A^{-1/2}$. The means $A_n^{-p/2}\bar s_n$ converge strongly exactly when every fixed coefficient $\bar s_n(k)$ converges and
$$
\lim_{R\to\infty}\limsup_n
\sum_{\substack{k\in K_n\\|k|>R}}\frac{|\bar s_n(k)|^2}{\lambda_n(k)^p}=0.
\tag{I.3j.4.3}
$$
For $\phi_n=A_n^{-1}s_n$, the exact normalizations are
$$
\mathbb E\|\phi_n\|^2=\|A_n^{-1}\bar s_n\|^2+\operatorname{tr}C_{n,2},\qquad
\mathbb E\mathcal E_n(\phi_n)=\frac12\left(\|A_n^{-1/2}\bar s_n\|^2+\operatorname{tr}C_{n,1}\right).
\tag{I.3j.4.4}
$$
Thus the generator gap is twice the Cheeger-gap convention of Definition I.3e; on the unit flat torus they are $4\pi^2$ and $2\pi^2$, respectively.

For any $\alpha\in\mathbb R$ and $C>0$, consider the entire covariance class
$$
0\le q_n(k,k)\le C\lambda_n(k)^{-\alpha}.
\tag{I.3j.4.5}
$$
It permits arbitrary positive off-diagonal correlations and includes $0\preceq Q_n\preceq CA_n^{-\alpha}$. Every sequence in this class with convergent fixed source blocks has trace-norm response passage at exponent $p$ if and only if $\alpha+p>2$. In that range its tails are uniformly $O(R^{4-2(\alpha+p)})$. The admissible choice $Q_n=CA_n^{-\alpha}$ has response trace $\Theta(\log n)$ at $\alpha+p=2$ and $\Theta(n^{4-2(\alpha+p)})$ below that threshold. Hence the universal solution threshold is $\alpha>0$ and the universal energy threshold is $\alpha>1$.

*Proof.* Equation (C.6c.4.7) gives
$$
c_\eta|k|^2\le\lambda_n(k)\le4\pi^2|k|^2,\qquad
\lambda_n(k)\to\lambda(k),\qquad c_\eta=16(1-\eta)>0.
$$
The Fourier matrix of $C_{n,p}$ is $q_n(k,l)/(\lambda_n(k)\lambda_n(l))^{p/2}$. Every fixed denominator has a positive limit, so finite-block convergence is equivalent to convergence of the full source block. The tail trace is exactly the sum in (I.3j.4.1). Lemma I.3j.2 proves the equivalence and (I.3j.4.2). The $p=2$ tail is at most $c_\eta^{-1}$ times the $p=1$ tail; this proves the joint assertion, and its operator identity follows from the limiting matrices. For the mean vectors, each finite projected difference tends to zero, while the squared complementary norm is exactly the sum in (I.3j.4.3). The triangle inequality bounds a full difference by that finite projected difference plus the two complementary norms. This proves sufficiency; strong convergence and exhaustion of the limiting vector prove necessity. Centering the source and expanding the two quadratic forms proves (I.3j.4.4).

Put $b=\alpha+p$. The spectral bounds compare $\lambda_n(k)^{-b}$ to $|k|^{-2b}$ with constants depending on $b$ and $\eta$, including negative $b$. The integer shell $\|k\|_\infty=r$ contains exactly
$$
(2r+1)^4-(2r-1)^4=64r^3+16r
$$
points and has $r\le|k|\le2r$. Its contribution is therefore comparable to $r^{3-2b}$. For $b>2$, summing the shells beyond $R/2$ gives the asserted uniform tail and covariance passage. For $b=2$, summing through $(n-1)/2$ gives $\Theta(\log n)$; for $b<2$ it gives $\Theta(n^{4-2b})$. These are the response traces of $Q_n=CA_n^{-\alpha}$, whose fixed source blocks converge. A centered Gaussian vector realizes each of these finite covariances and has finite second moment at every $n$. Thus every excluded exponent has an explicit counterexample within the class. ∎

A uniform bound $\operatorname{tr}Q_n\le M$ is another sufficient source condition: the weighted tail is at most $M(c_\eta R^2)^{-p}$. Convergence of fixed blocks then gives both response limits.

The hypotheses have independent counterexamples. For an escaping real Fourier unit mode $f_n$ with eigenvalue $\Lambda_n\to\infty$, the covariance $Q_n=\Lambda_nf_n\otimes f_n$ gives $\|C_{n,2}\|_1=\Lambda_n^{-1}\to0$ and $C_{n,1}=f_n\otimes f_n$ with trace one. The choice $Q_n=\Lambda_n^2f_n\otimes f_n$ instead leaves an escaping solution covariance with trace one. Thus bounded traces and solution convergence each leave the energy tail undecided. On two fixed modes, alternating the positive matrices $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ and $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&-1\\-1&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ preserves their diagonals and all high tails while the low off-diagonal response oscillates. Deterministic sources $s_n=\Lambda_nf_n$ have zero covariance and solutions $f_n$, establishing the separate mean requirement.

For the distinction between ordinary Mosco convergence and compact identification, take $H_n=\operatorname{span}(e_1,\ldots,e_n)\subset\ell^2$, $A=\operatorname{diag}(1,2,\ldots)$, and $A_n=\operatorname{diag}(1,2,\ldots,n-1,1)$. Finite-coordinate lower bounds and the recoveries $P_{n-1}u$ prove Mosco convergence. The gaps are one, but $Q_n=e_n\otimes e_n$ has zero eigenvalue tails above every $R>1$ and an escaping covariance of trace one. Its extra low mode prevents (I.3j.3.1). Replacing the last eigenvalue by $1/n$ preserves Mosco convergence and the positive limit gap; with $Q_n=n^{-2}e_n\otimes e_n\to0$, the solution covariance remains $e_n\otimes e_n$. This isolates the common-gap requirement.

Replacing $Q_n$ by $Q_n+\bar s_n\otimes\bar s_n$ gives the same exact criterion for the total response second-moment operator. A single scalar trace can converge while mass escapes, and equal first and second moments can belong to distinct laws, as with a Rademacher and a Gaussian coefficient on one fixed mode. The criterion controls the stated second-order objects.

<a id="proposition-i3j5-noncollapsed-four-dimensional-rough-source-obstruction"></a>**Proposition I.3j.5 (Noncollapsed Four-Dimensional Rough-Source Obstruction).** Let $X$ be a compact connected noncollapsed $\mathrm{RCD}^*(K,4)$ space with positive finite $\mathcal H^4(X)$, and let $A$ be its positive mean-zero Laplacian with eigenvalues $\lambda_j$. Then
$$
\sum_j\lambda_j^{-b}<\infty\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad b>2.
\tag{I.3j.5.1}
$$
White source covariance therefore has infinite solution variance $\operatorname{tr}A^{-2}$ and infinite expected Cheeger energy $\frac12\operatorname{tr}A^{-1}$. For source spectrum $A^{-\alpha}$, the corresponding thresholds are $\alpha>0$ and $\alpha>1$. The corresponding Gaussian elliptic-solution eigenmode series belong almost surely to $L^2$, respectively $W^{1,2}$, exactly in these ranges.

*Proof.* Noncollapse gives four-dimensional Euclidean tangents almost everywhere by De Philippis–Gigli (2018), Theorem 1.12. The $k=N$ case of Ambrosio–Honda–Tewodrose (2018), Corollary 4.4, gives
$$
N(\Lambda)\sim c_X\Lambda^2,\qquad c_X=\frac{\omega_4\mathcal H^4(X)}{(2\pi)^4}>0.
$$
Consequently $\lambda_j$ is comparable to $j^{1/2}$, and the series test proves (I.3j.5.1). Partial integration gives $\sum_{\lambda_j\le\Lambda}\lambda_j^{-2}\sim2c_X\log\Lambda$, identifying the logarithmic endpoint. Constant normalization of the reference measure leaves the generator unchanged.

For the Gaussian assertion, the squared norm is $\sum_j a_jZ_j^2$, where $Z_j$ are independent real standard Gaussians and $a_j=\lambda_j^{-(\alpha+2)}$ or $\lambda_j^{-(\alpha+1)}$. A finite sum of the $a_j$ gives finite expectation and almost-sure finiteness. If their sum diverges, independence gives
$$
\mathbb E e^{-\sum_{j\le J}a_jZ_j^2}=\prod_{j\le J}(1+2a_j)^{-1/2}\longrightarrow0.
$$
Either infinitely many weights exceed a fixed positive constant, or the weights tend to zero and $\log(1+2a_j)$ is eventually comparable to $a_j$. Dominated convergence now implies that the infinite squared norm is almost surely infinite. ∎

The four-dimensional bi-Laplacian critical field is the established log-correlated case described by Lodhia–Sheffield–Sun–Watson (2016). Proposition I.3j.5 applies that spectral obstruction to the retained elliptic covariance. An arbitrary Neumann averaging subdomain requires its own compact-resolvent and spectral-counting record.

<a id="corollary-i3j6-elliptic-quadratic-readout-passage"></a>**Corollary I.3j.6 (Elliptic Quadratic-Readout Passage).** If $C_n\to C$ in trace norm and bounded readouts $T_n:H\to Y$ converge strongly to $T$ with a common norm bound, then $T_nC_nT_n^*\to TCT^*$ in trace norm. If uniformly bounded self-adjoint $O_n\to O$ strongly, then $\operatorname{tr}(O_nC_n)\to\operatorname{tr}(OC)$.

*Proof.* The contribution of $C_n-C$ is bounded by $\sup_n\|T_n\|^2\|C_n-C\|_1$. Approximate $C$ in trace norm by a finite-rank operator; strong convergence is uniform on its finite-dimensional range, and the uniform readout bound controls the remainder. The same argument, with $|\operatorname{tr}(O_n(C_n-C))|\le\sup_n\|O_n\|\|C_n-C\|_1$, proves the scalar assertion. ∎

The $p=2$ criterion transports supplied bounded solution readouts; $p=1$ transports readouts of the form $TA^{1/2}\phi$ with bounded $T$. On the flat torus the gradient has this form: its Fourier multiplier after $A^{-1/2}$ is $ik/|k|$, an isometry into the vector-field space. The expected centered Cheeger energy is $\frac12\operatorname{tr}C_1$, with the mean contribution in (I.3j.4.4). Definition I.3e's expansion and shear, the predictive-stress forcing, the physically normalized source-control inequality (I.3h.2), defect budgets and observation maps remain their named realization entries. Once those readouts and their uniform bounds are supplied, the covariance and quadratic-observable passage follows from these results.

<a id="theorem-i3j7-source-controlled-nonlinear-readouts-and-moving-domains"></a>**Theorem I.3j.7 (Source-Controlled Nonlinear Readouts and Moving Domains).** Use exactly the graph sequence, Fourier identification and normalized measure of Theorem I.3j.4. All fields in this theorem are real mathematical readouts on its unit flat four-torus. The symmetric Fourier set $K_n$ preserves conjugate coefficients, so interpolation and projection preserve real fields. Let deterministic real mean-zero sources $s_n$ obey $\sup_n\|s_n\|_2\le M<\infty$, and suppose every fixed Fourier coefficient converges to $s(k)$. Put $\phi_n=A_n^{-1}s_n$ and $\phi=(-\Delta)^{-1}s$, with Fourier interpolation understood. Then $s\in L^2_0$, the interpolated $\phi_n$ are uniformly bounded in $H^2$, and $\phi_n\to\phi$ strongly in $H^1$. If in addition $s_n\to s$ strongly in the common $L^2$ space, then $\phi_n\to\phi$ strongly in $H^2$.

There are two nonlinear passage statements on this same sequence.

1. Fix $0<q<2$. Let $F_\theta,F_\sigma:\mathbb T^4\times\mathbb R^4\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, with $F_\sigma\ge0$ and
$$
|F_\theta(x,z)|+|F_\sigma(x,z)|\le C(1+|z|^q).
\tag{I.3j.7.1}
$$
Define $\theta_n=F_\theta(x,\nabla\phi_n)$, $\sigma_n=F_\sigma(x,\nabla\phi_n)$ and define $\theta,\sigma$ by the same maps at $\phi$. Then both fields converge strongly in $L^2$.

2. On the stronger source branch $s_n\to s$ in $L^2$, the same conclusion holds for continuous readouts of $D^2\phi_n$ with at most linear growth, allowing all Hessian components and their trace-free combinations simultaneously. In particular, supplied linear expansion and shear-tensor maps of the Hessian and the norm of that shear tensor pass to the same limit.

For either branch let $D_n,D\subset\mathbb T^4$ be measurable, $|D|>0$, and $\mathbf1_{D_n}\to\mathbf1_D$ in measure. Then $|D_n|\to|D|$, and for all sufficiently large $n$ the normalized Buchert expression
$$
Q_n=\frac23\left(\fint_{D_n}\theta_n^2-
\left(\fint_{D_n}\theta_n\right)^2\right)-2\fint_{D_n}\sigma_n^2
\tag{I.3j.7.2}
$$
converges to the expression $Q$ with $(D,\theta,\sigma)$. This includes products of any two strongly $L^2$ readouts from the same source.

The passage has an explicit error decomposition. For $f_n,f\in L^1$, $v_n=|D_n|>0$, $v=|D|$, set
$$
\epsilon_n(f_n,f)=\frac{\|f_n-f\|_1+
\int|\mathbf1_{D_n}-\mathbf1_D|\,|f|
+|v_n-v|\,|\fint_Df|}{v_n}.
\tag{I.3j.7.3}
$$
Writing $m_n=\fint_{D_n}\theta_n$, $m=\fint_D\theta$, one has
$$
|Q_n-Q|\le\frac23\left[\epsilon_n(\theta_n^2,\theta^2)
+(|m_n|+|m|)\epsilon_n(\theta_n,\theta)\right]
+2\epsilon_n(\sigma_n^2,\sigma^2).
\tag{I.3j.7.4}
$$
Here $\|u_n^2-u^2\|_1\le(\|u_n\|_2+\|u\|_2)\|u_n-u\|_2$. No boundary smoothness is needed for this averaging result. To invoke Definition I.3e's energy bound as well, the expansion must also carry its stated $W^{1,2}$ regularity and the physical source-control estimate.

*Proof.* Fatou's inequality on finite Fourier sums gives $\sum_{k\ne0}|s(k)|^2\le M^2$. The lower eigenvalue bound $\lambda_n(k)\ge c_\eta|k|^2$, with $c_\eta=16(1-\eta)>0$, implies
$$
\sum_{k\ne0}(1+4\pi^2|k|^2)^2|\phi_n(k)|^2
\le\frac{(1+4\pi^2)^2}{c_\eta^2}M^2.
$$
For the $H^1$ tail outside $|k|\le R$, $R\ge1$, the same estimate gives an upper bound $C_\eta M^2/R^2$, with $C_\eta=(1+4\pi^2)/c_\eta^2$. Every finite block converges by $\lambda_n(k)\to4\pi^2|k|^2$. Finite-block convergence and the displayed tails prove strong $H^1$ convergence. If $s_n\to s$ strongly, the multipliers
$(1+4\pi^2|k|^2)/\lambda_n(k)$ are uniformly bounded and converge on each fixed mode. Finite-mode approximation of $s$ and the uniform multiplier bound prove strong $H^2$ convergence.

We give the compactness estimate needed for the nonlinear products. For a Fourier block $u_j$ on $2^j\le|k|<2^{j+1}$ in four dimensions, counting modes and Cauchy--Schwarz give $\|u_j\|_\infty\le C2^{2j}\|u_j\|_2$. The inequality $\|u\|_p^p\le\|u\|_\infty^{p-2}\|u\|_2^2$ therefore gives
$$
\|u_j\|_p\le C_p2^{j(2-4/p)}\|u_j\|_2\qquad(2\le p<\infty).
$$
For a uniformly $H^1$-bounded family $u$, summing over $j\ge J$ and applying Cauchy--Schwarz bounds the $L^p$ tail by
$C_p2^{-J(4/p-1)}\|u\|_{H^1}$ whenever $2\le p<4$. Apply this to each component of $u=\nabla\phi_n$. The fixed blocks converge, so $\nabla\phi_n\to\nabla\phi$ strongly in every $L^p$, $2\le p<4$.

Choose $p$ with $\max\{2,2q\}<p<4$. The continuous readouts converge in measure: truncate gradients to a fixed ball, use uniform continuity on the compact product with that ball and strong $L^p$ convergence, then let the ball grow. Their squared magnitudes satisfy, on every measurable set $E$,
$$
\int_E|F(x,\nabla\phi_n)|^2
\le 2C^2\left[|E|+\|\nabla\phi_n\|_p^{2q}|E|^{1-2q/p}\right].
$$
Thus their squares are uniformly integrable. Convergence in measure and this bound imply strong $L^2$ convergence: outside a set where the difference exceeds a prescribed small number, its squared integral is small by that number; the exceptional set has vanishing measure and its integral is small by uniform integrability. This proves item 1. In item 2, strong $L^2$ convergence of the full Hessian makes its squared norm uniformly integrable. Linear growth gives the same property for the readout squares; the identical convergence-in-measure argument applies. The norm of a shear tensor is continuous and bounded by a constant times the Hessian norm whenever its supplied tensor map is bounded linear.

Products pass in $L^1$ by

$$
\|u_nv_n-uv\|_1\le\|u_n-u\|_2\|v_n\|_2+\|u\|_2\|v_n-v\|_2.
$$

Indicator convergence in measure implies convergence in $L^1$ because the indicators are bounded and the torus has finite measure. For every fixed $f\in L^1$, truncating $|f|$ at a large constant shows $\int|\mathbf1_{D_n}-\mathbf1_D||f|\to0$. Subtracting the two normalized integrals gives an absolute difference bounded by (I.3j.7.3). Apply it to the first and second moments of $\theta$ and the second moment of $\sigma$, and factor $m_n^2-m^2=(m_n-m)(m_n+m)$ to obtain (I.3j.7.4) and the claimed convergence. ∎

<a id="theorem-i3j8-critical-concentration-and-domain-selection-obstructions"></a>**Theorem I.3j.8 (Critical Concentration and Domain-Selection Obstructions).** The growth threshold $q<2$ in Theorem I.3j.7, item 1, is sharp for its entire bounded-$L^2$ source class, even with smooth fields on the fixed noncollapsed limit and even along the same graph refinement. There are deterministic mean-zero sources $s_n$ with bounded $L^2$ norm and convergent fixed coefficients for which $\phi_n\to0$ strongly in $H^1$, while the smooth expansion readout $\theta_n=|\nabla\phi_n|^2$, $\sigma_n=0$, on $D_n=D=\mathbb T^4$ obeys
$$
Q_n\longrightarrow\frac23\int_{\mathbb R^4}|\nabla\psi|^4>0,
\qquad Q[0,0]=0,
\tag{I.3j.8.1}
$$
for an explicitly chosen nonconstant $\psi\in C_c^\infty(B_{1/8}(0))$. For every $q>2$, the continuous readout $\theta_n=|\nabla\phi_n|^q$, $\sigma_n=0$, instead gives $Q_n\to+\infty$ along such a sequence. Thus convergence of the elliptic solution and its gradient does not remove the critical concentration defect. These deterministic sources have zero covariance at every stage; their means and higher readout integrability carry the obstruction.

The moving-domain hypothesis is independent. With the fixed smooth expansion $\theta(x)=\sin(2\pi x_1)$, $\sigma=0$, alternating $D_n=\mathbb T^4$ and $D_n=\{0<x_1<1/2\}$ gives respectively
$$
Q_n=\frac13,\qquad Q_n=\frac13-\frac{8}{3\pi^2}.
\tag{I.3j.8.2}
$$
Every domain has volume at least $1/2$, but the backreaction values have no common limit.

*Proof.* For example choose $\psi(x)=\exp[-1/(1-256|x|^2)]$ for $|x|<1/16$ and zero otherwise. This is a nonconstant smooth bump with the stated support. Fix a point $x_*$ inside one torus coordinate cube and, for $\varepsilon>0$ small, set

$$
u_\varepsilon(x)=\psi((x-x_*)/\varepsilon),
$$

extended by zero. Subtract its torus mean when a mean-zero field is needed. Change of variables gives
$$
\|\nabla u_\varepsilon\|_2^2=\varepsilon^2\int|\nabla\psi|^2,
\quad \|D^2u_\varepsilon\|_2^2=\int|D^2\psi|^2,
\quad \int|\nabla u_\varepsilon|^{2q}
=\varepsilon^{4-2q}\int|\nabla\psi|^{2q}.
\tag{I.3j.8.3}
$$
Also $\int|\nabla u_\varepsilon|^q=\varepsilon^{4-q}\int|\nabla\psi|^q$. The ratio of the square of this mean to its second moment is a constant times $\varepsilon^4$, hence tends to zero. This proves the critical nonzero value and the supercritical divergence in the continuum. For the endpoint $q=2$, the readout is smooth and the limit constant is positive because $\psi$ is nonconstant.

To place the construction on exactly the admitted graph sequence, let $\varepsilon_n=n^{-1/4}$, let $P_n$ be Fourier projection onto $K_n$, and put
$$
\phi_n=P_nu_{\varepsilon_n}-\int u_{\varepsilon_n},\qquad s_n=A_n\phi_n.
$$
The upper bound $\lambda_n(k)\le4\pi^2|k|^2$ gives $\|s_n\|_2\le\|\Delta u_{\varepsilon_n}\|_2$, uniformly bounded by (I.3j.8.3). Each fixed coefficient of $u_{\varepsilon_n}$ is $O(\varepsilon_n^4)$, and each fixed $\lambda_n(k)$ remains bounded, so every fixed source coefficient tends to zero. Projection contracts Sobolev norms, proving $\phi_n\to0$ in $H^1$.

Projection preserves the critical and supercritical readout asymptotics as follows. For any integer $m>3$, Cauchy--Schwarz on the omitted Fourier coefficients gives
$$
\|\nabla(P_n-I)u_{\varepsilon_n}\|_\infty
\le C_m n^{3-m}\|u_{\varepsilon_n}\|_{H^m}
\le C'_m n^{3-m}\varepsilon_n^{2-m}.
$$
Indeed the squared summation factor is bounded by a constant times $\sum_{|k|>cn}|k|^{2-2m}=O(n^{6-2m})$ in four dimensions. At $m=6$ the right side is $O(n^{-2})$. Consequently the gradient error tends to zero in every finite $L^p$. For $p=4$, the unprojected gradient has a fixed nonzero $L^4$ norm, so its fourth moment converges to the same value. For $p=2q>4$, its norm diverges by (I.3j.8.3), while the error tends to zero; the ratio of the projected and unprojected $L^{2q}$ norms tends to one. The $L^q$ norm differs by at most $O(n^{-2})$, so its squared $q$th power remains negligible compared with the diverging second moment. The endpoint mean tends to zero by strong $H^1$ convergence. This proves (I.3j.8.1) and its supercritical counterpart on the graph sequence. Finally, the full-torus mean of $\sin(2\pi x_1)$ is zero and its second moment is $1/2$; on the half-torus these normalized moments are $2/\pi$ and $1/2$. Substitution gives (I.3j.8.2). ∎

Theorems I.3j.7–I.3j.8 give nonlinear product and domain passage, with sharp source-class failure modes, on the same mathematical refinement as Theorem I.3j.4. The physical expansion/shear maps, predictive-stress forcing, time and length units, averaging domains and inequality (I.3h.2) remain the source entries required by Definition I.3h. The white-source divergence of Proposition I.3j.5 is preserved.

<a id="remark-i3k-definite-answer-to-the-rcd-elliptic-backreaction-question"></a>**Remark I.3k (Definite Answer to the RCD Elliptic-Backreaction Question).** The conditional theorem-level form is the following: if an averaging domain $D$ on a noncollapsed $\mathrm{RCD}^*(K,4)$ branch supplies $\lambda_1(D)>0$, $\theta\in W^{1,2}(D)$, $\sigma\in L^2(D)$, and an elliptic scale-bridge estimate of dimension $L^{-2}$
$$
\frac{1}{\lambda_1(D)}\mathrm{Ch}_D(\theta)
+
\langle\sigma^2\rangle_D
\le
\mathcal B_D^{\mathrm{ell}}
\left[
\operatorname{Var}_D(T_{\mathrm{pred}}),
\dot\rho_{\mathrm{src}},
\mathfrak B_D,
\mathfrak H_D
\right],
\tag{I.3k.1}
$$
then $|\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{PU}}|\le2\mathcal B_D^{\mathrm{ell}}$ for the same declared arguments. Without (I.3k.1), Appendix I has only a conditional analytic target, not a theorem-level numerical estimate.

A canonical-domain value such as $C_D\approx10^{20}$ in Planck units requires the domain geometry, Poincaré constant, Hölder regularity scale, field-equation elliptic gauge, and finite defect budgets computed on the same branch.

<a id="theorem-i3l-an-exact-einstein-sigma-model-branch-carrying-the-backreaction-datum"></a>**Theorem I.3l (An Exact Einstein–Sigma-Model Branch Carrying the Backreaction Datum).** Use $c=\hbar=1$, a length $\ell>0$, a gravitational coupling $\kappa>0$ of dimension $L^2$, and $\epsilon=1/100$. On $D=[1,2]\times\mathbb T^3$ with dimensionless coordinates $(\tau,x,y,z)$, where $x,y,z$ have period $2\pi$, put
$$
b=\tau e^{\epsilon\tau\cos x},
\qquad
H=\frac1\tau+\epsilon\cos x,
$$
$$
g_L=\ell^2\bigl[-d\tau^2+b^2(dx^2+dy^2+dz^2)\bigr],
\qquad
g_E=\ell^2\bigl[d\tau^2+b^2(dx^2+dy^2+dz^2)\bigr].
\tag{I.3l.1}
$$
Let $g^*$ denote the formula for $g_L$ as a function of its four coordinate arguments. Four material fields $\Phi^A$ with values in a neighbourhood of $D$ have the action
$$
S=\frac1{2\kappa}\int R[g]\sqrt{-g}\,d^4x
-\int\Bigl[\tfrac12F_{AB}(\Phi)g^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\Phi^A\partial_\nu\Phi^B+V(\Phi)\Bigr]\sqrt{-g}\,d^4x,
\tag{I.3l.2}
$$
$$
F_{AB}(\Phi)=\frac1\kappa\Bigl[R_{AB}[g^*](\Phi)-\frac{g^*_{AB}(\Phi)}{\ell^2(\Phi^0)^2}\Bigr],
\qquad
V(\Phi)=\frac1{\kappa\ell^2(\Phi^0)^2}.
\tag{I.3l.3}
$$
The coefficients $F$ and $V$ are fixed functions of the fields and do not depend on the dynamical metric. Averages $\langle\cdot\rangle_D$ use the volume of $g_E$, proportional to $b^3\,d\tau\,dx\,dy\,dz$. The unit normal is $u=\ell^{-1}\partial_\tau$, the spatial frame is $e_i=(\ell b)^{-1}\partial_i$, $\operatorname{Var}_D(T)$ is the Frobenius variance of the frame components of a tensor $T$, and $\mathrm{Ch}_D(f)=c_{\mathrm{Ch}}\langle|\nabla_Ef|^2\rangle_D$ with the normalization constant $c_{\mathrm{Ch}}>0$ of the Cheeger energy in use. The following statements hold.

1. **Positive material sector.** On $D$ the matrix $\operatorname{diag}(1,b^{-1},b^{-1},b^{-1})\,\kappa F\,\operatorname{diag}(1,b^{-1},b^{-1},b^{-1})$ has smallest eigenvalue greater than $0.14$, and $V>0$.

2. **Solution.** The configuration $g=g_L$, $\Phi^A=(\tau,x,y,z)$ solves the Einstein equation and the four material equations of (I.3l.2). Its stress tensor is $T_{\mu\nu}=G_{\mu\nu}[g_L]/\kappa$.

3. **Congruence.** The congruence of $u$ is geodesic and hypersurface orthogonal, with
$$
\theta=\frac3\ell\Bigl(\frac1\tau+\epsilon\cos x\Bigr),
\qquad
\sigma=0,
\qquad
\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{PU}}=\tfrac23\operatorname{Var}_D(\theta)>0.
\tag{I.3l.4}
$$

4. **Source and rate.** With $\rho=T(u,u)$, $j_i=-T(u,e_i)$ and $r=u(\rho)$,
$$
\kappa\ell^2\rho=3H^2+\frac{2\epsilon\tau\cos x-\epsilon^2\tau^2\sin^2x}{b^2},
\qquad
T(u,e_1)=\frac{2\epsilon\sin x}{\kappa\ell^2b},
\qquad
T(u,e_2)=T(u,e_3)=0,
\tag{I.3l.5}
$$
$|r|\ge3/(\kappa\ell^3\tau^3)$, $\operatorname{Var}_D(T)>0$, and the momentum constraint reads $\nabla_h\theta=\tfrac{3\kappa}2\,j$ on every slice.

5. **Elliptic source control.** Put $\alpha=u(\theta)/r$ and $W=\alpha r\,\ell\,d\tau+\tfrac{3\kappa}2j_\flat$. Then $|\alpha|\le2\kappa\ell$, $\nabla_E\theta=W^\sharp$, and therefore $\int_D\langle\nabla_E\theta,\nabla_Ev\rangle=\int_D\langle W,\nabla_Ev\rangle$ for every $v\in W^{1,2}(D)$, with no boundary condition imposed on $\theta$. Moreover
$$
\langle|\nabla_E\theta|^2\rangle_D
\le
\kappa^2\Bigl[\tfrac94\operatorname{Var}_D(T)+4\ell^2\langle r^2\rangle_D\Bigr].
\tag{I.3l.6}
$$

6. **Spectral gap and certificate.** Every $f\in W^{1,2}(D)$ satisfies $\operatorname{Var}_D(f)\le P_D\langle|\nabla_Ef|^2\rangle_D$ with $P_D=32e^{13\epsilon}\ell^2$, so $\lambda_1(D)\ge c_{\mathrm{Ch}}/P_D>0$, and
$$
\frac1{\lambda_1(D)}\mathrm{Ch}_D(\theta)+\langle\sigma^2\rangle_D
\le
P_D\kappa^2\Bigl[\tfrac94\operatorname{Var}_D(T)+4\ell^2\langle r^2\rangle_D\Bigr],
\qquad
\frac1{\lambda_1(D)}\mathrm{Ch}_D(\theta)+\langle\sigma^2\rangle_D
\le
20000\,P_D\kappa^2\operatorname{Var}_D(T).
\tag{I.3l.7}
$$
Both right-hand sides have dimension $L^{-2}$.

Consequently items 1–3 of Definition I.3e and the source-control estimate (I.3h.2) hold on $D$ with $T_{\mathrm{pred}}=T$, $\dot\rho_{\mathrm{src}}=r$ and zero defect budgets, and (I.3f.1) gives $0<\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{PU}}\le\tfrac2{3\lambda_1(D)}\mathrm{Ch}_D(\theta)$, which is at most twice either right-hand side of (I.3l.7). Here $r$ is the change of material energy density along the flow, including cosmological dilution; the second bound in (I.3l.7) uses no rate. With $\eta(v)=e^{-1/v}$ for $v>0$ and $\eta(v)=0$ otherwise, $\chi(v)=\eta(v)/[\eta(v)+\eta(1-v)]$ and $\psi(s)=\chi(2s-1)\chi(5-2s)$, define on the period interval $0\le s<4$ the function $b_{\mathrm{ext}}(s,x)=\exp\{\psi(s)[\ln s+\epsilon s\cos x]\}$ for $\tfrac12<s<\tfrac52$ and $b_{\mathrm{ext}}=1$ otherwise, and extend it with period $4$ in $s$; it is smooth and equals $b$ on $[1,2]$. The compact manifold $X=(\mathbb R/4\mathbb Z)\times\mathbb T^3$ with $g_X=\ell^2[ds^2+b_{\mathrm{ext}}^2(dx^2+dy^2+dz^2)]$ and its Riemannian volume is a noncollapsed $\mathrm{RCD}^*(K,4)$ space, for any lower bound $K$ of its Ricci curvature, and contains $(D,g_E)$ isometrically. The Lorentzian solution of item 2 is asserted on the slab $D$ only.

The branch is a continuum solution with a designed material sector. The finite MPU network sequence of Definition I.3h, items 1–5, its convergence to $(X,g_X)$, and the identification of $T$ with the predictive stress of a selected MPU branch are separate requirements.

*Proof.* Write $q=\epsilon\tau\cos x$. A direct computation from the Christoffel symbols of $g^*$ gives the coordinate Ricci components
$$
\begin{split}
R_{00}&=-\frac{6\epsilon\cos x}\tau-3\epsilon^2\cos^2x,
\qquad
R_{01}=R_{10}=2\epsilon\sin x,\\
R_{11}&=2\epsilon\tau\cos x+\Bigl(3H^2-\frac1{\tau^2}\Bigr)b^2,\\
R_{22}&=R_{33}=\epsilon\tau\cos x-\epsilon^2\tau^2\sin^2x+\Bigl(3H^2-\frac1{\tau^2}\Bigr)b^2,
\end{split}
\tag{I.3l.8}
$$
and all other components vanish. Item 1. After the stated congruence, the diagonal entries of $\kappa F$ are $R_{00}+\tau^{-2}$ and $R_{ii}b^{-2}-\tau^{-2}$. On $D$, $\tau^{-2}\ge\tfrac14$, $|q|\le2\epsilon$ and $b\ge e^{-\epsilon}$, so the $00$ entry is at least $\tfrac14-6\epsilon-3\epsilon^2$, the $11$ entry at least $\tfrac14-6\epsilon-2\epsilon e^{4\epsilon}$, and the $22$ and $33$ entries at least $\tfrac14-6\epsilon-(\epsilon+\epsilon^2)e^{4\epsilon}$; here $3H^2-2\tau^{-2}\ge\tau^{-2}-6\epsilon$. The only off-diagonal entry has absolute value at most $2\epsilon e^{\epsilon}$. Gershgorin's theorem gives the bound $\tfrac14-6\epsilon-2\epsilon e^{4\epsilon}-2\epsilon e^{\epsilon}>0.14$.

Item 2. Varying the matter integral of (I.3l.2) with respect to the metric, with $F$ held fixed as a function of $\Phi$, gives
$$
T_{\mu\nu}=F_{AB}\partial_\mu\Phi^A\partial_\nu\Phi^B
-g_{\mu\nu}\Bigl[\tfrac12F_{AB}g^{\alpha\beta}\partial_\alpha\Phi^A\partial_\beta\Phi^B+V\Bigr].
\tag{I.3l.9}
$$
On the stated configuration $\partial_\mu\Phi^A=\delta^A_\mu$ and, with $c=\ell^{-2}\tau^{-2}$, $F=\kappa^{-1}(\mathrm{Ric}-cg)$ and $V=c/\kappa$. Hence $\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}_gF+V=\kappa^{-1}(R/2-c)$ and $T=\kappa^{-1}(\mathrm{Ric}-\tfrac12Rg)$, which is the Einstein equation. The matter action is invariant under diffeomorphisms, so $\nabla_\mu T^\mu{}_\nu=E_A\partial_\nu\Phi^A$ up to an overall sign convention, where $E_A$ are the material Euler–Lagrange expressions. The left side vanishes by the contracted Bianchi identity and $d\Phi$ has full rank, so every $E_A$ vanishes.

Item 3. The metric is synchronous, so the $\tau$-lines are geodesics orthogonal to the slices. Since $\partial_\tau h_{ij}=2(\partial_\tau\ln b)h_{ij}$ for the spatial metric $h_{ij}=\ell^2b^2\delta_{ij}$, the expansion tensor is pure trace: $\sigma_{ij}=0$ and $\theta=3\ell^{-1}\partial_\tau\ln b$. The function $\theta$ is not constant on any open set and the volume density is positive, so $\operatorname{Var}_D(\theta)>0$, and (I.3e.1) gives $\mathcal Q_D^{\mathrm{PU}}$.

Item 4. The displayed $\rho$ and $T(u,e_i)$ are the frame components of $G[g_L]/\kappa$ computed from (I.3l.8). Differentiation gives
$$
\kappa\ell^3r=-\frac6{\tau^3}-\frac{6\epsilon\cos x}{\tau^2}
-\frac{2\epsilon\cos x\,e^{-2q}}{\tau^2}
-\frac{4\epsilon^2\cos^2x\,e^{-2q}}\tau
+2\epsilon^3\cos x\sin^2x\,e^{-2q}.
\tag{I.3l.10}
$$
For $1\le\tau\le2$ the deviation of $\kappa\ell^3\tau^3r$ from $-6$ is at most $12\epsilon+(4\epsilon+16\epsilon^2+16\epsilon^3)e^{4\epsilon}<0.164$, which gives the bound on $|r|$. The component $T(u,e_1)$ is odd in $x$ and the volume density is even, so its mean vanishes while it is nonzero on a set of positive measure; hence $\operatorname{Var}_D(T)\ge\langle|j|^2\rangle_D>0$. Finally $\nabla_h\theta$ has the single frame component $(\ell b)^{-1}\partial_x\theta=-3\epsilon\sin x/(\ell^2b)=\tfrac{3\kappa}2j_1$.

Item 5. From (I.3l.4), $u(\theta)=-3/(\ell^2\tau^2)$, so $|u(\theta)|\le6/(\ell^2\tau^3)\le2\kappa\ell|r|$ for $\tau\le2$, which is the bound on $\alpha$. The $g_E$-gradient of $\theta$ has normal component $u(\theta)=\alpha r$ and tangential part $\nabla_h\theta=\tfrac{3\kappa}2j$, that is $\nabla_E\theta=W^\sharp$; pairing with $\nabla_Ev$ and integrating gives the weak identity. The two parts are orthogonal, so $|\nabla_E\theta|^2=\alpha^2r^2+\tfrac94\kappa^2|j|^2\le4\kappa^2\ell^2r^2+\tfrac94\kappa^2|j|^2$; averaging and using $\langle|j|^2\rangle_D\le\operatorname{Var}_D(T)$ gives (I.3l.6).

Item 6. For the product metric $g_0=\ell^2(d\tau^2+dx^2+dy^2+dz^2)$ on $D$ the Neumann Poincaré inequality $\int_D(f-\bar f_0)^2\le\ell^2\int_D|\nabla_0f|^2$ holds with respect to the coordinate measure, where $\bar f_0$ is the coordinate mean: the first nonzero Neumann eigenvalue of the coordinate Laplacian is $\pi^2$ on $[1,2]$ and $1$ on $\mathbb T^3$. Unweighted integrals below use that coordinate measure. On $D$, $e^{-\epsilon}\le b\le2e^{2\epsilon}$, so the density $w=b^3$ satisfies $w_{\max}/w_{\min}\le8e^{9\epsilon}$, and $g_E\le4e^{4\epsilon}g_0$ gives $|\nabla_0f|^2\le4e^{4\epsilon}|\nabla_Ef|^2$. Since the weighted mean minimizes the weighted variance,
$$
\operatorname{Var}_D(f)\le\frac{w_{\max}\int_D(f-\bar f_0)^2}{\int_Dw}
\le\frac{w_{\max}}{w_{\min}}\,\ell^2\langle|\nabla_0f|^2\rangle_D
\le32e^{13\epsilon}\ell^2\langle|\nabla_Ef|^2\rangle_D.
$$
The definition of $\lambda_1(D)$ then gives $\lambda_1(D)^{-1}\mathrm{Ch}_D(\theta)\le P_D\langle|\nabla_E\theta|^2\rangle_D$, and (I.3l.6) with $\sigma=0$ gives the first bound of (I.3l.7). For the second, (I.3l.5) gives $|\kappa\ell^2\rho-3\tau^{-2}|\le6\epsilon+3\epsilon^2+(2\epsilon+\epsilon^2)e^{4\epsilon}<0.082$, so every value of $\rho$ on $[1,\tfrac54]\times\mathbb T^3$ exceeds every value on $[\tfrac74,2]\times\mathbb T^3$ by more than $3/(4\kappa\ell^2)$. Each of these bands has normalized measure at least $e^{-9\epsilon}/32$, and the identity $\operatorname{Var}(\rho)=\tfrac12\mathbb E[(\rho(X)-\rho(X'))^2]$ for independent points $X,X'$ gives
$$
\operatorname{Var}_D(T)\ge\operatorname{Var}_D(\rho)\ge\frac{9e^{-18\epsilon}}{16384\,\kappa^2\ell^4}.
$$
On the other hand $|\nabla_E\theta|^2\le(9+9\epsilon^2e^{2\epsilon})/\ell^4$ on $D$. The ratio of the two bounds is $16384(1+\epsilon^2e^{2\epsilon})e^{18\epsilon}\kappa^2<20000\kappa^2$, which gives the second bound of (I.3l.7). The dimensions are $[\operatorname{Var}_D(T)]=L^{-8}$, $[r^2]=L^{-10}$, $[P_D]=L^2$ and $[\kappa^2]=L^4$.

The stated consequences are the definitions of items 1–3 of Definition I.3e and of (I.3h.2), and (I.3f.1) with $\sigma=0$. The functions $\eta$, $\chi$ and $\psi$ are smooth, $\psi=1$ on $[1,2]$ and $\psi=0$ outside $(\tfrac12,\tfrac52)$, which gives the properties of $b_{\mathrm{ext}}$; a compact smooth Riemannian four-manifold with $\mathrm{Ric}\ge K$ and its volume measure is a noncollapsed $\mathrm{RCD}^*(K,4)$ space. ∎

<a id="proposition-i3m"></a>

<a id="proposition-i3m-all-function-dimension-obstruction-for-shrinking-homogeneous-jumps"></a>**Proposition I.3m (All-Function Dimension Obstruction for Shrinking Homogeneous Jumps).** On a flat four-torus take any translation-invariant symmetric finite jump generator $L f(x)=\sum_s a_s(f(x+s)-f(x))$ on a finite periodic grid, with $a_s=a_{-s}\ge0$, $0<|s|\le h$, and no wrap ambiguity in the radius-two stencil at a base vertex. Normalize its second moment to $\sum_s a_s ss^{\mathsf T}=2I_4$ in the physical distance and generator units. Suppose the finite all-function inequality
$$
\Gamma_2(f)(x)\ge K\Gamma(f)(x)+\tfrac14(Lf(x))^2
\tag{I.3m.1}
$$
holds for every graph function, using the jump carré du champ of Theorem C.6c.4. Then $K\le-101/(625h^2)$. In particular the homogeneous shrinking-stencil geometries and generators of Theorems C.6c.4 and C.6c.6 cannot supply the uniform all-function four-dimensional curvature bound of Definition I.3h by their jump generators. This obstruction allows arbitrary positive relative weights and arbitrary numbers of jump directions on every mesh.

*Proof.* Center the local lift at the base vertex. All expressions in (I.3m.1) depend only on the two-step stencil, so assign there the values of $q(x)=|x|^2$ and $u(x)=|x|^4$. Extend their values arbitrarily to other vertices. Write $M_j=\sum_s a_s|s|^j$, so $M_2=8$ and $M_4>0$. The commuting jump translations give the bilinear form
$$
\Gamma_2(v,w)(0)=\tfrac14\sum_{s,t}a_sa_t\Delta_s\Delta_t v(0)\Delta_s\Delta_t w(0).
$$
The identity is also the polarization of the exact all-function translation formula in Theorem C.6c.4. Put $A=|s|^2$, $B=|t|^2$ and $c=s\cdot t$. The two increments of $q$ and $u$ are respectively $2c$ and $2AB+4c(A+B)+4c^2$. Thus $Lq=8$, $Lu=M_4$, and $\Gamma_2(q)=16$. In the cross term, the $cAB$ and $c^3$ sums vanish by changing the sign of one jump. The second moment gives $\sum_t a_t c^2=2A$, so the remaining cross term is
$$
\Gamma_2(q,u)=2\sum_{s,t}a_sa_t c^2(A+B)=8M_4 .
\tag{I.3m.2}
$$
In the quartic term $|2AB+4c(A+B)+4c^2|\le7(A+B)\sqrt{AB}$, since $|c|\le\sqrt{AB}\le(A+B)/2$. As $A+B\le2h^2$, this gives
$$
\Gamma_2(u)\le\tfrac{49}{2}h^2\sum_{s,t}a_sa_t AB(A+B)=392h^2M_4.
\tag{I.3m.3}
$$
Take $f=q-u/(100h^2)$ on the two-step stencil. Expanding the two quadratic forms and retaining the sign of the crossed term yields
$$
\begin{aligned}
\Gamma_2(f)-\tfrac14(Lf)^2
&=-\frac{12M_4}{100h^2}+
\frac{\Gamma_2(u)-M_4^2/4}{10000h^4}\\
&\le-\frac{101}{1250}\frac{M_4}{h^2} .
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.3m.4}
$$
On each one-step neighbor, $f(s)-f(0)=|s|^2(1-|s|^2/(100h^2))$, so $0<\Gamma(f)\le M_4/2$. Dividing (I.3m.4) gives the stated upper bound on $K$. The exact second moment and two-step lift hold in the cited endpoint family for all sufficiently fine meshes, with $h\to0$ at its fixed physical length. No stochastic error estimate is needed for this finite generator test. ∎

<a id="theorem-i3n"></a>

<a id="theorem-i3n-paid-weighted-networks-for-the-inhomogeneous-backreaction-geometry"></a>**Theorem I.3n (Paid Weighted Networks for the Inhomogeneous Backreaction Geometry).** Fix the smooth compact Riemannian extension $(X,g_X)$ of Theorem I.3l before evaluating any cosmological observable. There is one finite qualified graph sequence with paid propagation distances, capacity measures and reversible graph half-forms converging to the distances, volume and Cheeger energy of $(X,g_X)$ under the same cell identifications. At all scales above the actual mesh, the graphs have uniform four-volume bounds, doubling and weak $(1,2)$-Poincaré bounds. The compared length spaces satisfy the full global $\mathrm{BE}(K,4)$ hypothesis of Theorem C.6c for one fixed $K$. The result supplies the geometric limit and the length-space stability inputs of Theorem I.3i on the inhomogeneous geometry of Theorem I.3l. The finite jump-generator curvature condition of Definition I.3h(1) retains its separate test.

*Frozen grid and geometry.* In the periodic coordinates of Theorem I.3l the Riemannian tensor is diagonal, smooth and uniformly elliptic. Write $g=g_X$, $w=\sqrt{\det g}$ and $A_i=w g^{ii}$. Use centered rectangular product grids with side lengths $h_i$ in the four coordinate directions and $\max_i h_i=h\to0$, with all $h_i/h$ bounded below. The periods need not be commensurable, since each coordinate is divided into the same integer number of equal intervals. Let $Q_x$ be the centered cell about $x$ and $v_h=\prod_i h_i$. Every axis edge is retained. Also retain all nonaxis displacements of coordinate length between $r_h/2$ and $r_h$, with $h/r_h\to0$ and $r_h\to0$. Choose the shortest coordinate lift at each edge. Its positive length is the $g$-length of the corresponding straight segment.

The finite physical meter can use rational timers. With $\eta_h\to0$, round each positive segment length up to a rational $\ell_{xy}$ with relative error at most $\eta_h$, using a common positive rational unit small enough for the entire finite list. Define $d_h$ to be the shortest-path distance with these paid lengths. By the triangle inequality for $d_g$, $d_h(x,y)\geq d_g(x,y)$. Conversely, on the compact manifold choose a minimizing $g$-geodesic, parameterize it by coordinate arc length and partition it into subarcs of length at most $3r_h/4$. A subarc of that size has chord length $3r_h/4+O(r_h^2)$, since the coefficients and first derivatives of $g$ are bounded and the geodesic has bounded coordinate curvature after this reparameterization. Round intermediate points to grid centers at distance $O(h)$. Every resulting full chord lies in the paid shell at all sufficiently fine grades. The last remainder, of length $O(r_h)$, is realized by axis steps at cost $O(r_h+h)$. The cost change from chords, rounding and rational timers is $O(r_h+h/r_h+\eta_h)$, uniformly for the compact pair budget. Thus $\sup_{x,y}|d_h(x,y)-d_g(x,y)|\to0$. The same estimates apply with a center and radius buffer for every fixed bounded coordinate chart. Axis paths also give a uniform upper bound by the coordinate $\ell^1$ grid distance, and every paid path has length bounded below by a fixed multiple of the coordinate torus distance. This gives the uniform comparability needed for small-scale volume and Poincaré tests, independently of the additive limiting distortion.

*Capacity and actual form.* The target physical cell mass is $\int_{Q_x}w\,dx$. At each stage choose positive rational masses $m_x$ with common physical volume unit and relative error at most $\eta_h$ from those integrals, and write $\mu_x=m_x/\sum_y m_y$. Supply at each port a ready pure qubit with the exclusive local one-use control angle of Theorem 46g.15 chosen to have reliable capacity $\sigma m_x$ for a fixed $\sigma>0$ in nats per physical volume. At all sufficiently fine grades these angles are below $\pi/4$. The product sign encoders attain the entropy bound on any finite collection of cells, with exactly additive capacity and complete receiver output. The positive bounded-control, clock, collection and retained cost construction is the local-pulse source of Proposition 46g.52, used here on the registered weighted cells. Private commands remain at the source. Divide the resulting capacity measure by $\sigma$ to obtain $m_h=\sum_xm_x\delta_x$. Thus its nonconstant volume weights are fixed by the independently programmed cell calibration, and have an actual finite response rather than an inferred density from backreaction.

On axis edges put a positive rational conductance $c_{x,x+h_i e_i}$ within relative error $\eta_h$ of $v_h A_i(x+h_i e_i/2)/h_i^2$. On shell edges choose positive rational conductances so that the total exit rate from shell edges satisfies $\sum_{y\ {\rm shell}}c_{xy}/m_x\leq\eta_h$ at each vertex. This can be done by taking one sufficiently small positive rational common value at each grade. Define the reversible physical-rate operator and half-energy by
$$
L_h f(x)=\sum_y\frac{c_{xy}}{m_x}(f(y)-f(x)),\qquad
\mathrm{Ch}_h(f)=\frac12\sum_{\{x,y\}}c_{xy}|f(y)-f(x)|^2.
$$
The conductance graph is exactly the paid graph. The small shell rates still have complete jump and endpoint records. They add a nonnegative form with value at most $\eta_h\|f\|^2_{\ell^2(m_h)}$, by the elementary difference-square bound and detailed balance. This allows the cost metric to use the shell and the heat comparison to use the physical rates without equating the two services.

*Finite implementation and selection.* Encode each paid edge by the nonzero integer descriptor $(\ell_{xy}/\ell_0,0,0,0)$ up to orientation, where $\ell_0$ is the common positive rational length unit of the grade. The integer descriptor timer of Definition C.6c.4a gives exactly its declared length and retains the fixed tariff and all clock, route, lane, pulse and holding entries. The descriptor is an integer timer word. For the rational reversible heat generator choose a positive lag $\Delta_h$ satisfying the diagonal period condition. For a source position $x$, use a fresh binary register and prepare the row of $e^{\Delta_h L_h}$ by conditional rotations with its subtree probabilities. Retain the source vertex, chosen destination and invalid control outcomes. Each destination takes a deterministic registered route and transports the unchanged payload with full-reference swaps, padding shorter paths with common idle slots. The complete channel retains its source port, endpoint state, choice and route records. The row entries are finite computable data from the matrix exponential with certified tail. The ideal rotations define the kernel and finite synthesis approximates its full channel to any declared tolerance. This weighted implementation does not require the uniform-mass specialization of Theorem C.6c.7. Detailed balance holds for the mathematical form and its declared normalized comparison probabilities $\mu_x$. A copy of the independently qualified P17 ready-cell preparation and complete control ports is reserved at each graph vertex. The same finite owned-source convention covers the weighted probabilities and encoded capacity experiments, with the full old and auxiliary stocks charged.

Freeze the graph, measure, rates and their complete finite protocol schedule before the admitted normal forecast comparisons, in the fixed-geometry reservation sense of Theorem C.6c.5c. The entire additional task payoff, slot maximum and resource reserve are common on those comparisons. The teacher-mean forecast still attains the core minimum by the same common-duration additive reservation identity. This is selection on the declared fixed geometric source, independently of the measured value of expansion, shear or backreaction.

*Volume and local Poincaré bounds.* The cell masses are bounded above and below by fixed multiples of $h^4$, since $w$ is uniformly bounded and positive. For radii $r\geq c_0h$ below a fixed coordinate injectivity range, the metric comparison with coordinate torus distance sandwiches a graph ball between coordinate cubes of side comparable to $r$; if the inner cube has fewer than a fixed number of vertices, the center mass supplies the lower bound. Counting gives $c r^4\leq m_h(B_r)\leq C r^4$ and uniform doubling on these scales. For a graph ball use a containing axis grid box of side comparable to $r+h$. The box, including all its axis edges, lies in a graph ball of radius $C'(r+h)$ by the axis path bound. On an axis box the counting-measure Poincaré inequality follows by tensorizing the one-dimensional interval eigenvalue $4\sin^2(\pi/(2N))\geq4/N^2$ for an $N$-site path. Uniform comparability of cell masses to $h^4$ and axis conductances to $h^2$ turns it into the weighted estimate
$$
\sum_{x\in B_r}m_x|f(x)-f_{B_r}|^2
\leq C r^2\!\!\sum_{\substack{\{x,y\}\ {\rm axis}\\x,y\in B_{C''r}}}
c_{xy}|f(y)-f(x)|^2 .
$$
Here the mean minimizes the weighted quadratic error on the ball, so it may be bounded by using the containing box's mean. The upper volume bound on the enlarged ball and the lower bound on $B_r$ give the equivalent normalized weak $(1,2)$-Poincaré form. The shortcut form is positive, so it may also be included on the right. The compact global radius range is covered by the same argument using the periodic axis box.

*Measured and form limits.* Use the center maps and the cell-constant identification for $L^2$. To make that identification exactly isometric in the presence of rational rounding, multiply the value on $Q_x$ by $\bigl(m_x/\int_{Q_x}w\bigr)^{1/2}$. This differs from the unscaled interpolation by $O(\eta_h)$ in $L^2$ on bounded families. The cell mesh and the uniform metric convergence give measured Gromov–Hausdorff convergence, with the mass rounding changing the total variation of the cell comparison by $O(\eta_h)$. The weak liminf uses the four forward difference quotients, constant on each base cell. Uniform ellipticity bounds them in $L^2(dx)$ along bounded-energy sequences. Discrete summation by parts against smooth periodic vector fields identifies every weak limit as the four distributional derivatives of the $L^2$ limit. The midpoint weights tend uniformly on their cells to $A_i$, so weak lower semicontinuity gives
$$
\liminf_h \mathrm{Ch}_h(f_h)\geq
\frac12\int_X\sum_i A_i|\partial_i f|^2\,dx=\mathrm{Ch}_{g}(f).
$$
For a smooth fixed $f$, sampling at the centers and the midpoint Taylor estimates give equality in the limit, with the shell energy bounded by $\eta_h\|f_h\|^2$. Smooth periodic density in $H^1(X,g)$ and a diagonal give recovery for every form-domain vector. Theorem 35b.6 supplies the corresponding semigroup and resolvent comparisons under these same maps.

Use the actual compact smooth length space $(X,g)$ as the compared cell interpolation at every stage. It has the same volume and limit form just proved. Smoothness and compactness give a finite Ricci lower bound $K$, and the Bochner identity with $|\operatorname{Hess}f|^2\geq(\Delta_gf)^2/4$ gives its full $\mathrm{BE}(K,4)$ after heat regularization. The interpolant heat and integrated curvature comparisons are constant under the common identity, and the cell projection converges strongly on every fixed $L^2$ test. These are the length-space hypotheses of Theorem C.6c, with noncollapse in the actual Hausdorff volume normalization.

This proves items 2–5 of Definition I.3h on the stated graph sequence and its geometric $\mathrm{RCD}$ and Cheeger stability. It realizes the inhomogeneous metric and capacity geometry before any cosmological output is evaluated. The full-function finite jump estimate of item 1 fails for these actual rates, as shown below. Identifying the stress and its finite source-energy response with the exact predictive material source, and its joint cosmological observable record, retain their own tests. $\square$

<a id="corollary-i3n1"></a>

<a id="corollary-i3n1-raw-curvature-on-the-inhomogeneous-weighted-networks"></a>**Corollary I.3n.1 (Raw Curvature on the Inhomogeneous Weighted Networks).** On the actual weighted networks of Theorem I.3n, any full-function $\mathrm{BE}(K_h,4)$ lower bound for their jump generator satisfies $K_h\leq-c h^{-2}$ for some fixed $c>0$ at all sufficiently fine grades.

*Proof.* Work with the normalized generator $\widehat L_h=h^2L_h$. Fix a base vertex $x$, and in its local axis grid write $z=x+\sum_i k_i h_i e_i$. For comparison freeze the constant symmetric axis rates $a_i=(h/h_i)^2 g^{ii}(x)$ in both signs. They are bounded above and below by fixed positive constants. In the two-jump axis neighborhood use the test $f(z)=\sum_i |k_i|/a_i$, extending it by zero to other vertices. The local lift is unambiguous at fine grades, and the test is uniformly bounded. For the frozen generator, the one-jump increments are $1/a_i$ in both signs. The only nonzero double differences are for pairs of opposite jumps on the same axis, each of value $-2/a_i$. The commuting-axis formulas therefore give
$$
\widehat L_{\rm fr}f(x)=8,\qquad
\widehat\Gamma_{\rm fr}(f)(x)=\sum_i a_i^{-1},\qquad
\widehat\Gamma_{2,\rm fr}(f)(x)=8.
$$
At the base and each axis neighbor, midpoint coefficients, cell masses, smoothness and relative rounding give actual normalized axis rates $a_i+O(h+\eta_h)$ for both signs. The total normalized shell rate is at most $h^2\eta_h$ at every vertex. All normalized row sums are bounded. In the expansion $\Gamma_2=\tfrac12L\Gamma-\Gamma(f,Lf)$ at the base, an outer shell row contribution is therefore $O(h^2\eta_h)$ for this bounded test, even when a shortcut neighbor is far from the axis neighborhood in lattice steps. For the outer axis rows the differences of the coefficients and the inner extra shell terms are $O(h+\eta_h)$. The same local estimates apply to $Lf$ and $\Gamma(f)$. It follows that
$$
\widehat\Gamma_2(f)(x)-\tfrac14(\widehat L_h f(x))^2
=-8+O(h+\eta_h),\qquad
\widehat\Gamma(f)(x)=\sum_i a_i^{-1}+O(h+\eta_h).
$$
The latter quantity is bounded above and below by positive constants at sufficiently fine grades. Thus every normalized dimension-four curvature constant is bounded above by a fixed negative number. Undoing $\widehat L_h=h^2L_h$ gives the asserted bound. This applies to the raw axis-dominated generator on the inhomogeneous source and leaves other generators on that geometry to their own tests. $\square$

<a id="proposition-i3o"></a>

<a id="proposition-i3o-stable-dimension-obstruction-for-anisotropic-and-directed-jump-stencils"></a>**Proposition I.3o (Stable Dimension Obstruction for Anisotropic and Directed Jump Stencils).** Consider finite four-dimensional physical grids with jump generators \(L_h\), one marked vertex on each grid, and a local lift at that vertex through two jumps of physical length at most \(h\). Suppose the rows of \(\widehat L_h=h^2L_h\) at the vertex and its one-step comparison neighbors approach a locally frozen translation generator
$$
L_{\mathrm{fr},h}f(x)=\sum_s a_s(f(x+s)-f(x)),\qquad a_s\ge0,
\tag{I.3o.1}
$$
in the following sense. Use coordinates in units of \(h\), so \(|s|\le1\). At the vertex and every neighbor of either base row, compare the outgoing rates in the common local lift by their summed absolute difference, treating absent destinations as zero. The maximum of these differences tends to zero. Assume a uniform bound on the total frozen exit rate and a uniform positive lower bound on the smallest eigenvalue of the frozen matrix \(A_h=\frac12\sum_s a_s ss^{\mathsf T}\). The frozen rates may depend arbitrarily on \(h\), and can be directed with nonzero mean jump. Then any all-function dimension-four curvature bound for the actual generator at the marked vertex satisfies \(K_h\le-c h^{-2}\) at all sufficiently fine grades, with \(c>0\) fixed by those bounds. Thus neither directed skew in a locally frozen jump law nor bounded anisotropy can supply the finite curvature gate of Definition I.3h on this class.

*Frozen polynomial test.* Work in coordinates \(\xi=A_h^{-1/2}x\) for this grade. The transformed jumps have second moment \(2I_4\) and lengths at most \(H\), where a fixed \(H>0\) can be chosen from the lower eigenvalue bound. Write \(q(\xi)=|\xi|^2\), \(u(\xi)=|\xi|^4\), \(M_j=\sum_s a_s|\xi_s|^j\), and let \(A=|\xi_s|^2\), \(B=|\xi_t|^2\), \(c_{st}=\xi_s\cdot\xi_t\). At the marked origin the commuting-translation identity for the frozen generator is
$$
\Gamma_{2,\mathrm{fr}}(v,w)=
\tfrac14\sum_{s,t}a_sa_t\,\Delta_s\Delta_t v\,\Delta_s\Delta_t w .
\tag{I.3o.2}
$$
This holds for directed rates as well: in \(\tfrac12L\Gamma(v,w)-\tfrac12\Gamma(v,Lw)-\tfrac12\Gamma(w,Lv)\), the two first-difference cross terms cancel by the product rule for each translation, leaving the second-difference product. The increments of \(q,u\) are the polynomials used in Proposition I.3m. In the crossed term the two sums that previously vanished by reversal are nonnegative even without reversal:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\Gamma_{2,\mathrm{fr}}(q,u)
 &=8M_4+
 \left|\sum_s a_s|\xi_s|^2\xi_s\right|^2
 +2\left\|\sum_s a_s\xi_s^{\otimes3}\right\|_F^2
 \ \ge 8M_4 .
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.3o.3}
$$
Indeed the terms are respectively \(2\sum a_sa_t c_{st}^2(A+B)\), \(\sum a_sa_t c_{st}AB\), and \(2\sum a_sa_t c_{st}^3\); isotropy gives the first equality for the first sum, and the last two are Euclidean tensor squares. The quartic-square estimate of (I.3m.3) uses only \(|c_{st}|\le\sqrt{AB}\), \(M_2=8\) and the upper length bound, so it gives \(\Gamma_{2,\mathrm{fr}}(u)\le392H^2M_4\) also here. Likewise \(L_{\mathrm{fr}}q=8\), \(L_{\mathrm{fr}}u=M_4\), and \(\Gamma_{2,\mathrm{fr}}(q)=16\). Therefore the same test \(f=q-u/(100H^2)\) gives
$$
\Gamma_{2,\mathrm{fr}}(f)-\tfrac14(L_{\mathrm{fr}}f)^2
\le-\frac{101}{1250H^2}M_4 .
\tag{I.3o.4}
$$
The total exit bound \(J\) gives \(M_4\ge M_2^2/J=64/J\) by Cauchy–Schwarz. Also \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{fr}}(f)\le M_4/2\le4H^2\), and its value is positive and uniformly bounded below, since \(f(\xi_s)\ge(99/100)|\xi_s|^2\) on one jump.

*Local perturbation.* Evaluate the same polynomial on the common two-step lift at each grade. Its values on this lift are uniformly bounded by the length and covariance bounds, and it may be extended boundedly to the rest of the graph. In \(\widehat L_h f\) and \(\widehat\Gamma_h(f)\) the actual base-row rate replacement changes the result by at most a constant times its summed rate error. The expression \(\tfrac12\widehat L_h\widehat\Gamma_h(f)-\widehat\Gamma_h(f,\widehat L_hf)\) uses only the base row and the outgoing rows at its one-step neighbors. Subtract the corresponding frozen sums by first replacing the outer row and then each inner row. All rate sums and values of \(f\) and its differences are bounded uniformly, so the error is bounded by a fixed constant times the maximum summed rate error, regardless of the number of directions. The square of \(\widehat L_h f\) obeys the same estimate. Thus the defect in (I.3o.4) stays strictly negative with a uniform margin and the actual \(\widehat\Gamma_h(f)\) stays positive and bounded above. It follows that the dimension-four curvature constant of \(\widehat L_h\) is bounded above by a fixed negative number. Scaling \(\widehat L_h=h^2L_h\) multiplies the curvature constant by \(h^2\), proving the result. This uses the all-function test in the actual generator units. The matrix criterion for general weighted graph curvature gives a complementary finite test on other local geometries (Cushing et al. 2021).

<a id="proposition-i3p"></a>

<a id="proposition-i3p-dimension-four-curvature-obstruction-without-an-exit-rate-bound"></a>**Proposition I.3p (Dimension-Four Curvature Obstruction without an Exit-Rate Bound).** At a vertex of a finite jump network, suppose the two-step rows have a consistent local physical lift. The base row is a finite translation stencil with nonnegative rates and positive definite covariance $Q=\tfrac12\sum_s a_s ss^{\mathsf T}$ in four physical dimensions. Write $\ell$ for its largest physical jump length and $\lambda$ for the smallest eigenvalue of $Q$. The stencil may have arbitrarily large total exit rate. Under either condition below, every all-function dimension-four Bakry–Émery lower bound at the marked vertex is strictly negative.

1. If the rows at its one-step neighbors are translates of the base row, the rates may be directed. Then $K\le-101\lambda/(625\ell^2)$.
2. If the base stencil is symmetric, the one-step neighbor rows may be arbitrary positive scalar multiples of its translates as follows.
