1. The masses and charges are uniquely determined, up to simultaneous permutations, by
   $$
   c_i=\frac\mu{\sqrt b},\qquad m_i^2=\frac{\mu^2}{bp_i}.
   \tag{I.12b.2c.1}
   $$
   The retarded scalar response is the actual Green-operator sum
   $$
   \mathcal K_p^{\mathrm{ret}}J
   =\frac{\mu^2}{b}\sum_i(m_i^2-\Box_g)_{\mathrm{ret}}^{-1}J.
   \tag{I.12b.2c.2}
   $$
   It exists for all stated test sources, has causal support and is diffeomorphism covariant.

2. On Minkowski space its static spatial multiplier at $z=|\mathbf k|^2/\mu^2$ is
   $$
   H_p(z)=\sum_{i=1}^b\frac{p_i}{1+bp_i z}.
   \tag{I.12b.2c.3}
   $$
   Its normalized spatial convolution kernel is
   $$
   k_p(\mathbf x)=\frac{\mu^2}{4\pi b|\mathbf x|}\sum_i e^{-m_i|\mathbf x|},
   \qquad k_p\ge0,\quad k_p\in L^1(\mathbb R^3),\quad\int k_p\,d^3x=1.
   \tag{I.12b.2c.4}
   $$
   Its normalization and second radial moment are
   $$
   H_p(0)=1,\qquad\lim_{z\to\infty}zH_p(z)=1,
   \qquad\int |\mathbf x|^2 k_p(\mathbf x)d^3x
       =\frac{6b}{\mu^2}\sum_i p_i^2.
   \tag{I.12b.2c.5}
   $$
   Static response is the zero-frequency **adiabatic** projection of (I.12b.2c.2), not an assertion that an undamped step response relaxes.

3. The derivative identity
   $$
   H_p^{(n)}(0)=(-1)^n n!\,b^n s_{n+1},
   \qquad s_q=\sum_i p_i^q,
   \tag{I.12b.2c.6}
   $$
   holds for every integer $n\ge0$. Hence the jet through order $b-1$, with fixed $b,\mu$, determines the response and the action in (I.12b.2c.1). Equality of these jets is equivalent to permutation equality of the cascade weights. For pairwise distinct weights, a jet through order $b-2$ leaves a continuum of inequivalent responses; order $b-1$ is sharp. The latter statement transports the already proved Corollary I.12b.2b rather than introducing a second moment-minimality argument.

4. Write $r=|\{p_i\}|$. Among all finite positive canonical scalar actions with constant positive definite mass matrix and one conjugate source/output port, exactly $r$ observable scalar modes are necessary and sufficient to reproduce $H_p$. The $b$-field equal-charge construction reduces orthogonally to $r$ bright modes and $b-r$ source-decoupled modes. A source-decoupled mode remains a field of the full action, although it contributes no scalar-port response.

*Proof.*

Equal charges and $\sum c_i^2=\mu^2$ give $c_i^2=\mu^2/b$. Equation (I.12b.1a.3) then gives $m_i^2=c_i^2/p_i$, proving uniqueness and positivity in (I.12b.2c.1). The Euler–Lagrange equations are

$$
(m_i^2-\Box_g)\phi_i=c_iJ.
\tag{I.12b.2c.7}
$$

The operators are normally hyperbolic up to an overall sign convention. The global Green-operator theorem for normally hyperbolic operators on a smooth globally hyperbolic boundaryless spacetime supplies unique smooth future-supported solutions for compact smooth sources; see Bär, Ginoux and Pfäffle [2008, Corollary 3.4.3]. Apply that theorem to each scalar equation and sum the outputs, obtaining (I.12b.2c.2). Under a time-orientation-preserving diffeomorphism, the pulled-back solution solves the pulled-back equation with the pulled-back source and the same future-support condition. Uniqueness identifies it with the pulled-back Green solution. This proves covariance, rather than asserting it for an unspecified function of $\Box$.

For completeness, on Minkowski space the construction is explicitly

$$
\phi_i(t)=c_i\int_{-\infty}^t
 \frac{\sin((t-s)\sqrt{-\Delta+m_i^2})}{\sqrt{-\Delta+m_i^2}}J(s)\,ds.
\tag{I.12b.2c.8}
$$

For compact-time sources the spectral multiplier is bounded by $\min(t-s,m_i^{-1})$, so the integral is well defined in each spatial Sobolev space and differentiation verifies (I.12b.2c.7) and zero past Cauchy data. Uniqueness follows from the positive free Klein–Gordon energy. Finite propagation follows from its local energy identity: flux through a future light cone has the sign of an outward nonnegative sum of tangential and null-derivative squares, so zero energy and source on the backward cone of a point imply a zero field at that point. Thus (I.12b.2c.8) has the same causal support as the abstract Green solution.

The static equation is $(m_i^2-\Delta)\phi_i=c_iJ$. The decaying fundamental solution in three spatial dimensions is $e^{-m_i r}/(4\pi r)$: away from zero the radial Laplacian gives $\Delta(e^{-m_i r}/r)=m_i^2 e^{-m_i r}/r$, and integration over a shrinking ball gives unit distributional source. Multiplication by $c_i^2$ and summation yields (I.12b.2c.4). Its Fourier transform is $\sum c_i^2/(|\mathbf k|^2+m_i^2)=H_p(z)$. Near zero the kernel is $O(1/r)$ and at infinity it decays exponentially, so it is integrable and nonnegative. Direct radial integration gives

$$
\int \frac{c_i^2e^{-m_i r}}{4\pi r}d^3x=\frac{c_i^2}{m_i^2}=p_i,
\qquad
\int r^2\frac{c_i^2e^{-m_i r}}{4\pi r}d^3x=\frac{6c_i^2}{m_i^4}.
$$

Summing proves the spatial assertions and substituting (I.12b.2c.1) proves the second moment in (I.12b.2c.5). The endpoint formulas follow directly from (I.12b.2c.3).

For the adiabatic statement take $j\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ and $J_\epsilon(t,\mathbf x)=e^{\epsilon t}j(\mathbf x)$, $\epsilon>0$, and select the solution decaying at past infinity. Equation (I.12b.2c.8), extended by its convergent past integral, gives

$$
O_\epsilon(t)=e^{\epsilon t}\sum_i c_i^2(m_i^2-\Delta+\epsilon^2)^{-1}j.
$$

The spectral theorem bounds the $L^2\to L^2$ difference from the static operator by

$$
\left\|\sum_i c_i^2[(m_i^2-\Delta+\epsilon^2)^{-1}-(m_i^2-\Delta)^{-1}]\right\|
\le\epsilon^2\sum_i\frac{c_i^2}{m_i^4}
=\frac{\epsilon^2b}{\mu^2}s_2.
\tag{I.12b.2c.9}
$$

This proves a controlled static projection. It avoids any claim of pointwise nonnegative Lorentzian Green functions.

Expand each term of (I.12b.2c.3) in its convergent geometric series near zero. Differentiating yields (I.12b.2c.6). Theorem I.12b.2a applied to $s_1,\ldots,s_b$ proves the jet inverse statement. At distinct weights, Corollary I.12b.2b supplies a positive root family with unchanged $s_1,\ldots,s_{b-1}$ and changed $s_b$; (I.12b.2c.6) leaves the derivatives through $b-2$ fixed and changes the derivative of order $b-1$. Hence the resulting response operators are inequivalent. Fixed $b$ is essential: replacing each $p_i$ by $q$ copies of $p_i/q$ and replacing $b$ by $qb$ leaves (I.12b.2c.3) unchanged.

Group equal weights. A group of multiplicity $n_a$ and weight $p_a$ has one mass $m_a$ and total charge residue $n_a\mu^2/b$. The unit bright coordinate is the sum of its fields divided by $\sqrt{n_a}$, with charge $\mu\sqrt{n_a/b}$; the remaining orthogonal coordinates have zero charge. This supplies $r$ observable modes. Conversely, orthogonally diagonalize any positive mass matrix in an $N$-field canonical realization. Its static scalar transfer has the form $\sum_{a=1}^{r'}\gamma_a^2/(|\mathbf k|^2+\lambda_a)$ with positive residues at $r'\le N$ distinct active masses. Such poles cannot cancel. Equality on the positive real axis implies equality of the rational functions and therefore equality of their poles and residues. Since $H_p$ has exactly $r$ distinct active poles, $N\ge r$. This proves the exact minimum. ∎

<a id="proposition-i12b2c1-scalar-source-exchange-and-conserved-completion"></a>**Proposition I.12b.2c.1 (Scalar Source Exchange and Conserved Completion).**

The Hilbert stress tensor of (I.12b.1a.1), treating $J$ as an external scalar, is

$$
T^{(f)}_{ab}=\sum_i\nabla_a\phi_i\nabla_b\phi_i
-\frac12g_{ab}\sum_i[(\nabla\phi_i)^2+m_i^2\phi_i^2]
+g_{ab}JO.
\tag{I.12b.2c.1.1}
$$

On the mediator equations it satisfies $\nabla^a T^{(f)}_{ab}=O\nabla_bJ$. For an explicit dynamical source completion put $J=\kappa\psi$, add

$$
S_b=-\frac12\int dV_g[(\nabla\psi)^2+M^2\psi^2],
\qquad \kappa>0,\quad M^2>\kappa^2,
\tag{I.12b.2c.1.2}
$$

with the same fixed $\kappa,M$ for every comparator. The total stress is conserved on all scalar equations, the coupled equations are normally hyperbolic, and the flat-space Hamiltonian is positive definite in its field, momentum and gradient terms.

*Proof.* Direct divergence of the free scalar stress is $\sum_i(\Box\phi_i-m_i^2\phi_i)\nabla_b\phi_i=-J\nabla_bO$. The interaction divergence is $\nabla_b(JO)=J\nabla_bO+O\nabla_bJ$, yielding (I.12b.2c.1.1)'s Ward identity. The source equation is $(\Box-M^2)\psi+\kappa O=0$, so its free stress divergence is $-\kappa O\nabla_b\psi=-O\nabla_bJ$; the total divergence vanishes. The principal operator is diagonal $\Box$ on $b+1$ fields. The potential quadratic form completes the square:

$$
\sum_i m_i^2\phi_i^2+M^2\psi^2-2\kappa\psi\sum_i c_i\phi_i
=\sum_i m_i^2\left(\phi_i-\frac{\kappa c_i}{m_i^2}\psi\right)^2
+(M^2-\kappa^2)\psi^2,
\tag{I.12b.2c.1.3}
$$

where (I.12b.1a.2) was used. It is positive definite, and the kinetic and spatial-gradient terms are positive. ∎

This is an actual dynamical scalar source completion of the response family. In the coupled system, $H_p$ remains the mediator response conditional on $J=\kappa\psi$; the evolution of $\psi$ includes feedback and requires its own Cauchy data. It does not realize every arbitrary prescribed compact source as an unforced closed-system trajectory. Zero Cauchy data for every field with no external forcing gives the zero solution. Its source field is a mathematical realization entry. Identifying that field with baryonic stress and deriving Definition I.13d's galaxy, lensing, CMB and homogeneous readouts requires their separate physical projection record. Eliminating local fields with retarded boundary data produces (I.12b.2c.2); no ordinary single-field quadratic nonlocal action with a purely retarded Hessian is asserted.

<a id="theorem-i12b2d-sharp-normalized-scalar-resolvent-comparison"></a>**Theorem I.12b.2d (Sharp Normalized Scalar-Resolvent Comparison).**

Let $A$ be a positive definite real symmetric $N\times N$ matrix and $B$ an $N\times d$ matrix obeying

$$
B^TB=I_d,\qquad B^TA^{-1}B=I_d.
\tag{I.12b.2d.1}
$$

Define $F(z)=B^T(zI_N+A)^{-1}B$ and $C=A^{-1}$. This is the dimensionless static transfer of a positive canonical multi-scalar action with conjugate $d$-component scalar source/output and the same two endpoint normalizations. For $z>0$,

$$
\frac1{1+z}I_d-F(z)
=\frac{z}{(1+z)^2}B^T(C-I_N)(I_N+zC)^{-1}(C-I_N)B
\succeq0.
\tag{I.12b.2d.2}
$$

Equality on a source direction $v$ at any one $z>0$ holds exactly when $(C-I_N)Bv=0$. Equality as matrices at one positive $z$, equality at all positive $z$, and $AB=B$ are equivalent. Extra mass sectors in the latter case are source-decoupled.

For Theorem I.12b.2c the identity reduces to

$$
d_p(z):=\frac1{1+z}-H_p(z)
=\frac{z}{b(1+z)^2}\sum_i\frac{(bp_i-1)^2}{1+bp_i z}.
\tag{I.12b.2d.3}
$$

Consequently $d_p(z)>0$ for every $z>0$ exactly when the cascade is nonuniform. The one-pole comparator $H_0(z)=1/(1+z)$ is uniquely determined among scalar one-pole transfers by $H(0)=1$ and $\lim zH(z)=1$.

*Proof.* The scalar rational identity

$$
\frac{x}{1+zx}=\frac1{1+z}+\frac{x-1}{(1+z)^2}
-\frac{z(x-1)^2}{(1+z)^2(1+zx)}
\tag{I.12b.2d.4}
$$

holds after multiplying by the nonzero denominators. Apply spectral calculus to the positive symmetric matrix $C$. Since $(zI+A)^{-1}=C(I+zC)^{-1}$, compress (I.12b.2d.4) by $B$. Conditions (I.12b.2d.1) make the constant term $I_d/(1+z)$ and cancel the linear term. This is (I.12b.2d.2). Its quadratic form equals $z/(1+z)^2$ times the squared norm of $(I+zC)^{-1/2}(C-I)Bv$, proving positivity and the equality criterion. Invertibility of $C$ gives $(C-I)B=0$ iff $AB=B$. A symmetric $A$ then preserves $\operatorname{ran}B$ and its orthogonal complement; the latter is source-decoupled.

For the equal-charge model choose $A=\operatorname{diag}(1/(bp_i))$ and $B=b^{-1/2}(1,\ldots,1)^T$. Conditions (I.12b.2d.1) hold and the identity is (I.12b.2d.3). Its summands are nonnegative with positive denominators, and all vanish exactly when every $p_i=1/b$. Finally a one-pole response $a/(z+\lambda)$ satisfying the two normalizations has $a=1$ and $a/\lambda=1$, hence $\lambda=1$. ∎

**Registered comparison.**

For any fixed finite nonnegative measure $\omega$ on $(0,\infty)$ with nonzero mass, $\int H_p\,d\omega<\int H_0\,d\omega$ for a nonuniform cascade. Therefore a task that **maximizes** this Euclidean-response functional has no strict multifractal advantage in this entire two-endpoint-normalized positive scalar class. Charging a nonnegative nondecreasing cost for the minimal observable mode count cannot reverse that ordering. This is a sharp conditional no-gain result for the named task, not a definition of PCE.

For a preregistered real target $T$ in $L^2(\omega)$, a squared-error task instead has the exact decision criterion

$$
\|H_0-T\|_\omega^2-\|H_p-T\|_\omega^2
=2\langle d_p,H_0-T\rangle_\omega-\|d_p\|_\omega^2.
\tag{I.12b.2d.5}
$$

With a recorded additive description/resource cost difference $\Delta C=C_p-C_0$, the $p$ branch wins this task strictly iff the right-hand side exceeds $\Delta C$. Expansion of the two squares proves the identity. For example $T=H_0$ gives strict loss, whereas $T=H_p$ gives improvement $\|d_p\|_\omega^2$ before costs. These examples demonstrate dependence on a supplied target; selecting the target after observing a response supplies no forward-selection evidence.

The one-pole comparator here is a massive scalar resolvent. The Appendix I galaxy relaxation law in Equation I.4 is a different named response family. Using (I.12b.2d.5) as a comparison against it requires its admissible covariant realization, a common task, source/readout normalization, complexity code and finite error budget. Theorem I.12b.2f supplies a registered task, code and error budget for the two-scale halo law and proves its exhaustive separation from the whole Equation I.4 family. Real-frequency response is also separate: undamped poles are on the real axis, so a squared-frequency task must declare its source window, damping or distributional/readout prescription. The Euclidean inequality cannot be analytically continued as an inequality through those poles.

<a id="theorem-i12b2e-complete-charge-simplex-and-local-inverse-classification"></a>**Theorem I.12b.2e (Complete Charge-Simplex and Local-Inverse Classification).**

Fix known $b\ge2$, $\mu>0$ and all positive weights $p_i$ in (I.12b.1a.3). All actions of (I.12b.1a.1) satisfying (I.12b.1a.2)–(I.12b.1a.3) are parametrized exactly by

$$
w_i>0,\quad\sum_iw_i=1,\qquad
c_i^2=\mu^2w_i,\quad m_i^2=\mu^2\frac{w_i}{p_i}.
\tag{I.12b.2e.1}
$$

Their scalar static responses are

$$
H_{p,w}(z)=\sum_i\frac{p_i}{1+x_i z},\qquad x_i=\frac{p_i}{w_i},\qquad
\sum_i\frac{p_i}{x_i}=1.
\tag{I.12b.2e.2}
$$

The following statements hold.

1. $w=p$ gives $H_{p,w}=H_0$ for **every** cascade, including a nonuniform one. Every $w\ne p$ gives $H_{p,w}(z)<H_0(z)$ for every $z>0$. Thus fixing all cascade moments, both endpoint normalizations, canonical kinetic terms, causal covariance and the explicit source completion of Proposition I.12b.2c.1 leaves inequivalent scalar responses. Equal charge selects the additional point $w_i=1/b$.

2. The full rational response identifies the discrete positive measure $\sum_i p_i\delta_{x_i}$ exactly. If the $p_i$ are pairwise distinct and the $x_i$ are pairwise distinct, it identifies the entire labeled $w$ record; for arbitrary degeneracies, the exact equivalence criterion is equality of these grouped measures. In particular, labels among equal weights and modes at coincident $x$ retain their proper quotient.

3. On every point with pairwise distinct $x_i$, the first $b-1$ low-momentum moments
   $$
   M_k=\sum_i p_i x_i^k=\frac{(-1)^k}{k!}H_{p,w}^{(k)}(0),\qquad k=1,\ldots,b-1,
   \tag{I.12b.2e.3}
   $$
   form local smooth identifying coordinates on the normalized charge simplex. Their number is minimal for smooth measurements having a smooth local reconstruction. This local assertion does not imply global uniqueness from the same jet.

4. For $p=(1/3,2/3)$, the records $w=(1/2,1/2)$ and $\widetilde w=(1/5,4/5)$ satisfy the identical cascade and endpoint data and have
   $$
   H'(0)=\widetilde H'(0)=-10/9,
   \qquad H(1)=17/35,\quad\widetilde H(1)=43/88.
   \tag{I.12b.2e.4}
   $$
   They explicitly refute global identification by the locally sufficient $(b-1)$-jet in the unequal-charge class.

*Proof.*

Put $w_i=c_i^2/\mu^2$. Positivity and the second normalization make $w$ an open-simplex point; the static-share equations give $m_i^2=\mu^2w_i/p_i$. Conversely these choices satisfy both normalizations and every share equation. This proves the complete parametrization and (I.12b.2e.2), while Theorem I.12b.2c's Green construction and Proposition I.12b.2c.1 apply unchanged because they used positivity and (I.12b.1a.2).

Apply Theorem I.12b.2d with $A=\operatorname{diag}(w_i/p_i)$ and $B=(\sqrt{w_i})_i$. Then $B^TB=1$, $B^TA^{-1}B=\sum_i p_i=1$. Equality holds exactly when $(p_i/w_i-1)\sqrt{w_i}=0$ for every $i$, which is $w=p$. This proves item 1.

In (I.12b.2e.2), a distinct $x>0$ contributes a simple pole at $-1/x$ whose residue is $x^{-1}\sum_{i:x_i=x}p_i$. Positive residues preclude cancellation. Equality on $z>0$ is equality of rational functions, and uniqueness of their partial-fraction expansions determines each $x$ and the total $p$ weight at that $x$. This proves the grouped-measure criterion. If both sets of coordinates are pairwise distinct, the known distinct value of $p_i$ at a pole identifies its label and $w_i=p_i/x_i$ follows. The same grouped spectrum determines the retarded Green sum on every background, so equality of the rational response is also equivalence for this constant minimally coupled scalar class.

For item 3 define $N(x)=\sum_i p_i/x_i$. The Jacobian of the full $b$-component map $(N,M_1,\ldots,M_{b-1})$ is

$$
\det D(N,M_1,\ldots,M_{b-1})
=-(b-1)!\left(\prod_i\frac{p_i}{x_i^2}\right)
\left(\prod_{i<j}(x_j-x_i)\right)e_{b-1}(x),
\tag{I.12b.2e.5}
$$

where $e_{b-1}(x)=\sum_i\prod_{j\ne i}x_j>0$. To verify this identity, factor $p_i/x_i^2$ out of each column and $k$ out of row $M_k$. The remaining rows are $-1,x_i^2,x_i^3,\ldots,x_i^b$. The alternant with rows $1,x_i^2,\ldots,x_i^b$ is the Vandermonde determinant times $e_{b-1}$. Indeed the polynomial $\prod_i(t-x_i)$ expresses row $x_i^b$ in lower powers; only its coefficient $(-1)^{b-2}e_{b-1}$ multiplying row $x_i$ contributes, since the other rows already occur. Moving that row into the second position contributes another $(-1)^{b-2}$, proving the identity and its sign. This yields (I.12b.2e.5).

For distinct positive $x_i$ the determinant is nonzero. The inverse function theorem supplies a smooth local inverse for the full map. Restricting $N=1$ gives the asserted local coordinates on the smooth $(b-1)$-dimensional normalized hypersurface, equivalently the open charge simplex. If $k$ real $C^1$ measurements had a $C^1$ local inverse there, the chain rule would factor its identity differential through a vector space of dimension $k$, so $k\ge b-1$. This proves the stated sharp smooth local measurement count, without asserting a bound on discontinuous real-number encodings.

For item 4 the $x$ records are $(2/3,4/3)$ and $(5/3,5/6)$. Each obeys $\sum p_i/x_i=1$, and their $M_1$ values are both $10/9$. Direct substitution at $z=1$ gives the two fractions in (I.12b.2e.4). Their difference is $9/3080\ne0$. ∎

<a id="corollary-i12b2e1-continuum-of-fixed-cascade-responses"></a>**Corollary I.12b.2e.1 (Continuum of Fixed-Cascade Responses).**

For any fixed positive cascade $p$ with $b\ge2$, the class in Theorem I.12b.2e contains a continuum of inequivalent responses with identical full cascade and endpoint data.

*Proof.* Choose a nonzero $v$ with $\sum_i v_i=0$ and set $w(t)=p+tv$ for sufficiently small $t\ge0$ so every coordinate stays positive. Its first response moment is $M_1(t)=\sum_i p_i^2/(p_i+tv_i)$. It has $M_1'(0)=-\sum_i v_i=0$ and

$$
M_1''(t)=2\sum_i\frac{p_i^2v_i^2}{(p_i+tv_i)^3}>0.
$$

Thus $M_1(t)$ is strictly increasing for small $t>0$, so their slopes and their responses are distinct. ∎

<a id="corollary-i12b2e2-global-finite-sample-response-identification"></a>**Corollary I.12b.2e.2 (Global Finite-Sample Response Identification).**

Two scalar responses of (I.12b.1a.1)–(I.12b.1a.2), each with at most $b$ distinct active masses and with the same $\mu$, coincide if they agree at $2b-2$ distinct positive values of the dimensionless static variable $z$. These samples therefore determine their common scalar response and its positive pole/residue realization up to observable-mode equivalence. Branch labels and charge allocations inside an aliased representation retain Theorem I.12b.2e's grouped-measure qualification. The count is sufficient for every $b\ge2$; no global sharpness claim for $b>2$ is made.

For $b=2$ and fixed $p=(1/3,2/3)$, one positive sample is insufficient, for every location of that sample. In particular,

$$
w=(1/2,1/2),\qquad\widetilde w=(5/27,22/27)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
H_{p,w}(1)=H_{p,\widetilde w}(1)=17/35,
\qquad H'_{p,w}(0)=-10/9,\quad H'_{p,\widetilde w}(0)=-63/55.
\tag{I.12b.2e.6}
$$

*Proof.* Write each reduced response as $P_i(z)/Q_i(z)$, with $Q_i$ monic of degree $n_i\le b$ and all its zeros strictly negative. The endpoint $\lim zH_i(z)=1$ makes $P_i$ have degree $n_i-1$ with leading coefficient one. Therefore $P_1Q_2-P_2Q_1$ has degree at most $n_1+n_2-2\le2b-2$, because its highest coefficients cancel. The common static endpoint gives a zero at $z=0$. Agreement at $2b-2$ distinct positive samples gives $2b-1$ distinct zeros, so this polynomial is zero. Partial-fraction uniqueness then identifies the common poles and residues. This is the degree argument of source Theorem I.3c.6 specialized to the two fixed endpoints.

For any one chosen $z_0>0$, put $p_1=p=1/3$, $p_2=q=2/3$ and parameterize $w=(u,1-u)$. The sample response is

$$
h(u)=\frac{pu}{u+pz_0}+\frac{q(1-u)}{1-u+qz_0},\quad0<u<1.
$$

It has $h'(p)=0$ and

$$
h''(u)=-\frac{2p^2z_0}{(u+pz_0)^3}-\frac{2q^2z_0}{(1-u+qz_0)^3}<0.
$$

It is strictly increasing before $p$ and decreasing after $p$. Any value sufficiently close to and below $h(p)$ has one preimage on each side. At both points the two mass ratios are distinct, and the $p_i$ are distinct, so Theorem I.12b.2e, item 2, implies that the two different charge records have inequivalent full responses. This proves insufficiency of one sample at every positive location. Substitution gives the rational example (I.12b.2e.6). ∎

The construction has exactly $r$ observable scalar modes and uses $r$ retarded scalar solves per arbitrary source; $N$ scalar spectral-parameter evaluations use $Nr$ reciprocal terms. Exact inverse computation requires a registered arithmetic and root-isolation representation; numerical source/PDE/discretization errors require their own bounds. The target remains `M+C+R / A→B`: deriving the response-active source-share, charge and scale selector, the physical source-to-stress and observation maps of Definition I.13d, and strict preference over Equation I.4 under Theorem I.12b.2's actual common task and description code remain its named obligations. The previously selected predictive processor and spectrum extractor of Theorem P.8.9a.12.10d retain their own source, proper task and response map; they supply no identification of that task with dark-sector utility.

<a id="theorem-i12b2f-exhaustive-equation-i4-separation-of-the-two-scale-halo-law-and-a-registered-description-cost-criterion"></a>**Theorem I.12b.2f (Exhaustive Equation-I.4 Separation of the Two-Scale Halo Law and a Registered Description-Cost Criterion).** Put
$$
h(x)=1-\tfrac12\left(e^{-x}+e^{-2x}\right),\qquad
(x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4)=\left(\tfrac14,\tfrac12,1,2\right),
\tag{I.12b.2f.1}
$$
and write $f_{A,L,m}(x)=A\left(1-e^{-(x/L)^m}\right)$ for the enhancement profile of Equation I.4 with amplitude, length and steepness $A,L,m>0$.

1. *Two-scale halo law.* Let two field halos about a common point have active densities $\rho_j(r)=A_jq_j^2e^{-2k_jr}/r^2$, $j=1,2$, with $A_j,q_j>0$, $k_1=\kappa$, $k_2=2\kappa$ and $\kappa>0$, and equal total active masses. Their normalized enclosed active mass at radius $r$ is $h(2\kappa r)$.

2. *Exhaustive separation.* For every $A,L,m>0$,
$$
\max_{1\le i\le4}\left|f_{A,L,m}(x_i)-h(x_i)\right|>\frac1{2000}.
\tag{I.12b.2f.2}
$$

3. *Registered description-cost criterion.* Fix $e=10^{-4}$ and $\eta=10^{-5}$. In the four-radius binary task, trial $j=1,\dots,N$ queries $x_{i(j)}$ with $i(j)=1+((j-1)\bmod4)$, $N$ is a multiple of four, and each trial records an independent bit with mean $\mu_{i(j)}$, where $|\mu_i-h(x_i)|\le e$ for every $i$. A forecast is a table $q\in(0,1)^4$ fixed before the outcomes. A halo table satisfies $|q_i-h(x_i)|\le\eta$, and an Equation-I.4 table satisfies $|q_i-f_{A,L,m}(x_i)|\le\eta$ for one triple $A,L,m>0$ and every $i$. An outcome string $y$ is described with forecast $q$ by a prefix code whose length obeys
$$
-\log_2P_q(y)\le\ell_q(y)<-\log_2P_q(y)+2,
\qquad
P_q(y)=\prod_{j=1}^Nq_{i(j)}^{y_j}\left(1-q_{i(j)}\right)^{1-y_j},
\tag{I.12b.2f.3}
$$
for example the shortest dyadic prefix of the midpoint of the arithmetic-code interval of $y$ whose dyadic cell lies in that interval. Then for every halo table $q_s$ and every Equation-I.4 table $q_I$,
$$
\mathbb E\,\ell_{q_I}-\mathbb E\,\ell_{q_s}>\frac{N\gamma}{\ln2}-2,
\qquad
\gamma=\frac{41147}{1440000000000}.
\tag{I.12b.2f.4}
$$
If the halo description carries an additional source-only setup cost of $C_s\ge0$ bits and all other description costs are common to both, it has strictly lower expected registered cost than every Equation-I.4 description once $N>(C_s+3)/\gamma$.

*Proof.* Item 1. Integration gives $\int_{|y|<r}\rho_j\,d^3y=4\pi A_jq_j^2\int_0^re^{-2k_js}\,ds=H_j\left(1-e^{-2k_jr}\right)$ with $H_j=2\pi A_jq_j^2/k_j$. For $H_1=H_2$ the normalized enclosed mass is $\tfrac12(1-e^{-2\kappa r})+\tfrac12(1-e^{-4\kappa r})=h(2\kappa r)$.

Item 2. Suppose a triple violates (I.12b.2f.2), put $\delta=1/2000$ and $v_i=f_{A,L,m}(x_i)$. Then $v_i\in Y_i:=[h(x_i)-\delta,h(x_i)+\delta]$ and $0<v_i<A$. The function $F(z)=\log(-\log(1-z))$ is increasing on $(0,1)$, and $F(v_i/A)=m\log x_i-m\log L$. The radii are geometric with ratio two, so the second differences
$$
D_1=F(v_1/A)-2F(v_2/A)+F(v_3/A),\qquad
D_2=F(v_2/A)-2F(v_3/A)+F(v_4/A)
$$
vanish. Every $A>0$ is excluded. If $A\le\min Y_4$, then $v_4\ge A$, which is impossible. For $A\ge16$ write $F(z)=\log z+\phi(z)$ with $0\le\phi(z)\le-\log(1-z)$. The terms $-\log A$ cancel in a second difference, so
$$
D_1\le\log\frac{\max Y_1\,\max Y_3}{(\min Y_2)^2}-2\log\left(1-\frac{\max Y_3}{16}\right)<-0.033 .
$$
For $A$ in an interval $[a,b]\subset(\min Y_4,16]$, monotonicity of $F$ encloses $D_1$ and $D_2$ by endpoint values, for example $D_2\ge F(\min Y_2/b)-2F(\max Y_3/a)+F(\min Y_4/b)$ and $D_1\le F(\max Y_1/a)-2F(\min Y_2/b)+F(\max Y_3/a)$. Bisection of $(\min Y_4,16]$ gives a cover by $85$ intervals on each of which one such enclosure excludes zero, evaluated in outward-rounded interval arithmetic at sixty significant digits with the values $h(x_i)$ enclosed in the same arithmetic. Hence no triple satisfies all four bounds. The same construction succeeds with $\delta=0.00086$, and the triple $(A,L,m)=(0.98024,0.68359,0.96853)$ has maximal error $8.66\times10^{-4}$.

Item 3. Pinsker's inequality in natural logarithms gives $D(\mu\Vert q)\ge2(\mu-q)^2$ for Bernoulli means. For an Equation-I.4 table, item 2 gives an $i$ with $|f_{A,L,m}(x_i)-h(x_i)|>\delta$, hence $|q_{I,i}-\mu_i|>\delta-e-\eta$, and the four equally frequent queries give a mean divergence per trial of at least $(\delta-e-\eta)^2/2$. For a halo table, $\mu_i$ and $q_{s,i}$ lie in $[h(x_i)-e-\eta,h(x_i)+e+\eta]$, on which $z(1-z)\ge\varsigma_i$ with $(\varsigma_1,\varsigma_2,\varsigma_3,\varsigma_4)=(1/5,6/25,9/50,3/50)$. The second derivative of $z\mapsto D(z\Vert q)$ is $1/(z(1-z))$, so Taylor's formula gives $D(\mu_i\Vert q_{s,i})\le(e+\eta)^2/(2\varsigma_i)$ and the mean is at most $(e+\eta)^2\sum_i\varsigma_i^{-1}/8$. Exact rational arithmetic gives
$$
\frac{(\delta-e-\eta)^2}2-\frac{(e+\eta)^2}8\sum_{i=1}^4\frac1{\varsigma_i}=\gamma .
$$
By independence, $\mathbb E[-\ln P_q(y)]$ is the sum over trials of the Bernoulli entropy of $\mu_{i(j)}$ and of $D(\mu_{i(j)}\Vert q_{i(j)})$. The entropies are common to both tables, and (I.12b.2f.3) gives (I.12b.2f.4). If $N>(C_s+3)/\gamma$, then $N\gamma/\ln2-2>N\gamma-2>C_s+1$, so $C_s+\mathbb E\,\ell_{q_s}<\mathbb E\,\ell_{q_I}$. ∎

<a id="theorem-i12b2g"></a>

<a id="theorem-i12b2g-static-metric-response-of-canonical-yukawa-halos"></a>**Theorem I.12b.2g (Static Metric Response of Canonical Yukawa Halos).** Let a smooth static spherically symmetric source be supported inside radius $a>0$ in Minkowski space. Outside that radius let the only fields carrying stress be finitely many canonical real scalar fields with a positive mass matrix. Use the static decaying solutions and include the source support, including its stresses, in a conserved total stress tensor. Read the radial weak-field acceleration from linearized Einstein gravity with fixed $G>0$. The following conclusions concern this readout on the same fields.

1. For minimal coupling, the exterior active gravitational density is nonpositive. It is strictly negative at every exterior radius if any of the exterior Yukawa amplitudes is nonzero. After subtracting a compact-core contribution and dividing by a positive normalization, the cumulative acceleration enhancement is nonincreasing outside the source. On four exterior radii corresponding to $x=(1/4,1/2,1,2)$, its uniform error from the increasing two-scale halo law of Theorem I.12b.2f is at least $(h(2)-h(1/4))/2>1/10$.
2. Allow a constant symmetric improvement matrix, obtained by adding $-\frac12 R\,\phi^{\mathsf T}\Xi\phi$ to the scalar Lagrangian. The active density may then be positive. Yet the radial acceleration cannot equal the nonzero two-scale halo profile of Theorem I.12b.2f on any open interval of exterior radii, even after adding a compact-core contribution and choosing a constant positive normalization. This conclusion concerns exact equality on an interval. A finite-radius approximation with the improved stress requires its own error bound.

*Proof.* In the weak-field approximation the matter stress is evaluated on the unperturbed flat solution. With signature $(-,+,+,+)$, the trace-reversed static Einstein equation in harmonic gauge gives
$$
\Delta\Phi=4\pi G\left(T_{00}+\sum_{j=1}^3T_{jj}\right),
\qquad g_{00}=-(1+2\Phi).
\tag{I.12b.2g.1}
$$
Indeed $\bar h_{00}$ and the three $\bar h_{jj}$ satisfy $\Delta\bar h_{\mu\nu}=-16\pi G T_{\mu\nu}$, and $h_{00}=(\bar h_{00}+\sum_j\bar h_{jj})/2=-2\Phi$. Conservation gives the harmonic gauge constraints. With spherical symmetry, the measured slow-probe signed inward radial acceleration is $\Phi'(r)=GM_{\mathrm{act}}(r)/r^2$, with $M_{\mathrm{act}}'(r)=4\pi r^2(T_{00}+\sum_jT_{jj})(r)$. These are signed identities, and the source stress inside the core supplies the integration constant.

Diagonalize the mass matrix by an orthogonal change of fields. For a mass $m_i>0$ the exterior static radial equation has the decaying solution $\phi_i(r)=Q_i e^{-m_i r}/r$. Here $Q_i$ is determined by the actual source and the boundary matching, and no sign assumption on it is needed. In the minimally coupled Hilbert stress,
$$
T_{00}=\frac12\sum_i\bigl(|\nabla\phi_i|^2+m_i^2\phi_i^2\bigr),
\qquad
\sum_jT_{jj}=-\frac12\sum_i|\nabla\phi_i|^2-\frac32\sum_i m_i^2\phi_i^2 .
$$
Thus the gradient contributions cancel from the active density, leaving $-\sum_i m_i^2\phi_i^2$. A compact-core subtraction changes only an additive constant in $M_{\mathrm{act}}(r)$ for $r>a$. Multiplication by a positive constant leaves it nonincreasing. For any nonincreasing profile $H$ on the four test radii, $H(1/4)\ge H(2)$, so
$$
2\max_i|H(x_i)-h(x_i)|\ge h(2)-h(1/4)
=\frac{e^{-1/4}+e^{-1/2}-e^{-2}-e^{-4}}2>\frac15 .
$$
For the last bound use $e^{-1/4}\ge3/4$, $e^{-1/2}\ge1/2$, $e^{-2}<1/4$ and $e^{-4}<1/16$. The estimate applies whenever all four registered radii lie outside the source. It rules out the $10^{-4}$ halo tolerance on this minimally coupled metric branch.

For item 2, variation of the curvature coupling adds $(\eta_{\mu\nu}\Delta-\partial_\mu\partial_\nu)(\phi^{\mathsf T}\Xi\phi)$ to the flat static stress. Its contribution to $T_{00}+\sum_jT_{jj}$ is $\Delta(\phi^{\mathsf T}\Xi\phi)$ and it is identically conserved at this order. In a mass eigenbasis the improvement scalar is $\sum_{\nu}B_\nu e^{-\nu r}/r^2$, where $\nu$ ranges over the finitely many pair sums $m_i+m_j$ and $B_\nu=\sum_{m_i+m_j=\nu}\Xi_{ij}Q_iQ_j$. Set $A_\nu=\sum_{2m_i=\nu}m_i^2Q_i^2$, with zero if no such diagonal term occurs. Differentiation gives
$$
r^2\left(T_{00}+\sum_jT_{jj}\right)
=\sum_\nu e^{-\nu r}
 \left[-A_\nu+\left(\nu^2+\frac{2\nu}{r}+\frac2{r^2}\right)B_\nu\right].
\tag{I.12b.2g.2}
$$
For example the factor in parentheses comes from $\Delta(e^{-\nu r}/r^2)$ in three spatial dimensions. Exact equality of an acceleration enhancement with the positive two-scale profile, with any core constant removed, would give equality of its derivative with a sum of two pure exponentials with positive coefficients. Multiply that identity by $r^2$. Polynomials times exponentials with distinct real exponents are linearly independent on an exterior interval: real analyticity extends an identity to the exterior ray, and dividing by the slowest exponential and taking $r\to\infty$ shows its polynomial must vanish before proceeding to the next. The constant term in the polynomial for each exponent in (I.12b.2g.2) forces $B_\nu=0$. The coefficient of $r^2$ then equals $-A_\nu\le0$, in contradiction to either positive target coefficient. All equations used here are derived from the specified action and metric readout. In particular the positive scalar output port of Definition I.12b.1a does not change the stress entering (I.12b.2g.1). ∎

<a id="theorem-i12b2h"></a>

<a id="theorem-i12b2h-stationary-active-stress-from-rotating-scalar-pairs"></a>**Theorem I.12b.2h (Stationary Active Stress from Rotating Scalar Pairs).** Use the static weak-field metric readout (I.12b.2g.1). A pair of canonical real scalar fields of common mass $m>0$, with an internal rotation at frequency $\omega>0$ and with spatial profile $f(r)$, has stationary exterior stress. If $k^2=m^2-\omega^2>0$ and $f(r)=Qe^{-kr}/r$ outside its compact driver, its active density there is
$$
\rho_{\rm act}(r)=(\omega^2-k^2)Q^2\,e^{-2kr}/r^2 .
\tag{I.12b.2h.1}
$$
For $\omega>k$ it is positive, and the active mass outside radius $a$ is $(\omega^2-k^2)/\omega$ times the exterior internal-rotation charge in the normalization below. Two such driven pairs with $k_1=\kappa$, $k_2=2\kappa$, the same positive ratio $(\omega_j^2-k_j^2)/\omega_j$, and equal exterior charges have equal exterior active masses. On this source the normalized exterior mass, measured from the actual radial acceleration, equals $h(2\kappa(r-a))$ for $r\ge a$. In particular, if $4\kappa a<10^{-4}$, its four exterior responses at the unshifted test radii of Theorem I.12b.2f satisfy that theorem's tolerance. The rotating-driver branch and its maintained charge balance are supplied source data.

*Proof.* Fix a smooth bounded radial $f$ equal to a constant on a neighborhood of zero and to $Qe^{-kr}/r$ outside a ball of radius $a$, with smooth matching. Write the pair as $\boldsymbol\phi=f(r)(\cos(\omega t),\sin(\omega t))$. Put $\boldsymbol J=j(r)(\cos(\omega t),\sin(\omega t))$, where $j=(k^2-\Delta)f$. It is smooth and supported in the ball. The field solves the canonical driven equation $(m^2-\Box)\boldsymbol\phi=\boldsymbol J$. It is a stationary stress configuration with prescribed rotating drive and initial data. Let $T^\phi$ be the sum of the free canonical Hilbert stresses of the two fields. Its divergence is $-\boldsymbol J\cdot\partial_\nu\boldsymbol\phi$, with zero time component and radial spatial component $-jf'$. An explicit static core support stress has spatial part $p(r)\delta_{ij}$ where $p(r)=-\int_r^\infty j(s)f'(s)\,ds$, zero energy flux and a smooth compactly supported stationary energy density. Its divergence is $jf'\,\widehat r_j$ and has zero time component. Thus the total stress entering the linearized Einstein equation is conserved. All core and driver support stresses are included in the measured acceleration before subtracting the compact contribution. This supplies a prescribed conserved stress source in the weak-field calculation. Dynamical constitutive equations of a medium that produces the driver are additional data.

For any real scalar pair the exact canonical identity is $T^\phi_{00}+\sum_iT^\phi_{ii}=2|\partial_t\boldsymbol\phi|^2-m^2|\boldsymbol\phi|^2$. This gives (I.12b.2h.1), and all quadratic stress components are time independent by orthogonality of the rotating real amplitudes. The internal rotation has charge density $\phi_1\partial_t\phi_2-\phi_2\partial_t\phi_1=\omega f^2$. Its source divergence vanishes on this preparation because the driver is parallel to $\boldsymbol\phi$. The exterior integral is $2\pi\omega Q^2 e^{-2ka}/k$. Integrating (I.12b.2h.1) gives the stated ratio of total exterior active mass to this charge. A positive common ratio $E_*$ can be implemented at any prescribed $k$ by using $\omega=(E_*+\sqrt{E_*^2+4k^2})/2$ and $m^2=k^2+\omega^2$. This is a family of explicitly specified driver and mass coefficients. Scale both profiles to give the same specified exterior charge. This fixes their amplitudes using their charge integrals.

Denote the total exterior active mass by $M_{\rm ext}>0$. The metric readout
$$
\frac{r^2\Phi'(r)-a^2\Phi'(a)}{G M_{\rm ext}}
=1-\tfrac12\left(e^{-2\kappa(r-a)}+e^{-4\kappa(r-a)}\right)
=h(2\kappa(r-a))
\tag{I.12b.2h.2}
$$
follows from (I.12b.2g.1) and the two exact exterior masses. It uses the same stress as the field equations and the actual support readout at $a$. For $x\ge2\kappa a$, $0\le h'(x)\le3/2$, so the error in replacing $h(x-2\kappa a)$ by $h(x)$ is at most $3\kappa a$. Under the stated bound every registered radius lies beyond $a$ and the error is less than $10^{-4}$. The four numbers lie in $[0,1]$ because they are normalized positive exterior masses. On the registered binary task a fresh independent Bernoulli readout at each radius can use this calibrated probability, with a finite dyadic readout error smaller than the unused tolerance. For example, choose units with $\kappa=1$, take $a=10^{-5}$ and $E_*=1$, and give both pairs the same positive exterior charge. Round each probability to a multiple of $2^{-20}$ and compare it with a fresh uniform twenty-bit integer. The combined probability error is bounded by $3\cdot10^{-5}+2^{-20}<10^{-4}$. Theorem I.12b.2f then gives the cost comparison on that readout and its specified code. The acceleration calculation is at linear order in $G T$, which can be made arbitrarily small on the fixed core and probe region by an overall amplitude reduction. The theorem uses the declared metric approximation and the driver, mass, relative-charge and radial normalization inputs. ∎

<a id="theorem-i12b2i"></a>

<a id="theorem-i12b2i-two-active-screening-scales-from-a-single-triangle-port"></a>**Theorem I.12b.2i (Two Active Screening Scales from a Single Triangle Port).** Use the prescribed conserved-source weak-field branch of Theorems I.12b.2g–I.12b.2h. Give three canonical real scalar pairs the same rotating carrier clock $\omega$ and one common positive stiffness scale $\kappa^2$. Their screened spatial form consists of one onsite unit and one spring of the same strength on each edge of an unweighted triangle. Drive one marked vertex with one common scalar boundary amplitude at radius $a$. The resulting source fixes its response-active spectral shares, exterior charges and screening scales. Its conserved stress and metric acceleration give the strict Equation-I.4 preference of Theorem I.12b.2f on the same four-radius binary task, code and error budget, for the independently declared clock and radius range
$$
\omega\ge128\kappa,\qquad 0<\kappa a\le10^{-5}.
\tag{I.12b.2i.1}
$$
There is no fitted relative driver amplitude.

*Proof.* Take the invariant Euclidean real pair norm and the local source quadratic form
$$
\frac12\sum_{j=1}^3(\omega^2+\kappa^2)|\boldsymbol\phi_j|^2
+\frac{\kappa^2}{2}\sum_{\{j,\ell\}\in E(K_3)}
                   |\boldsymbol\phi_j-\boldsymbol\phi_\ell|^2 .
\tag{I.12b.2i.2}
$$
The external clock has frequency $\omega$ in units with the scalar propagation speed one. One way to specify the clock and onsite spring independently is a common unit inertia with positive carrier and screening stiffnesses $\omega^2$ and $\kappa^2$, respectively, while each pairwise spring uses the same screening stiffness. The couplings in (I.12b.2i.2) fix the masses; the retarded inverse range of a driven component is not its rest mass. This is a frozen local architecture with a single common frequency, one graph and one marked vertex. It uses no halo-response data, fitted spectral amplitude or Equation-I.4 parameter.

On a globally hyperbolic background, the scalar kinetic term is the canonical covariant one of Definition I.12b.1a on each real component. Together with (I.12b.2i.2) it gives the actual retarded Green family of the three-field mass matrix. For a small source at vertex one and the conjugate local linear readout, this family is
$$
\frac13(\omega^2+\kappa^2-\Box_g)_{\rm ret}^{-1}
+\frac23(\omega^2+4\kappa^2-\Box_g)_{\rm ret}^{-1}
\tag{I.12b.2i.8}
$$
on each real component, with the common overall port unit removed. The orthogonal mode decomposition proves this equality and shows why the unused high-eigenspace direction remains a field but is invisible to this port. This covariant scalar-port response and the gravitational response below are different outputs of the same canonical fields.

On the common rotating preparation put $\boldsymbol\phi_j=f_j(r)(\cos\omega t,\sin\omega t)$. Write $P_0=\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}/3$ for the constant projection, $P_1=I-P_0$, and $e_1=(1,0,0)^{\mathsf T}$. The screened exterior mass matrix is
$$
\kappa^2(I+L_{K_3})=\kappa^2P_0+4\kappa^2P_1 .
\tag{I.12b.2i.3}
$$
At $r=a$ supply the one-coordinate boundary drive $f(a)=A e_1$, $A>0$, in the original vertex coordinates. The common amplitude and the radius are the single spatial driver data. The unique radial decaying solution is
$$
f(r)=\frac{Aa}{r}\left[e^{-\kappa(r-a)}P_0e_1+
                     e^{-2\kappa(r-a)}P_1e_1\right],\qquad r\ge a .
\tag{I.12b.2i.4}
$$
Indeed after projecting to either eigenspace, $r f$ solves the scalar second-order constant-coefficient equation. Decay excludes the growing solution and the boundary value fixes the other coefficient. Its two nonzero selected spectral amplitudes have squared shares $1/3$ and $2/3$. The orthogonal direction in the two-dimensional $P_1$ eigenspace has zero driver overlap. These are determined by the vertex port, including its phase and scale, before the probe or score is constructed.

For a smooth source, choose a radial cutoff $\chi(r)$ equal to zero for $r\le a/2$ and one for $r\ge3a/4$. Multiply (I.12b.2i.4), extended algebraically to $r>0$, by $\chi(r)$ and set the profile to zero near the origin. The resulting smooth profile has the same exterior data. Its canonical compact driver is
$$
j=\bigl(\kappa^2(I+L_{K_3})-\Delta\bigr)f
$$
times the common rotating vector. The source supplies this actual vector profile in the collar. Its fixed channel transfers are the two displayed spectral projections applied to the marked boundary port, and there is one adjustable amplitude $A$ for the entire drive. The exterior boundary condition at the marked vertex alone specifies the exterior response. The particular smooth continuation is one realization with an explicit spatial support ledger, rather than a requirement that the volume force vanish on the other vertices. The flat-space canonical Hilbert stress has divergence $-\sum_j\boldsymbol J_j\cdot\partial_\nu\boldsymbol\phi_j$. The time component vanishes since the drive and field in each component have the same rotational phase. The spatial component is $-\langle j,f'\rangle\widehat r$. As in Theorem I.12b.2h, add the actual compact support stress $p(r)\delta_{ij}$ with $p(r)=-\int_r^\infty\langle j(s),f'(s)\rangle\,ds$, and a fixed smooth compact support energy density with zero flux. Its divergence is $+\langle j,f'\rangle\widehat r$. This makes the total stationary source conserved for the linearized Einstein response. The displayed collar and clock specify the drive on this source.

Orthogonal mode rotation diagonalizes the full canonical stress. For the two response-active modes write $w_0=1/3$, $w_1=2/3$, $k_0=\kappa$, $k_1=2\kappa$. Let $C_i$ be the actual exterior charge of the simultaneous internal rotation, restricted to the indicated orthogonal sector. Applying the identities in Theorem I.12b.2h to the orthogonal components gives
$$
C_i=2\pi\omega A^2a^2\frac{w_i}{k_i},
\qquad
M_i=2\pi A^2a^2\frac{(\omega^2-k_i^2)w_i}{k_i}.
\tag{I.12b.2i.5}
$$
Both charges are positive and equal, since $w_0/k_0=w_1/k_1$. These are the actual integrated Noether charges on the exterior, not weights chosen in the observation map. In the diagonal mode basis each component of the drive is parallel to its rotating field, so the local divergence of the internal current vanishes on the specified preparation. The compact support energy and pressure remain in the total metric source. Subtract the measured core acceleration contribution at radius $a$ as in (I.12b.2h.2). With the measured total exterior mass as normalization, the exact linearized acceleration observable is
$$
H(r)=\frac{r^2\Phi'(r)-a^2\Phi'(a)}{G(M_0+M_1)}
=1-p\,e^{-2\kappa(r-a)}-(1-p)e^{-4\kappa(r-a)},
\quad
p=\frac{\omega^2-\kappa^2}{2\omega^2-5\kappa^2}.
\tag{I.12b.2i.6}
$$
This is the field-to-stress and metric-to-observation map for the same source and includes the core subtraction. Its active mass share satisfies
$$
0<p-\frac12
=\frac{3\kappa^2}{2(2\omega^2-5\kappa^2)}
\le\frac{3}{65526}<\frac1{20000}.
\tag{I.12b.2i.7}
$$
For $x=2\kappa r$ and $r\ge a$, replacing $p$ by $1/2$ changes $H(r)$ by at most $|p-1/2|/4$, since $\sup_{y\ge0}(e^{-y}-e^{-2y})=1/4$. Moving the origin from $r-a$ to $r$ changes the equal-mass law by at most $3\kappa a$ as in Theorem I.12b.2h. Hence the mean error before readout is below $1/80000+3/100000$ at every registered radius. The value lies in $[0,1]$. Round it to a multiple of $2^{-20}$ and produce a bit by comparing an independent uniform twenty-bit word with the resulting integer threshold. At each radius the readout error is at most $2^{-20}$ and the total error is less than $10^{-4}$. This uses the actual calibrated acceleration input. Any separately supplied acceleration calibration error is owned once and must fit within the remaining margin. The small-source weak-field branch is available by taking the common driver amplitude and its support density sufficiently small on the fixed region. Within the declared linearized metric model the formula is exact.

The four-radius sample preparation uses independent bits with the just derived means. Apply Theorem I.12b.2f with its same radius schedule, fixed coding convention and errors. It compares the derived source to the entire three-parameter Equation-I.4 class. If the triangle source has a separately counted finite setup description $C_s$, use the same repeated protocol with $N>(C_s+3)/\gamma$ as in that theorem. No price, clock or mode amplitude is selected from the resulting scores. The three identical onsite modules, three equal spring coefficients, one vertex label, fixed collar, one carrier clock, acceleration and binary readout calibrations give finite source specifications. The proof requires neither an exact half-mass identity nor a numerical equality to a prescribed halo. The common triangle architecture determines both positive screening responses, equal exterior charges, the near-equal mass share and their strict preference under the registered comparison. ∎

<a id="theorem-i12b2j"></a>

<a id="theorem-i12b2j-operational-cascade-selection-of-a-coupled-triangle-source"></a>**Theorem I.12b.2j (Operational Cascade Selection of a Coupled Triangle Source).** Fix a positive integer $m$, put $n=3m$, and use the maintained rotating, prescribed-source weak-field setting of Theorem I.12b.2i. There is a single declared source family consisting of a finite predictive cascade, a type-address task, a rate-controlled common spring, and the same scalar triangle, collar, stress and acceleration ports. The predictive task selects the unique type $m$ before the scalar preparation. The retained local exponent and rate function of Definition I.12b.1 set the actual triangle stiffness through a common source actuator. At the selected type the scalar and metric responses are those of Theorem I.12b.2i with its same four-radius comparison. Changing the type changes the stress response at fixed physical radii. The source has an explicit covariant response action and its source and calibration inputs remain part of the record.

*Proof.* **Predictive capacities and physical covers.** Use a finite material line of length $\ell_0>0$ supplied in fixed ruler units, small enough to lie inside the compact source mount. At depths $j=0,\ldots,n$ divide it into the $3^j$ ternary subintervals with a fixed boundary convention for their endpoints. The scale variable is the relative material length $\ell_j/\ell_0=3^{-j}$. The source addresses label these subintervals. The physical interval coordinate is a material scalar. At every leaf address $w$ supply $\prod_{i=1}^n d_{w_i}$ independent complete binary predictive channels, where the elementary fan-out counts are $d=(1,1,2)$. These counts are the immutable wire and fresh-stock rules: of the three child banks, two have one descendant supplier per incoming unit and the third has two. The total stock has $4^n$ binary channels. A parent interval contains all supplier factors belonging to its descendants. Their clocks, ready and spent factors, and interval placement are independently registered. No sample count is substituted for this physical stock.

Each binary channel generates a fair input bit $B$ and an independent innovation $F$ with $\Pr(F=1)=1/4$. The predictor commits $B$ before the outcome $B\oplus F$ is disclosed. Verification records equality and the next model can be updated to the disclosed bit. The capacity credited to that channel is its actual predictive information $J=\ln2-h_{\rm bin}(1/4)>0$ in nats. Indeed the binary symmetric channel's output entropy is at most $\ln2$, the conditional entropy is exactly $h_{\rm bin}(1/4)$ and the supplied fair input attains the bound. Independent channels have additive capacity: subadditivity bounds joint output entropy by the sum of the single-output maxima, while their product conditional law has the summed conditional entropy. The supplied independent fair inputs attain equality. All operations can be performed by finite reversible Boolean gates on neutral inputs, with fresh record cells and the finite driven control of Construction C.5d. These are the predictive-capacity factors of this source. Their normalized capacity at a depth-$j$ interval of address $w$ is
$$
\mu(w)=\frac{4^{n-j}J\prod_{i=1}^{j}d_{w_i}}{4^nJ}
=\prod_{i=1}^{j}p_{w_i},\qquad
(p_1,p_2,p_3)=\left(\frac14,\frac14,\frac12\right).
\tag{I.12b.2j.1}
$$
This computes the measure on the complete finite scale cover, including all positive-capacity cells. The remaining scalar and gravitational apparatus is separately owned and does not enter the predictive-channel capacity count.

With $\ell_j/\ell_0=3^{-j}$, Theorem I.12b.2a gives the exact partition sum and exponent
$$
Z_q(\ell_j)=\left(2\,4^{-q}+2^{-q}\right)^j,\qquad
\tau(q)=-\frac{\ln(2\,4^{-q}+2^{-q})}{\ln3}.
\tag{I.12b.2j.2}
$$
For a leaf with $k$ heavy symbols, write $x=k/n$. Its measured finite-scale exponent is
$$
\alpha(x)=\frac{\ln4-x\ln2}{\ln3}.
\tag{I.12b.2j.3}
$$
The Legendre formula of Definition I.12b.1 gives $D_{\rm eff}=1$ and
$$
I_{\rm PCE}(\alpha(x))
=\frac{x\ln(3x)+(1-x)\ln(3(1-x)/2)}{\ln3},
\qquad 0\le x\le1 ,
\tag{I.12b.2j.4}
$$
with zero terms defined by continuity. For $0<x<1$ differentiation with respect to $q$ gives the heavy fraction $x=2^q/(2+2^q)$ at the unique minimizer. Substitution gives (I.12b.2j.4), and the two endpoint limits give the remaining cases. The rate is nonnegative by the relative-entropy inequality and vanishes exactly at $x=1/3$. The normalized capacity weights and local exponent are measured on this same material line. The geometric child count of the line is three and its supplier count is four.

**Physical address selector and spring control.** The finite address challenge uses a uniformly random independent word of length $n$, supplied by $n$ fair three-state selectors. Each word visits its actual leaf address through the same finite ternary routing tree. At that leaf the readout uses its stored heavy-symbol count and returns the verified type. Before the challenge the controller has one type selector $k\in\{0,\ldots,n\}$ and commits the prediction that the address has type $k$. A count circuit checks that outcome and retains the result, the actual address and the forecast. The same counter stock, word length, positive clock schedule, ready and retained supplies, and fixed-length type code are reserved for every candidate $k$. The predictor's success law is
$$
P_n(k)=3^{-n}\binom{n}{ k}2^{n-k}.
\tag{I.12b.2j.5}
$$
Its consecutive ratio is $(n-k)/(2(k+1))$. It is greater than one through $k=m-1$ and less than one from $k=m$. Thus $k=m$ uniquely maximizes the success objective at this equal-cost selection cut, even among randomized initial selectors. The source uses this registered objective to choose the initial type setting. The selector commits before any spring actuation. Its equal-cost claim concerns this separately metered selection cut, and downstream work and storage retain their actual branch-dependent values. No minimization of the combined source and actuator invoice is used. In the subsequent scalar word the spring controller reads the physical leaf $w_k$ whose first $k$ symbols are heavy and whose remaining symbols are the first light symbol. It reads its actual binary channel inventory or the typed port count obtained by traversing its fan-out wires. This leaf has $2^k$ complete unit channels, so the readout determines $k$ and the local exponent $\alpha(k/n)$ of the same physical cover. The leaf is fixed by the initial selection, independently of the random challenge outcome.

Supply one positive spring calibration $\kappa_*^2$ and the following independent logarithmic calibration law for the common stiffness $\kappa_k^2$: its base-three logarithmic gain over the zero-rate setting is the selected local rate (I.12b.2j.4). This is an installed constitutive law of the apparatus. Its implementation does not need an exact logarithm gate. The controller reads the actual marked capacity, and a fixed algebraic transducer selects the positive root
$$
\frac{\kappa_k^2}{\kappa_*^2}
=3^{I_{\rm PCE}(\alpha(k/n))}
=\left[\left(\frac{3k}{n}\right)^k
\left(\frac{3(n-k)}{2n}\right)^{n-k}\right]^{1/n}.
\tag{I.12b.2j.6}
$$
Interpret an empty power as one. The bracket is a positive rational. Each of the $n+1$ settings is a unique positive root of a polynomial with rational coefficients. Supply a finite switched array of these calibrated spring modules, with one bank per setting, and a fixed Boolean decoder driven by the actual counted $k$. Their coefficient list, preparation, switching and idle stock are retained at their owners. This is the same finite calibrated-parameter convention as Construction C.5d. The rule applies to every count; no controller coefficient is selected from a scalar or metric outcome. The scale $\kappa_*$, the gain convention, the triangular connectivity and the support stock are declared physical source inputs.

**One covariant response functional.** Let $Q$ be a material scalar register for the local rate, prepared uniformly at the chosen value $I_{\rm PCE}(\alpha(k/n))$. On each of the three canonical scalar pairs $\boldsymbol\phi_i$, the switched spring acts through the common term
$$
-\frac{\kappa_*^2\,3^Q}{2}
\left(\sum_{i=1}^3|\boldsymbol\phi_i|^2+
\sum_{\{i,l\}\in E(K_3)}|\boldsymbol\phi_i-\boldsymbol\phi_l|^2\right)
\tag{I.12b.2j.7}
$$
in the Lorentzian Lagrangian density, in addition to its canonical kinetic term and the carrier mass term $-\omega^2\sum_i|\boldsymbol\phi_i|^2/2$. Thus the retained predictive rate changes an actual non-derivative mass operator. To hold $Q$ constant as part of the covariant source, include a real three-form $B$ with the metric-independent constraint term $\int B\wedge dQ$ and hold the branch value of $Q$ fixed on the preparation boundary. Varying $B$ gives $dQ=0$. Varying $Q$ determines $dB$ by the top-form density obtained from the remaining action. Locally, or on the product laboratory region with free terminal $B$ flux, any smooth source top form has such a primitive. For example integrate its coefficient with respect to the laboratory material clock and use the resulting coefficient of the spatial volume three-form. This defines an explicit auxiliary solution, with its boundary data retained. The constraint term has zero Hilbert stress. It supplies no additional matter response in the metric variation at fixed material source.

The prescribed collar can itself be written as a covariant material action, including its support stress. Introduce three spatial material rod scalars $X^i$ and a material clock $\vartheta$ with their registered laboratory preparation $X^i=x^i$, $\vartheta=t$ in the flat probe region. Put $R=|\mathbf X|$ in material units. For fixed $Q$ write $\kappa=\kappa_*3^{Q/2}$. Take the regular collar profile $f(R;Q)$ of Theorem I.12b.2i with this $\kappa$ and the fixed radius $a$, amplitude $A$, and one marked boundary port. Its canonical driver coefficient is $j(R;Q)=(\kappa^2(I+L_{K_3})-\Delta_{\mathbf X})f$. Here the flat material Laplacian is used to compute a constitutive function of the rods and does not vary with the spacetime metric. Let $e(\vartheta)=(\cos\omega\vartheta,\sin\omega\vartheta)$. Set
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal L_{\rm sup}
={}&-\frac12\big(\rho(R;Q)+P(R;Q)\big)
       \sum_{i=1}^3g^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu X^i\,\partial_\nu X^i
       -V(\mathbf X,Q)
       +\sum_i j_i(R;Q)\,e(\vartheta)\cdot\boldsymbol\phi_i,\\
P(R;Q)
={}&-\int_R^\infty \langle j(s;Q),\partial_s f(s;Q)\rangle\,ds,\qquad
V(\mathbf X,Q)=\langle j(R;Q), f(R;Q)\rangle
                       -\frac{\rho(R;Q)+3P(R;Q)}{2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.12b.2j.8}
$$
Choose a smooth compactly supported nonnegative $\rho$ dominating $|P|$ at every retained setting, using a fixed smooth majorant on the compact collar family. The declared compact mount includes the predictive line, source supplies, controller and their thermal or retained outputs inside radius $a$ during the stationary probe cut. Its stationary stress is a material-source premise with stock and energy calibration independent of the scalar gain. At the retained resolution take the total compact support to have the spherical stress in (I.12b.2j.8), including the mounted apparatus and its balancing support. A spherical mount with enough positive compact reserve is a supplied constitutive source. Its calibrated energy includes the finite electronics and their terminal output energy. It is counted once in $\rho$. These functions can be set before observation by the displayed material profile and the positive source reserve. The source action is the integral of the canonical scalar terms, (I.12b.2j.7) and (I.12b.2j.8) against $\sqrt{-g}$ plus the metric-independent constraint. It is diffeomorphism invariant because all its labels are spacetime scalar fields, and the material functions are fixed functions of those labels. In the notation of Definition I.12b.1, the rate enters $\Psi$ through (I.12b.2j.7), with the retained stock, rods, clock and material condition included in $\chi$. The constraint term is a metric-independent part of the material-source action and contributes zero to the defined stress.

On the displayed flat preparation, $\boldsymbol\phi_i=f_i(R;Q)e(t)$ solves the driven scalar equation. The support Lagrangian evaluates to $-\rho$. Its Hilbert tensor consequently has $T_{00}^{\rm sup}=\rho$, $T_{0j}^{\rm sup}=0$ and $T_{ij}^{\rm sup}=P\delta_{ij}$. This uses $\partial_j X^i=\delta^i_j$, and the metric derivative of the rod kinetic term adds $(\rho+P)\delta_{ij}$ to the spatial stress. The clock Euler equation holds because $e'(\vartheta)\cdot e(\vartheta)=0$. The chosen $B$ solves the $Q$ equation. The support pressure derivative is $\langle j,\partial_R f\rangle$. It cancels the spatial divergence of the free canonical scalar tensor, and both time divergences are zero. The diffeomorphism identity for the total action now gives $E_{X^i}\partial_\nu X^i=0$, where $E_{X^i}$ are the remaining rod Euler expressions. Since the rods have three independent spatial gradients, all $E_{X^i}$ vanish on this preparation. Thus the covariant material completion yields the actual conserved tensor used in the linearized readout. It imposes no nonlinear gravitational completion or dynamical stability of every rod perturbation.

**Metric comparison and causal record.** On the selected type $k=m$, equation (I.12b.2j.6) gives $\kappa=\kappa_*$. Choose $\omega\ge128\sqrt3\,\kappa_*$ and $0<\kappa_*a\le10^{-5}$ before the experiment. The maximum of the Bernoulli relative entropy in (I.12b.2j.4) on $[0,1]$ is $\ln3$ by convexity and the endpoint values. Thus every retained $\kappa$ lies in $[\kappa_*,\sqrt3\,\kappa_*]$ and every active exterior density is positive. The source pressure and density are confined to the core. Its measured contribution at $a$ is subtracted as in Theorem I.12b.2i. On the selected branch the exact exterior Noether charges, active masses and normalized weak-field acceleration are therefore those of (I.12b.2i.5)–(I.12b.2i.7). The same probe radii are fixed at $2\kappa_*r=(1/4,1/2,1,2)$. The existing field and readout error bound is within $10^{-4}$, and Theorem I.12b.2f gives the strict comparison against every Equation-I.4 table with its same task, code and any finite source setup description charged as in that theorem.

The coupling acts on a retained physical response. If $k\ne m$, the rate is positive, hence $\kappa>\kappa_*$. The independent fixed-radius calibration is not rerun. For example, the leading exterior inverse range is now $\kappa$ instead of $\kappa_*$ with positive residue, so even the normalized acceleration law cannot coincide on an open exterior interval. This follows directly from its two positive exponential terms and their different smallest exponent. The covariant stress and observation changes therefore persist beyond the numerical label of a control. Each branch keeps the same core profile rules and the same finite task and response ports. The clock and charged record combine the initial predictive stock and address data, the selected type and spring module, the rotating preparation, the core subtraction and the independent dyadic observation readout. No selected input is inferred from a comparison outcome.

This fills Definition I.12b.1 on the declared finite material cascade and driven weak-field source. The scaling window is the finite set of physical covers in (I.12b.2j.1). The rate formula is exact on its tagged type classes and the convex Legendre envelope on the retained continuous interval. The physical mechanism realizing the coupling is the calibrated finite actuator in (I.12b.2j.6), not a general derivation of the actuator law from diffeomorphism invariance or PCE. For the status record in Definition I.12b.1(6), the finite cover, partition sums, exponent and rate are theorem-level on the declared predictive stock. The form $\Psi$ and the logarithmic stiffness law are declared constitutive inputs, and their resulting field and metric response is derived on that same branch. The support condition is the displayed prepared laboratory experiment with its compact source, stationary mount and retained exterior fields. An early homogeneous cosmological stress statement would require its own support and projection premises. ∎

**I.13 Expected Parameter Ranges**

Order-of-magnitude reasoning based on galaxy scaling laws and the empirical $g_0$ scale suggests the following ranges for the universal parameters:
$$
L_0\sim1\!-\!10\,\mathrm{kpc},\qquad
A_G\sim1\!-\!9,\qquad
m\simeq2\!-\!4.
$$
These ranges will be constrained by the forthcoming rotation-curve fits. Through Section I.9's relation $A_G=f-1$, the range for $A_G$ corresponds to asymptotic enhancements $f$ of 2–10 times. Proposition I.13c.3 confines $A_G$ to the menu $\{1,3,7\}$ on its product-tracking branch, and Theorem I.13c.10 selects $A_G=1$ on the source of Construction I.13c.9.

**Definition I.13a (Backbone-Channel-Recruitment Benchmark Branch).** The backbone-channel-recruitment benchmark branch is the subbranch of the galaxy-scale relaxation kernel (I.4) on which the discrete backbone is used to choose the preregistered test pair
$$
A_G=d_0-1=7,
\qquad
m=K_0=3.
\tag{I.13a.1}
$$
The choice $A_G=d_0-1$ and $m=K_0$ is a backbone-motivated benchmark inside the Section I.13 phenomenological range; on the Definition I.13c.1 spatial-clock bridge branch the steepness $m=K_0=3$ and the scale map $L_0=\mathcal L(g_\Lambda,M_b)$ are derived by Proposition I.13c.2, while $A_G=d_0-1$ is the $k=K_0$ endpoint of the Proposition I.13c.3 multiplicity menu rather than a closed theorem-level value. The pair is a falsifiable benchmark with a declared amplitude choice. A constitutive-kernel record gives the origin of each entry $(L_0,A_G,m)$: a derivation from the backbone and bridge, a stated branch assumption, or a declared empirical input with its uncertainty. An amplitude selected using rotation-curve outcomes is calibrated on those outcomes. The structural obstruction to a theorem-level derivation of $A_G$ is recorded in Remark I.13c, together with the floor-respecting menu that bounds it. The cluster parameters $(K,q,A_{\mathrm{PM}})$ remain outside this benchmark.

**Proposition I.13b (Benchmark Kernel Form).** On the benchmark branch of Definition I.13a, Equation I.4 becomes
$$
G(R)=G_0\left[1+7\left(1-e^{-(R/L_0)^3}\right)\right].
\tag{I.13b.1}
$$
The branch is falsified if a rotation-curve analysis of the stated kernel requiring a single universal $(A_G,m)$ excludes $(7,3)$ within its stated model and uncertainty ledger.

*Proof.* Substitute $A_G=d_0-1=7$ and $m=K_0=3$ from (I.13a.1) into Equation I.4. The final sentence is the direct falsification condition for a benchmark subbranch with a fixed parameter pair. ∎

**Remark I.13c (No Capacity-Floor Derivation of $A_G$).** Equation E.9 has $G\propto\eta\delta^2/(\chi C_{\max})$ only after the remaining substrate parameters are fixed. It does not, by itself, imply $G_{\mathrm{large}}/G_0=d_0$. In particular, setting an effective $C_{\max}$ below the structural floor $\varepsilon_0=\ln2$ is not an admissible theorem-level derivation. The pair $(A_G,m)=(7,3)$ is therefore retained as a benchmark branch rather than a closed dark-sector theorem. Definition I.13c.1 and Propositions I.13c.2--I.13c.3 record the branch-conditional route consistent with this floor: the steepness and the $L_0$ system map are fixed on the spatial-clock bridge branch, while the amplitude is confined to the multiplicative menu $2^j-1$, $1\le j\le K_0$, with no per-direction tracked capacity below $\varepsilon_0$.

<a id="definition-i13c1-spatial-clock-bridge-branch"></a>**Definition I.13c.1 (Spatial-Clock Bridge Branch).** On the acceleration-lock branch, a spatial-clock bridge branch registers: (1) the local sparsity variable
$$
s_{\mathrm{loc}}:=\frac{\beta_\chi}{\chi_b}=\frac{\beta_\chi g_\Lambda}{|\nabla\Phi_b|}
$$
with a single dimensionless rate modulus $\beta_\chi>0$; (2) adoption of the exact power-clock branch of Remark K.9.5i as the static relaxation clock,
$$
\sigma_{\mathrm{loc}}:=s_{\mathrm{loc}}^{3/2};
$$
and (3) the Definition K.9.5b--Theorem K.9.5c response-cost selection for the static coupling, so that the Equation I.4 response is
$$
\varepsilon_G=A_G\left(1-e^{-\sigma_{\mathrm{loc}}}\right),
$$
with the amplitude $A_G$ a separate branch input. The registrations (1)--(3) are branch premises in the sense of Convention P.14.1a; the branch inherits the acceleration-lock status of $g_\Lambda$ and additionally registers $\beta_\chi$ and the amplitude $A_G$. On the source of Construction I.13c.9, Theorem I.13c.10 derives registrations (1)--(3) and the rate $\beta_\chi$ and selects the amplitude.

<a id="proposition-i13c2-derived-steepness-and-the-l_0-system-map"></a>**Proposition I.13c.2 (Derived Steepness and the $L_0$ System Map).** On a Definition I.13c.1 branch with exterior Keplerian baryonic field $|\nabla\Phi_b|=GM_b/R^2$, where $M_b$ is the registered baryonic mass scale of the system,
$$
\sigma_{\mathrm{loc}}=\left(\frac{\beta_\chi g_\Lambda R^2}{GM_b}\right)^{3/2}=\left(\frac{R}{L_0}\right)^{3},
\qquad
L_0=\sqrt{\frac{GM_b}{\beta_\chi g_\Lambda}}.
\tag{I.13c.2.1}
$$
Hence Equation I.4 holds on this branch with derived steepness
$$
m=3=K_0=2n,
$$
twice the registered static clock exponent $n=3/2$, and with $L_0=\mathcal L(g_\Lambda,M_b)$ a dimensionally valid system map of the form required in Section I.6, carrying the mass datum $M_b$ and the exterior-Keplerian geometry datum; its validation certificate remains a separate obligation. The doubling $m=2n$ records that $s_{\mathrm{loc}}$ is quadratic in $R$ through the Keplerian field, while the temporal clock is evaluated at the sparsity variable directly.

*Proof.* Substituting the Keplerian field into the Definition I.13c.1 registration gives $s_{\mathrm{loc}}=\beta_\chi g_\Lambda R^2/(GM_b)$, so
$$
\sigma_{\mathrm{loc}}=s_{\mathrm{loc}}^{3/2}=\left(\frac{\beta_\chi g_\Lambda}{GM_b}\right)^{3/2}R^{3},
$$
which equals $(R/L_0)^3$ if and only if $L_0^3=\left(GM_b/(\beta_\chi g_\Lambda)\right)^{3/2}$, that is $L_0=\sqrt{GM_b/(\beta_\chi g_\Lambda)}$; the quantity $GM_b/g_\Lambda$ has the dimensions of an area, so $L_0$ is a length. Comparing with Equation I.4 identifies the argument $(R/L_0)^m$ with $m=3$, and $3=K_0=2\cdot\tfrac32=2n$ by Proposition K.9.5h. ∎

<a id="proposition-i13c3-floor-respecting-multiplicity-menu-for-the-amplitude"></a>**Proposition I.13c.3 (Floor-Respecting Multiplicity Menu for the Amplitude).** Register the further premise that the sparse static response tracks the inverse product of independently composing per-direction retained distinguishabilities over $j$ participating interface directions, $1\le j\le K_0$, with each direction's tracked capacity running from the dense operating value $C_{\max}^{*}=2\varepsilon_0$ to the de Sitter floor $\varepsilon_0$, both as registered on the Definition K.9.5e capacity-tracking branch. Then the static enhancement is
$$
\frac{G_{\mathrm{large}}}{G_0}=\left(\frac{e^{2\varepsilon_0}}{e^{\varepsilon_0}}\right)^{j}=e^{j\varepsilon_0}=2^{j},
\qquad
A_G=2^{j}-1\in\{1,3,7\},
\tag{I.13c.3.1}
$$
and no direction's tracked capacity falls below $\varepsilon_0$, so the Remark I.13c inadmissibility is never invoked. The endpoint $j=K_0$ gives $A_G=2^{K_0}-1=d_0-1$, the Definition I.13a benchmark amplitude, since $d_0=2^{K_0}=8$; the serialized case $j=1$ reproduces the temporal amplitude $A_c=1$ of Proposition K.9.5f. On the source of Construction I.13c.9, Theorem I.13c.10 selects $j=1$, hence $A_G=1$; a universal-$(A_G,m)$ analysis with the same response model and declared uncertainty budget excluding every member of the menu falsifies the product-tracking branch.

*Proof.* Per direction, the ratio of dense to floor distinguishability is $e^{2\varepsilon_0}/e^{\varepsilon_0}=e^{\varepsilon_0}=2$, and the product over $j$ independent directions is $2^j$; with the inverse-distinguishability tracking of the registered premise, $G_{\mathrm{large}}/G_0=2^j$ and $A_G=2^j-1$, taking the values $1$, $3$, $7$ at $j=1,2,3$. Every direction's minimum tracked capacity is $\varepsilon_0$, which is the structural floor, so no sub-floor value occurs. The identities $2^{K_0}=2^3=8=d_0$ and $2^1-1=1=A_c$ give the endpoint and serialized statements by Definition I.13a and Proposition K.9.5f. The falsification sentence restates the exclusion condition for a finite menu. ∎

For a field scaling $|\nabla\Phi_b|\propto R^{-p}$ and a registered power clock $\sigma_{\mathrm{loc}}=s_{\mathrm{loc}}^{n}$, the same substitution gives $m=pn$. A common $\beta_\chi$ and fixed $g_\Lambda$ therefore predict $L_0\propto\sqrt{M_b}$ in the exterior-Keplerian class. A redshift-invariant transition additionally requires a common, time-independent $\beta_\chi$, the same mass and geometry definitions, and a calibrated observable map. These are tested across the registered galaxy class.

<a id="theorem-i13c4-spherical-classification-of-power-clock-kernels"></a>**Theorem I.13c.4 (Spherical Classification of Power-Clock Kernels).** On a Definition I.13c.1 branch with registered power clock $\sigma_{\mathrm{loc}}=s_{\mathrm{loc}}^{\,n}$, $n>0$ (the registered branch has $n=3/2$), put $a_\chi:=\beta_\chi g_\Lambda$. Let the baryonic mass distribution be spherically symmetric and nonnegative, with enclosed mass $M_b(R)$ and Newtonian field $|\nabla\Phi_b|(R)=GM_b(R)/R^2>0$ on an open interval $I\subset(0,\infty)$. There are constants $L>0$ and $m>0$ with
$$
\sigma_{\mathrm{loc}}(R)=\Bigl(\frac RL\Bigr)^m\qquad(R\in I)
\tag{I.13c.4.1}
$$
exactly when
$$
M_b(R)=\frac{a_\chi L^{m/n}}{G}\,R^{2-m/n}\qquad(R\in I).
\tag{I.13c.4.2}
$$
Every such pair has $m\le2n$. Equality $m=2n$ holds exactly when $I$ carries no baryonic mass, and then $L=\sqrt{GM_b/a_\chi}$ is the Proposition I.13c.2 map. For $m<2n$ the baryonic density on $I$ is
$$
\rho_b(R)=\frac{(2-m/n)\,a_\chi L^{m/n}}{4\pi G}\,R^{-1-m/n}>0.
\tag{I.13c.4.3}
$$
Hence, on the registered branch, the clock has the Equation I.4 form $(R/L_0)^m$ with fixed $(L_0,m)$ on an interval exactly for power-law enclosed-mass profiles $M_b\propto R^{\alpha}$ with $0\le\alpha<2$; its steepness is $m=3$ exactly on baryon-free exterior intervals and $m<3$ on every interval that carries baryons. For $A_G\ne0$ the same classification holds for the response $\varepsilon_G(R)=A_G\bigl(1-e^{-(a_\chi/|\nabla\Phi_b(R)|)^{n}}\bigr)$ and the Equation I.4 form $A_G\bigl(1-e^{-(R/L_0)^m}\bigr)$ with the branch amplitude, so on an interval where $M_b$ is not a power of $R$ that response has no such form. For $A_G=0$ the response vanishes identically.

*Proof.* By Definition I.13c.1, $\sigma_{\mathrm{loc}}=(a_\chi/|\nabla\Phi_b|)^n$. All quantities are positive on $I$, so (I.13c.4.1) is equivalent to $a_\chi/|\nabla\Phi_b|=(R/L)^{m/n}$, that is, to $GM_b(R)/R^2=a_\chi L^{m/n}R^{-m/n}$, which is (I.13c.4.2). The enclosed mass of a nonnegative distribution is nondecreasing in $R$, so the exponent obeys $2-m/n\ge0$. It vanishes exactly when $M_b$ is constant on $I$, that is, when $I$ carries no mass; then (I.13c.4.2) reads $M_b=a_\chi L^2/G$, which is the stated map. For $m<2n$, differentiation of (I.13c.4.2) and $M_b'(R)=4\pi R^2\rho_b(R)$ give (I.13c.4.3). For $A_G\ne0$ the map $x\mapsto A_G(1-e^{-x})$ is injective, so the response has the form $A_G(1-e^{-(R/L_0)^m})$ on $I$ exactly when (I.13c.4.1) holds there; the statement about non-power profiles is the contrapositive. ∎

<a id="theorem-i13c5-static-action-realization-of-the-spatial-clock-kernel"></a>**Theorem I.13c.5 (Static Action Realization of the Spatial-Clock Kernel).** On the branch of Theorem I.13c.4 with amplitude $A_G\ge0$, define for $y>0$
$$
\nu_\chi(y):=1+A_G\bigl(1-e^{-y^{-n}}\bigr),
\qquad
h_\chi(y):=y\,\nu_\chi(y),
\tag{I.13c.5.1}
$$
so that the Definition I.13c.1 response at $y=|\nabla\Phi_b|/a_\chi$ is $1+\varepsilon_G=\nu_\chi(y)$.

1. $h_\chi$ is strictly increasing on $(0,\infty)$ exactly when $A_G\le A_{\mathrm{crit}}(n)$, where $A_{\mathrm{crit}}(n)=\infty$ for $n\le1$ and
$$
A_{\mathrm{crit}}(n)=\frac1{n\,e^{-(n-1)/n}-1}\qquad(n>1).
\tag{I.13c.5.2}
$$
For $n=3/2$, $A_{\mathrm{crit}}=1/(\tfrac32e^{-1/3}-1)=13.3695\ldots$, so the menu $\{1,3,7\}$ of Proposition I.13c.3 lies strictly below it.

2. If $A_G\le A_{\mathrm{crit}}(n)$, let $k_\chi:=h_\chi^{-1}$ on $(0,\infty)$ with $k_\chi(0)=0$, $F(x):=\int_0^xk_\chi(t)\,dt$ and $\mathcal F(\xi):=a_\chi^2F(|\xi|/a_\chi)$ on $\mathbb R^3$. Then $\mathcal F$ is $C^1$, strictly convex and coercive, with
$$
\frac{|\xi|^2}{2(1+A_G)}\le\mathcal F(\xi)\le\frac{|\xi|^2}2;
\tag{I.13c.5.3}
$$
its response $\mu(x):=F'(x)/x$ satisfies $\mu(h_\chi(y))=1/\nu_\chi(y)$, $\mu(x)\to1$ as $x\to\infty$ and $\mu(x)\to1/(1+A_G)$ as $x\downarrow0$; and the static energy
$$
\mathcal E[\Phi]=\frac1{4\pi G}\int\mathcal F(\nabla\Phi)\,d^3x+\int\rho_b\Phi\,d^3x
\tag{I.13c.5.4}
$$
has the Euler-Lagrange equation $\nabla\cdot[\mu(|\nabla\Phi|/a_\chi)\nabla\Phi]=4\pi G\rho_b$; its integrand satisfies the hypotheses that Theorem I.6 imposes on $F$ with $p=2$, so on every bounded Lipschitz domain that theorem gives a unique weak solution for every source in $W^{-1,2}$ and every Dirichlet datum with a $W^{1,2}$ lifting.

3. Under the hypothesis of item 2, for every spherically symmetric baryonic distribution the radial field with $|\nabla\Phi|=a_\chi h_\chi(g_N/a_\chi)$, $g_N=GM_b(R)/R^2$ and $h_\chi(0):=0$, satisfies $\mu(|\nabla\Phi|/a_\chi)\nabla\Phi=\nabla\Phi_b$, hence the Euler-Lagrange equation with the outward-flux normalization, and
$$
|\nabla\Phi|=\nu_\chi\Bigl(\frac{g_N}{a_\chi}\Bigr)g_N.
\tag{I.13c.5.5}
$$
In an exterior region this is Equation I.4 with $G_0=G$, $m=2n$ and $L_0=\sqrt{GM_b/a_\chi}$, for every baryonic mass with the same $(a_\chi,A_G,n)$. For an infinite sheet of surface density $\Sigma_b$, the planar solution with even potential and odd field has $|\nabla\Phi|=\nu_\chi(2\pi G\Sigma_b/a_\chi)\,2\pi G\Sigma_b$, and $\sigma_{\mathrm{loc}}=1$ exactly at
$$
\Sigma_b=\Sigma_\times:=\frac{a_\chi}{2\pi G},
\qquad\text{so that}\qquad
M_b=2\pi\Sigma_\times L_0(M_b)^2\quad\text{for every }M_b>0.
\tag{I.13c.5.6}
$$

4. Under the hypothesis of item 2, for every $C^2$ solution whose flux $\mu(|\nabla\Phi|/a_\chi)\nabla\Phi$ is $C^1$, the field stress
$$
T^{\Phi}_{ij}=\frac1{4\pi G}\Bigl[\mu\Bigl(\frac{|\nabla\Phi|}{a_\chi}\Bigr)\partial_i\Phi\,\partial_j\Phi-\delta_{ij}\mathcal F(\nabla\Phi)\Bigr]
\tag{I.13c.5.7}
$$
obeys $\partial_jT^{\Phi}_{ij}=\rho_b\,\partial_i\Phi$. For compactly supported $\rho_b$, the total self-force $\int\rho_b\nabla\Phi\,d^3x$ vanishes whenever $\oint_{|x|=r}|T^{\Phi}|\,dS\to0$ along a sequence $r\to\infty$.

5. If $A_G>A_{\mathrm{crit}}(n)$, no $C^1$ radial potential $a_\chi^2F(|\xi|/a_\chi)$ has flux-normalized spherical solutions obeying (I.13c.5.5) for all spherical sources.

6. If $A_G>0$, no response map that is positively homogeneous of degree one in the baryonic source, in particular no linear response kernel and no action of Theorem I.13h whose source coordinate is $\rho_b$, reproduces the exterior law of item 3 for a spherical source and its rescaling by any factor $\lambda\ne1$ at any exterior radius.

For $A_G>0$ the weak-field projection of the branch is therefore intrinsically nonlinear in the source; the susceptibility of Definition I.3b and the finite quadratic test of Theorem I.13h apply to it as linearizations about a fixed background.

*Proof.* Item 1. Put $u=y^{-n}$. Differentiation gives
$$
h_\chi'(y)=1+A_G\bigl[1-\varphi_n(u)\bigr],
\qquad
\varphi_n(u)=e^{-u}(1+nu),
\qquad
\varphi_n'(u)=e^{-u}(n-1-nu).
$$
