If those entries and acceptance conditions are independently supplied, their union with $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{CS}}$ is an accepted $\mathfrak X_{\mathrm{DS}}$, so Theorem I.13e applies. If any required entry is absent, the antecedent of Theorem I.13e is false and the theorem cannot be invoked. ∎

<a id="theorem-i13h-finite-common-quadratic-action-realizability-and-no-retuning-test"></a>**Theorem I.13h (Finite Common Quadratic-Action Realizability and No-Retuning Test).** Let $Y$ be a finite real source space, let $X$ be a finite real field space, let $K:X\to X$ be symmetric positive definite, and let $B:X\to Y$. For the common static action
$$
\Gamma(x;y)=\frac12\langle x,Kx\rangle-\langle Bx,y\rangle,
\tag{I.13h.1}
$$
the unique stationary field and conjugate output are
$$
x_y=K^{-1}B^*y,
\qquad
o_y=Bx_y=Ry,
\qquad
R:=BK^{-1}B^*\succeq0.
\tag{I.13h.2}
$$
Conversely, every symmetric positive-semidefinite response $R:Y\to Y$ has such a realization, for example $X=Y$, $K=I$, and $B=R^{1/2}$. Hence, when the finite galaxy, cluster, lensing, homogeneous and thin-sheet/source responses are registered in common conjugate source/output coordinates with the same inner product, they are generated without retuning by one convex quadratic action of (I.13h.1) exactly when the assembled static response matrix is symmetric positive semidefinite. Independently projected or differently normalized observational outputs require their specified projection maps and are not covered by this matrix criterion alone. Its blocks necessarily obey reciprocity and
$$
|\langle u,Rv\rangle|^2
\le
\langle u,Ru\rangle\langle v,Rv\rangle.
\tag{I.13h.3}
$$
For a source covariance $\Sigma_y$, the same action predicts $\operatorname{Cov}(o)=R\Sigma_yR$ with no new parameter. This is a complete finite static quadratic test; retarded causality, spacetime covariance, stress conservation, and the physical projection maps remain separate entries of Definition I.13d.

*Proof.* Strict convexity gives the unique stationary equation $Kx=B^*y$, and substitution gives (I.13h.2). The response is symmetric positive semidefinite because $\langle y,Ry\rangle=\|K^{-1/2}B^*y\|^2$. The square-root construction proves the converse. Applying Cauchy--Schwarz to $K^{-1/2}B^*u$ and $K^{-1/2}B^*v$ proves (I.13h.3). The covariance identity follows from linearity. ∎

<a id="theorem-i13i-exact-finite-harmonic-recoverability-census"></a>**Theorem I.13i (Exact Finite Harmonic-Recoverability Census).** Let
$$
C^0\xrightarrow{d_0}C^1\xrightarrow{d_1}C^2,
\qquad d_1d_0=0,
\tag{I.13i.1}
$$
be a finite cochain complex over $\mathbb Q$ with rational positive-definite inner-product matrices, and let $\delta_0$ be the adjoint of $d_0$. Then
$$
\mathcal H^1=\ker d_1\cap\ker\delta_0,
\qquad
\dim\mathcal H^1=\dim C^1-\operatorname{rank}d_0-\operatorname{rank}d_1,
\tag{I.13i.2}
$$
and an exact rational basis and Hodge projector are obtained by Gaussian elimination. A current is simultaneously closed and coclosed exactly when it equals its harmonic projection.

If a rational self-adjoint operator $\Lambda_h$ is supplied on $\mathcal H^1$, the compressed static kernel $\Lambda_h^{-1}$ exists and is positive exactly when every leading principal minor of the quadratic-form matrix $[\langle e_i,\Lambda_he_j\rangle]$ in any declared rational basis is positive. These rank and minor tests terminate. For a complete terminating algebraic test, additionally supply the current, harmonic-to-null-response map, nine normalized null-response values, normalized trace datum and normalization constants as exact rational data in the registered bases, or supply terminating exact arithmetic and equality/order comparison for their declared number representation. Under that effective-data contract, elimination also checks harmonic stationarity and the nine-vector quotient tomography with its trace datum, deciding the finite algebraic subcertificate. The real-data identities remain valid without a claim of a uniform decision procedure. They do not create the covariant, causal, or physical projection entries of Definition I.13d.

*Proof.* Finite Hodge decomposition gives $C^1=\operatorname{im}d_0\oplus\mathcal H^1\oplus\operatorname{im}\delta_1$ orthogonally. Rank-nullity and $\operatorname{im}d_0\subseteq\ker d_1$ give (I.13i.2). All matrices are rational, so exact elimination constructs the kernels, their intersection, and the orthogonal projector. The stationary equations are precisely $d_1J=0=\delta_0J$. Sylvester's criterion gives the final positive-definiteness equivalence and is a finite rational computation. ∎

<a id="theorem-i13j-linear-covariant-conserved-response-classification"></a>**Theorem I.13j (Linear Covariant Conserved-Response Classification).** On Minkowski space with signature $(-,+,+,+)$, let $h_{\mu\nu}$ be a symmetric perturbation, $h=\eta^{\mu\nu}h_{\mu\nu}$ and $\Box=\eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\partial_\nu$, and let $\mathfrak L$ be the class of Lorentz-invariant, parity-even quadratic actions
$$
S[h;T]=-\int\Bigl[\tfrac12h_{\mu\nu}a(\Box)\Box h^{\mu\nu}+h_\mu{}^{\sigma}b(\Box)\partial_\sigma\partial_\nu h^{\mu\nu}+h\,c(\Box)\partial_\mu\partial_\nu h^{\mu\nu}+\tfrac12h\,d(\Box)\Box h+h^{\lambda\sigma}\frac{f(\Box)}{\Box}\partial_\sigma\partial_\lambda\partial_\mu\partial_\nu h^{\mu\nu}\Bigr]d^4x+\frac\kappa2\int h_{\mu\nu}T^{\mu\nu}\,d^4x
\tag{I.13j.1}
$$
with real form factors $a,b,c,d,f$ and a fixed coupling $\kappa\ne0$. The classification is carried out on Fourier symbols: under $\partial_\mu\mapsto ik_\mu$ and $\Box\mapsto-k^2$, $k^2=k_\mu k^\mu$, the form factors are real functions of $\Box$, each member is identified with the symbol of (I.13j.1) at the wave vectors with $k^2\ne0$, where $f(\Box)/\Box$ is defined, and every statement below is an identity between such symbols.

1. The gravitational part of the action is invariant under $h_{\mu\nu}\mapsto h_{\mu\nu}+\partial_\mu\xi_\nu+\partial_\nu\xi_\mu$ for every $\xi$, equivalently the symbol of its field-equation tensor is transverse, exactly when
$$
b=-a,\qquad d=-c,\qquad f=\tfrac12(a-c)
\tag{I.13j.2}
$$
at every nonzero value of $\Box$. The source term is invariant under the same maps exactly when $\partial_\mu T^{\mu\nu}=0$. On the subclass (I.13j.2) the gravitational side of the field equation is identically divergence-free, so the divergence of the field equation imposes on the source exactly the conservation law $\partial_\mu T^{\mu\nu}=0$. Solvability for a given conserved source is a further nondegeneracy condition on the form factors: the member $a=c=0$ satisfies (I.13j.2) and solves no nonzero source. Item 2 gives the nondegenerate static case. Linearized general relativity is the member $a=c=1$.

2. On this gauge-invariant subclass, let $T^{\mu\nu}$ be a static conserved dust source with $T^{00}=\rho(\mathbf x)$, and fix a wave vector $\mathbf k\ne0$ at which $a\ne0$ and $a\ne3c$, both evaluated at $\Box=-|\mathbf k|^2$. The static field mode at $\mathbf k$ is unique up to gauge, and the gauge-invariant potentials of $ds^2=-(1+2\Phi)dt^2+(1-2\Psi)d\mathbf x^2$ are
$$
\Phi=\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}\Phi_{\mathrm{GR}},
\qquad
\Psi=\nu_{\mathrm{sl}}\Phi_{\mathrm{GR}},
\qquad
\frac{\Phi+\Psi}2=\Sigma_{\mathrm{lens}}\Phi_{\mathrm{GR}},
$$
$$
\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}=\frac{2(a-2c)}{a(a-3c)},
\qquad
\nu_{\mathrm{sl}}=\frac{-2c}{a(a-3c)},
\qquad
\Sigma_{\mathrm{lens}}=\frac1a,
\tag{I.13j.3}
$$
where $\Phi_{\mathrm{GR}}$ is the potential of the same source and coupling at $a=c=1$. Nonrelativistic dynamics responds to $\Phi$ and light deflection to $\Phi+\Psi$.

3. The map $(a,c)\mapsto(\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}},\Sigma_{\mathrm{lens}})$ is a bijection from $\{a\ne0,\ a\ne3c\}$ onto $\{\Sigma\ne0,\ \mu\ne\tfrac43\Sigma\}$, with inverse
$$
a=\frac1\Sigma,
\qquad
c=\frac{2\Sigma-\mu}{\Sigma(4\Sigma-3\mu)}.
\tag{I.13j.4}
$$
Hence every pair of real functions $\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}(|\mathbf k|)$ and $\Sigma_{\mathrm{lens}}(|\mathbf k|)$ on $|\mathbf k|>0$ with $\Sigma_{\mathrm{lens}}\ne0$ and $\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}\ne\tfrac43\Sigma_{\mathrm{lens}}$ pointwise is the pair of static response symbols of the form factors $a,c$ that (I.13j.4) fixes on $\Box<0$, with $b,d,f$ given by (I.13j.2); every extension of $a,c$ to $\Box>0$, with $b,d,f$ again given by (I.13j.2), is a gauge-invariant member of $\mathfrak L$ with these static projections. The galaxy projection therefore does not determine the lensing projection on $\mathfrak L$, and the no-slip condition $\Psi=\Phi$, which is the negligible-anisotropic-stress premise of Theorem I.5 on $\mathfrak L$, holds at a wave vector exactly when $a=c$ there, equivalently when $\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}=\Sigma_{\mathrm{lens}}$.

4. At every static wave vector with $a\ne0$ and $a\ne3c$, the static response of item 2 is linear in $\rho$. Hence, for $A_G>0$, no gauge-invariant member with $a\ne0$ and $a\ne3c$ on all of $\Box<0$ reproduces the Proposition I.13c.2 exterior law with its mass-dependent $L_0$, by Theorem I.13c.5, item 6. The translation-invariant linear kernel whose point-mass response is Equation I.4 with a fixed $L_0$ has a real continuous ratio $\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}$ and is realized through item 3 with any lensing function obeying the conditions there.

*Proof.* Work with symbols at $k^2\ne0$, and let $E^{\mu\nu}$ be the symbol of the gravitational part of $\delta S/\delta h_{\mu\nu}$, so that the field equation is $E^{\mu\nu}+\tfrac\kappa2T^{\mu\nu}=0$. Since $E^{\mu\nu}$ is symmetric, $\delta_\xi S=2\int E^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\xi_\nu\,d^4x=-2\int\xi_\nu\partial_\mu E^{\mu\nu}\,d^4x$ for the gravitational part, so invariance for all $\xi$ is equivalent to $k_\mu E^{\mu\nu}=0$ identically in $h$ at every such $k$. Contracting the five terms of (I.13j.1) gives, up to a nonzero common factor,
$$
k_\mu E^{\mu\nu}\propto(a+b)\,k^2k_\mu h^{\mu\nu}+(b+c+2f)\,k^\nu k_\alpha k_\beta h^{\alpha\beta}+(c+d)\,k^2k^\nu h.
$$
For $k^2\ne0$ choose $\epsilon\perp k$ with $\epsilon^2\ne0$. The perturbations $\epsilon_\mu\epsilon_\nu$, $k_\mu\epsilon_\nu+\epsilon_\mu k_\nu$ and $k_\mu k_\nu$ isolate $c+d$, $a+b$ and then $b+c+2f$, so invariance is (I.13j.2) at the value $\Box=-k^2$, and every nonzero real value arises. The source term changes by $\kappa\int\partial_\mu\xi_\nu T^{\mu\nu}\,d^4x=-\kappa\int\xi_\nu\partial_\mu T^{\mu\nu}\,d^4x$, which vanishes for every $\xi$ exactly when $T$ is conserved. On (I.13j.2) the identity $k_\mu E^{\mu\nu}=0$ reduces the divergence of the field equation to $\tfrac\kappa2ik_\mu T^{\mu\nu}=0$. At $a=c=0$, (I.13j.2) makes every form factor vanish, so $E^{\mu\nu}=0$ and the field equation reads $\tfrac\kappa2T^{\mu\nu}=0$. At $a=c=1$, (I.13j.2) gives $b=d=-1$ and $f=0$, which is the Fierz--Pauli operator of linearized general relativity.

For item 2, rotate so that $\mathbf k=K\mathbf e_3$ with $K>0$; then $k^0=0$ and $k^2=K^2$. A gauge transformation shifts $h_{\mu3}$ by $iK\xi_\mu$ for $\mu\ne3$ and $h_{33}$ by $2iK\xi_3$ and leaves $h_{AB}$ with $A,B\in\{0,1,2\}$ unchanged, so a gauge with $h_{\mu3}=0$ exists and $\Phi=-h_{00}/2$ and $\Psi=-h_{11}/2$ are the gauge-invariant Newtonian-gauge potentials. Transversality gives $KE^{3\nu}=0$ identically and conservation gives $T^{3\nu}=0$, so only the components with indices in $\{0,1,2\}$ carry equations. In this gauge, (I.13j.1) with (I.13j.2) reduces to
$$
\frac{K^2}2\Bigl[a\,h_{AB}h^{AB}-c\,\bigl(h^C{}_C\bigr)^2\Bigr]+\frac\kappa2h_{AB}T^{AB},
$$
with field equations $K^2\bigl(a\,h^{AB}-c\,\eta^{AB}h^C{}_C\bigr)+\tfrac\kappa2T^{AB}=0$. For $T^{00}=\rho$ and $a\ne0$ they give $h_{AB}=0$ for $A\ne B$, $h_{22}=h_{11}$, and
$$
c\,\Phi=(2c-a)\Psi,
\qquad
2(c-a)\Phi-4c\Psi=-\frac{\kappa\rho}{2K^2},
$$
a linear system with determinant $2a(a-3c)\ne0$. Its unique solution is
$$
\Phi=\frac{\kappa\rho\,(a-2c)}{4K^2a(a-3c)},
\qquad
\Psi=-\frac{\kappa\rho\,c}{4K^2a(a-3c)},
$$
which at $a=c=1$ gives $\Phi_{\mathrm{GR}}=\Psi_{\mathrm{GR}}=\kappa\rho/(8K^2)$. Division gives (I.13j.3). In the metric of item 2, slow test bodies accelerate by $-\nabla\Phi$, and the transverse deflection of null geodesics is governed by $\Phi+\Psi$.

For item 3, $\Sigma_{\mathrm{lens}}=1/a\ne0$, and $\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}/\Sigma_{\mathrm{lens}}=2(a-2c)/(a-3c)$ equals $4/3$ only if $a=0$. Conversely, given $\Sigma\ne0$ and $\mu\ne\tfrac43\Sigma$, put $a=1/\Sigma$ and solve $\mu a(a-3c)=2(a-2c)$, which is linear in $c$ with coefficient $4-3\mu a\ne0$; this gives (I.13j.4), and then $a-3c=-2a/(4-3\mu a)\ne0$. The two maps are mutually inverse. At $a=c$, $\nu_{\mathrm{sl}}=\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}=\Sigma_{\mathrm{lens}}$; conversely $\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}=\Sigma_{\mathrm{lens}}$ reads $2(a-2c)=a-3c$, that is, $a=c$. Static projections evaluate the form factors only on $\Box=-|\mathbf k|^2<0$, which proves the extension statement.

For item 4, the static equations of item 2 are linear in $\rho$, so the static response is homogeneous of degree one in the source and Theorem I.13c.5, item 6, applies when $A_G>0$. The point-mass potential of Equation I.4 with fixed $L_0$ differs from $-G_0M(1+A_G)/r$ by $G_0MA_G\int_r^\infty e^{-(s/L_0)^m}s^{-2}\,ds$, which is at most $G_0MA_G/r$ near $r=0$ and decays faster than any power; this difference is integrable on $\mathbb R^3$, so its Fourier transform is real, radial and continuous, and the ratio of the potential to the Newtonian potential of $G_0$ is a real continuous function of $|\mathbf k|$. ∎

<a id="theorem-i13k-operator-level-realization-and-retarded-solvability-for-polynomial-form-factors"></a>**Theorem I.13k (Operator-Level Realization and Retarded Solvability for Polynomial Form Factors).** Work on the gauge-invariant subclass (I.13j.2) with $a,c$ real polynomials in $\Box$, $a\not\equiv0$ and $a-3c\not\equiv0$. Let $\bar V_+=\{(t,\mathbf x):t\ge|\mathbf x|\}$ and let $\mathcal A_+$ be the space of distributions on $\mathbb R^4$ supported in $x_0+\bar V_+$ for some $x_0$; it is a commutative convolution algebra and contains every compactly supported distribution. Put $\theta_{\mu\nu}=\eta_{\mu\nu}-\partial_\mu\partial_\nu\Box^{-1}$, $P^{0s}h=\tfrac13\theta_{\mu\nu}\theta^{\alpha\beta}h_{\alpha\beta}$ and $P^{2}h=\theta_\mu{}^{\alpha}\theta_\nu{}^{\beta}h_{\alpha\beta}-P^{0s}h$, and let $G^{(1)}_{\mu\nu}=\tfrac12(-\Box h_{\mu\nu}+\partial_\mu\partial^\alpha h_{\alpha\nu}+\partial_\nu\partial^\alpha h_{\alpha\mu}-\partial_\mu\partial_\nu h)+\tfrac12\eta_{\mu\nu}(\Box h-\partial^\alpha\partial^\beta h_{\alpha\beta})$ and $R^{(1)}=\partial^\alpha\partial^\beta h_{\alpha\beta}-\Box h$ be the linearized Einstein tensor and Ricci scalar.

1. *Projector form.* On the subclass (I.13j.2) the symbol of the gravitational Lagrangian density is $\tfrac{k^2}{2}\big[a\,hP^{2}h+(a-3c)\,hP^{0s}h\big]$ with $a,c$ evaluated at $\Box=-k^2$, and the field-equation tensor of Theorem I.13j is
 $$E[h]_{\mu\nu}=-\Box\big[a(\Box)P^{2}+(a-3c)(\Box)P^{0s}\big]h=2a(\Box)\,G^{(1)}_{\mu\nu}[h]+\frac{(a-c)(\Box)}{\Box}\big(\eta_{\mu\nu}\Box-\partial_\mu\partial_\nu\big)R^{(1)}[h].$$
 $E$ is a differential operator exactly when $a(0)=c(0)$; otherwise it contains one inverse power of $\Box$, acting on $R^{(1)}$.
2. *Inverse-$\Box$ prescription.* On $\mathcal A_+$ the operator $\Box$ is a bijection, with inverse the convolution with the retarded Green function. With this prescription $\theta$, $P^{2}$, $P^{0s}$ and $E$ are maps of $\mathcal A_+$-valued symmetric tensor fields, $P^{2}$ and $P^{0s}$ are commuting idempotents with $P^{2}P^{0s}=0$, $E$ annihilates $\partial_\mu\xi_\nu+\partial_\nu\xi_\mu$, and $\partial^\mu E[h]_{\mu\nu}=0$. For every nonzero real polynomial $p$ the operator $p(\Box)$ is hyperbolic with respect to the time direction, has a unique fundamental solution $G_p\in\mathcal A_+$, supported in $\bar V_+$, and is a bijection of $\mathcal A_+$ with inverse $G_p*$.
3. *Retarded solution.* Let $G_2$ and $G_0$ be the fundamental solutions in $\mathcal A_+$ of $\Box a(\Box)$ and $\Box(a-3c)(\Box)$. For every symmetric $T\in\mathcal A_+$ with $\partial^\mu T_{\mu\nu}=0$,
 $$h^{\mathrm{ret}}_{\mu\nu}=\frac\kappa2\Big[G_2*\big(T_{\mu\nu}-\tfrac13\eta_{\mu\nu}T^\lambda{}_\lambda\big)+\tfrac13\,G_0*\big(\eta_{\mu\nu}T^\lambda{}_\lambda\big)\Big]\tag{I.13k.1}$$
 lies in $\mathcal A_+$, has support in $\operatorname{supp}T+\bar V_+$, and solves $E[h]+\tfrac\kappa2T=0$. Every solution in $\mathcal A_+$ equals $h^{\mathrm{ret}}+\partial_\mu\xi_\nu+\partial_\nu\xi_\mu$ with $\xi\in\mathcal A_+$, so the linearized curvature of the retarded solution is unique. If $\partial^\mu T_{\mu\nu}\neq0$ there is no solution. At $a=c=1$, (I.13k.1) is $h=\tfrac\kappa2G_{\mathrm{ret}}*(T-\tfrac12\eta T^\lambda{}_\lambda)$, the retarded solution of linearized general relativity.
4. *Static sector and degenerate shells.* For static dust $T^{00}=\rho(\mathbf x)$ the potentials of item 2 of Theorem I.13j satisfy a constant-coefficient system on $\mathbb R^3$ whose determinant is a nonzero constant multiple of $K^4q(-K^2)$, $q:=a(a-3c)$, $K=|\mathbf k|$. For every tempered $\rho$ a tempered solution exists; two tempered solutions differ by a solution of the homogeneous system whose Fourier transform is supported in $\{0\}\cup\bigcup_j\{|\mathbf k|=K_j\}$, where $K_j>0$ are the zeros of $q(-K^2)$. If $q$ has no negative real zero, the homogeneous solutions are polynomials, so a solution vanishing at infinity is unique when it exists; for $q(0)\neq0$ and smooth compactly supported $\rho$ it exists, and its Fourier transform is given by (I.13j.3) for $\mathbf k\neq0$. If $q(-K_*^2)=0$ with $K_*>0$, the static solution is not unique, since the homogeneous system has bounded standing-wave solutions of wave number $K_*$, and $z=-K_*^2$ is a tachyonic zero: $E[h]=0$ has solutions growing like $e^{t\sqrt{K_*^2-|\mathbf k|^2}}$ for every $|\mathbf k|<K_*$. Degenerate static shells therefore occur only on members whose field equation has exponentially growing solutions.
5. *Spin-two residue sum rule.* If $\deg a\ge1$, $a(0)\ne0$ and all zeros $z_j$ of $a$ are real and simple, then $\dfrac1{za(z)}=\dfrac1{a(0)z}+\sum_j\dfrac{r_j}{z-z_j}$ with $r_j=1/(z_ja'(z_j))$ and $\dfrac1{a(0)}+\sum_jr_j=0$, so at least one massive spin-two pole has residue of sign opposite to that of the massless pole. Since $\Sigma_{\mathrm{lens}}=1/a$ by (I.13j.3), a scale-dependent lensing response within polynomial form factors requires $\deg a\geq1$ and therefore a negative zero of $a$ (tachyonic by item 4), a non-real zero, a multiple zero of $za(z)$, or an opposite-sign massive spin-two pole. For constant $a$, $\Sigma_{\mathrm{lens}}$ is constant and all scale dependence of $\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}$ is carried by the scalar form factor $a-3c$.

*Proof.* Item 1: with $\partial_\mu\mapsto ik_\mu$, the five terms of (I.13j.1) on (I.13j.2) give the density $\tfrac12ak^2h_{\mu\nu}h^{\mu\nu}-a(hk)_\mu(hk)^\mu+c\,h\,(khk)-\tfrac12ck^2h^2+\tfrac{a-c}{2k^2}(khk)^2$, and expanding the projectors shows that this equals $\tfrac{k^2}{2}[a\,hP^{2}h+(a-3c)\,hP^{0s}h]$; variation gives $E=k^2[aP^{2}+(a-3c)P^{0s}]h$. Writing $aP^{2}+(a-3c)P^{0s}=a(P^{2}-2P^{0s})+3(a-c)P^{0s}$ and expanding, $-\Box(P^{2}-2P^{0s})h=2G^{(1)}[h]$, in which the inverse powers of $\Box$ cancel, and $-3\Box P^{0s}h=(\eta_{\mu\nu}\Box-\partial_\mu\partial_\nu)\Box^{-1}R^{(1)}[h]$. The quotient $(a-c)(z)/z$ is a polynomial exactly when $a(0)=c(0)$. Item 2: $\bar V_+$ is a closed convex salient cone, so $\mathcal A_+$ is a convolution algebra. Factor $p(\Box)=p_0\prod_j(\Box-z_j)$ over $\mathbb C$; each factor is hyperbolic with respect to $t$ because the frequencies $\omega=\pm\sqrt{|\mathbf k|^2+z_j}$ of its plane waves have imaginary part bounded in $\mathbf k$, and products of hyperbolic operators are hyperbolic. A hyperbolic operator has a unique fundamental solution supported in the forward half-space, and its support lies in the propagation cone of the principal part $\Box^{\deg p}$, which is $\bar V_+$ (Gårding 1951). If $p(\Box)u=0$ with $u\in\mathcal A_+$, then $u=G_p*p(\Box)u=0$ by associativity, so $p(\Box)$ is injective, and $G_p*$ is a two-sided inverse. The algebraic identities for $\theta,P^{2},P^{0s}$ follow from $\partial^\mu\theta_{\mu\nu}=0$ and $\theta^2=\theta$, which hold on $\mathcal A_+$ because $\Box^{-1}\Box=1$ there. Item 3: conservation gives $\theta T=T$, so $P^{2}T=T-\tfrac13\theta T^\lambda{}_\lambda$ and $P^{0s}T=\tfrac13\theta T^\lambda{}_\lambda$, and $h_\theta:=\tfrac\kappa2[G_2*P^{2}T+G_0*P^{0s}T]$ satisfies $\Box[aP^{2}+(a-3c)P^{0s}]h_\theta=\tfrac\kappa2T$. Replacing $\theta$ by $\eta$ changes $h_\theta$ by $\partial_\mu\partial_\nu$ of an element of $\mathcal A_+$, a pure gauge term, which $E$ annihilates. If $E[h]=0$ with $h\in\mathcal A_+$, applying $P^{2}$ and $P^{0s}$ and the injectivity of $\Box a(\Box)$ and $\Box(a-3c)(\Box)$ gives $\theta h\theta=0$, and then $h=\partial_\mu\xi_\nu+\partial_\nu\xi_\mu$ with $\xi_\nu=\Box^{-1}\partial^\alpha h_{\alpha\nu}-\tfrac12\partial_\nu\Box^{-2}\partial^\alpha\partial^\beta h_{\alpha\beta}$. Necessity of conservation is $\partial^\mu E[h]_{\mu\nu}=0$. At $a=c=1$, $G_2=G_{\mathrm{ret}}$ and $G_0=-\tfrac12G_{\mathrm{ret}}$. Item 4: the $2\times2$ system in the proof of Theorem I.13j, with each equation multiplied by $K^2$, has polynomial symbol matrix with determinant $2K^4a(a-3c)$; for a square system with nonzero polynomial determinant, a tempered solution is obtained from the adjugate matrix after dividing the transformed data by the determinant, which is possible for every tempered distribution (Hörmander 1958), and homogeneous tempered solutions have Fourier support in the real zero set of the determinant. Support at the origin means a polynomial. For the growing modes take, if $a(-K_*^2)=0$, $h_{\mu\nu}=\epsilon_{\mu\nu}e^{i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x+\gamma t}$ with $\epsilon$ spatial, transverse to $\mathbf k$ and traceless and $\gamma^2=K_*^2-|\mathbf k|^2$: then $\Box h=-K_*^2h$, $R^{(1)}[h]=0$, $G^{(1)}[h]=-\tfrac12\Box h$ and $E[h]=-a(\Box)\Box h=0$. If $(a-3c)(-K_*^2)=0$ take $h_{\mu\nu}=\eta_{\mu\nu}\phi$ with $\Box\phi=-K_*^2\phi$: then $E[h]=-(\eta_{\mu\nu}\Box-\partial_\mu\partial_\nu)(a-3c)(\Box)\phi=0$. Item 5: the sum of all residues of a rational function vanishing at infinity to second order is zero; the list of alternatives is exhaustive because zeros of $a$ that are real, simple, positive and distinct from $0$ fall under the sum rule. ∎

Items 2 and 3 use only that $\Box a(\Box)$ and $\Box(a-3c)(\Box)$ are invertible elements of the convolution algebra $\mathcal A_+$ commuting with derivatives. On members that are also in the rational class of Theorem I.13l, its zero-past solution (I.13l.4) lies in $\mathcal A_+$ and solves the same equation, so it differs from (I.13k.1) by a pure gauge term. For form factors outside these two classes, in particular for the symbols that item 3 of Theorem I.13j assigns to a prescribed pair $(\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}},\Sigma_{\mathrm{lens}})$, that invertibility is a separate multiplier-class problem.

<a id="corollary-i13ka-short-distance-limits-and-band-rigidity-of-polynomial-form-factors"></a>**Corollary I.13k.a (Short-Distance Limits and Band Rigidity of Polynomial Form Factors).** Let $a,c$ be real polynomials in $\Box$ of degree at most $n\ge1$ on the subclass of Theorem I.13k, and evaluate $\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}$, $\Sigma_{\mathrm{lens}}$ and $\Psi/\Phi=\nu_{\mathrm{sl}}/\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}$ of (I.13j.3) at $\Box=-K^2$, at the wave numbers $K>0$ where $a\ne0$ and $a\ne3c$.

1. $\Sigma_{\mathrm{lens}}$ has a finite nonzero limit as $K\to\infty$ exactly when $a$ is constant. For constant $a$ and nonconstant $c$, $\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}/\Sigma_{\mathrm{lens}}\to\tfrac43$ and $\Psi/\Phi\to\tfrac12$ as $K\to\infty$. For constant $a$, $\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}=\Sigma_{\mathrm{lens}}$ at every admissible $K$ exactly when $c=a$, which is linearized general relativity with its coupling divided by $a$.
2. Let $0<K_1<K_2$ and $\epsilon\ge0$. If $|a(-K^2)-1|\le\epsilon$ and $|c(-K^2)-1|\le\epsilon$ for $K_1\le K\le K_2$, then for $0\le K\le K_1$
$$
|a(-K^2)-1|,\ |c(-K^2)-1|\ \le\ \epsilon\,T_n\!\left(\frac{K_2^2+K_1^2}{K_2^2-K_1^2}\right)
=\epsilon\cosh\!\left(2n\operatorname{artanh}\frac{K_1}{K_2}\right),
\tag{I.13k.a.1}
$$
where $T_n$ is the Chebyshev polynomial of degree $n$. The factor tends to one as $nK_1/K_2\to0$.

A polynomial pair that agrees with linearized general relativity to accuracy $\epsilon$ on a band of wave numbers therefore agrees with it to accuracy $\epsilon\cosh(2n\operatorname{artanh}(K_1/K_2))$ at every lower wave number, that is, on every larger scale. A large-scale departure of size $\delta>\epsilon$ therefore requires $n\ge\operatorname{arccosh}(\delta/\epsilon)/(2\operatorname{artanh}(K_1/K_2))$, which for $K_1\ll K_2$ is about $\tfrac12(K_2/K_1)\operatorname{arccosh}(\delta/\epsilon)$.

*Proof.* Item 1. By (I.13j.3), $\Sigma_{\mathrm{lens}}=1/a$, and a polynomial with a finite nonzero limit at infinity is a nonzero constant. For constant $a$ and $|c|\to\infty$, $\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}/\Sigma_{\mathrm{lens}}=2(a-2c)/(a-3c)\to\tfrac43$ and $\Psi/\Phi=-c/(a-2c)\to\tfrac12$. By item 3 of Theorem I.13j, $\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}=\Sigma_{\mathrm{lens}}$ at a wave vector exactly when $a=c$ there, and a polynomial equal to the constant $a$ at infinitely many values $\Box=-K^2$ equals $a$ identically.

Item 2. Put $x=K^2$, $\alpha=K_1^2$, $\beta=K_2^2$ and $L(x)=(2x-\alpha-\beta)/(\beta-\alpha)$, and let $P$ be $a-1$ or $c-1$, a polynomial of degree at most $n$ in $x$ with $|P|\le\epsilon$ on $[\alpha,\beta]$. For $\epsilon=0$, $P$ vanishes identically. For $\epsilon>0$, Chebyshev's extremal inequality gives $|P(x)|\le\epsilon|T_n(L(x))|$ for $x\notin[\alpha,\beta]$: if $|P(x_0)|>\epsilon|T_n(L(x_0))|$ at such an $x_0$, put $\lambda=\epsilon T_n(L(x_0))/P(x_0)$, so $|\lambda|<1$; then $Q=\epsilon\,T_n\circ L-\lambda P$ vanishes at $x_0$ and takes the signs $(-1)^k$ at the $n+1$ points of $[\alpha,\beta]$ where $T_n\circ L=(-1)^k$, so $Q$ has $n+1$ zeros and vanishes identically, and then $\epsilon=\epsilon T_n(L(\beta))=\lambda P(\beta)$ contradicts $|\lambda P(\beta)|<\epsilon$. For $0\le x\le\alpha$, $-L(x)\in\bigl[1,(\alpha+\beta)/(\beta-\alpha)\bigr]$, and $|T_n(-y)|=T_n(y)$ increases for $y\ge1$, which gives the inequality in (I.13k.a.1). Finally, with $r=K_1/K_2$, $\operatorname{arccosh}\bigl((1+r^2)/(1-r^2)\bigr)=\log\bigl((1+r)/(1-r)\bigr)=2\operatorname{artanh}r$ and $T_n=\cosh(n\operatorname{arccosh})$ on $[1,\infty)$. ∎

<a id="theorem-i13x-an-explicit-single-metric-scalar-vector-model-and-its-retained-projections"></a>**Theorem I.13x (An Explicit Single-Metric Scalar–Vector Model and Its Retained Projections).** Let $n>1$, $A>0$, $a_\chi>0$, $G>0$, $\Lambda\ge0$ and
$$
\begin{aligned}
\nu(y)&=1+A(1-e^{-y^{-n}}),& h(y)&=y\nu(y),\\
\delta&=1-A[ne^{-(n-1)/n}-1]>0,&r&=\delta/2,\\
f_*(y)&=h(y)-ry,&k_*&=f_*^{-1},\\
F_*(z)&=\int_0^z k_*(v)\,dv,&U(p)&=a_\chi^2F_*(|p|/a_\chi).
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.13x.1}
$$
Use the continuous smooth radial extension at zero. The function $U$ is uniformly convex and quadratic-coercive, with
$$
\frac{I}{1+A-r}\preceq D_p^2U\preceq\frac{I}{\delta-r}.
\tag{I.13x.2}
$$
On signature $(-+++)$ and units $c=1$, let $u$ be an independent unit future-timelike vector, $\varphi$ a response scalar and $\psi$ canonical matter with a fixed smooth nonnegative potential $W$; $W(\psi)=m^2\psi^2/2$, $m\ge0$, is an explicit example. Put
$$
h^{\mu\nu}=g^{\mu\nu}+u^\mu u^\nu,\quad
Q=u^\mu\partial_\mu\varphi,\quad
Y=h^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\varphi\partial_\nu\varphi,\quad
 a^\mu=u^\nu\nabla_\nu u^\mu,\quad F_{\mu\nu}=2\nabla_{[\mu}u_{\nu]},
$$
$$
J(Y)=2r a_\chi^2F_*(\sqrt Y/a_\chi),\qquad G_b=rG/2.
\tag{I.13x.3}
$$
The following is one specified local covariant action:
$$
\begin{aligned}
S={}&\frac1{16\pi G_b}\int\sqrt{-g}\,\bigl[
R-2\Lambda-\tfrac12F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu}-(\nabla_\mu u^\mu)^2
+2a^\mu\partial_\mu\varphi-Y-J(Y)+10Q^2
+\lambda_u(u_\mu u^\mu+1)\bigr]d^4x\\
&-\int\sqrt{-g}\,[\tfrac12g^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\psi\partial_\nu\psi+W(\psi)]d^4x\\
&-m_b\int d\mu(\zeta)\int\sqrt{-g_{\alpha\beta}\dot x_\zeta^\alpha\dot x_\zeta^\beta}\,d\lambda,\qquad m_b>0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.13x.4}
$$
The particle label measure $d\mu$ is fixed and nonnegative; a species with zero population contributes zero. Matter and response use this same metric. The independent fields and couplings in (I.13x.4) define this model; it is a different action class from the hypersurface-orthogonal minimal clock of Theorem I.13o. Compactly supported variations, or the corresponding fixed-data Einstein boundary term, are understood. Related scalar–vector architectures appear in Skordis and Zlosnik (2021) and their Minkowski stability analysis (Skordis and Zlosnik 2022). The divergence-squared term and every coefficient of the present model are retained explicitly below.

*Proof. Constitutive construction and exact equations.* With $t=y^{-n}$,
$$
h'=1+A-Ae^{-t}(1+nt),\quad \min_{t\ge0}h'=\delta,
\qquad \delta-r\le f_*'\le1+A-r.
\tag{I.13x.5}
$$
The maximum of $e^{-t}(1+nt)$ occurs at $t=(n-1)/n$. Also $1-r\le f_*(y)/y\le1+A-r$. Thus $f_*$ is a smooth increasing bijection on $[0,\infty)$. The radial and tangential Hessian eigenvalues of $U$ are
$$
b_\parallel=\frac1{h'(y)-r},\qquad b_\perp=\frac1{\nu(y)-r},\qquad |p|/a_\chi=f_*(y),
\tag{I.13x.6}
$$
which prove (I.13x.2). The exponential correction is flat at zero, and inversion preserves this smooth radial extension. The two-sided quadratic bounds follow by integrating the Hessian bounds.

The response scalar is shift symmetric, with exact current equation
$$
\nabla_\mu[2a^\mu-2(1+J_Y)h^{\mu\nu}\partial_\nu\varphi+20Q u^\mu]=0.
\tag{I.13x.7}
$$
Varying all fields before restriction and then applying a compactly supported diffeomorphism gives the total Ward identity in the physical metric. Indeed the nonmetric Euler terms vanish on their field equations, while $\delta g_{\mu\nu}=2\nabla_{(\mu}\xi_{\nu)}$; integration by parts gives $\nabla_\mu(T_m^{\mu\nu}+T_{\rm extra}^{\mu\nu})=0$, with the Einstein term and bare $\Lambda$ counted once. The minimally coupled matter equations also give their separate stress conservation; the vector/response-scalar fields retain their joint Euler identity.

**Retained static action.** On an aligned static branch $u=N^{-1}\partial_t$, $Q=\nabla\!\cdot u=0$ and $a_i=D_i\log N$. The spatial vector variation of the acceleration term is a time derivative with a stationary coefficient; the first variations of $Y$ and $Q$ in that direction vanish. Thus its spatial equation holds, while the parallel equation fixes $\lambda_u$. To take the weak-field action coefficient set
$$
g_{00}=-e^{2\epsilon\Phi},\quad g_{ij}=e^{-2\epsilon\Psi}\delta_{ij},\quad
\varphi=\epsilon s,\quad a_\chi=\epsilon a_*,\quad\Lambda=\epsilon^2\Lambda_*.
$$
For this static coefficient put the canonical field at a zero-energy stationary state $W(\psi_v)=W_\psi(\psi_v)=0$; the explicit quadratic example has $\psi_v=0$. For the minimally coupled slow massive-source term $-\epsilon\rho N$, subtract the field-independent rest/vacuum terms. Eliminate $\Psi=\Phi$ with the same fixed boundary traces. The coefficient of $\epsilon^2$ is
$$
S_2=-\frac1{8\pi rG}\int\bigl[|\nabla(\Phi-s)|^2+2ra_*^2F_*(|\nabla s|/a_*)\bigr]d^3x-\int\rho\Phi\,d^3x.
\tag{I.13x.8}
$$
The divergence-squared and $Q^2$ terms vanish on this static restriction and have not been dropped from the underlying action. With $v=\Phi-s$ its Euler equations are
$$
\Delta v=4\pi rG\rho,\qquad
\nabla\!\cdot\left[\frac{k_*(|\nabla s|/a_*)}{|\nabla s|/a_*}\nabla s\right]=4\pi G\rho.
\tag{I.13x.9}
$$
For a spherical source of enclosed mass $M(R)$, let $y=GM(R)/(a_*R^2)$. Gauss' law gives $|\nabla v|=ra_*y$, $|\nabla s|=a_*f_*(y)$, hence $|\nabla\Phi|=a_*h(y)$ and $\Phi+\Psi=2\Phi$. The same normal-flux calculation applies to a planar sheet. These are retained action/field projections. They do not assert that an externally prescribed stationary dust density is an exact geodesic source; an actual dynamical matter realization has its own source and time domain. The scaling just displayed is a retained chart-family statement. A single fixed dimensional action has the exact homothety $x_{\rm phys}=\epsilon x$, $t_{\rm phys}=\epsilon t$, $a_{\chi,\rm chart}=\epsilon a_{\chi,\rm phys}$, $\Lambda_{\rm chart}=\epsilon^2\Lambda_{\rm phys}$ and $W_{\rm chart}=\epsilon^2W_{\rm phys}$. With the same particle rest mass/momenta and $f_{\rm phys}=\epsilon^{-2}f_{\rm chart}$, curvature and stress scale together as $\epsilon^{-2}$ and both Liouville terms as $\epsilon^{-3}$. This is a shrinking physical domain/time, not a fixed-size or orbital-time limit.

**Exact homogeneous equations and a populated branch.** For $ds^2=-dt^2+a(t)^2d\mathbf x^2$, $u=\partial_t$, $Q=\dot\varphi$ and $D=5/2$, the same action gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
3DH^2&=\Lambda+8\pi G_b\rho_m+5Q^2,\\
-2D\dot H&=8\pi G_b(\rho_m+p_m)+10Q^2,\\
\dot Q+3HQ&=0,\qquad \dot\rho_m+3H(\rho_m+p_m)=0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.13x.10}
$$
Before setting the homogeneous lapse to one, the gravitational/response/canonical density per comoving volume is
$$
-\frac{3Da\dot a^2}{8\pi G_bN}-\frac{\Lambda Na^3}{8\pi G_b}
+\frac{5a^3\dot\varphi^2}{8\pi G_bN}
+\frac{a^3\dot\psi^2}{2N}-Na^3W(\psi),
$$
with the same minimally coupled particle term. Varying $N,a,\varphi,\psi$ gives (I.13x.10) and the canonical equation; no homogeneous stress is prescribed independently of its matter action. For the canonical source, $\rho_\psi=\dot\psi^2/2+W(\psi)$, $p_\psi=\dot\psi^2/2-W(\psi)$ and $\ddot\psi+3H\dot\psi+W_\psi=0$. Homogeneous collisionless matter uses its actual redshifting momentum measure. The response-scalar charge has $Q=q_0/a^3$ and energy $5Q^2/(8\pi G_b)$, with equal pressure. Thus generic initial response charge is stiff; it is not an automatically dustlike component. Differentiating the first equation using the remaining equations gives zero constraint defect.

For nonvacuity choose $W=m^2\psi^2/2$ with $m>0$, initial scale one, $\psi=\psi_0\ne0$, $\dot\psi=0$, $Q=q_0\ne0$ and $\Lambda\ge0$. The positive root of
$$
3(5/2)H^2=\Lambda+8\pi G_bm^2\psi_0^2/2+5q_0^2
\tag{I.13x.11}
$$
satisfies the Hamiltonian constraint; homogeneous momentum constraints vanish. Isotropy makes the spatial vector equation zero and its parallel part fixes the multiplier. The smooth homogeneous ODEs give an actual local positive-source development. Theorem I.13y supplies the open-jet Cauchy and physical-cone statement, including mixed spatial/time derivatives. These explicit fields/couplings are hypotheses of this model; the retained projections are not a derivation of those fields from the predictive source. $\square$

<a id="corollary-i13xa-the-exact-oblique-source-defect-of-the-additive-split"></a>**Corollary I.13x.a (The Exact Oblique-Source Defect of the Additive Split).** The retained equations (I.13x.9) do not reproduce the frozen single-potential constitutive action on every nonspherical source. Freeze a nonzero parallel background $y>0$, let $a=\nu(y)$, $b=h'(y)$ and let $p\in[0,1]$ be the squared cosine between a perturbing spatial covector and that background. With $D_p=(1-p)b+pa$,
$$
\begin{aligned}
R_{\rm original}(p)&=\frac1{(1-p)/a+p/b}=\frac{ab}{D_p},\\
R_{\rm split}(p)&=r+\frac1{(1-p)/(a-r)+p/(b-r)},\\
R_{\rm split}-R_{\rm original}
&=-\frac{rp(1-p)(a-b)^2}{D_p(D_p-r)}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.13x.a.1}
$$
*Proof.* The original constitutive Hessian has transverse and longitudinal eigenvalues $1/a,1/b$. The split scalar has eigenvalues $1/(a-r),1/(b-r)$ and the Newton component contributes $r$. Taking their Fourier responses and a common denominator gives the displayed identity. Its denominator is positive because $r<\min(a,b)$, while
$$
a-b=-y\nu'(y)=An y^{-n}e^{-y^{-n}}>0.
\tag{I.13x.a.2}
$$
The defect is strictly negative for every oblique $0<p<1$ and zero in the two exactly transverse/longitudinal directions. Linearize with common affine-background gradient data on a bounded smooth chart and localize compactly supported oscillatory source perturbations there. Equality for every source would force equality of these principal multipliers, contradicting (I.13x.a.1). One can preserve positive source density by using a smooth positive background and sufficiently small localized perturbations. No globally periodic affine potential is assumed. This refutes the all-source identification for this additive split, while retaining its spherical/sheet projection; it is not a refutation of the broader existential covariant-action target. $\square$

<a id="theorem-i13y-complete-mixed-gauge-constraint-cauchy-system-on-the-physical-cone"></a>**Theorem I.13y (Complete Mixed Gauge–Constraint Cauchy System on the Physical Cone).** For the action (I.13x.4), let the fields lie in a compact regular chart with Lorentzian $g$, future unit $u$, and a common spacelike initial slice. The full metric/vector/response-scalar principal system admits a smooth positive directional symmetrizer, including its gauge and constraint modes. Constraint-compatible sufficiently regular data have a unique local development and continuous dependence, with physical domain of dependence contained in the $g$ light cone. The canonical matter wave and nonnegative smooth compact-momentum collisionless sources preserve this statement at the regularity specified below. This is a local finite-time result; the continuation margins are part of its domain.

*Proof. Full principal input and gauge convention.* At an arbitrary event use a $g$-orthonormal frame with $u=(1,0,0,0)$. The fourteen independent perturbations are the ten $h_{\mu\nu}=\delta g_{\mu\nu}$, three $v_i=\delta u_i$, and $s=\delta\varphi$. The unit constraint gives $\delta u_0=h_{00}/2$. With $h=\eta^{\mu\nu}h_{\mu\nu}$ define
$$
A_i=\partial_0v_i-\tfrac12\partial_i h_{00},\quad
\Theta=\partial_i(v_i-h_{0i})+\tfrac12\partial_0h_{ii},\quad
F_{ij}=\partial_iv_j-\partial_jv_i,\quad B=D_p^2U(\nabla_\perp\varphi).
\tag{I.13y.1}
$$
Up to the fixed positive factor and terms with fewer than two perturbation derivatives, the exact quadratic density is
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal L_{\rm pr}={}&-\tfrac12(\partial_\mu h)(\partial_\nu h^{\mu\nu})
+\tfrac14(\partial_\rho h)(\partial^\rho h)
+\tfrac12(\partial_\mu h^{\mu\rho})(\partial_\nu h^\nu{}_{\rho})
-\tfrac14(\partial_\rho h^{\mu\nu})(\partial^\rho h_{\mu\nu})\\
&+A_iA_i-\tfrac12F_{ij}F_{ij}-\Theta^2
+2A_i\partial_i s-|\nabla s|^2-rB^{ij}\partial_i s\partial_j s+10(\partial_0s)^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.13y.2}
$$
The acceleration mixing is bilinear in first derivatives with coefficients algebraic in $g,u$; coefficient variations have at most one perturbation derivative. The $Q^2$ temporal Hessian is constant. The nonlinear spatial term contributes exactly $B$. Background $\nabla u$ and arbitrary finite $Q\ne0$ affect lower-order terms, so this formula is valid on open sets of jets, including mixed spatial/time derivatives.

For a unit spatial covector $n$, the constitutive dependence is the one number
$$
\lambda=r n^{\mathsf T}Bn,\qquad
0<\lambda_{\min}=\frac r{1+A-r}\le\lambda\le\frac r{\delta-r}=1.
\tag{I.13y.3}
$$
A rotation carrying $n$ to $e_3$ transforms the entire frozen tensor expression, not just sampled directions. Choose a smooth reference connection $\bar\Gamma$ and auxiliary inverse metrics
$$
\widetilde q^{\mu\nu}=h^{\mu\nu}-\tfrac{25}{16}u^\mu u^\nu,\quad
\widehat q^{\mu\nu}=h^{\mu\nu}-\tfrac{100}{81}u^\mu u^\nu,\qquad
H^\alpha=\widetilde q^{\rho\sigma}(\Gamma^\alpha_{\rho\sigma}-\bar\Gamma^\alpha_{\rho\sigma}).
\tag{I.13y.4}
$$
Here the $h^{\mu\nu}$ in (I.13y.4) is the spatial projector in Theorem I.13x, while the perturbation $h_{\mu\nu}$ and its $\eta$-raised components are those in (I.13y.1)–(I.13y.2). The two auxiliary speeds are $4/5,9/10$. Use the covariant-metric Euler derivative multiplied by $16\pi G_b/\sqrt{-g}$; its Einstein part is $-G^{\mu\nu}$. Add only to those metric rows
$$
\mathcal Q^{\mu\nu}=\widehat P_\alpha{}^{\beta\mu\nu}\nabla_\beta H^\alpha,
\qquad
\widehat P_\alpha{}^{\beta\mu\nu}
=\delta_\alpha^{(\mu}\widehat q^{\nu)\beta}-\tfrac12\delta_\alpha^\beta\widehat q^{\mu\nu}.
\tag{I.13y.5}
$$
For modified harmonic gauge constructions, see Kovacs and Reall (2020). The mixed-field symbol and complete eigenspaces for (I.13x.4) are computed here. The vector/scalar equations remain unchanged. In the ten independent symmetric metric coordinates, multiply off-diagonal tensor equations by two; diagonal rows have weight one.

**Every entry of the finite pencil.** Replace $\partial_\mu$ in (I.13y.2) by $k_\mu=(w,0,0,1)$ and take the Hessian in the ordered coordinates
$$
(h_{00},h_{01},h_{02},h_{03},h_{11},h_{12},h_{13},h_{22},h_{23},h_{33},v_1,v_2,v_3,s).
$$
Call it $P_0(w)$. Compute $H$ with the linear Christoffel formula $\Gamma^\alpha_{\rho\sigma}=\tfrac12\eta^{\alpha\beta}(k_\rho h_{\beta\sigma}+k_\sigma h_{\beta\rho}-k_\beta h_{\rho\sigma})$, then (I.13y.5) with the stated row weights. This defines every entry of $M(w)=P_0(w)+\mathcal Q(w)$, without additional matrix data. For lower-index $\xi$, its four diffeomorphism columns are
$$
\delta h_{\mu\nu}=k_\mu\xi_\nu+k_\nu\xi_\mu,\quad
\delta v_i=k_i\xi_0,\quad\delta s=0.
\tag{I.13y.6}
$$
Writing their matrix as $R(k)$, direct substitution gives $P_0R=0$ and $H(R\xi)=\widetilde q(k,k)\eta^{-1}\xi$. The Ward identity gives the corresponding left kernel, retaining the vector contribution. Expansion of the completely specified finite matrix gives
$$
\det M(w)=\frac{(w-1)^4(w+1)^4(5w-4)^4(5w+4)^4(10w-9)^4(10w+9)^4
[50w^4-(20+5\lambda)w^2+\lambda]}{5642219814912}.
\tag{I.13y.7}
$$
For $M(w)=A_tw^2+B_tw+C_t$,
$$
\det A_t=\frac{3814697265625}{11019960576}\ne0.
\tag{I.13y.8}
$$
These rational-polynomial identities follow from the printed Hessian and gauge prescription. Diagonalizability requires the further kernel construction below; it is not inferred from the determinant.

**Physical quotient and every repeated-root eigenspace.** The scalar/vector/tensor decompositions use the smooth longitudinal/transverse projectors $n\otimes n$ and $I-n\otimes n$. In the scalar sector remove longitudinal $v_i$ by the time gauge and remove spatial scalar shear. Write the remaining curvature, lapse and scalar shift as $v_c,n_l,b_s$. Keeping lapse/shift variations gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal L_{\rm kin}&=-6\dot v_c^2-4\dot v_c\Delta b_s-(3\dot v_c+\Delta b_s)^2+10\dot s^2,\\
\mathcal L_{\rm grad}&=2|\nabla v_c|^2-4\nabla v_c\cdot\nabla n_l+|\nabla n_l|^2
+2\nabla n_l\cdot\nabla s-|\nabla s|^2-rB^{ij}\partial_i s\partial_j s.
\end{aligned}
$$
The shift gives $\Delta b_s=-5\dot v_c$ and the lapse gives $n_l=2v_c-s$ for nonzero spatial frequency. Substitution, before any dispersion conclusion, gives
$$
\mathsf T=10I_2,\quad
\mathsf V=\begin{pmatrix}2&-2\\-2&2+\lambda\end{pmatrix},\quad
c_\pm^2=\frac{4+\lambda\pm\sqrt{16+\lambda^2}}{20}.
\tag{I.13y.9}
$$
The two speeds are distinct, positive and less than $1/2$ in square. The two tensor and two transverse-vector modes have positive physical kinetic/spatial forms and speed one; the divergence and response mixing are longitudinal and do not alter them. The physical quotient therefore has six second-order degrees of freedom. The scalar constraint elimination used only nonzero spatial $|k|^2$ and fixed positive kinetic coefficients. Reversing it shows that at a scalar root the quotient kernel has dimension one and at a light root it has dimension four. Away from the physical roots $P_0$ has rank ten and only the four diffeomorphisms in its kernel, including at either auxiliary-cone root.

At a physical root the two auxiliary quadratics are nonzero. Contracted gauge-fixed equations force $H=0$; every physical quotient vector has exactly one gauge representative with $H=0$ because $H(R\xi)=\widetilde q(k,k)\eta^{-1}\xi$ is invertible. This constructs four light-root vectors or one vector at each scalar root.

At a $\widetilde q$-null root, $\widehat q(k,k)\ne0$ forces $H=0$. The physical quotient is invertible, so exactly the four pure-gauge vectors remain. At a $\widehat q$-null root prescribe any four-component $H_{\rm target}$. Its gauge source pairs to zero with every diffeomorphism column by the contracted identity $\widehat q(k,k)H_{\rm target}=0$. Since the symmetric Hessian $P_0$ has rank ten, its image is exactly the annihilator of its four-dimensional kernel. Solve $P_0z=-\mathcal QH_{\rm target}$ modulo gauge and uniquely adjust the gauge components to obtain $H(z)=H_{\rm target}$. This constructs four independent constraint-mode vectors.

Thus the companion pencil has $2(4+1+1+4+4)=28$ real independent eigenvectors, its entire dimension. For
$$
\mathsf P=\begin{pmatrix}0&I\\-A_t^{-1}C_t&-A_t^{-1}B_t\end{pmatrix},\quad
\beta_j\in\{\pm1,\pm4/5,\pm9/10,\pm c_+,\pm c_-\},
$$
$$
\Pi_j=\prod_{i\ne j}\frac{\mathsf P-\beta_iI}{\beta_j-\beta_i},\qquad
\mathsf S=\sum_j\Pi_j^{\mathsf T}\Pi_j,
\tag{I.13y.10}
$$
the ten roots remain separated on $\lambda\in[\lambda_{\min},1]$. Hence these projectors are smooth in direction and regular jets, without a global transverse-polarization basis. They satisfy
$$
\mathsf S\mathsf P=\sum_j\beta_j\Pi_j^{\mathsf T}\Pi_j=\mathsf P^{\mathsf T}\mathsf S,\qquad
x^{\mathsf T}\mathsf Sx=\sum_j|\Pi_jx|^2\ge|x|^2/10.
\tag{I.13y.11}
$$
The last inequality follows from $x=\sum_j\Pi_jx$. Compactness of the direction sphere, the fixed constitutive chamber and a bounded regular coordinate neighborhood gives the finite upper bound. This symmetrizes the full gauge-fixed symbol, including its repeated gauge/constraint roots.

**Propagated constraints and a local differential reduction.** Solve the unit constraint algebraically near the timelike branch. Take original metric-constraint data with $H=0$ on the initial slice and choose the gauge lapse/shift derivatives accordingly. Spatial derivatives of $H$ vanish there. The $0\mu$ equations of $\widehat P\nabla H$ have invertible normal coefficients proportional to $\widehat q^{00}$; the original constraints therefore give the initial normal derivative of $H$ equal to zero. The diffeomorphism Noether identity, using the unchanged vector/scalar equations, makes the divergence of the added metric term a homogeneous equation for $H$ with principal part $\widehat q^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\partial_\nu H$. Its lower terms are linear in $H,\nabla H$ with smooth solution-dependent coefficients. Zero initial data imply $H=0$, so the modified solution solves the original equations.

Set $V=\partial_0z$, $W_i=\partial_i z$ and retain $z$ itself. The local differential system is
$$
A_t\partial_0V+B_t^i\partial_iV+C_t^{ij}\partial_iW_j=\text{lower order},\qquad
\partial_0W_i=\partial_iV,\qquad\partial_0z=V.
\tag{I.13y.12}
$$
For spatial direction $n$, its $(V,W_n)$ block is the companion block up to ordering. The transverse $W$ and undifferentiated $z$ have zero speed. Since $C_t(n,n)=M(0,n)$ is invertible by (I.13y.7), their forcing into the companion block is uniquely eliminated. Thus the zero eigenspace has dimension 42 and the entire seventy-variable reduction is diagonalizable. Adding its zero-root projector to (I.13y.10) gives a positive smooth symmetrizer. The constraints $\partial_i z-W_i$ and $\partial_iW_j-\partial_jW_i$ propagate by commuting the displayed derivatives.

On a bounded admissible chart take initial fields in $H^{s+1}$ and normal derivatives in $H^s$, integer $s\ge5$, with bounded coefficients and spacelike/metric margins. The reduced coefficients depend smoothly on $(z,V,W)$. Differentiated energy and the Sobolev product estimates give, with the corresponding forced/difference estimates,
$$
\frac{dE_s}{dt}\le C_R(E_s+E_s^{3/2}).
\tag{I.13y.13}
$$
Regularized iteration yields local existence/uniqueness, lower-norm continuous dependence and persistence of higher regularity. Continuation requires bounds on this regularity norm and on inverse symmetrizer, Lorentzian and common-slice margins; no global stability is inferred.

**Physical causal cone.** Every rest-frame characteristic speed has magnitude at most one, with fastest roots exactly the physical metric light roots. This cone statement also holds for the time normals used in localized energy uniqueness. The scalar spatial pencil is
$$
10\omega^2I-
\begin{pmatrix}2|k|^2&-2|k|^2\\-2|k|^2&2|k|^2+r k^{\mathsf T}Bk\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{I.13y.14}
$$
Its spatial form is strictly below $5|k|^2I$, so the scalar time energy is positive for every physical timelike normal. The auxiliary cones stay strictly separated from scalar and physical light cones. Repeating the gauge-kernel/range construction gives real complete characteristics and smooth symmetrizers on compact sets of such normals. Local uniqueness on overlapping spacelike charts, or energy uniqueness on slightly spacelike approximations to a physical null boundary, yields domain of dependence inside the $g$ cone. This uses complete eigenspaces and the spacelike-normal condition, rather than a determinant alone.

**Actual matter fields and transport.** The canonical wave has metric $g$ and only lower-order mixing: its stress and vector/metric forces depend on field/first-derivative variables, while its connection terms are algebraic in the gravitational derivative variables. Smooth potential terms are lower order. Its positive wave symmetrizer appends as a direct block even where its light roots coincide with the gravitational ones. For $W\ge0$ its observer energy is nonnegative.

For a smooth nonnegative future massive-shell distribution $f$ with initially compact spatial/momentum support, the fixed positive worldline measure of (I.13x.4) gives geodesic Liouville evolution and, in an orthonormal frame,
$$
p^\mu\partial_\mu f-\Gamma^i_{\alpha\beta}p^\alpha p^\beta\partial_{p^i}f=0,\qquad
T^{ab}=\int f\,p^ap^b\frac{d^3p}{p^0}.
\tag{I.13y.15}
$$
Push forward the initial worldline labels to obtain this $f$. Integration by parts on the mass shell has no momentum boundary term and proves conservation of particle current and stress. Every positive massive momentum is future timelike, so the stress obeys the dominant energy condition. The field source is an algebraic moment of $f$; transport sees the connection as algebraic first-order gravitational variables. Thus no new second-derivative field mixing is introduced.

For the coupled transport class take field first-order data in $H^s_x$ and $f\in H^s_{x,p}$, integer $s\ge8$, with compact momentum support. The differentiated transport identity and gravitational symmetrizer close the same local energy estimates: source moments are bounded $H^s_x$ maps by Cauchy–Schwarz on the compact momentum support, Sobolev products are controlled in dimensions three/six, and the force estimate keeps momentum support bounded on a short common interval. Regularized iteration gives constraint-compatible local evolution with timelike particle characteristics, hence the same physical causal domain. This smooth-distribution theorem does not silently include a singular circular-orbit measure as $H^s$ data.

For the explicit vacuum reference $\Lambda=0$, $W=m^2\psi^2/2$, constant $u,\varphi$ and zero source, the physical kinetic/spatial forms and dispersions above have no exponentially growing nonzero-wave-number modes. Sourced backgrounds have the proved finite-time energy control, not a global cosmological attractor assertion. Fixing the initial data defines a causal nonlinear response; its linearization has the same local support and energy estimate. The classical doubled parent is $S[z_+]-S[z_-]$ with common initial data and matched final variations, selecting the diagonal by that initial-value problem. It is not a retarded symmetric single-history Hessian or a quantum influence-state construction. $\square$

<a id="theorem-i13z-canonical-power-clock-embedding-and-a-common-clock-spatial-amplitude"></a>**Theorem I.13z (Canonical Power-Clock Embedding and a Common-Clock Spatial Amplitude).** Use the single physical metric, independent unit vector and response scalar of Theorems I.13x–I.13y, in units $c=1$. Let $A_G$ satisfy the strict ellipticity bound there, keep $r=\delta_G/2$ and $G_b=rG/2$ fixed, and put $D=5/2$ and $\beta=G_b/(DG)=\delta_G/10\in(0,1/10)$. A specified formal homogeneous power-clock law admits the following canonical action realization. A separate specified constitutive extension ties the spatial amplitude to that same canonical coordinate. Neither construction selects its initial state or derives that constitutive tie from a predictive-source principle.

##### I. The field coordinate and the actual potential

Let $\Lambda_{\rm phys}=\Lambda/D>0$, $\rho_\Lambda=\Lambda_{\rm phys}/(8\pi G)$ and
$$
U_c(s)=2-e^{-s^{3/2}},\quad s>0,\qquad
D_U(s)=U_c(s)-\beta-sU_c'(s).
\tag{I.13z.1}
$$
Writing $x=s^{3/2}$ gives $D_U=2-\beta-e^{-x}(1+3x/2)$. The maximum of the last product is $(3/2)e^{-1/3}$, whence
$$
D_U(s)\ge2-\beta-\tfrac32e^{-1/3}>0.
\tag{I.13z.2}
$$
Define a strictly increasing canonical coordinate and its potential by
$$
\psi(s)=\frac1{\sqrt{24\pi G\beta}}\int_1^s
 \frac{\sqrt{D_U(z)}}{z\sqrt{z+U_c(z)}}\,dz,\qquad
W(\psi(s))=\frac{\rho_\Lambda[U_c(s)-\beta+sU_c'(s)]}{2\beta s}.
\tag{I.13z.3}
$$
Here $W$ is a physical energy density, outside the gravitational prefactor. Add its actual action
$$
S_\psi=-\int\sqrt{-g}\,[\tfrac12g^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\psi\partial_\nu\psi+W(\psi)]\,d^4x.
\tag{I.13z.4}
$$
The origin $\psi(1)=0$ fixes only a coordinate on field space. Positivity in (I.13z.2) makes (I.13z.3) a single-valued smooth positive potential on its image. At the dense end $\psi\to-\infty$. At the other end $\psi\to\psi_\infty<\infty$, with
$$
\psi_\infty-\psi=\frac{2\sqrt{2-\beta}}{\sqrt{24\pi G\beta s}}[1+o(1)],\quad
W=\frac{3\Lambda_{\rm phys}}8(\psi_\infty-\psi)^2+o((\psi_\infty-\psi)^2),\quad
W''(\psi_\infty)=\frac{3\Lambda_{\rm phys}}4.
\tag{I.13z.5}
$$
There is a smooth nonnegative extension across this endpoint. For the comparison $U_c\equiv2$ the exact expression is $[\rho_\Lambda(2-\beta)/(4\beta)]\sinh^2[c_0(\psi_\infty-\psi)]$ with $c_0=\sqrt{12\pi G\beta/(2-\beta)}$. The $e^{-s^{3/2}}$ corrections are flat in $\psi_\infty-\psi$; extending their flat part evenly preserves smoothness and nonnegativity near the positive quadratic minimum. This extension leaves the displayed trajectory unchanged. Endpoint smoothness for another clock law requires that law's own asymptotics.

##### II. The exact homogeneous solution and its selection boundary

On the expanding, isotropic, aligned-vector branch set the response scalar constant ($Q=0$), and use pressureless comoving worldlines with positive density $\rho_b=\rho_\Lambda/s$. Put
$$
H=\sqrt{\Lambda_{\rm phys}/3}\sqrt{(s+U_c)/s},\qquad
\dot s=3Hs,\qquad
\dot\psi^2=\frac{\rho_\Lambda D_U}{\beta s},\qquad
\rho_\psi=(U_c/\beta-1)\rho_b,\quad
p_\psi=-\frac{sU_c'}\beta\rho_b.
\tag{I.13z.6}
$$
The derivative of (I.13z.3) yields this positive kinetic term. Its potential equals $(\rho_\psi-p_\psi)/2$ and $\dot\psi^2=\rho_\psi+p_\psi$. Differentiation and $\dot\rho_b=-3H\rho_b$ give $\dot\rho_\psi+3H(\rho_\psi+p_\psi)=0$. Since $\dot\psi\ne0$ at every finite $s$, this is exactly $\ddot\psi+3H\dot\psi+W_\psi=0$. Substituting $\beta=G_b/(DG)$ and $\Lambda=D\Lambda_{\rm phys}$ in the actual constraint gives
$$
3DH^2=\Lambda+8\pi G_b(\rho_b+\rho_\psi)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
3H^2=\Lambda_{\rm phys}+8\pi G U_c(s)\rho_b.
\tag{I.13z.7}
$$
The second Friedmann equation follows by differentiation and conservation. The vector's parallel equation fixes its multiplier, and its spatial equation and response current vanish on this isotropic branch. This is an action solution, not a reassignment of a desired density to a stress tensor. The exact cold worldline source is distinct from a positive-dispersion Vlasov distribution or a collisional baryon/photon model.

The canonical wave block has physical characteristic speed one. Its smooth potential changes only lower-order terms of Theorem I.13y on each compact regular field interval; the constraint propagation and local cone construction therefore persist. The nonnegative $W$ gives nonnegative observer energy. Along (I.13z.6),
$$
\dot H=-4\pi G\rho_b(U_c-sU_c')<0,\qquad
m_V^2=-3\dot H\ge0.
\tag{I.13z.8}
$$
Here $m_V^2$ is the coefficient for the transverse **covariant** aether perturbation $v_i^{(V)}=\delta u_i$. For a nonzero comoving Fourier mode $k$ in the homogeneous canonical-matter block with no independently supplied transverse matter source, the transverse metric shift is nondynamical and zero. At $Q=0$ and $K_B=d=1$, the exact quadratic action and its equation are
$$
S_V^{(2)}=\frac1{16\pi G_b}\int dt\,b\left[|\dot v_V|^2-\frac{k^2}{b^2}|v_V|^2-6Hv_V\cdot\dot v_V-3H^2|v_V|^2\right],\qquad
\ddot v_V+H\dot v_V+\left(\frac{k^2}{b^2}-3\dot H\right)v_V=0.
\tag{I.13z.8a}
$$
Here $b(t)$ is the physical FLRW scale factor. Direct expansion uses $a_i=\dot v_i$, $Q_{\rm full}=Q[1+|v|^2/(2b^2)]$, $Y=Q^2|v|^2/b^2$ and $\delta(\nabla\cdot u)=[v\cdot\dot v+H|v|^2/2]/b^2$. The shift has its Einstein constraint term $k^2|B_V|^2/(2b)$ and vanishes for this source. Setting $Q=0$ yields the displayed density; integrating its mixed term once leaves $+3b\dot H|v_V|^2$, fixing the sign in its Euler equation. The physical orthonormal tilt is $y=v_V/b$. Substituting $v_V=by$, with $\dot b=Hb$, gives
$$
\ddot y+3H\dot y+\left(\frac{k^2}{b^2}+m_V^2+\dot H+2H^2\right)y
=\ddot y+3H\dot y+\left(\frac{k^2}{b^2}+2H^2-2\dot H\right)y=0.
\tag{I.13z.8b}
$$
Thus (I.13z.8) is specifically the covariant-vector coefficient. No independently sourced transverse matter sector, full scalar cosmological stability or global stability follows from its sign alone.

The data $\psi,\dot\psi$ remain initial-state inputs. For each dust density the curve (I.13z.6) gives one pair; other pairs are legitimate solutions of the same action and constraint. Limited homogeneous stability can be calculated without inferring global selection. As $s\downarrow0$,
$$
\psi=\alpha\log s+O(1),\quad \alpha^2=\frac{1-\beta}{24\pi G\beta},\quad
W\sim W_0e^{-\psi/\alpha}.
\tag{I.13z.9}
$$
For the limiting dust/exponential system, the effective cosmological coupling is $\beta G$ and $\lambda^2=3/(1-\beta)>3$. In its normalized kinetic/potential variables,
$$
x_N=-3x+\sqrt{3/2}\lambda y^2+\tfrac32x(1+x^2-y^2),\qquad
y_N=-\sqrt{3/2}\lambda xy+\tfrac32y(1+x^2-y^2).
\tag{I.13z.10}
$$
At $x=y=\sqrt{(1-\beta)/2}$ the Jacobian has trace $-3/2$, determinant $9\beta/2$ and eigenvalues $-3/4\pm(3/4)\sqrt{1-8\beta}$, both negative. This proves attraction only in that limiting homogeneous system. At the vacuum end $H_\Lambda^2=\Lambda_{\rm phys}/3$, the canonical perturbation solves
$$
\delta\ddot\psi+3H_\Lambda\delta\dot\psi+\tfrac94H_\Lambda^2\delta\psi=0,
\qquad \delta\psi=(c_1+c_2t)e^{-3H_\Lambda t/2}.
\tag{I.13z.11}
$$
The field sector is damped, while the relative dust/scalar tracking ratio can retain the second mode. No unique full-transition trajectory follows.

##### III. A specified common-clock amplitude and all its feedback terms

For $0\le A\le A_G$ retain the same constants $r,G_b$ and define
$$
L(y)=1-e^{-y^{-n}},\quad h_A(y)=y[1+AL(y)],\quad
f_A(y)=h_A(y)-ry,\quad k_A=f_A^{-1},\quad
F(z;A)=\int_0^zk_A(v)\,dv,\quad
\mathcal U(p;A)=a_\chi^2F(|p|/a_\chi;A).
\tag{I.13z.12}
$$
The inverse exists throughout the range, since $\delta_G-r\le f_A'\le1+A_G-r$. Its radial and tangential Hessians obey
$$
(1+A_G-r)^{-1}I\preceq B_s\preceq(\delta_G-r)^{-1}I.
\tag{I.13z.13}
$$
Choose the additional constitutive relation
$$
A(\psi(s))=A_G[U_c(s)-1]=A_G(1-e^{-s^{3/2}}),\qquad
J(Y,\psi)=2r\mathcal U(\sqrt Y;A(\psi)).
\tag{I.13z.14}
$$
Only this response function in the action is replaced. The potential, kinetic terms, masses and fixed gravitational/vector coefficients remain as above. As $\psi\to-\infty$, $s$ is exponentially small and the amplitude and its derivatives decay. At $\psi_\infty$ the correction is flat; extend by $A=A_G$ beyond it. Thus this is a smooth specified amplitude in $[0,A_G]$, without a moving $G$ or an inserted switching threshold.

Let $y=k_A(z)$, $z=\sqrt Y/a_\chi$. Implicit differentiation and change of variable give
$$
\partial_Ak_A(z)=-\frac{yL(y)}{h_A'(y)-r},\quad
F_A(z;A)=-\int_0^y tL(t)\,dt,\quad
J_\psi=-2ra_\chi^2A_\psi\int_0^ytL(t)\,dt,\quad
|J_\psi|\le\frac{r|A_\psi|Y}{(1-r)^2}.
\tag{I.13z.15}
$$
Write $c_J=(2-K_B)/(16\pi G_b)=1/(16\pi G_b)$. The actual canonical equation is $\Box\psi-W_\psi-c_JJ_\psi=0$. The response current contains $J_Y(Y,\psi)$ and hence its derivative includes $\partial_\mu\psi J_{Y\psi}$. The vector equation uses the same $J_Y$. With independent contravariant $u$, the contribution from $-c_JJ$ is
$$
T^{(J)}_{\mu\nu}=2c_JJ_Y\partial_\mu\phi\partial_\nu\phi-c_JJg_{\mu\nu}.
\tag{I.13z.16}
$$
The unit multiplier and other vector terms remain in the total stress. There is no metric derivative of $A$ in (I.13z.16), since $\psi$ is independent during variation. The total diffeomorphism Ward identity includes the energy exchanged through $J_\psi$; the canonical component need not be separately conserved away from the homogeneous branch.

The amplitude depends on $\psi$, not its derivatives. Thus $J_{Y\psi}$ contributes at most one derivative of a perturbation, leaving the principal Hessian as the gravity/vector/response block of Theorem I.13y at $A(\psi)$ plus the canonical wave block. The complete projectors, symmetrizer and constraint propagation apply on the uniform chamber (I.13z.13). Lower-order constants depend on bounded amplitude derivatives and field jets.

On the homogeneous branch $Q=Y=0$ one has $J(0,\psi)=J_\psi(0,\psi)=J_{\psi\psi}(0,\psi)=0$, so (I.13z.6)–(I.13z.7) remain exact. Near zero spatial gradient,
$$
J=\frac{rY}{1+A(\psi)-r}+o(Y),\qquad
J_\psi=-\frac{rA_\psi Y}{[1+A(\psi)-r]^2}+o(Y).
\tag{I.13z.17}
$$
The new canonical/response mixing consequently starts at cubic perturbation order. Its quadratic spatial coefficient is $\ell(t)=r/[1+A(\psi(t))-r]$. Time differentiation retains the actual coefficients
$$
A_N=\tfrac92A_Gs^{3/2}e^{-s^{3/2}},\qquad
\ell_N=-\frac{rA_N}{(1+A-r)^2},\qquad N=\log a_{\rm FLRW}.
\tag{I.13z.18}
$$
They are uniformly bounded. This coefficient statement does not supply radiation/recombination transport or primordial data.

##### IV. The local constitutive residual and its controlled feedback

Freeze a local canonical boundary value $\psi_b$. The retained spherical split constraints then give
$$
g=a_\chi h_{A(\psi_b)}(g_N/a_\chi),\qquad
|g-a_\chi h_{A_G}(y)|=a_\chi yL(y)A_Ge^{-s_b^{3/2}},\qquad
\frac{|g-g_{A_G}|}{g_{A_G}}\le\frac{A_G}{1+A_G}e^{-s_b^{3/2}}.
\tag{I.13z.19}
$$
The last estimate uses $0\le L\le1$ and the increasing ratio $L/(1+A_GL)$. For an already specified tolerance $\eta<A_G/(1+A_G)$, the sufficient domain is $s_b\ge\{\log[A_G/((1+A_G)\eta)]\}^{2/3}$; larger tolerances satisfy this amplitude bound for every $s_b>0$. Also $A(s)\le A_Gs^{3/2}$. These are mathematical domain bounds, without selection of an actual source state. At a finite cosmic $s$, this action generally has a different amplitude from $A_G$; an unprovided plateau is not inserted.

In the conditional slow, sub-sound-horizon limit, taking the small-gradient linearization first, the split constraints give $G_{\rm QS}(s)=[1+A(s)]G$ and leading $\Phi=\Psi$. Hence $G_{\rm QS}/(GU_c)=1+(A_G-1)s^{3/2}+O(s^3)$ at the dense end. For $A_G=1$ those two coupling functions coincide identically, without equating their full dynamical transfer. On a fixed e-fold interval within $s\le s_{\max}$, the limiting dust-growth equation differs from its matter-dominated GR coefficient equation by $O(s_{\max}+s_{\max}^{3/2})$. Subtracting the two linear second-order equations at identical initial data and applying Gronwall gives the same order solution difference. This is a result for that limiting ODE; a finite-wavenumber estimate cannot be obtained by dropping time derivatives.

On a finite smooth ball with canonical Dirichlet value $\psi_b$, the leading induced response has inverse $(-\Delta+W''(\psi_b))^{-1}$ only in the coercive regime
$$
\gamma=\lambda_D+W''(\psi_b)>0.
\tag{I.13z.20}
$$
Its constitutive forcing has $L^2$ norm at most $c_Jr\|A_\psi\|_\infty(1-r)^{-2}\||\nabla\phi|^2\|_2$. Divide this and the metric/background/time-dependent forcing norms by $\gamma$ for the $L^2$ bound; elliptic regularity supplies the corresponding $H^2$ estimate. Negative $W''$ cannot be ignored on an arbitrary large ball. The exact further coefficients satisfy
$$
F_{AA}=\frac{y^2L(y)^2}{h_A'(y)-r},\quad
|J_{\psi\psi}|\le\frac{rY}{(1-r)^2}\left[|A_{\psi\psi}|+\frac{2|A_\psi|^2}{\delta_G-r}\right],\quad
|J_{p\psi}|\le\frac{2r|A_\psi||p|}{(1-r)(\delta_G-r)},\quad p=\nabla_\perp\phi.
\tag{I.13z.21}
$$
These follow by another implicit derivative of (I.13z.15), including both $A_{\psi\psi}F_A$ and $A_\psi^2F_{AA}$. In the fixed-chart weak-field family $\nabla\phi=O(\varepsilon)$ and $a_\chi=O(\varepsilon)$, the canonical diagonal perturbation is $O(\varepsilon^2)$ and the mixed block $O(\varepsilon)$ between the $H^1$ energy spaces. The response Dirichlet inverse is bounded by (I.13z.13), so its Schur correction is $O(\varepsilon^2)$. Require the sum of this correction, the canonical diagonal perturbation and the local $W$ Taylor variation to be at most $\gamma/2$. The coupled elliptic implicit-function theorem then gives a nearby actual solution and canonical inverse norm at most $2/\gamma$. Boundary and rolling-background forcing obey the same neighborhood bound. Forcing size remains explicit. Lift a nonzero boundary perturbation by a specified smooth $b_\psi$ and let $r_{\rm other}$ be the remaining metric/background/time-dependent forcing after the lift. Put $\mathcal F_\psi=\|r_{\rm other}\|_2+\|b_\psi\|_{H^2}$. The inverse and elliptic regularity bounds yield
$$
\|\delta\psi\|_{H^2}\le C_\gamma(\varepsilon^2+\mathcal F_\psi),\qquad
\|\delta A\|\le C(\varepsilon^2+\mathcal F_\psi),\qquad
\|\hbox{extra scalar flux}\|\le C(\varepsilon^3+\varepsilon\mathcal F_\psi)
\tag{I.13z.21a}
$$
in the corresponding controlled elliptic norms, with fixed-domain regularity constants and bounded amplitude derivatives. The $\varepsilon^2$ term is the constitutive forcing above; all other forcing and boundary lift remain counted. The orders $\delta\psi=O(\varepsilon^2)$, $\delta A=O(\varepsilon^2)$ and extra flux $O(\varepsilon^3)$ hold only when $\mathcal F_\psi=O(\varepsilon^2)$, including zero extra forcing. Arbitrary small forcing sufficient for local existence alone does not imply these orders. Other gauge/source/rolling errors remain separate.

Under $x_{\rm phys}=\varepsilon x$, $t_{\rm phys}=\varepsilon t$, the actual fixed-action chart conversion is $a_{\chi,\rm chart}=\varepsilon a_{\chi,\rm phys}$, $\Lambda_{\rm chart}=\varepsilon^2\Lambda$ (with $\Lambda$ the fixed physical action parameter and $\Lambda_{\rm phys}=\Lambda/D$ its homogeneous effective value) and $W_{\rm chart}=\varepsilon^2W_{\rm phys}$, with dimensionless $A,r,\beta$ fixed. The homogeneous canonical stress is chart order $\varepsilon^2$, below a clump density of order $\varepsilon$. This retains the leading local equations on the stated shrinking domain and duration; it is not an orbital-time or all-radius equilibrium. The stationary transverse-current coefficient stays $G_b/G=r/2$ when the canonical scalar has no leading transverse gradient/current. The full selected source, complete perturbation transfer and registered empirical residuals remain separate from the proved action and local solution statements. $\square$

<a id="theorem-i13aa-a-positive-moving-source-and-rolling-background-on-one-local-causal-domain"></a>**Theorem I.13aa (A Positive Moving Source and Rolling Background on One Local Causal Domain).** Retain the physical single-metric action of Theorems I.13x–I.13y, optionally with the canonical potential and common-clock amplitude of Theorem I.13z. There is a smooth, constraint-compatible, positive collisionless source family on a common finite chart interval containing two separated moving nonspherical populations. The same local solution can contain a regular rolling homogeneous canonical state and conserved massive or massless background populations. The estimates below concern a shrinking physical domain and duration under the exact fixed-action homothety; they are not an orbital-time merger or a global cosmological gluing theorem.

##### I. The positive source, its normalization and its local evolution

Use a nonnegative smooth distribution $f$ on $g^{\mu\nu}p_\mu p_\nu=-m_b^2$, $m_b>0$, with compact initial momentum support. A variational realization is the fixed nonnegative worldline-label measure in Theorem I.13x. Its geodesic equation and pushed-forward distribution obey
$$
p^\mu\partial_\mu f-\Gamma^i_{\alpha\beta}p^\alpha p^\beta\partial_{p^i}f=0,
\qquad T^{ab}=\int f\,p^ap^b\frac{d^3p}{p^0}
\tag{I.13aa.1}
$$
in an orthonormal frame. Mass-shell integration by parts, with zero compact-support boundary term, gives $\nabla_aT^{ab}=0$ and conservation of the particle current. Each future massive momentum is timelike; the nonnegative integral satisfies the dominant energy condition. All source, vector and scalar fields couple to this same physical metric.

The source moment is algebraic in $f$ in the gravitational derivative reduction, and its transport connection is algebraic in that reduction's first-order fields. Hence no second-derivative mixing is added. On bounded momentum support, differentiated transport energy and the full symmetrizer of Theorem I.13y close the coupled local estimate. For integer $s\ge8$, take field first-order variables in $H_x^s$, distributions in $H_{x,p}^s$ and compact momentum supports. Sobolev product bounds in dimensions three and six and Cauchy–Schwarz for velocity moments bound the source maps. The force bound retains bounded momentum support on a short interval. Regularized iteration yields smooth local evolution for constraint-compatible data, with the physical-metric causal domain. This is a positive classical source class; no identification with a microscopic predictive carrier is made.

Put $\varepsilon=e^2>0$, $p=m_be w$, and prescribe in a local orthonormal frame
$$
f_\varepsilon(x,p)=\frac{\varepsilon}{m_b(m_be)^3}F_0(x,p/(m_be)),\quad
\rho_0=\int F_0\,dw,\quad F_0\ge0,\quad\operatorname{supp}_wF_0\subset\{|w|\le V\}.
\tag{I.13aa.2}
$$
The exact initial moments and bounds are
$$
\begin{aligned}
T^{00}&=\varepsilon\int\sqrt{1+\varepsilon|w|^2}F_0\,dw,&
0\le T^{00}-\varepsilon\rho_0&\le\tfrac12\varepsilon^2V^2\rho_0,\\
T^{0i}&=\varepsilon^{3/2}\int w_iF_0\,dw,& |T^{0i}|&\le\varepsilon^{3/2}V\rho_0,\\
T^{ij}&=\varepsilon^2\int\frac{w_iw_jF_0}{\sqrt{1+\varepsilon|w|^2}}\,dw,& |T^{ij}|&\le\varepsilon^2V^2\rho_0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.13aa.3}
$$
The inequalities use $\sqrt{1+x}-1\le x/2$. The actual initial rest mass on a set $B$ is $\varepsilon\int_B\rho_0\sqrt{\det\gamma_\varepsilon}\,d^3x=\varepsilon\int_B\rho_0\,d^3x+O(\varepsilon^2)$; alternatively include this volume factor in the initial label density. An even nonnegative compact velocity bump $\chi$ of integral one realizes every smooth positive density by $F_0=\rho_0\chi$ and gives zero initial current.

##### II. One joint nonlinear field and simultaneous exact constraints

Fix a smooth bounded ball $\Omega$, smooth compact nonnegative densities $\rho_1,\rho_2$ with positive masses and initial support gap $d_0>0$. Let $\chi$ be even, supported in $|w|\le\sigma$, and use
$$
F_{i,0}(x,w)=\rho_i(x)\chi(w-U_i),\qquad U_1=U\widehat e,\quad U_2=-U\widehat e,\quad U>0.
\tag{I.13aa.4}
$$
Here the centroid difference is parallel to $\widehat e$ and the velocity means point inward. Both species have the same rest mass and metric and distinguish disjoint conserved worldline-label populations. Set $\rho_0=\rho_1+\rho_2$. For a chosen local amplitude $A_0\in[0,A_G]$, set $a_{\chi,\rm chart}=\varepsilon a_*$ and solve the single Dirichlet pair
$$
\Delta v_0=4\pi rG\rho_0,\qquad
\operatorname{div}\mathcal A_s(\nabla s_0;A_0)=4\pi G\rho_0,\qquad
\Phi_0=v_0+s_0=\Psi_0,
\tag{I.13aa.5}
$$
where $\mathcal A_s(p;A)=\partial_p\mathcal U_*(p;A)$ and $\mathcal U_*=a_*^2F(|p|/a_*;A)$ uses (I.13z.12), or its constant-amplitude specialization in Theorem I.13x. Its Hessian has fixed bounds $mI\preceq D\mathcal A_s\preceq MI$, $m>0$. The strictly convex Dirichlet functional gives a unique $H^1$ solution and elliptic regularity gives the needed smoothness for smooth compatible boundary data. The response to $\rho_1+\rho_2$ is not the sum of two separate nonlinear solutions.

This class is nonempty with nonspherical sources: choose $\Omega=B(0,10)$, centers $(-3,0,0),(3,0,0)$ and bumps proportional to $\exp[-1/(1-|B_i(x-c_i)|^2)]$ on $|B_i(x-c_i)|<1$, zero outside, with $B_1=\operatorname{diag}(1,2,3)$ and $B_2=\operatorname{diag}(2,1,3)$. Normalize to any positive masses; use $U=1$, $\sigma=1/10$ and zero Dirichlet potentials. The support gap is at least four. These are explicit existence data, without measured-source calibration.

Start with $N=e^{\varepsilon\Phi_0}$, $\gamma_{ij}=e^{-2\varepsilon\Phi_0}\delta_{ij}$, $\phi=\varepsilon s_0$, $u_i=0$ and $Q=0$. Set the normal aether derivative so $a_i=D_i\log N$. The aether canonical momentum need not vanish, but its spatial constraint term $\pi_u^jD_iu_j-D_j(\pi_u^ju_i)$ does vanish on these data. The response momentum vanishes at $Q=u_i=0$. With divergence coefficient $d=1$ and $K_B=1$, the actual metric kinetic and momentum terms are
$$
K_{ij}K^{ij}-2K^2,\qquad
D_j[K^j{}_i-2K\delta^j_i]=-8\pi G_bJ_i,\quad J_i=-T_{ni}.
\tag{I.13aa.6}
$$
The static lapse expression obtained by variation before imposing that lapse equation is
$$
\begin{aligned}
C_{\rm stat}={}&R(\gamma)-2\Lambda_{\rm chart}-2\Delta_\gamma\log N-|D\log N|^2\\
&-2\Delta_\gamma\phi-[|D\phi|^2+J(|D\phi|^2,\psi_0)].
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.13aa.7}
$$
For time-symmetric zero-current data its leading lapse constraint is $2\Delta\Psi_0-\Delta\Phi_0-\Delta s_0=8\pi G_b\rho_0$, which holds by $G_b=rG/2$ and (I.13aa.5). The residual is $O(\varepsilon^2)$. Keeping $N,\phi$ and the even matter labels fixed, the rescaled conformal correction has linearization $2\Delta:H^{s+2}\cap H_0^1\to H^s$, a Dirichlet isomorphism. Thus the implicit-function theorem supplies an exact constraint correction of unscaled size $O(\varepsilon^2)$.

For moving populations take $K_{ij}=e^3(L_\gamma W_{\rm vec})_{ij}$, where
$$
(L_\gamma W_{\rm vec})_{ij}=D_iW_j+D_jW_i-\tfrac23\gamma_{ij}D_kW^k.
\tag{I.13aa.8}
$$
The zero-Dirichlet leading momentum equation is
$$
\Delta W_i+\tfrac13\partial_i\operatorname{div}W=-8\pi G_b\sum_a\rho_aU_{a,i}.
\tag{I.13aa.9}
$$
Integration by parts gives the negative form $-\tfrac12\int|LW|^2$. A conformal Killing field with zero boundary trace is zero, so the kernel vanishes and coercivity/elliptic regularity give the inverse. The exact Hamiltonian equation adds $-K_{ij}K^{ij}+2K^2=O(e^6)$ and the kinetic-source correction is $O(e^4)$. The joint conformal/York linearization at zero is block diagonal $(2\Delta,\Delta+\tfrac13\nabla\operatorname{div})$: cross derivatives vanish because the momentum limit uses the flat metric and fixed leading current and $K^2$ enters at higher order. The joint implicit-function theorem supplies exact data, an unscaled conformal correction $O(e^4)$ and $K=O(e^3)$, retaining positivity, compact momentum support and the scalar ellipticity chamber.

##### III. A rolling homogeneous state and the exact cancellation

Choose a regular expanding homogeneous solution of the same action on $Q=0$, with a canonical value $\psi_0$ in a compact regular interval, $P_0=\dot\psi_0$, Hubble rate $H_0$ and actual positive homogeneous particle distributions of total energy density $\rho_{{\rm bg},0}$. It obeys
$$
3DH_0^2=\Lambda+8\pi G_b[\rho_{{\rm bg},0}+P_0^2/2+W(\psi_0)],\qquad D=5/2.
\tag{I.13aa.10}
$$
Homogeneous massive distributions retain their actual energy, pressure and redshifting momentum moments. Smooth compact momentum profiles, and massless profiles separated from zero momentum, may be used. A positive-dispersion source is not silently identified with the exact cold power-clock trajectory. The chosen background data are inputs, without source selection.

The exact active homothety is
$$
\begin{gathered}
x_{\rm phys}=\varepsilon x,\quad t_{\rm phys}=\varepsilon t,\quad
a_{\chi,\rm chart}=\varepsilon a_{\chi,\rm phys},\quad
\Lambda_{\rm chart}=\varepsilon^2\Lambda,\quad W_{\rm chart}=\varepsilon^2W,\\
H_{\rm chart}=\varepsilon H_0,\quad P_{\rm chart}=\varepsilon P_0,\quad
f_{{\rm bg},\rm chart}(x,p)=\varepsilon^2f_{{\rm bg},\rm phys}(\varepsilon x,p).
\end{gathered}
\tag{I.13aa.11}
$$
The physical rest masses and momenta and dimensionless constitutive data do not change. Thus the background chart energy is exactly $\varepsilon^2\rho_{{\rm bg},0}$. Use $A_0=A(\psi_0)$, and instead of trace zero prescribe
$$
K_{ij}=\varepsilon H_0\gamma_{ij}+e^3(L_\gamma W_{\rm vec})_{ij},\quad K=3\varepsilon H_0,\quad
\psi=\psi_0,\quad n(\psi)=\varepsilon P_0.
\tag{I.13aa.12}
$$
Homogeneous distributions are prescribed in the local orthonormal frame with zero flux, smoothly depending on $\gamma$. Canonical spatial momentum is zero and the constant trace has zero covariant derivative, so (I.13aa.9) is unchanged. The exact Hamiltonian equation is
$$
C_{\rm stat}-K_{ij}K^{ij}+2K^2
=16\pi G_b[\rho_{\rm cl}+\varepsilon^2\rho_{{\rm bg},0}+\varepsilon^2(P_0^2/2+W(\psi_0))].
\tag{I.13aa.13}
$$
Trace-freeness gives
$$
-K_{ij}K^{ij}+2K^2=6D\varepsilon^2H_0^2-e^6|L_\gamma W_{\rm vec}|^2,
\quad
6D\varepsilon^2H_0^2-2\varepsilon^2\Lambda
=16\pi G_b\varepsilon^2[\rho_{{\rm bg},0}+P_0^2/2+W(\psi_0)].
\tag{I.13aa.14}
$$
The homogeneous terms cancel by the actual constraint, rather than being neglected. The same joint Dirichlet implicit-function theorem now supplies exact rolling-background/clump data; the conformal correction is $O(e^4)$ and the additional tracefree curvature $O(e^3)$.

##### IV. The actual reduced gauge and the two-scale energy estimate

The finite and limiting states must be compared in the same gauge. Prepare the spatial modified-harmonic condition by its zero-Dirichlet spatial coordinate equation. At leading order, if $H^i_{\rm raw}=\widetilde\eta^{\alpha\beta}\Gamma_1^i{}_{\alpha\beta}(h_{\rm raw})$, solve $\Delta\xi^i=H^i_{\rm raw}$ and transform $h\mapsto h-2\partial_{(\mu}\xi_{\nu)}$. Its unscaled displacement is $O(\varepsilon)$, so it changes the normalized metric by $O(1)$; include it in both comparisons. The full exact coordinate preparation has the same invertible linearization. For nonzero curvature choose initial lapse and shift derivatives through the invertible gauge-normal block of Theorem I.13y, rather than imposing time symmetry. This sets $H^\mu=0$ initially. The exact original constraints set its normal derivative to zero, and its homogeneous propagation preserves it.

In comoving physical comparison coordinates the leading fields are
$$
h_{00}=-2\Phi_0,\quad h_{0i}=0,\quad
h_{ij}=-2\Phi_0\delta_{ij}+2H_0t\delta_{ij},\quad
\psi=\psi_0+\varepsilon\chi,\quad \chi=P_0t.
\tag{I.13aa.15}
$$
The homogeneous mode alone has $H^0=3H_0$. With $v_g=4/5$ and $\widetilde\eta^{00}=-1/v_g^2$, the lower-component gauge generator $\xi_0^{(g)}=(3/2)v_g^2H_0t^2$, $\xi_i^{(g)}=0$, produces $h_{00}^{(g)}=-6v_g^2H_0t$ and hence
$$
H^0=(2v_g^2)^{-1}\partial_t h_{00}^{(g)}+3H_0=0,\qquad H^i=0.
\tag{I.13aa.16}
$$
Transform the aether covector too: its unit-fixed component is $\delta u_0=h_{00}/2$ and its spatial components remain zero under this temporal transformation. Add the static spatial gauge correction already specified. Their sum, with $\chi=P_0t$, is the actual reduced-gauge limiting solution; this order-$\varepsilon$ lapse mode is not included in an $e^3$ error.
