For a local inertial comparison, the generator $\xi_i=H_0tx_i$, $\xi_0=-H_0|x|^2/2$ removes the spatial homogeneous expansion mode and leaves $h_{0i}=0$. The normalized aether acquires $u_i/\varepsilon=H_0x_i$, whose curl vanishes and divergence is constant $3H_0$. The divergence-squared vector force therefore vanishes at leading order and self-acceleration is $O(\varepsilon^2)$. The scalar transformation includes $-\varepsilon^2H_0t,x\cdot\nabla s_0$, cancelling the corresponding $u^i\partial_i\phi$ term in $Q$ at that order. This does not assert exact $Q=0$ in the inhomogeneous evolution or gauge-removal of physical background expansion.

Apply the change only to an interior tube of an already constructed common two-sided slab, with spatial margin and time buffer $T_{\rm buf}$. Require $\varepsilon|H_0|\sup_{\rm tube}|x|^2/2<T_{\rm buf}$. The slice shift changes known leading field data by $O(\varepsilon^2)$ and clump data within their $O(e)$ normalized bound. Use the same bounded diffeomorphisms on the finite and limiting solutions after the difference estimate.

The clumps evolve in $(x,w)$ with $p=m_be w$, while homogeneous massive distributions evolve as $f_{\rm bg}=\varepsilon^2F_{\rm bg}$ in their original compact physical $p$ variables; null distributions similarly retain support away from zero. Placing the latter in $w$ would create a false unbounded $1/e$ support. In the first-order reduction the exact clump equation is
$$
\partial_tF+e[w\cdot\nabla_xF-\nabla\Phi\cdot\nabla_wF]=O(e^2)
\tag{I.13aa.17}
$$
with bounded coefficient in the stated Sobolev norms. Its zero-parameter limit is stationary. Normalized background source moments are $O(\varepsilon)$; their speeds are bounded by one and connection coefficients are $O(\varepsilon)$. The canonical block has a fixed wave principal part and $O(\varepsilon)$ forcing after division by $\varepsilon$, since $W_{\rm chart,\psi}$ and $J_{\rm chart,\psi}$ are $O(\varepsilon^2)$. Thus $A(\psi)=A_0+O_T(\varepsilon)$ on the fixed clock interval.

Extend both finite data and their parameter expansion smoothly to a common compact auxiliary torus. Evolve the limiting extension by its own equations; do not falsely declare an arbitrary exterior extension static. Domain of dependence identifies it with the specified leading fields on the causal interior. Exterior constraint errors cannot enter this interior. The direct sum of the gravitational symmetrizer and separate bounded-momentum transport/wave energies is uniformly controlled. The clump transport/current defect is $O(e)$ and the added rolling/background defects are $O(e^2)$. The squared normalized difference energy satisfies
$$
E_{\rm diff}'\le CE_{\rm diff}+Ce^2,\qquad E_{\rm diff}(0)\le Ce^2
\tag{I.13aa.18}
$$
on a common fixed chart interval $[0,T]$, below the local lifespan and boundary causal distance. In the static even-source subclass the sharper initial bound is $Ce^4$. Uniform coefficient/initial derivative suprema on the fixed bootstrap set determine $C$. Gronwall and bootstrap close the estimate, yielding
$$
\|g_\varepsilon-g_{\rm lead,\varepsilon}\|_{C^2}+\|\phi_\varepsilon-\varepsilon s_0\|_{C^2}\le C_T\varepsilon^{3/2},\quad
\|F_i(t)-F_{i,0}\|_{H^{s-q_{\rm loss}}}\le C_Te,\quad
\psi=\psi_0+\varepsilon P_0t+O_T(\varepsilon e).
\tag{I.13aa.19}
$$
Choose a fixed derivative loss $q_{\rm loss}$ below the initial Sobolev regularity to control coordinate pullbacks and source moments; $s\ge8$ leaves $C^2$ metric and $C^1$ force control on a smaller interior. The normalized clock forcing actually has the stronger $O(\varepsilon)$ order, not needed for the displayed bound.

##### V. Actual source motion, lensing and stable aperture readouts

Characteristics satisfy $\dot x=ew+O(e^2)$ and $\dot w=-e\nabla\Phi_0+O(e^2)$. Their conserved-label centroids therefore satisfy
$$
\begin{aligned}
x(t)&=x_0+ew_0t+O(e^2(t+t^2)),\\
c_i(t)&=c_i(0)+eU_it+O(e^2(t+t^2)),\\
\operatorname{dist}(\operatorname{supp}_xF_1(t),\operatorname{supp}_xF_2(t))
&\ge d_0-2e(U+\sigma)T-C_Te^2(T+T^2).
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.13aa.20}
$$
Use the initial measure $\rho_i\sqrt{\det\gamma_\varepsilon}\,d^3x$, not uncorrected coordinate volume; its centroid differs from the latter by $O(e^2)$. For small $e$ the supports remain separated and their centroid separation decreases to leading order, without reaching overlap at time $O(1/e)$.

For $\rho_t=\sum_i\int F_i(t,w)\,dw$, solve the same joint Dirichlet pair at time $t$. Subtracting its weak scalar equations and using monotonicity gives
$$
m\|\nabla(s_t-s_0)\|_2\le4\pi G\|\rho_t-\rho_0\|_{H^{-1}}.
\tag{I.13aa.21}
$$
Poisson gives the analogous bound for $v_t$. Differentiated uniform elliptic estimates on the bounded smooth set improve this to the required lower $C^2$ norm, with size $C_Te$. Thus the exact dynamical metric differs from its instantaneous joint elliptic readout by $C_T\varepsilon^{3/2}$. This comparison uses the actual evolution; it is not instantaneous propagation of the physical dynamics.

On a finite noncaustic optical tube within the causal interior, keep the initial/end frames fixed in the local comparison gauge, or retain/subtract the known homogeneous observer-frame term in comoving coordinates. Geodesic smooth dependence then gives
$$
\alpha_\varepsilon(b,t)=2\varepsilon\int_{\rm path}\nabla_\perp\Phi_t(b,z)\,dz+O_T(\varepsilon^{3/2}).
\tag{I.13aa.22}
$$
It also controls the first transverse derivative on a smaller tube. Path displacement and quadratic metric corrections are $O(\varepsilon^2)$. Currents are retained in the larger stated error. The same joint potential determines both massive-particle acceleration and light deflection. In the spherical static subclass the acceleration is $\varepsilon a_*h(GM_0(R)/(a_*R^2))+O(\varepsilon^{3/2})$ on annuli away from zero. The actual enclosed mass is $\varepsilon M_0+O(\varepsilon^{3/2})$ and the global Lipschitz bound for $h$ permits this same-order substitution, retaining the initial volume/areal-radius correction.

For smooth bounded nonnegative aperture weight $w(b)$, put
$$
L_t=(4\pi G)^{-1}\int\Delta_\perp\Phi_t\,dz,\quad
C_L=\frac{\int b wL_t}{\int wL_t},\quad
L_{\rm exact}=\frac{\operatorname{div}_\perp\alpha_\varepsilon}{8\pi G\varepsilon}.
\tag{I.13aa.23}
$$
If $\int wL_t\ge m_L>0$, then $\|L_{\rm exact}-L_t\|_\infty\le C_Te$. For $C_Te\|w\|_1\le m_L/2$ the exact denominator stays at least $m_L/2$, and the exact ratio identity yields
$$
|C_{\rm exact}-C_L|\le\frac{2C_Te}{m_L}[\|bw\|_1+|C_L|\|w\|_1].
\tag{I.13aa.24}
$$
The leading $L_t$ can change sign; $|C_L|$ cannot be replaced by the aperture radius without further positivity. It is finite here, or bounded by $\|bw\|_1\|L_t\|_\infty/m_L$. Combining with (I.13aa.20) controls offsets relative to either conserved source centroid. It predicts no universal nonzero offset, gas lag or peak location without their additional physical or nondegeneracy data.

##### VI. Fixed-action units and the owned cluster-kernel discrepancy

The full equations map by
$$
g_{\rm phys}(t,x)=g_{\rm chart}(t/\varepsilon,x/\varepsilon),\quad
\phi_{\rm phys}(t,x)=\phi_{\rm chart}(t/\varepsilon,x/\varepsilon),\quad
f_{\rm phys}(t,x,p)=\varepsilon^{-2}f_{\rm chart}(t/\varepsilon,x/\varepsilon,p),
\tag{I.13aa.25}
$$
with the same rest masses and the parameter conversion (I.13aa.11). Geometric/source tensors scale by $\varepsilon^{-2}$ and both Liouville terms by $\varepsilon^{-3}$. Every extra inverse-length parameter must scale by $\varepsilon$ in the chart; the quadratic temporal response used here needs no such parameter. The fixed physical action then has clump density $O(\varepsilon^{-1})$, mass $O(\varepsilon^2)$, size $O(\varepsilon)$, speed $O(e)$ and guaranteed duration $\varepsilon T$, shorter than crossing/orbital duration $O(e)$. Physical centroid/length errors acquire an extra factor $\varepsilon$; physical acceleration error is $O(e)$ and the dimensionless deflection error remains $O(\varepsilon^{3/2})$. Physical homogeneous curvature stays $O(1)$; its chart curvature is $O(\varepsilon^2)$ because the domain shrinks. These limits do not establish a fixed-size equilibrium or remove an independently applicable microscopic cutoff.

For the original cluster projection I.7, retain the registered physical kernel, threshold and source extension. Its normalized pullback is
$$
K_\varepsilon(x)=\varepsilon^3K_{\rm phys}(\varepsilon x;L_{0,\rm phys}),\quad\int K_\varepsilon dx=1,\qquad
\rho_{{\rm resp},t}=(r-1)\rho_t+(4\pi G)^{-1}\Delta s_t.
\tag{I.13aa.26}
$$
Replacing it by one fixed chart kernel is valid only for a supplied scale-covariant family, such as $L_{0,\rm phys}=\varepsilon L_{0,*}$ and $K_{\rm phys}=L_{0,\rm phys}^{-3}k(x/L_{0,\rm phys})$. The threshold $g_*$ is physical acceleration. With $\Delta\Phi_{b,t}=4\pi G\rho_t$ and its actual background subtraction/boundary record, the leading normalized discrepancy is
$$
\mathcal D_{{\rm cl},t,\varepsilon}=\rho_{{\rm resp},t}
 -A_{\rm PM}K_\varepsilon*[\rho_t(|\nabla\Phi_{b,t}|/g_*)^q].
\tag{I.13aa.27}
$$
A local Dirichlet chart does not determine the convolution's global extension. Once it is supplied, this is a definite map without fitting $K,q,A_{\rm PM}$ to its output. For a smooth compactly supported weak test $f$ with $\|f\|_\infty,\|\nabla f\|_\infty\le1$, extend $f$ by zero. Positivity and unit mass of $K_\varepsilon$ give
$$
|\mathcal D_{{\rm cl},t,\varepsilon}[f]|\le|r-1|M_t+\frac{\|\nabla s_t\|_{L^1(\operatorname{supp}\nabla f)}}{4\pi G}+A_{\rm PM}M_{w,t},\quad
M_t=\int\rho_t,\quad M_{w,t}=\int\rho_t(|\nabla\Phi_{b,t}|/g_*)^q.
\tag{I.13aa.28}
$$
The original integrability premise makes $M_{w,t}$ finite; a uniform interval bound retains its finite time supremum and any $q<0$ zero-acceleration exclusion. The exact finite-parameter local readout, pulled back and multiplied by $\varepsilon$ to these normalized density units, differs from its leading source by $O_T(e)$ in the controlled weak norm. Comparing the nonlinear weight also retains its bounded modulus of continuity on the specified source/acceleration domain; for $q<0$ this requires the stated positive acceleration margin. Apply that modulus to the known source/force errors. For tests $f(x_{\rm phys}/\varepsilon)$ the integrated physical mass residual has factor $\varepsilon^2$. This is a computable finite weak residual, not a pointwise stress equality, an asserted small empirical residual or a choice of the registered kernel. The local nonlinear map may instead be compared to an explicitly accepted replacement. The original full cluster/source/window residual is retained beyond the proved finite collisionless overlap. $\square$

<a id="theorem-i13ab-the-movingrolling-finite-window-metric-hierarchy"></a>**Theorem I.13ab (The Moving/Rolling Finite-Window Metric Hierarchy).** Use the exact positive source and common rolling solution of Theorem I.13aa, with its fixed physical action and actual reduced gauge. There is a uniquely specified metric through order $e^4$, including moving density, currents, pressure, nonlinear field terms and conserved homogeneous/clock sources. Its coefficient fields solve the triangular initial-value problems below, with metric/readout remainder $O(e^5)$ on a fixed interior chart interval. This is a local chart-time expansion, not an orbital-time limit or a frozen-symbol replacement of the source equations.

##### I. Family, regularity and coefficient convention

Put $\varepsilon=e^2$ and
$$
g=\eta+e^2h,\quad u_i=e^2v_i,\quad\phi=e^2s,\quad\psi=\psi_0+e^2\chi,\quad
 a_{\chi,\rm chart}=e^2a_*,\quad\Lambda_{\rm chart}=e^4\Lambda,\quad W_{\rm chart}=e^4W.
\tag{I.13ab.1}
$$
Keep every physical/chart conversion, static spatial gauge correction and leading homogeneous lapse mode of Theorem I.13aa. Work on a compact causal interior and fixed chart interval $[0,T]$, with its spatial and two-sided time buffers. Use smooth fixed spatial and compact momentum profiles and the exact joint constraint/gauge data there; a singular circular measure is not inserted in this Cauchy theorem. For example take first-order fields and distributions bounded in $H^{s+4}$, $s\ge8$, with uniform compact momentum, metric, slice and ellipticity margins. Four spare spatial/phase-space derivatives are used below.

The rescaled coefficients and data are $C^3$ in $e$ into lower norms. First rewrite $J$ as $e^4$ times its smooth fixed-scale function; no artificial $0/0$ is differentiated. Negative $e$ may define a smooth parameter extension using the positive momentum Jacobian $|m_be|^3$. Rescaled moment equations extend smoothly; only the physical branch $e\ge0$ is used in Taylor's estimate. Homogeneous particles retain their separate unscaled momenta. There is no $1/e$ evolution generator on this chart interval.

##### II. Complete action coefficients

Use $\eta$ to raise leading indices and write $h=\eta^{\mu\nu}h_{\mu\nu}$. Set
$$
a_{1,i}=\partial_tv_i-\tfrac12\partial_ih_{00},\quad
\theta_1=\partial_i(v_i-h_{0i})+\tfrac12\partial_th_{ii},\quad
F_{1,ij}=\partial_iv_j-\partial_jv_i.
\tag{I.13ab.2}
$$
After removing the Einstein boundary divergence, the leading density is
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal L_{4,g}&=\frac1{16\pi G_b}\left[\mathcal L_{\rm FP}+a_{1,i}a_{1,i}-\tfrac12F_{1,ij}F_{1,ij}-\theta_1^2+2a_{1,i}\partial_is-|\nabla s|^2-2r\mathcal U_*(\nabla s;A_0)+10\dot s^2\right],\\
\mathcal L_{\rm FP}&=-\tfrac14\partial_\lambda h_{\mu\nu}\partial^\lambda h^{\mu\nu}+\tfrac12(\partial_\mu h^{\mu\nu})(\partial^\rho h_{\rho\nu})-\tfrac12(\partial_\mu h^{\mu\nu})\partial_\nu h+\tfrac14\partial_\lambda h\partial^\lambda h.
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.13ab.3}
$$
Here $A_0=A(\psi_0)$, or the fixed amplitude in the constant-amplitude specialization, and $\mathcal U_*$ is (I.13aa.5). The canonical leading density is $\mathcal L_{4,\psi}=-(\partial\chi)^2/2-W(\psi_0)$; its constant has no field Euler derivative at this order. The leading clump coupling is $\rho h_{00}/2$.

The cubic density has a finite coefficient-extraction definition from the actual action:
$$
C_{6,g}=[e^6]\frac{\sqrt{-g}}{16\pi G_b}\left[R-\tfrac12F_u^2-(\nabla\cdot u)^2+2a^\mu\partial_\mu\phi-Y-J(Y;A_0)+10Q^2\right].
\tag{I.13ab.4}
$$
Insert (I.13ab.1), solve the future unit root for $u_0$, and replace $J$ by its exactly equal $e^4$ fixed-scale expression. All local tensors are those defined in Theorem I.13x. Equivalently use $\partial_e^6/6!$ of this specified smooth density at zero. It is a finite definition, not a premise that an unknown effective tensor exists. The needed series are
$$
\begin{aligned}
g^{\mu\nu}&=\eta^{\mu\nu}-e^2h^{\mu\nu}+e^4h^\mu{}_{\alpha}h^{\alpha\nu}+O(e^6),\\
\sqrt{-g}&=1+e^2h/2+e^4(h^2/8-h_{\mu\nu}h^{\mu\nu}/4)+O(e^6),\\
u_0&=-1+e^2h_{00}/2+e^4[h_{00}^2/8-|v_i-h_{0i}|^2/2]+O(e^6),\\
\Gamma^\alpha_{\mu\nu}&=\tfrac12g^{\alpha\beta}(\partial_\mu g_{\beta\nu}+\partial_\nu g_{\beta\mu}-\partial_\beta g_{\mu\nu}),\\
R^\alpha{}_{\beta\mu\nu}&=\partial_\mu\Gamma^\alpha_{\nu\beta}-\partial_\nu\Gamma^\alpha_{\mu\beta}+\Gamma^\alpha_{\mu\lambda}\Gamma^\lambda_{\nu\beta}-\Gamma^\alpha_{\nu\lambda}\Gamma^\lambda_{\mu\beta}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.13ab.5}
$$
An expanded recipe removes even the coefficient notation. Put
$$
\begin{gathered}
u^{(0)}_\mu=-\delta^0_\mu,\quad u^{(1)}_\mu=(h_{00}/2,v_i),\quad u^{(2)}_\mu=(h_{00}^2/8-|v-h_{0i}|^2/2,0),\\
U_0^\mu=\delta_0^\mu,\quad U_1^\mu=\eta^{\mu\nu}u^{(1)}_\nu-h^{\mu\nu}u^{(0)}_\nu,\\
U_2^\mu=\eta^{\mu\nu}u^{(2)}_\nu-h^{\mu\nu}u^{(1)}_\nu+h^\mu{}_{\alpha}h^{\alpha\nu}u^{(0)}_\nu,\\
\Gamma_1^\alpha{}_{\mu\nu}=\tfrac12\eta^{\alpha\beta}(\partial_\mu h_{\beta\nu}+\partial_\nu h_{\beta\mu}-\partial_\beta h_{\mu\nu}),\quad\Gamma_2^\alpha{}_{\mu\nu}=-h^\alpha{}_{\beta}\Gamma_1^\beta{}_{\mu\nu},\\
F_{j,\mu\nu}=\partial_\mu u^{(j)}_\nu-\partial_\nu u^{(j)}_\mu\quad(j=1,2),\\
\theta_1=\partial_\mu U_1^\mu+\Gamma_1^\mu{}_{\mu0},\quad\theta_2=\partial_\mu U_2^\mu+\Gamma_1^\mu{}_{\mu\nu}U_1^\nu+\Gamma_2^\mu{}_{\mu0},\\
a_{1,\mu}=\partial_0u^{(1)}_\mu+\Gamma_1^0{}_{0\mu},\\
a_{2,\mu}=\partial_0u^{(2)}_\mu+\Gamma_2^0{}_{0\mu}-\Gamma_1^\beta{}_{0\mu}u^{(1)}_\beta+U_1^\alpha(\partial_\alpha u^{(1)}_\mu+\Gamma_1^0{}_{\alpha\mu}),\\
q_1=\partial_0s,\quad q_2=U_1^\mu\partial_\mu s,\quad Y_0=|\nabla s|^2,\\
Y_1=(-h^{\mu\nu}+U_0^\mu U_1^\nu+U_1^\mu U_0^\nu)\partial_\mu s\partial_\nu s,\quad j(Y_0)=2r\mathcal U_*(\sqrt{Y_0};A_0).
\end{gathered}
\tag{I.13ab.6}
$$
The radial value is intended in $\mathcal U_*(\sqrt{Y_0};A_0)$. All contractions below use $\eta$. Define
$$
\begin{aligned}
E_{6,\rm EH}={}&(h\eta^{\mu\nu}/2-h^{\mu\nu})(\Gamma_1^\alpha{}_{\mu\beta}\Gamma_1^\beta{}_{\nu\alpha}-\Gamma_1^\alpha{}_{\mu\nu}\Gamma_1^\beta{}_{\alpha\beta})\\
&+\eta^{\mu\nu}(\Gamma_2^\alpha{}_{\mu\beta}\Gamma_1^\beta{}_{\nu\alpha}+\Gamma_1^\alpha{}_{\mu\beta}\Gamma_2^\beta{}_{\nu\alpha}-\Gamma_2^\alpha{}_{\mu\nu}\Gamma_1^\beta{}_{\alpha\beta}-\Gamma_1^\alpha{}_{\mu\nu}\Gamma_2^\beta{}_{\alpha\beta}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.13ab.7}
$$
Up to the Einstein divergence, every cubic term is
$$
\begin{aligned}
16\pi G_b C_{6,g}={}&E_{6,\rm EH}-F_{1,\mu\nu}F_2^{\mu\nu}+h^{\mu\alpha}\eta^{\nu\beta}F_{1,\mu\nu}F_{1,\alpha\beta}-\tfrac h4F_{1,\mu\nu}F_1^{\mu\nu}\\
&-2\theta_1\theta_2-\tfrac h2\theta_1^2+2(a_2^\mu-h^{\mu\nu}a_{1,\nu})\partial_\mu s+h a_1^\mu\partial_\mu s\\
&-[1+j'(Y_0)]Y_1-\tfrac h2[Y_0+j(Y_0)]+20q_1q_2+5h q_1^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.13ab.8}
$$
The smooth radial extension defines $j'$ at zero. This expression also covers spatially variable $\nabla s_0$. Inverse-metric and unit-root series through $e^4$ suffice since differentiated/kinetic factors start at $e^2$.

The remaining order-$e^6$ field densities are
$$
\begin{aligned}
C_{6,\rm clock}&=-\frac{2r}{16\pi G_b}A_\psi(\psi_0)\chi\mathcal U_{*,A}(\nabla s;A_0),\\
C_{6,\Lambda}&=-\frac{\Lambda h}{16\pi G_b},\quad C_{6,\psi}=\tfrac12h_{\mu\nu}T_{\chi,0}^{\mu\nu}-W_\psi(\psi_0)\chi,\\
T_{\chi,0}^{\mu\nu}&=\partial^\mu\chi\partial^\nu\chi-\eta^{\mu\nu}[(\partial\chi)^2/2+W(\psi_0)].
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.13ab.9}
$$
These follow by expanding $W_{\rm chart}=e^4W$ and $A(\psi_0+e^2\chi)$. The finite amplitude offset and actual canonical/background stress are retained.
##### III. Actual moving-source coefficients

Use canonical clump momentum $p_i=m_be w_i$, phase density $e^2F/[m_b|m_be|^3]$ and the exact particle Hamiltonian
$$
H_{\rm part}=N\sqrt{m_b^2+\gamma^{ij}p_ip_j}-N^ip_i.
\tag{I.13ab.10}
$$
With $\rho=\int Fdw$, $j_i=\int w_iFdw$ and $\Pi_{ij}=\int w_iw_jFdw$, its metric interaction coefficients are
$$
\mathcal L_{4,\rm cl}=\rho h_{00}/2,\quad\mathcal L_{5,\rm cl}=j_ih_{0i},\quad
\mathcal L_{6,\rm cl}=-\rho|h_{0i}|^2/2+\rho h_{00}^2/8+(\operatorname{tr}\Pi)h_{00}/4+\Pi_{ij}h_{ij}/2.
\tag{I.13ab.11}
$$
For example $N=1-e^2h_{00}/2+e^4(|h_{0i}|^2/2-h_{00}^2/8)+O(e^6)$ fixes the lapse-quadratic sign. Field-independent rest/kinetic terms do not enter these field Euler derivatives, but remain in source transport and resource energy. Homogeneous particles contribute $\mathcal L_{6,\rm bg}=h_{\mu\nu}T_{{\rm bg},0}^{\mu\nu}/2$ with their actual unscaled momentum energy and pressure moments, including null species. No dust equation of state replaces them.

Write $F=F_0+eF_1+e^2F_2+O(e^3)$. The fixed reduced-gauge leading solution has $h_{0i}^{(0)}=0$ and $\nabla n_0=\nabla\Phi_0$, $n_0=-h_{00}^{(0)}/2$. Its exact Hamilton equations give
$$
\partial_tF_0=0,\quad\partial_tF_1=-L_0F_0,\quad
L_0=w\cdot\nabla_x-\nabla\Phi_0\cdot\nabla_w,\quad
\partial_tF_2=-L_0F_1+\nabla n_1\cdot\nabla_wF_0,\quad n_1=-h_{00}^{(1)}/2.
\tag{I.13ab.12}
$$
If another chosen spatial gauge has leading shift $b_0$, add $b_0\cdot\nabla_xF_0-[(\partial_ib_0^j)w_j]\partial_{w_i}F_0$ in the last equation. A change of gauge cannot discard it; the representative in Theorem I.13aa has $b_0=0$.

Initial $F_1,F_2$ are Taylor coefficients of the exact constraint-compatible canonical data. They need not vanish when their orthonormal-frame version is fixed. Before the specified spatial gauge correction, $\gamma_{ij}=e^{-2e^2\Phi_0}\delta_{ij}$ gives
$$
F_{{\rm can},\rm initial}=F_0(x,e^{e^2\Phi_0}w),\quad F_{1,\rm initial}=0,\quad
F_{2,\rm initial}=\Phi_0w\cdot\nabla_wF_0.
\tag{I.13ab.13}
$$
Pull the known coordinate correction through this same scalar phase-space map. For zero initial $F_1$, $\rho_1=-t\operatorname{div}j_0$ and $j_1=-t[\operatorname{div}\Pi_0+\rho_0\nabla\Phi_0]$. Integrate the displayed $F_2$ equation once $n_1$ is known. The actual ADM moments check density, pressure and coordinate volume:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\rho_{\rm ADM}/e^2&=\rho_0+e\rho_1+e^2[\rho_2+\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}\Pi_0-\tfrac12(\operatorname{tr}h_{ij}^{(0)})\rho_0]+O(e^3),\\
J_i/e^2&=ej_{0,i}+e^2j_{1,i}+O(e^3),\qquad S_{ij}/e^2=e^2\Pi_{0,ij}+O(e^3).
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.13ab.14}
$$

##### IV. Three retarded coefficient problems and the varying gauge density

Let $Z=(h_{\mu\nu},v_i,s,\chi)=Z_0+eZ_1+e^2Z_2+O(e^3)$. Let $E_4$ be the Euler operator of $\mathcal L_{4,g}+\mathcal L_{4,\psi}$ and $\mathcal L=DE_4|_{Z_0}$ plus the leading modified-harmonic gauge operator, using metric Euler-density normalization $\mathcal Q_1/(16\pi G_b)$. It has the retarded evolution of Theorem I.13y at the actual spatially variable constitutive Hessian; it need not be a constant-coefficient operator. Put $S_j(F)=\operatorname{EL}_Z\mathcal L_{j,\rm cl}[F]$ for $j=4,5$. The exact coefficient equations are
$$
\begin{aligned}
E_4(Z_0)+S_4(F_0)&=0,\\
\mathcal LZ_1&=-S_4(F_1)-S_5(F_0),\\
\mathcal LZ_2&=-\tfrac12D^2E_4|_{Z_0}[Z_1,Z_1]-S_4(F_2)-S_5(F_1)\\
&\quad-\operatorname{EL}_Z[C_{6,g}+C_{6,\rm clock}+C_{6,\Lambda}+C_{6,\psi}+\mathcal L_{6,\rm cl}[F_0]+\mathcal L_{6,\rm bg}]-\mathcal Q_6(Z_0).
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.13ab.15}
$$
Evaluate all last-line densities on $Z_0$. These are Euler **densities**. Thus $\mathcal Q_6$ is the order-$e^2$ coefficient of $\sqrt{-g}\mathcal Q^{\mu\nu}/(16\pi G_be^2)$, not the coefficient of $\mathcal Q$ alone. For the auxiliary speeds $v=4/5,9/10$, put
$$
q_{v,0}^{\mu\nu}=\eta^{\mu\nu}+(1-v^{-2})U_0^\mu U_0^\nu,\quad
\delta q_v^{\mu\nu}=-h^{\mu\nu}+(1-v^{-2})(U_0^\mu U_1^\nu+U_1^\mu U_0^\nu).
\tag{I.13ab.16}
$$
Use a tilde for $v=4/5$, a hat for $v=9/10$, and the flat reference connection. Define
$$
H_1^\alpha=\widetilde q_0^{\mu\nu}\Gamma_1^\alpha{}_{\mu\nu},\quad
H_2^\alpha=\widetilde q_0^{\mu\nu}\Gamma_2^\alpha{}_{\mu\nu}+\delta\widetilde q^{\mu\nu}\Gamma_1^\alpha{}_{\mu\nu}.
\tag{I.13ab.17}
$$
Let $P(q)_\alpha{}^{\beta\mu\nu}=\delta_\alpha^{(\mu}q^{\nu)\beta}-\delta_\alpha^\beta q^{\mu\nu}/2$, $\widehat P_0=P(\widehat q_0)$ and $\widehat P_1=P(\delta\widehat q)$. The metric entries of $\mathcal Q_6$ are explicitly
$$
\frac1{16\pi G_b}\left\{
\widehat P_{0,\alpha}{}^{\beta\mu\nu}(\partial_\beta H_2^\alpha+\Gamma_1^\alpha{}_{\beta\lambda}H_1^\lambda)
+\widehat P_{1,\alpha}{}^{\beta\mu\nu}\partial_\beta H_1^\alpha
+\tfrac h2\widehat P_{0,\alpha}{}^{\beta\mu\nu}\partial_\beta H_1^\alpha\right\}.
\tag{I.13ab.18}
$$
Multiply off-diagonal tensor rows by two in the ten independent symmetric metric coordinates; diagonal weight is one and other field components are zero. At the leading reduced-gauge solution $H_1=0$ only the derivative of $H_2$ remains. This retains variation of auxiliary metrics, connection and density rather than freezing the gauge term at second order.

For a response-scalar component illustration only, multiply its raw Euler-density equation by $-8\pi G_b$, equivalently remove $1/(16\pi G_b)$ and divide by $-2$. The leading equation is $10\ddot s+\operatorname{div}a_1-\Delta s-r\operatorname{div}\mathcal A_s=0$. Moving nonlinear flux terms to the right gives $(r/2)\operatorname{div}\{D^2\mathcal A_s(\nabla s_0)[\nabla s_1,\nabla s_1]\}$ and $r\operatorname{div}\{\mathcal A_{s,A}(\nabla s_0)A_\psi(\psi_0)\chi_0\}$. Every remaining geometric term is the finite $C_{6,g}$ Euler expression with the stated normalization.

Initial $Z_j,\dot Z_j$ are the first three coefficients of the exact joint constraint/gauge implicit-function data. Differentiating exact constraints and their propagation gives the coefficient constraints; no independent incoming scalar/vector wave is erased. The leading gauge includes the homogeneous lapse mode (I.13aa.16), not the raw comoving field. The algorithm is triangular: compute $Z_0,F_0$; integrate $F_1$; solve the retarded linear problem for $Z_1$; integrate $F_2$; solve for $Z_2$. Each solve uses its specified initial jet and the retarded evolution $E_{\mathcal L}(t,s)$ of the same operator. Boundary/extension data are those already fixed on the auxiliary domain. A numerical solver may evaluate a non-elementary instance but is not needed for existence/remainder, and no further constitutive/source premise is introduced.

##### V. Uniform remainder on the fixed interval

Differentiate the rescaled first-order field/transport equations three times in $e$. The highest parameter derivative at each stage has the same uniformly strongly hyperbolic principal operator, plus bounded lower-order linear terms and products of lower parameter derivatives with one spatial/phase-space derivative. Estimate stage $j$ in $H^{s+3-j}$ for $j=1,2,3$. The four spare derivatives, compact momenta, Moser bounds and full symmetrizer control the products. Differentiated constraint/gauge initial norms are bounded by the same implicit-function data. There is no division by $e$. Induction and Gronwall give
$$
\sup_{0\le t\le T,\ 0\le e\le e_0}\|\partial_e^3U_e(t)\|_{H^s}\le C_T,\quad
\|U_e-U_0-eU_1-e^2U_2\|_{H^s}\le C_Te^3/6,
\tag{I.13ab.19}
$$
where $U_e$ is the complete first-order state, distinct from the clock function $U_c$. Recursively take $C_T$ from finite coefficient/initial derivative suprema on the fixed bootstrap set and its energy constants. Since $g_e=\eta+e^2h_e$, Sobolev embedding gives
$$
\|g_e-\eta-e^2h_0-e^3h_1-e^4h_2\|_{C^2}\le C'_Te^5.
\tag{I.13ab.20}
$$
The response field and specified gauge/frame pullbacks have the same Taylor control. Physical lengths use $x_{\rm phys}=e^2x$: the dimensionless metric error remains $e^5$ while force errors carry the inverse length. This is uniform finite-chart-time control, without a derivative-losing slow-time argument or orbital-time conclusion.
##### VI. Null/timelike endpoint coefficients and the local residual

On a finite noncaustic tube first use endpoint/frame data with zero order-$e$ jet. Write $x=x_0+e^2x_2+e^3x_3+e^4x_4+O(e^5)$ and $k=\dot x_0$. With $\Gamma_1[h]$ the linear Christoffel expression and $\Gamma_2[h,h]$ its quadratic part, the coefficient ODEs are
$$
\begin{aligned}
\ddot x_2^\mu&=-\Gamma_1[h_0]^\mu{}_{\alpha\beta}(x_0)k^\alpha k^\beta,\\
\ddot x_3^\mu&=-\Gamma_1[h_1]^\mu{}_{\alpha\beta}(x_0)k^\alpha k^\beta,\\
\ddot x_4^\mu&=-(\Gamma_1[h_2]+\Gamma_2[h_0,h_0])^\mu{}_{\alpha\beta}k^\alpha k^\beta
-x_2^\nu\partial_\nu\Gamma_1[h_0]^\mu{}_{\alpha\beta}k^\alpha k^\beta
-2\Gamma_1[h_0]^\mu{}_{\alpha\beta}k^\alpha\dot x_2^\beta.
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.13ab.21}
$$
Moving clump endpoints or frames instead have an order-$e$ jet and require $x_1$. The complete finite formula retaining every aberration term is
$$
\ddot x_j^\mu=-[e^j]\left\{\Gamma^\mu_{\alpha\beta}(g_{\rm PN})
\left(x_0+\sum_{1\le\ell<j}e^\ell x_\ell\right)
\left(k+\sum_{1\le\ell<j}e^\ell\dot x_\ell\right)^\alpha
\left(k+\sum_{1\le\ell<j}e^\ell\dot x_\ell\right)^\beta\right\},\quad j=1,\ldots,4,
\tag{I.13ab.22}
$$
where $g_{\rm PN}=\eta+e^2h_0+e^3h_1+e^4h_2$ and $\ddot x_1=0$. For example the third-order equation also contains $-x_1\cdot\partial\Gamma_1[h_0]kk-2\Gamma_1[h_0]k\dot x_1$; the extraction retains every fourth-order term too. Expand initial/null normalization or endpoint data from the same physical frame prescription with order-$e^5$ remainder. An endpoint following a source/test timelike geodesic uses this same equation with its actual order-$e$ initial velocity. An externally prescribed nongeodesic readout keeps its full prescribed trajectory as data.

The metric estimate, initial remainder and bounded geodesic/Jacobi inverse on the noncaustic tube yield order-$e^5$ travel-time, deflection and frame-readout errors by smooth dependence of the geodesic flow. No source motion is suppressed in that comparison. For a coordinate-stationary clock,
$$
\frac{d\tau}{dt}=1-\tfrac12e^2h_{0,00}-\tfrac12e^3h_{1,00}
-e^4[h_{2,00}/2+(h_{0,00})^2/8]+O(e^5).
\tag{I.13ab.23}
$$
Rolling-frame and homogeneous aberration belong to the computed $h_j$ and transformed endpoints, without replacing them by GR values. Relative to a specified GR comparator, the local residual consists of its calculated coefficient differences at orders $e^2,e^3,e^4$, plus $C_Te^5$, any finite high-acceleration simplification defect, the actual amplitude offset $A_G-A(\psi_0)$ and stated source/measurement uncertainties. The transverse coefficient remains $G_b/G=r/2$. No residual tolerance or source selector is chosen. The resulting bounded local metric/readout map has the proved source/window; the original item-8 comparison retains its registered residual interval. $\square$

**I.14 Timescale Separation (Quasistatic Local-Relaxation Branch)**

On the quasistatic local-relaxation branch, the adaptation dynamics of local MPU parameters ($\delta, C_{\max}$) governing $G(R)$ are assumed to reach local PCE equilibrium on timescales (Myr–Gyr in this branch) short compared with potential cosmological drift of the environment or fundamental parameters that might cause $(L_0, A_G, m)$ to evolve (Gyr–Hubble time). Under this branch assumption, $G(R)$ may be treated as quasi-static when analyzing galaxy dynamics, while allowing for a slow cosmic evolution of the universal parameters themselves. A first-principles derivation of the Myr–Gyr local equilibration scale from the Appendix D adaptation dynamics ($\eta_{\mathrm{adapt}}$ and the local-PL neighborhood structure of Theorem D.8) remains a separate closure lemma; the galaxy-scale phenomenology of Sections I.6-I.13 inherits this quasistatic branch label.

**I.15 Conclusion**

The appendix defines a multi-scale dark-sector research program. Its strongest test is whether one independently fixed response can account for all listed scales at once.

<a id="theorem-i13l-retarded-rational-two-form-factor-realization"></a>**Theorem I.13l (Retarded Rational Two-Form-Factor Realization).** Use the metric, coupling and Fourier convention of Theorem I.13j, with inverse temporal transform $e^{-i\omega t}$. Let $\mathscr F$ consist of smooth fields on $\mathbb R^{1,3}$ supported in $J^+(K)$ for some compact set $K$. Tensor components have this same support condition. Let $\mathscr R$ be the real rational functions whose finite poles belong to $[0,\infty)$. Choose nonzero rational functions $a,d_0$ such that $a,a^{-1},d_0,d_0^{-1}\in\mathscr R$, and put $c=(a-d_0)/3$. The action coefficients of Theorem I.13j remain $b=-a$, $d=-c$ and $f=(a-c)/2$; $d_0=a-3c$ denotes the spin-zero eigenvalue, distinct from the action coefficient $d$. These are a concrete operator subclass of the symbols in Theorem I.13j. Use one fixed unit system with light speed one: $z,\lambda$ have dimension $L^{-2}$ and the coefficients make $a,c,d,d_0$ dimensionless. For example, distinct positive inverse-length-squared constants $\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3,\lambda_4$ give the nonlocal members $a(z)=(z-\lambda_1)/(z-\lambda_2)$ and $d_0(z)=-2(z-\lambda_3)/(z-\lambda_4)$.

For $\lambda\ge0$, define $G_\lambda$ to be the zero-past solution operator for $\Box-\lambda$. If the source vanishes before $t_0$, its spatial Fourier transform is
$$
\widehat{G_\lambda u}(t,\mathbf k)
=-\int_{t_0}^t\frac{\sin((t-s)\sqrt{|\mathbf k|^2+\lambda})}{\sqrt{|\mathbf k|^2+\lambda}}\widehat u(s,\mathbf k)\,ds,
\tag{I.13l.1}
$$
where the quotient at zero frequency is $t-s$. For the unique partial fraction expansion
$$
R(z)=\sum_{l=0}^D p_lz^l+\sum_{\lambda,j}r_{\lambda j}(z-\lambda)^{-j},
$$
define $R_{\mathrm{ret}}(\Box)=\sum_l p_l\Box^l+\sum_{\lambda,j}r_{\lambda j}G_\lambda^j$. All sums are finite. Products mean compositions on $\mathscr F$.

1. This prescription is a unital algebra homomorphism on $\mathscr R$, maps $\mathscr F$ to itself and commutes with derivatives. Its support is retarded in the metric cone, and it is covariant under proper orthochronous Poincaré transformations. In temporal Fourier variables the inverse factors are the distributions
$$
\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}
[(\omega+i\epsilon)^2-|\mathbf k|^2-\lambda]^{-j}.
\tag{I.13l.2}
$$
The common analytic prescription, rather than a product of separately specified singular distributions, defines repeated factors and the null-cone value.

2. Define
$$
\vartheta_\mu{}^\nu=\delta_\mu{}^\nu-\partial_\mu\partial^\nu G_0,
\qquad
(P_0h)_{\mu\nu}=\tfrac13\vartheta_{\mu\nu}\vartheta^{\alpha\beta}h_{\alpha\beta},
\qquad
P_2h=\vartheta_\mu{}^\alpha\vartheta_\nu{}^\beta h_{\alpha\beta}-P_0h.
$$
The realized gravitational operator and its equation are
$$
E_{\mathrm{ret}}h=-\Box(a_{\mathrm{ret}}P_2+(d_0)_{\mathrm{ret}}P_0)h,
\qquad E_{\mathrm{ret}}h+\tfrac\kappa2T=0.
\tag{I.13l.3}
$$
They realize the full conserved symbol of Theorem I.13j, including its distributional inverse-$\Box$ term. For every conserved $T\in\mathscr F$, there is exactly one transverse zero-past solution and exactly one solution class modulo $h\mapsto h+\partial_\mu\xi_\nu+\partial_\nu\xi_\mu$ with $\xi\in\mathscr F$. Writing $\tau=\eta^{\alpha\beta}T_{\alpha\beta}$ and
$$
R_2(z)=\frac1{za(z)},\qquad R_0(z)=\frac1{zd_0(z)},\qquad B(z)=\frac{R_0(z)-R_2(z)}3,
$$
the transverse representative is
$$
h_{\mu\nu}=\frac\kappa2\left[(R_2)_{\mathrm{ret}}T_{\mu\nu}
+\eta_{\mu\nu}B_{\mathrm{ret}}\tau
-\partial_\mu\partial_\nu(G_0B_{\mathrm{ret}}\tau)\right].
\tag{I.13l.4}
$$
Conservation is necessary for every solution of (I.13l.3).

3. The construction has explicit finite-time estimates. For $L>0$, an integer $s\ge0$ and an integer $N\ge0$, write
$$
\|u\|_{s,N,L}=\sum_{|\alpha|\le N}\sup_{t_0\le t\le t_0+L}
\|\partial^\alpha u(t,\cdot)\|_{H^s(\mathbb R^3)}.
$$
With the partial fractions above,
$$
\|R_{\mathrm{ret}}u\|_{s,N,L}
\le\sum_l|p_l|4^l\|u\|_{s,N+2l,L}
+\sum_{\lambda,j}|r_{\lambda j}|\frac{L^{2j}}{(2j)!}\|u\|_{s,N,L}.
\tag{I.13l.5}
$$
Applying this bound separately to $R_2$, $B$ and $z^{-1}B$, with two additional derivatives in the last term, bounds every component of (I.13l.4). It proves continuous dependence with a finite, explicitly determined derivative loss. It does not impose positivity of physical mode energy.

4. At every nonzero static spatial wave number $K$, the transfer functions are regular and the simultaneous static projections are exactly (I.13j.3), evaluated at $z=-K^2$. These are stationary transfer coefficients; an eternal dust source is outside $\mathscr F$. They also equal the zero-frequency limit of the scalar transfer functions, where no pole is encountered. The same zero-past construction on spatially homogeneous fields is an ordinary differential system. Conservation then forces $T_{00}=T_{0i}=0$, and, for arbitrary smooth zero-past $T_{ij}(t)$,
$$
h_{00}=h_{0i}=0,\qquad
h_{ij}=\frac\kappa2\left[(R_2)_{\mathrm{ret}}T^{\mathrm{TF}}_{ij}
+\frac{\delta_{ij}}3(R_0)_{\mathrm{ret}}\tau\right].
\tag{I.13l.6}
$$
Here $\mathrm{TF}$ removes the three-dimensional spatial trace and the scalar operators use $\Box=-\partial_t^2$. This homogeneous extension has the same initial prescription and parameters. It is a linear perturbation response, with no independently chosen homogeneous density or cosmological background.

*Proof.* Spatial Fourier transformation reduces $(\Box-\lambda)v=u$ to $\ddot v+(|\mathbf k|^2+\lambda)v=-u$. Variation of constants with both zero initial data gives (I.13l.1), hence existence and uniqueness on every finite slab. Smoothness follows by differentiating the formula and using the rapid spatial Fourier decay on such slabs. The equation and uniqueness give both $(\Box-\lambda)G_\lambda=I$ and $G_\lambda(\Box-\lambda)=I$ on $\mathscr F$. Differentiation preserves zero-past data, so all derivatives commute with these inverses.

For completeness, cone support follows from the wave energy identity. For a real scalar solution set $e=(|v_t|^2+|\nabla v|^2+\lambda|v|^2)/2$ and $j=-v_t\nabla v$. Then $\partial_te+\operatorname{div}j=-uv_t$ and $|j\cdot n|\le e$. Integrate on a backward truncated light cone disjoint from the source. Its sloping boundary has nonnegative outward energy flux, and its past slice has zero energy, so the energy on every later slice is zero. For $\lambda=0$ this first gives vanishing derivatives; the zero-past value fixes the remaining constant. Exhaustion by such cones proves support in the source's causal future. The same argument applied to a homogeneous equation proves uniqueness with this support condition. The equation and its support condition are invariant under the stated Poincaré group, proving covariance.

All inverse factors commute: for example $G_\lambda G_\mu u$ and $G_\mu G_\lambda u$ solve the same successive zero-past equations, and uniqueness, or their scalar convolution formulas, identifies them. Moreover
$G_\lambda-G_\mu=(\lambda-\mu)G_\lambda G_\mu$.
These identities and the two-sided inverse identities show that evaluating a rational expression is unchanged by clearing denominators. They prove the algebra assertion and its agreement with unique partial fractions. Laplace transforming the causal sine kernel gives $[(\omega+i\epsilon)^2-|\mathbf k|^2-\lambda]^{-1}$. Repeated time convolutions give its powers before taking the boundary value. The sine kernels and their finite convolutions are tempered distributions; damping and then removing the damping gives their distributional limits. This establishes (I.13l.2), including $\lambda=0$.

Since $\Box G_0=I$, direct multiplication gives $\vartheta^2=\vartheta$, $\partial^\mu\vartheta_{\mu\nu}=0$ and $\eta^{\mu\nu}\vartheta_{\mu\nu}=3$. Thus $P_0,P_2$ are complementary idempotents on transverse symmetric tensors. Expanding (I.13l.3) gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
(E_{\mathrm{ret}}h)_{\mu\nu}={}&-a_{\mathrm{ret}}\Box h_{\mu\nu}
+a_{\mathrm{ret}}(\partial_\mu\partial^\alpha h_{\alpha\nu}
+\partial_\nu\partial^\alpha h_{\alpha\mu})
+c_{\mathrm{ret}}\eta_{\mu\nu}\Box h\\
&-c_{\mathrm{ret}}\eta_{\mu\nu}\partial^\alpha\partial^\beta h_{\alpha\beta}
-c_{\mathrm{ret}}\partial_\mu\partial_\nu h
+(c-a)_{\mathrm{ret}}\partial_\mu\partial_\nu G_0
\partial^\alpha\partial^\beta h_{\alpha\beta}.
\end{aligned}
$$
This is the variation symbol of (I.13j.1) under (I.13j.2), with the stipulated inverse prescription. Its divergence vanishes identically, proving source necessity. For conserved $T$, $P_0T=\vartheta\tau/3$ and $P_2T=T-P_0T$. Multiplying by the rational inverses gives

$$
h=(\kappa/2)G_0(a^{-1}_{\mathrm{ret}}P_2+(d_0^{-1})_{\mathrm{ret}}P_0)T,
$$

which expands to (I.13l.4). All factors commute and are invertible on their scalar domain, so substitution proves existence and uniqueness in the transverse subspace.

For an arbitrary $h$, its difference from its double transverse projection is the pure gauge generated by
$$
\xi_\nu=G_0\partial^\alpha h_{\alpha\nu}
-\tfrac12\partial_\nu G_0^2\partial^\alpha\partial^\beta h_{\alpha\beta}.
$$
Expansion verifies the identity. Conversely every such pure gauge is killed by both projectors. Hence the equation fixes exactly the asserted gauge class.

The bound $|\sin(\omega t)/\omega|\le t$ for $\omega\ge0$ gives

$$
\|G_\lambda u(t)\|_{H^s}\le\int_{t_0}^t(t-s)\|u(s)\|_{H^s}ds.
$$

The $j$-fold convolution of $t\mathbf1_{t\ge0}$ is $t^{2j-1}\mathbf1_{t\ge0}/(2j-1)!$, as follows by integrating monomials, or inductively by two elementary integrations. Integration against a supremum gives $L^{2j}/(2j)!$. Derivatives commute, and expansion of $\Box^l$ has total absolute coefficient $4^l$. Summing proves (I.13l.5).

For $K>0$, none of the allowed poles or zeros lies at $-K^2$. The static symbol is therefore the nondegenerate symbol already evaluated in Theorem I.13j. Continuity at zero temporal frequency proves the transfer limit. For spatially constant zero-past sources, $\partial_tT_{0\nu}=0$ and zero past imply $T_{0\nu}=0$. On zero-past scalar functions $\vartheta_{00}=0$, $\vartheta_{0i}=0$ and $\vartheta_{ij}=\delta_{ij}$; substituting gives (I.13l.6). ∎

<a id="theorem-i13la-fixed-scale-weibull-census-and-a-causal-continuum-realization"></a>**Theorem I.13l.a (Fixed-Scale Weibull Census and a Causal Continuum Realization).** Use the conventions, source space $\mathscr F$, zero-past operators $G_\lambda$ and seminorms of Theorem I.13l. Fix a length $L>0$, an enhancement $A>0$ and an exponent $m>0$, and put
$$
w_m(r)=\frac mL\Bigl(\frac rL\Bigr)^{m-1}e^{-(r/L)^m},\qquad
f_m(k)=\int_0^\infty w_m(r)\frac{\sin kr}{kr}\,dr,\qquad
\mu_m(k)=1+Af_m(k),
\tag{I.13l.a.1}
$$
with the quotient at $k=0$ defined by continuity. Then $\mu_m$ is the static dust multiplier of Equation I.4 with fixed $L_0=L$, $A_G=A$ and steepness $m$. On the negative symbol axis $s=-k^2$ write $\alpha=1/a$ and $\beta=1/(a-3c)$; the multipliers (I.13j.3) are then $\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}=(4\alpha+2\beta)/3$, $\nu_{\mathrm{sl}}=2(\alpha-\beta)/3$ and $\Sigma_{\mathrm{lens}}=\alpha$. An *admitted analytic retarded pair* is a nondegenerate static pair for which $g_2=-\alpha/s$ and $g_0=-\beta/s$ extend holomorphically to $\Omega=\mathbb C\setminus[0,\infty)$ and satisfy, for some constants $C,N$,
$$
|g_i(s)|\le C(1+|s|)^N\bigl(1+|\operatorname{Im}\sqrt s|^{-N}\bigr),
\qquad\operatorname{Im}\sqrt s>0.
\tag{I.13l.a.2}
$$

1. *Exponent census.* The multiplier (I.13l.a.1) belongs to an admitted pair if and only if $0<m\le1$. For every such exponent the no-slip pair $\alpha=\mu$, $\beta=-\mu/2$, equivalently $a=c=1/\mu$, is admitted, and it has the real cone-retarded tempered realization and the two-sided causal inverse on $\mathscr F$ of items 3 and 4. The exclusion for $m>1$ holds for every lensing choice obeying (I.13l.a.2). For $A=0$ the response is the general-relativistic one for every exponent.

2. *Signed spectrum.* For $0<m\le1$ there is a probability measure $\nu_m$ on $(0,\infty)$ with $e^{-(r/L)^m}=\int e^{-tr}\,\nu_m(dt)$; for $m=1$, $\nu_1=\delta_{1/L}$. The probability measure
$$
\sigma_m(dv)=\frac1{2v^{3/2}}\Bigl[\int_{(0,\sqrt v]}t\,\nu_m(dt)\Bigr]dv
\tag{I.13l.a.3}
$$
on $(0,\infty)$ satisfies
$$
f_m(k)=\int\frac v{v+k^2}\,\sigma_m(dv),\qquad
\frac{\mu_m(k)}{k^2}=\frac{1+A}{k^2}-A\int\frac{\sigma_m(dv)}{k^2+v}.
\tag{I.13l.a.4}
$$
For $m=1$ its density is $1/(2Lv^{3/2})$ on $v\ge L^{-2}$. For $0<m<1$ its density is strictly positive at every $v>0$, so the massive continuum extends down to zero and zero is not a separated pole; the first moment of $\sigma_m$ diverges. The response is a massless term of weight $1+A$ minus a massive continuum of total weight $A$.

3. *Causal form factor and its inverse.* With $s$ the symbol of $\Box$, put
$$
\mu(s)=1+A\int\frac v{v-s}\,\sigma_m(dv).
\tag{I.13l.a.5}
$$
There is a positive measure $\rho_A$ on $(0,\infty)$ of total mass $q_A=A/(1+A)$ with
$$
\frac1{\mu(s)}=a_0+s\int\frac{\rho_A(dv)}{s-v},\qquad a_0=\frac1{1+A}.
\tag{I.13l.a.6}
$$
For a finite signed measure $\eta$ on $[0,\infty)$ put $R_\eta=\int G_v\,\eta(dv)$, and on $\mathscr F$ define
$$
\mathcal M=(1+A)I-A\Box R_{\sigma_m},\qquad
\mathcal H=a_0I+\Box R_{\rho_A},\qquad
\mathcal R=(1+A)G_0-AR_{\sigma_m}.
\tag{I.13l.a.7}
$$
These are real continuous causal maps of $\mathscr F$ into itself. They commute with derivatives, are covariant under proper orthochronous Poincaré transformations, and satisfy
$$
\mathcal H\mathcal M=\mathcal M\mathcal H=I,\qquad
\Box\mathcal R=\mathcal R\Box=\mathcal M,\qquad
\mathcal R=G_0\mathcal M=\mathcal MG_0.
\tag{I.13l.a.8}
$$
Their kernels are tempered distributions supported in the forward metric cone, and the inverse factors use the common boundary prescription $s=(\omega+i0)^2-|\mathbf k|^2$.

4. *Conserved tensor equation.* With the projectors $P_2,P_0$ of Theorem I.13l, put
$$
Eh=-\Box\mathcal H(P_2-2P_0)h.
\tag{I.13l.a.9}
$$
For every symmetric conserved $T\in\mathscr F$ the equation $Eh+\kappa T/2=0$ has exactly one transverse zero-past solution and exactly one solution class modulo $h_{\mu\nu}\mapsto h_{\mu\nu}+\partial_\mu\xi_\nu+\partial_\nu\xi_\mu$, $\xi\in\mathscr F$. With $\tau=\eta^{\mu\nu}T_{\mu\nu}$ the transverse representative is
$$
h_{\mu\nu}=\frac\kappa2\Bigl[\mathcal RT_{\mu\nu}-\tfrac12\eta_{\mu\nu}\mathcal R\tau+\tfrac12\partial_\mu\partial_\nu G_0\mathcal R\tau\Bigr].
\tag{I.13l.a.10}
$$
Conservation is necessary for every solution. At every nonzero static spatial wave number the transfer functions are $\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}=\nu_{\mathrm{sl}}=\Sigma_{\mathrm{lens}}=\mu_m(k)$ and are nondegenerate. These are stationary transfer coefficients; an eternal dust source is outside $\mathscr F$.

5. *Estimates.* For a source in $\mathscr F$ evaluated on a time slab of duration $D$, with the seminorms $\|\cdot\|_{s,N,D}$ of Theorem I.13l, $\|G_vu\|_{s,N,D}\le\tfrac{D^2}2\|u\|_{s,N,D}$ uniformly in $v\ge0$, and
$$
\begin{aligned}
\|\mathcal Mu\|_{s,N,D}&\le(1+A)\|u\|_{s,N,D}+2AD^2\|u\|_{s,N+2,D},\\
\|\mathcal Hu\|_{s,N,D}&\le a_0\|u\|_{s,N,D}+2q_AD^2\|u\|_{s,N+2,D},\\
\|\mathcal Ru\|_{s,N,D}&\le(1+2A)\tfrac{D^2}2\|u\|_{s,N,D}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.13l.a.11}
$$

6. *Rigidity.* Two admitted pairs with the same static multipliers $(\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}},\Sigma_{\mathrm{lens}})$ on a set of wave numbers with an accumulation point in $(0,\infty)$ have the same holomorphic symbols $g_2,g_0$ on $\Omega$, hence the same boundary values on the null cone and at timelike momenta.

*Proof.* *Static multiplier.* For Equation I.4 with fixed $L_0=L$ and $A_G=A$, $G'(r)=G_0Aw_m(r)$ and $\int_0^\infty w_m=1$. The point-mass potential obeys $r^2\Phi'=G(r)M$, so $\nabla^2\Phi=4\pi G_0\rho_{\mathrm{eff}}$ with $\rho_{\mathrm{eff}}=M\delta^3+MAw_m(r)/(4\pi r^2)$. The Fourier transform of a radial density is $\int_0^\infty4\pi r^2\rho(r)\frac{\sin kr}{kr}\,dr$, so $\hat\rho_{\mathrm{eff}}/M=\mu_m(k)$. With $\alpha=1/a$ and $\beta=1/(a-3c)$, $(4\alpha+2\beta)/3=2(a-2c)/(a(a-3c))$ and $2(\alpha-\beta)/3=-2c/(a(a-3c))$, which are the first two multipliers of (I.13j.3).

*Positive mixture.* For $0<m<1$, integration by parts gives
$$
(r/L)^m=\frac{mL^{-m}}{\Gamma(1-m)}\int_0^\infty(1-e^{-rt})t^{-1-m}\,dt.
\tag{I.13l.a.12}
$$
Let $\ell(dt)=mL^{-m}t^{-1-m}dt/\Gamma(1-m)$, truncate it to $[1/n,n]$, and let $X_n$ be the compound-Poisson variable with that finite intensity. Then $\mathbb Ee^{-rX_n}=\exp[-\int_{[1/n,n]}(1-e^{-rt})\,\ell(dt)]$, and for every $K>0$
$$
\Pr(X_n>K)\le\frac{1-\mathbb Ee^{-X_n/K}}{1-e^{-1}}\le\frac{(LK)^{-m}}{1-e^{-1}},
$$
so these laws are tight on $[0,\infty)$. A weakly convergent subsequence has Laplace transform $\exp[-(r/L)^m]$ by (I.13l.a.12) and monotone convergence of the exponents. Laplace uniqueness identifies its law $\nu_m$, which does not depend on the subsequence. It has no atom at zero, because its transform tends to zero as $r\to\infty$. For every $\epsilon>0$, $\nu_m((0,\epsilon))>0$; otherwise the transform would be at most $e^{-\epsilon r}$, contradicting $m<1$ at large $r$. For $m=1$ the atom $\nu_1=\delta_{1/L}$ gives the transform directly.

Differentiation for $r>0$ gives $w_m(r)=\int te^{-tr}\,\nu_m(dt)$. Fubini applies because $|\sin(kr)/(kr)|\le1$ and each $te^{-tr}$ has unit integral, so
$$
f_m(k)=\int\frac tk\arctan\frac kt\,\nu_m(dt)=\int\nu_m(dt)\int_0^1\frac{t^2}{t^2+k^2u^2}\,du.
$$
For fixed $t$ the substitution $v=t^2/u^2$ gives (I.13l.a.3)–(I.13l.a.4). The conditional density $t/(2v^{3/2})$ on $v\ge t^2$ integrates to one, and Tonelli's theorem makes $\sigma_m$ a probability measure. The small-rate support of $\nu_m$ makes (I.13l.a.3) strictly positive at every $v>0$ when $m<1$. Each conditional first moment is infinite, so the first moment of $\sigma_m$ diverges; no later step uses it.

*Analyticity and growth.* The integrand $v/(v-s)$ is bounded uniformly in $v\ge0$ for $s$ in a compact subset of $\Omega$, so (I.13l.a.5) is holomorphic on $\Omega$. Since $\sigma_m$ is a probability measure,
$$
-\frac{\mu(s)}s=-\frac{1+A}s+A\int\frac{\sigma_m(dv)}{s-v}.
\tag{I.13l.a.13}
$$
Write $\sqrt s=u+ib$ with $b>0$. For $v\ge0$, $|s-v|=|\sqrt s-\sqrt v|\,|\sqrt s+\sqrt v|\ge b^2$ and $|s|\ge b^2$, so $|\mu(s)/s|\le(1+2A)b^{-2}$. The no-slip symbols $g_2=-\mu/s$ and $g_0=\mu/(2s)$ therefore satisfy (I.13l.a.2) with $N=2$. In the upper half-plane $\operatorname{Im}\mu(s)=A\operatorname{Im}s\int v\,\sigma_m(dv)/|v-s|^2>0$, the sign reverses in the lower half-plane, and $\mu(s)>1$ for real negative $s$; hence $\mu$ has no zero on $\Omega$. For nonzero static $k$, $1<\mu_m(k)<1+A$, which gives static nondegeneracy, and dominated convergence gives $\mu_m(0^+)=1+A$ and $\mu_m(k)\to1$ as $k\to\infty$.

*Inverse measure.* This step holds for every probability measure $\sigma$ on $(0,\infty)$. On $L^2(\sigma)$ let $e=1$, $P=|e\rangle\langle e|$, $V$ the multiplication by $v$, and $Q=I+AP$, so that $Q^{-1}=I-q_AP$. The closed nonnegative form $b[u]=\|V^{1/2}Q^{1/2}u\|^2$ on $Q^{-1/2}\operatorname{Dom}V^{1/2}$ defines the self-adjoint operator $\mathsf B=Q^{1/2}VQ^{1/2}$; the form is densely defined and closed because $Q^{1/2}$ is bounded and invertible, and $\ker\mathsf B=0$ because $V$ has no zero eigenspace. Let $\varpi$ be the spectral probability measure of $\mathsf B$ at $e$; it has no atom at zero. For $z>0$ put $r(z)=\langle e,(V+z)^{-1}e\rangle$. Since $zr(z)<1$, the rank-one resolvent identity for $V+zQ^{-1}=V+z-q_AzP$ gives
$$
\langle e,(V+zQ^{-1})^{-1}e\rangle=\frac{r(z)}{1-q_Azr(z)},
$$
and the form factorization gives $(V+zQ^{-1})^{-1}=Q^{1/2}(\mathsf B+z)^{-1}Q^{1/2}$. Since $Q^{1/2}e=\sqrt{1+A}\,e$ and $\mu(-z)=(1+A)(1-q_Azr(z))$,
$$
\frac1{\mu(-z)}=\frac1{1+A}+q_Az\langle e,(\mathsf B+z)^{-1}e\rangle=a_0+\int\frac z{z+v}\,\rho_A(dv),\qquad\rho_A=q_A\varpi .
$$
Both sides are holomorphic on the cut plane, and continuation to $s=-z$ proves (I.13l.a.6). In particular $\rho_A$ is finite, has mass $q_A$ and has no atom at zero.

*Mass-uniform causal kernels.* For a zero-past smooth source, (I.13l.1) with $\lambda=v$ gives the spatial transform of $G_vu$ with a kernel bounded by $t-r$, uniformly in $v\ge0$. This proves the first estimate of item 5, including all derivatives, since derivatives commute with the zero-past inverse. The cone-energy argument of Theorem I.13l gives finite propagation for every $v\ge0$, and uniqueness gives covariance. For a Schwartz test function $\phi$ the same bound gives
$$
|\langle G_v,\phi\rangle|\le C\int_0^\infty t\int_{\mathbb R^3}|\widehat\phi_{\mathrm{spatial}}(t,\mathbf k)|\,d\mathbf k\,dt,
\tag{I.13l.a.14}
$$
a continuous Schwartz seminorm independent of $v$. Integration against a finite signed measure therefore defines $R_\eta$ both as a tempered distribution and as a smooth causal map on $\mathscr F$, with norm bound $\|\eta\|_{\mathrm{TV}}D^2/2$ on a slab of duration $D$. Derivatives and measure integration commute in every finite-slab seminorm, and cone support and covariance survive the integration. This covers both spectral endpoints, including the continuum accumulating at zero for $m<1$. Since $\|\Box u\|_{s,N,D}\le4\|u\|_{s,N+2,D}$, summation gives (I.13l.a.11).

*Inverse identities.* First take a source compactly supported in spacetime. The finite-slab estimates give polynomial time growth in each fixed Sobolev seminorm for each finite composition in (I.13l.a.8), so temporal Laplace transforms exist for every $p>0$. Spatial Fourier and temporal Laplace transformation map $G_v$ to $-1/(p^2+|\mathbf k|^2+v)$, and the mass-uniform bounds justify the measure interchanges. With $z=p^2+|\mathbf k|^2$ the multipliers of $\mathcal M$, $\mathcal H$ and $\mathcal R$ are $\mu(-z)$, $1/\mu(-z)$ and $-\mu(-z)/z$. The inverse identity proved above and Laplace uniqueness give $\mathcal H\mathcal M=\mathcal M\mathcal H=I$ on compact sources; the other identities follow in the same way or from $\Box G_0=G_0\Box=I$. For a source in $\mathscr F$ and a finite terminal time, multiply the source by a smooth temporal cutoff equal to one up to that time and zero one unit later. The product is compactly supported, and causality makes every displayed operator and composition agree with its cutoff version up to the terminal time. This extends all identities to $\mathscr F$. Equivalently, the kernels lie in the convolution algebra of distributions supported in the forward cone, in which compositions are defined before any transform; temporal damping produces the common analytic prescription, and removal of the damping gives the distributional boundary values.

*Tensor equation.* On $\mathscr F$, $\Box G_0=I$ gives $\vartheta^2=\vartheta$, $\partial^\mu\vartheta_{\mu\nu}=0$ and $\eta^{\mu\nu}\vartheta_{\mu\nu}=3$, so $P_0,P_2$ are complementary projectors on transverse symmetric tensors. Equation (I.13l.a.9) is the conserved operator of Theorem I.13j with $a=c=\mathcal H$, $a-3c=-2\mathcal H$, $b=-a$, $d=-c$ and $f=0$, realized as in Theorem I.13l; it kills pure gauges and has identically vanishing divergence. For conserved $T$ put $h=\frac\kappa2\mathcal R(P_2-\tfrac12P_0)T$. Since $(P_2-2P_0)(P_2-\tfrac12P_0)=P_2+P_0$ and $(P_2+P_0)T=T$, (I.13l.a.8) gives $Eh=-\frac\kappa2\mathcal H\Box\mathcal RT=-\frac\kappa2T$, and expanding $P_0T=\vartheta\tau/3$ yields (I.13l.a.10). The same identities show that a transverse homogeneous solution vanishes. Every $h\in\mathscr F$ differs from its double transverse projection by the gauge generated by $\xi_\nu=G_0\partial^\alpha h_{\alpha\nu}-\tfrac12\partial_\nu G_0^2\partial^\alpha\partial^\beta h_{\alpha\beta}\in\mathscr F$, as in Theorem I.13l, which proves existence and uniqueness of the gauge class. The divergence of the equation gives necessity of conservation. The static transfer statement is the nondegenerate algebra of Theorem I.13j at $s=-k^2$ with $a=c=1/\mu_m(k)$.

*Exclusion for $m>1$.* Decay faster than every $e^{-cr}$ permits termwise integration of the sine series on compact complex $k$-sets, so
$$
\mu_m(k)=\mathsf M(-k^2),\qquad
\mathsf M(s)=1+A\sum_{n\ge0}\frac{L^{2n}\Gamma(1+2n/m)}{(2n+1)!}\,s^n .
\tag{I.13l.a.15}
$$
Stirling's formula gives $-\log c_n=2n(1-1/m)\log n+O(n)$ for the coefficients $c_n$, so $\mathsf M$ is entire of finite order $\varrho=m/[2(m-1)]$. If an admitted pair reproduces $\mu_m$ on a set of static wave numbers with an accumulation point in $(0,\infty)$, the identity theorem gives $\mathsf M(s)=-sg_\mu(s)$ on $\Omega$, where $g_\mu=(4g_2+2g_0)/3$. Fix $\delta\in(0,\pi/2)$ and $\varrho'>\varrho$ with $2\delta<\pi/\varrho'$. For $\delta\le\arg s\le2\pi-\delta$, $\operatorname{Im}\sqrt s\ge|s|^{1/2}\sin(\delta/2)$, so (I.13l.a.2) gives $|\mathsf M(s)|\le C'(1+|s|)^{N+1}$ there for $|s|\ge1$, and $\mathsf M$ is bounded on $|s|\le1$. In the sector $|\arg s|\le\delta$ the function $\mathsf M(s)/(1+s)^{N+1}$ is analytic, bounded on the two boundary rays and of growth at most $\exp(|s|^{\varrho'})$ with $\varrho'<\pi/(2\delta)$, so the Phragmén–Lindelöf theorem bounds it in the sector. Hence $\mathsf M$ is polynomially bounded on $\mathbb C$ and is a polynomial. It is bounded on the negative real axis because $|\mu_m-1|\le A$, so it is constant; but $\mathsf M(0)=1+A$ and $\mathsf M(-k^2)\to1$, which contradicts $A>0$. Only the bound (I.13l.a.2) on $g_\mu$ is used, so the exclusion holds for every lensing choice.

*Rigidity.* By (I.13j.3), $\alpha=\Sigma_{\mathrm{lens}}$ and $\beta=\tfrac12(3\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}-4\Sigma_{\mathrm{lens}})$. Two admitted pairs with the same static multipliers on such a set therefore have equal $g_2,g_0$ on a subset of $(-\infty,0)$ with an accumulation point in the connected domain $\Omega$, and the identity theorem gives equality on $\Omega$ and of the boundary values. ∎

<a id="theorem-i13lb-linear-covariant-kernels-of-one-symmetric-tensor-are-parity-even"></a>**Theorem I.13l.b (Linear Covariant Kernels of One Symmetric Tensor Are Parity-Even).** Let $k$ be a covector on four-dimensional Minkowski space with $k^2\ne0$, and let $K^{\mu\nu,\alpha\beta}$ be symmetric in $\mu\nu$ and in $\alpha\beta$ and invariant under the stabilizer algebra of $k$ in $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$.

1. $K$ is invariant under every reflection in $O(1,3)$ that fixes $k$. Hence a Lorentz-covariant kernel that changes sign under reflections vanishes at every $k$ with $k^2\ne0$, and everywhere if it is continuous. The parity-even class $\mathfrak L$ of Theorem I.13j is therefore the whole Lorentz-covariant quadratic class of one symmetric tensor field at $k^2\ne0$, and an $\varepsilon$-tensor term of Chern–Simons type cannot enter its linear covariant response.

2. With a constant background covector $v$ the conclusion fails. The symmetrization in $(\mu\nu)$ and in $(\alpha\beta)$ of $\varepsilon^{\mu\alpha\rho\sigma}v_\rho k_\sigma(k^2\eta^{\nu\beta}-k^\nu k^\beta)$ is transverse, antisymmetric under exchange of the two pairs and odd in $k$, so it defines a real gauge-invariant three-derivative term, and it changes sign under reflections. For timelike $v$ and static $k$ it annihilates the modes $h_{00}=-2\Phi$, $h_{ij}=-2\Psi\delta_{ij}$, so it leaves $\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}$ and $\Sigma_{\mathrm{lens}}$ unchanged.

Consequently a Chern–Simons inflow certificate enters a linear Lorentz-covariant conserved metric kernel only through a boundary-supported source or through a background that breaks Lorentz covariance.

*Proof.* Item 1. Let $W=k^\perp$, a nondegenerate three-dimensional space on which the stabilizer of $k$ acts as $\mathfrak{so}(W)$. Decompose $K$ by the number $j$ of its indices in $W$, the remaining indices lying along $k$. Each component is an $\mathfrak{so}(W)$-invariant tensor of rank $j$ on $W$. By the first fundamental theorem of invariant theory for $\mathfrak{so}(W)$, such tensors are spanned by products of the metric $g_W$ and at most one volume form $\varepsilon_W$, so $\varepsilon_W$ can occur only for $j=3$. In such a component the two indices of one symmetric pair both lie in $W$, and symmetry in that pair annihilates $\varepsilon_W$. Thus $K$ is built from $g_W$ and $k$ and is invariant under $O(W)$. If $K(Rk)=-R^{\otimes4}K(k)$ for a reflection $R$ fixing $k$, then $K(k)=-K(k)$. Item 2. Contraction with $k_\mu$ places two factors of $k$ in $\varepsilon$, and contraction with $k_\nu$ annihilates $k^2\eta^{\nu\beta}-k^\nu k^\beta$. Exchanging the pairs exchanges $\mu$ and $\alpha$ in $\varepsilon$. For $v=e_0$ and static $k$, $Y^{ij}=\varepsilon^{ij\rho\sigma}v_\rho k_\sigma$ is spatial and antisymmetric with $Y^{ij}k_j=0$, so on these modes the kernel returns the symmetrization of $k^2Y^{\mu\nu}$, which is zero. ∎

<a id="theorem-i13lc-spectral-positivity-forbids-large-scale-enhancement"></a>**Theorem I.13l.c (Spectral Positivity Forbids Large-Scale Enhancement).** Call a gauge-invariant member of $\mathfrak L$ with finite $\alpha,\beta$ *spectrally positive* if, for $k^2>0$,
$$
\frac\alpha{k^2}=\frac{c_2}{k^2}+q_2(k^2)+\int_{(0,\infty)}\frac{d\sigma_2(M^2)}{M^2+k^2},\qquad
\frac\beta{k^2}=\frac{c_0}{k^2}+q_0(k^2)+\int_{(0,\infty)}\frac{d\sigma_0(M^2)}{M^2+k^2},
\tag{I.13l.c.1}
$$
with positive measures $\sigma_2,\sigma_0$ obeying $\int d\sigma_i/(1+M^2)<\infty$, real polynomials $q_2,q_0$, and $c_2\ge0$, $c_0+\tfrac12c_2\ge0$. This is exchange of a massless spin-two mode of strength $c_2$, a massless scalar of strength $c_0+\tfrac12c_2$, and positive-norm massive spin-two and spin-zero modes.

1. If $\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}$ is bounded, then $\sigma_\mu=\tfrac13(4\sigma_2+2\sigma_0)$ is finite, $\tfrac13(4q_2+2q_0)=0$, and
$$
\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}(k)=\mu_0+\int_{(0,\infty)}\frac{k^2}{k^2+M^2}\,d\sigma_\mu(M^2),\qquad
\mu_0=\tfrac13(4c_2+2c_0)\ge c_2\ge0 .
\tag{I.13l.c.2}
$$
Thus $\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}$ is nondecreasing in $k$ and $\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}(0^+)\le\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}(\infty)$. The same holds for $\Sigma_{\mathrm{lens}}$ when it is bounded.

2. Let $K\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ be real and radial with $\int K=1$, and let $A>0$. No spectrally positive member has dust multiplier $\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}=1+A\widehat K$. This covers Equation I.4 with fixed $L_0$, $A_G>0$ and every $m>0$, where $K=w_m(r)/(4\pi r^2)$ with $w_m$ of (I.13l.a.1), and Equation I.7 with $q=0$, $A_{\mathrm{PM}}>0$ and every admitted kernel.

*Proof.* Item 1. Multiplying (I.13l.c.1) by $k^2$ and combining gives $\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}=\mu_0+k^2q_\mu(k^2)+I(k)$ with $q_\mu=\tfrac13(4q_2+2q_0)$ and $I(k)=\int\frac{k^2}{k^2+M^2}\,d\sigma_\mu\ge0$, which is nondecreasing, and $I(k)/k^2=\int\frac{d\sigma_\mu}{k^2+M^2}\to0$ by dominated convergence. If $q_\mu\ne0$, then $|k^2q_\mu(k^2)|\ge ck^2$ for large $k$ with some $c>0$, and $\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}$ is unbounded. Hence $q_\mu=0$, $I$ is bounded, and $\sigma_\mu$ is finite by monotone convergence. Also $\mu_0=\tfrac23(c_0+\tfrac12c_2)+c_2\ge c_2\ge0$. The same argument applies to $\Sigma_{\mathrm{lens}}=\alpha$. Item 2. $\widehat K$ is continuous with $\widehat K(0)=1$ and $\widehat K(k)\to0$ by the Riemann–Lebesgue lemma, so $\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}$ is bounded with $\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}(0^+)=1+A>1=\mu_{\mathrm{dyn}}(\infty)$, contradicting item 1. For Equation I.4 with fixed $L_0$ the static dust multiplier is $1+A_G\widehat K$ with $K=w_m/(4\pi r^2)$ by the first step of the proof of Theorem I.13l.a, and for Equation I.7 with $q=0$ it is $1+A_{\mathrm{PM}}\widehat K$. ∎

<a id="theorem-i13lad"></a>

<a id="theorem-i13ld-finite-positive-mode-sources-for-the-signed-weibull-cross-response"></a>**Theorem I.13l.d (Finite Positive-Mode Sources for the Signed Weibull Cross Response).** Retain the fixed-scale Weibull branch of Theorem I.13l.a with $0<m\leq1$ and $A>0$. Its signed retarded propagator is the limit, with explicit finite-time errors, of finite mass banks in which every wave oscillator has positive energy and the two probe legs are physically distinct. The reciprocal form factor at each finite stage is exactly the inverse of that same bank's forward form factor and converges with a controlled loss of derivatives. The signed response is a cross response on this source. The full two-port auto-response remains positive, and a source and detector represented by the same Hermitian operator cannot produce the signed massive spectral weights.

*One rational sequence and its errors.* Write $\sigma=\sigma_m$ for the probability measure of (I.13l.a.3), supported on $(0,\infty)$. At a stage choose $R>0$ and $\Delta>0$, partition $(0,R]$ into finitely many intervals of width at most $\Delta$, replace the mass of each nonempty interval by an atom at one positive point of that interval, and put the remaining mass at one fixed positive representative above $R$. Let $\sigma_N=\sum_\ell w_\ell\delta_{\lambda_\ell}$ be the resulting finite probability measure. It is determined by the declared $m,L,R,\Delta$ before any probe. Define
$$
\begin{split}
\mathcal R_N&=(1+A)G_0-A\sum_\ell w_\ell G_{\lambda_\ell},\\
\mathcal M_N&=(1+A)I-A\Box\sum_\ell w_\ell G_{\lambda_\ell},\qquad
\mathcal H_N=\mathcal M_N^{-1}.
\end{split}
$$
The inverse is the causal one from (I.13l.a.6)–(I.13l.a.8) applied to the finite positive mass measure $\sigma_N$. In particular its inverse-measure mass is $q_A=A/(1+A)$, independently of the partition. The same formula defines $\mathcal H$ for $\sigma$. The three finite symbols are rational, with the retarded prescription of Theorem I.13l. The common inverse is determined by the finite atom weights and locations and uses no independent fitted poles or subtractions.

For $t\geq0$ use $K_t(u)=\sin(t\sqrt u)/\sqrt u=\int_0^t\cos(r\sqrt u)\,dr$ on $u\geq0$. The continuous derivative at zero and $|\sin x|\leq|x|$ give $\sup_{u\geq0}|K_t'(u)|\leq t^3/6$. Thus the retarded Green operators of Theorem I.13l obey, on a fixed source-to-readout time slab of duration $D$,
$$
\|(G_\lambda-G_\nu)f\|_{s,N_0,D}
\leq \frac{D^4}{24}|\lambda-\nu|\|f\|_{s,N_0,D}.
$$
The estimate follows by integrating $K_t'$ against the source, and commutes with every time derivative in the seminorm by the zero-past convention. The uniform individual bound is $D^2/2$. Therefore, with
$$
B_D=\frac{D^4\Delta}{24}+D^2\sigma((R,\infty)),
$$
the difference of the two Green averages is bounded by $B_D$ on every such seminorm. In particular, writing $p_N=\|\cdot\|_{s,N,D}$ on this fixed slab,
$$
p_N((\mathcal R_N-\mathcal R)f)\leq A B_D p_N(f),\qquad
p_N((\mathcal M_N-\mathcal M)f)\leq4 A B_D p_{N+2}(f).
$$
Here the second estimate uses the same $\Box$ seminorm bound as Theorem I.13l.a. Let $J_D=(1+A)^{-1}+2q_A D^2$. The positive inverse measures give $p_N(\mathcal H_N f),p_N(\mathcal H f)\leq J_D p_{N+2}(f)$. The exact identity
$$
\mathcal H_N-\mathcal H
=\mathcal H_N(\mathcal M-\mathcal M_N)\mathcal H
$$
then yields
$$
p_N((\mathcal H_N-\mathcal H)f)\leq4 A J_D^2 B_D\,p_{N+6}(f).
$$
For a prescribed finite list of source and time budgets choose $R$ sufficiently large and $\Delta$ sufficiently small for all of them. This gives a single cofinal sequence with $B_D\to0$ on every fixed budget. Inserting $\mathcal R_N$ into the conserved tensor reconstruction (I.13l.a.10) gives the same convergence with at most the additional derivative loss of its explicit $\partial_\mu\partial_\nu G_0$ term. The finite source maps used below implement the scalar response and its signed readout; no positive dynamical spin-two realization of the signed tensor propagator is inferred from this algebraic reconstruction.

*Actual positive two-port source.* On a finite cubic torus use canonical real oscillators of frequency $\sqrt{|k|^2+\lambda_\ell}$ for the retained sine/cosine spatial modes, including a separate massless bank. For the massless bank use the nonzero spatial modes, so every retained oscillator has a normalizable positive-energy vacuum. Every $\lambda_\ell$ is strictly positive. Keep the vacuum reference energy and the fixed physical time convention. Write $\phi_0$ for the massless bank and $\phi_\ell$ for the massive banks. On these same physical oscillators define the source and detector coordinates by
$$
X_+=\sqrt{1+A}\,\phi_0+\sum_\ell\sqrt{Aw_\ell}\,\phi_\ell,\qquad
X_-=\sqrt{1+A}\,\phi_0-\sum_\ell\sqrt{Aw_\ell}\,\phi_\ell.
$$
Each coordinate denotes the corresponding spatially smeared mode sum. For a drive, couple $-J_+X_+-J_-X_-$ to the Hamiltonian, and retain separately the two conjugate detector responses. In the sign convention of (I.13l.1), a positive canonical Hamiltonian drive $-J\phi$ gives the response $-G_\lambda J$; the declared overall sign of the returned classical field is accordingly reversed when reporting $\mathcal R_N$. The relative minus between the two massive probe legs is a physical port sign. After that common sign convention the cross response is $\mathcal R_N$, and both auto responses have the sum of the same positive masses with positive sign in the spectral measure. More explicitly, the positive spectral weights of the two-port matrix at the massless and massive lines are
$$
(1+A)\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
Aw_\ell\begin{pmatrix}1&-1\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}.
$$
They are positive semidefinite at every atom. The resulting joint susceptibility includes every oscillator and both readout ports. In particular the negative cross coefficient is compatible with stable positive Hamiltonians. At any strictly positive massive mass of this sequence, an identical Hermitian source and detector would instead have a nonnegative diagonal spectral weight; the same conclusion holds for the continuum limit by testing nonnegative continuous functions supported in an open positive-mass interval with nonzero $\sigma$ mass. This gives the exact boundary between the signed transfer realized here and a positive single-port susceptibility.

*Finite carrier, spectrum and window comparison.* For each spatial and mass budget supply separate finite occupation matrices for every oscillator, with the ready vector its ground state, the physical energies $\hbar\omega n$ and the compressed canonical coordinate matrix. The occupation-zero to occupation-one energy and matrix elements are exact once level one is retained. Hence the vacuum linear response of each chosen mode, including the cross terms above, is exact in the ideal finite matrix comparison. A finite occupation cutoff gives a bounded drive and detector. All other supplied states and unused sectors remain in the finite matrix response, and the quoted exactness concerns its vacuum linear response. The two port coefficients multiply the same canonical drive and detector matrices and are implemented with their declared positive pulse support, clock, program and readout records, using the finite matrix controls of Proposition 46g.33. Allocate independent physical normal-mode stocks and the two port controls with their joint references. Keep the separate budgets for the two drives, both detector outputs, auxiliary copies, timing and reference moves. Charge the actual complete finite schedule by the fixed finite-service tariff of Proposition 46g.37. Finite synthesis errors can be made summable over the registered prefix. This is a finite modal source on a fixed flat background; its controls and readouts have their declared physical supports and are not an unproved uniform local relativistic field compiler.

For a finite time slab and a fixed compact spacetime source/test budget, the exact causal continuum operators have finite propagation speed. Put all those windows and their causal buffers in a sufficiently large periodic box so that periodic images of the source do not enter the retained comparison. At a fixed such box the omitted massless spatial constant contributes at most $D^2/2$ times the spatial average of the source. Its local error tends to zero with the inverse box volume for a fixed compact spatial support and bounded source. The same assertion holds for its time derivatives. On the finite box truncate the spatial Fourier lists after fixing the required derivative and error budgets. Smooth sources have summable Fourier tails after sufficiently many derivatives, and the mode-response estimate $D^2/2$ is uniform in all nonnegative masses. Thus the tails tend to zero also for the signed bank and the weighted positive auto-responses, whose total weights are at most $1+2A$. Take the finite mass quadrature, periodic box, spatial cutoff and paid finite synthesis along a single increasing finite-prefix diagonal. On each requested window this realizes the continuum cross response with the estimate above plus the separately controlled spatial and finite implementation errors.

This realizes the signed nonrational transfer as a limit of physically specified positive finite mode banks with a signed output leg. It does not identify the detector with the same physical source current, nor derive nonlinear metric variation, covariant curved-background completion or the joint cosmological projections of Definition I.13d. $\square$

<a id="theorem-i13m-retarded-variational-reciprocity-and-a-doubled-classical-response"></a>**Theorem I.13m (Retarded Variational Reciprocity and a Doubled Classical Response).** Let $M$ be a globally hyperbolic spacetime, and let a twice continuously differentiable real single-history functional have a distributional Hessian $H(x,y)$ on compactly supported variations of real fields. Suppose that Hessian is retarded: its support is contained in $\{(x,y):x\in J^+(y)\}$. Then its support is contained in the diagonal $x=y$. In particular, no genuinely off-diagonal retarded kernel can be the Hessian of such a functional. This conclusion applies at each background at which these hypotheses hold, including nonlinear functionals.

For the flat operator of Theorem I.13l there is instead the classical doubled response functional
$$
\mathcal I[h_c,h_\Delta;T]
=\int h_\Delta^{\mu\nu}(E_{\mathrm{ret}}h_c+\kappa T/2)_{\mu\nu}\,d^4x,
\tag{I.13m.1}
$$
where $h_c\in\mathscr F$, $T\in\mathscr F$ is conserved and $h_\Delta\in C_c^\infty$. The integral is finite. Variation in arbitrary compact $h_\Delta$ gives precisely (I.13l.3). Variation in compact directions of $h_c$ gives $E_{\mathrm{adv}}h_\Delta=0$, where every $G_\lambda$ in the formal transpose is replaced by its advanced Green operator. Thus the physical branch $h_\Delta=0$, with the zero-past condition on $h_c$, has exactly the response (I.13l.4). Compact gauge variations of either field leave (I.13m.1) invariant. This is a doubled classical variational representation; a quantum closed-time-path state, influence functional and positivity conditions are additional data.

*Proof.* Equality of mixed second variations gives $H_{AB}(x,y)=H_{BA}(y,x)$ in distributions. Retarded support is therefore also advanced support. In a globally hyperbolic spacetime, $x\in J^+(y)$ and $y\in J^+(x)$ imply $x=y$, since a distinct pair would produce a closed causal curve. Their intersection is the diagonal, proving the assertion without assuming translation invariance. It constrains the equation's Hessian, not the causal inverse of a local variational equation: local wave actions have diagonal Hessians and retarded propagators.

For (I.13m.1), compactness of $h_\Delta$ and smoothness of the response make every pairing finite. Its two first variations give the displayed equations. To verify the transpose, integrate the Green identity for two zero-past/zero-future solutions on a slab containing the compact test supports; the temporal end terms vanish by their respective support conditions and the spatial end terms vanish by finite propagation. This gives $\langle v,G_\lambda u\rangle=\langle G_\lambda^{\mathrm{adv}}v,u\rangle$. Reversing compositions and integrating ordinary derivatives proves the asserted formal transpose for every rational factor and projector. Equivalently it follows directly by transposing their retarded convolution kernels. The zero difference field solves the advanced equation identically. Gauge variation in $h_c$ vanishes because $E_{\mathrm{ret}}$ kills pure gauges; variation in $h_\Delta$ vanishes by integration by parts against the conserved expression $E_{\mathrm{ret}}h_c+\kappa T/2$. All these variations have compact support, so there is no omitted endpoint or spatial boundary term. The zero-past choice belongs to the solution domain and is not obtained by extremizing a symmetric kernel. ∎

Theorems I.13l–I.13m establish a retarded operator and classical variational realization on their rational linear class. Theorem I.13c.5, item 6, continues to exclude its source-linear responses from the mass-dependent spatial-clock law when $A_G>0$. Definition I.13d still requires the nonlinear common source, physical stress and all galaxy, cluster, lensing, local, CMB, homogeneous and backreaction projections with their shared units and residuals. The rational linear construction does not assert a nonlinear common-action source completion.

<a id="theorem-i13ma"></a>

<a id="theorem-i13ma-covariant-conserved-retarded-curvature-bank-for-the-weibull-equation"></a>**Theorem I.13m.a (Covariant Conserved Retarded Curvature Bank for the Weibull Equation).** Use the fixed-scale no-slip Weibull pair of Theorem I.13l.a with $0<m\le1$ and $A>0$. Write $\rho_A$ for the positive finite reciprocal measure of (I.13l.a.6) and $q_A=A/(1+A)$ for its mass. There is a sequence of finite, generally covariant local auxiliary actions whose retarded metric Euler tensors converge on every fixed smooth globally hyperbolic metric with compact Cauchy surfaces and a prescribed past Cauchy slice. The limit is a nonlinear, diffeomorphism-covariant and distributionally conserved metric functional on these metric histories. On Minkowski space its zero-past linearization is exactly the no-slip Weibull equation of Theorem I.13l.a, with $a=c=1/\mu$. This is a response functional on prescribed metric histories. Its signed auxiliary actions do not establish positivity or a coupled metric Cauchy theorem.

*Local actions and prescription.* For a smooth metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ let $\Box_g$ be its rough wave operator on symmetric covariant two-tensors, or its scalar wave operator on scalars, as typed by the argument. For $v\ge0$ let $X_v$ be a real symmetric two-tensor and $\phi_v$ a real scalar. Define the local expression
$$
\mathcal L_v
=2X_v^{\mu\nu}R_{\mu\nu}
  -X_v^{\mu\nu}(\Box_g-v)X_{v,\mu\nu}
  -\tfrac12\bigl[2\phi_v R-\phi_v(\Box_g-v)\phi_v\bigr].
\tag{I.13m.a.1}
$$
All tensor contractions are with $g$. Let $\rho_n=\sum_j w_j\delta_{v_j}$ be finite positive approximants of mass $q_A$, with compact mass meshes tending to zero and discarded tail mass tending to zero. The construction of such meshes is described below. On each finite bank use the local action
$$
S_n[g,X,\phi]=-2\int R\,d\mathrm{vol}_g
 -2\sum_j w_j\int\mathcal L_{v_j}\,d\mathrm{vol}_g
 +2q_A\int\mathcal L_0\,d\mathrm{vol}_g .
\tag{I.13m.a.2}
$$
Coincident auxiliary copies may be combined or kept distinct. The integrals define local first variations against compactly supported tests. Boundary terms are omitted only for those variations. Vary all fields independently first. The auxiliary equations are
$$
(\Box_g-v)X_v=\operatorname{Ric}(g),\qquad
(\Box_g-v)\phi_v=R(g).
\tag{I.13m.a.3}
$$
The rough wave operators are formally self-adjoint for their natural indefinite tensor contraction. Their principal part is the scalar Lorentzian wave symbol times the identity. Supply zero field and normal derivative on the chosen past Cauchy slice $\Sigma_0$. The ordinary normally hyperbolic Cauchy problem then gives unique auxiliary fields and causal support on the future slab. On Minkowski space use the zero-past response convention of Theorem I.13l, with metric perturbations vanishing before a Cauchy slice. The choice of auxiliary Cauchy data belongs to the solution prescription after variation. No retarded solution is substituted into an action before varying it. See Bär et al. (2007).

Let $\mathcal E_n(g)$ be the metric Euler distribution of (I.13m.a.2), evaluated only after solving (I.13m.a.3). For a compactly supported vector field $\xi$ in the interior of the slab, covariance of the local action gives a Noether identity by using $\delta g=\mathcal L_\xi g$, $\delta X=\mathcal L_\xi X$ and $\delta\phi=\mathcal L_\xi\phi$. The auxiliary terms vanish on their equations, so
$$
\langle\mathcal E_n(g),\mathcal L_\xi g\rangle=0 .
\tag{I.13m.a.4}
$$
Integration by parts gives covariant conservation in distributions. The finite response is natural under diffeomorphisms transporting $g$, the time orientation and $\Sigma_0$. It is causal as a metric functional: two histories agreeing on a common past domain with the same auxiliary data there give the same auxiliary fields in its domain of dependence, by the local wave uniqueness theorem. The metric variation in (I.13m.a.2) is local in those fields and the metric, so their metric Euler distributions agree there. Compactly supported tests in the interior avoid any imposed boundary variation at $\Sigma_0$.

*Mass-uniform response estimate on a curved slab.* Fix a compact Cauchy slab $0\le t\le T$ with a smooth spacelike foliation, lapse bounded away from zero, and fixed smooth $g$. Choose smooth positive fiber norms on its finite-rank bundles. For either auxiliary field $Y_v$, with source $J$ equal to $\operatorname{Ric}$ or $R$, one has
$$
\sup_{0\le t\le T}
\left(
\|Y_v\|_{L^2(\Sigma_t)}
+\|\nabla Y_v\|_{L^2(\Sigma_t)}
+\sqrt v\,\|Y_v\|_{L^2(\Sigma_t)}
\right)
\le C_{g,T}\|J\|_{L^1_tL^2_x},
\tag{I.13m.a.5}
$$
uniformly for $v\ge0$. To see the uniformity, choose a smooth connection preserving the positive fiber norm and express the rough wave equation using it. The difference consists of bounded first- and zero-order terms independent of $v$. Multiply the equation by the time-normal derivative and integrate on the compact slices.
