<a id="theorem-i13q-scalar-continuation-characteristic-cone-and-timelike-moduli-of-the-fixed-static-action"></a>**Theorem I.13q (Scalar Continuation, Characteristic Cone and Timelike Moduli of the Fixed Static Action).** Fix $a=a_\chi>0$, $G>0$, $n>0$ and a strict static branch of Theorem I.13c.5 with amplitude $A\ge0$. Write $\nu(y)=1+A(1-e^{-y^{-n}})$, $h(y)=y\nu(y)$, $k=h^{-1}$, $F(x)=\int_0^xk(t)dt$ and $\mu(x)=k(x)/x$. Use signature $(-,+,+,+)$, $x^0=ct$, a scalar $\Phi$ with Newtonian-potential units and
$$
X=g^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\Phi\partial_\nu\Phi,\qquad
S_\Phi=\frac1{4\pi Gc}\int\sqrt{-g}\,P(X)\,d^4x.
\tag{I.13q.1}
$$
The class has no additional field, preferred vector, curvature, higher derivative or nonlocal term; $P$ is $C^2$ wherever a principal response is claimed. Its $P(X)$ form includes reflection symmetry. Matching the entire fixed static integrand and $P(0)=0$ uniquely forces
$$
P_+(X)=-a^2F(\sqrt X/a),\qquad X\ge0.
\tag{I.13q.2}
$$
The action has the exact varied source/stress, positive background-frame quadratic energy and wider characteristic cone proved below. Time-retarded response exists on the constant-gradient test. The critical static endpoint has a precise $C^2$ obstruction. On the strict branch, complete static data and the vacuum constant leave the displayed smooth timelike source family undetermined, even with positive energy and regular timelike principal response.

**Proof. I. Static uniqueness, source normalization and Ward tensor.** On static fields the real-time Lagrangian is the negative of the energy of Theorem I.13c.5, which forces (I.13q.2). Equivalently, matching the flux at every positive magnitude fixes $-2P_X=\mu$; integration and $P(0)=0$ give the same result. There is no independent spacelike time-kinetic coefficient in this Lorentz-scalar class. Let an actual matter action $S_m[g,\Phi,\psi]$ supply $J=-(c/\sqrt{-g})\delta S_m/\delta\Phi$, with static convention $J=\rho_b$. Variation gives
$$
-2\nabla_\mu(P_X\partial^\mu\Phi)=4\pi GJ,\qquad
T_\Phi^{\mu\nu}=\frac1{4\pi G}[-2P_X\partial^\mu\Phi\partial^\nu\Phi+Pg^{\mu\nu}].
\tag{I.13q.3}
$$
The convention is $T_{\mu\nu}=-(2c/\sqrt{-g})\delta S/\delta g^{\mu\nu}$. On $X>0$, the equation is $\nabla_\mu(\mu\partial^\mu\Phi)=4\pi GJ$ and the static spatial tensor is $(4\pi G)^{-1}[\mu\partial_i\Phi\partial_j\Phi-a^2F\delta_{ij}]$, exactly the accepted static stress. Product differentiation cancels the symmetric second derivatives and gives $\nabla_\mu T_\Phi^{\mu\nu}=J\partial^\nu\Phi$. For a diffeomorphism-invariant matter action on its matter equations the opposite Ward term conserves the complete tensor. An externally prescribed $J$ alone supplies no matter/action realization. This scalar is not identified with both relativistic metric potentials or assigned a lensing response by that relabeling.

**II. Exact spacelike principal response and maximum speed.** At a regular point put $x=\sqrt X/a=h(y)>0$. Linearization gives
$$
\mathsf C^{\mu\nu}=\mu g^{\mu\nu}
+\frac{\mu'(x)}{a^2x}\partial^\mu\Phi\partial^\nu\Phi.
\tag{I.13q.4}
$$
In the orthonormal frame with gradient $(0,ax,0,0)$ it is $\operatorname{diag}(-\mu,k',\mu,\mu)$, since $\mu+x\mu'=k'$, $\mu=1/\nu(y)$ and $k'=1/h'(y)$. The quadratic action is
$$
S^{(2)}=-\frac1{8\pi Gc}\int\sqrt{-g}\,
\mathsf C^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\phi\partial_\nu\phi\,d^4x.
\tag{I.13q.5}
$$
For $h'>0$ its time and spatial energy coefficients in this background-adapted frame are positive. This is not an all-observer energy theorem on every metric-spacelike foliation. The characteristic ratios are
$$
\frac{c_\parallel^2}{c^2}=\frac{\nu(y)}{h'(y)},\quad
\frac{c_\perp^2}{c^2}=1,\quad
h'(y)=\nu(y)-Anue^{-u},\quad u=y^{-n}.
\tag{I.13q.6}
$$
For $A>0$, every finite positive spacelike gradient has $c_\parallel>c$. The cone is hyperbolic, its background-frame quadratic energy is positive, and Part III gives its time-retarded response. At $A=0$ the speeds equal $c$.

For $A>0$, let $u_A\in(0,1)$ be the unique root $(1-u_A)e^{u_A}=A/(1+A)$. The exact maximum is
$$
\sup_{y>0}\frac{c_\parallel^2}{c^2}
=\frac1{1-n(1-u_A)},\qquad y=u_A^{-1/n}.
\tag{I.13q.7}
$$
Indeed the ratio is $1/(1-z(u))$, $z(u)=Anu/[(1+A)e^u-A]$. Its derivative has the sign of $(1+A)e^u(1-u)-A$, strictly decreasing on $u>0$, positive at zero and negative at one. At the unique zero the denominator of $z$ is $(1+A)e^{u_A}u_A$, so $z=n(1-u_A)$. The strict static branch gives $1-z>0$. Both endpoint limits give speed $c$. At $n>1$ the maximum diverges as $A$ approaches the critical amplitude; for $n\le1$ every finite $A$ is regular.

**III. Time-retarded test and critical regularity.** On the fixed flat-metric scalar background $\Phi=ax\,x^1$, $J=0$, the tensor is constant. This is a scalar-equation test background; its nonzero stress is not declared a coupled Einstein solution. Put $v=\sqrt{\nu/h'}$ and $r_v=\sqrt{(x^1/v)^2+(x^2)^2+(x^3)^2}$. With a $\delta$ source relative to $dt\,d^3x$,
$$
G_{\mathrm{ret}}(t,\mathbf x)=-\frac{\delta(t-r_v/c)}{4\pi\mu v r_v}.
\tag{I.13q.8}
$$
The substitution $x^1=vz^1$ turns the operator into $\mu[-c^{-2}\partial_t^2+\Delta_z]$ and contributes $1/v$. The retarded radial distribution for the bracket is $-\delta(t-|z|/c)/(4\pi|z|)$, normalized by unit outward Coulomb flux. Thus (I.13q.8) vanishes at negative time; a scalar source variation has response $4\pi G G_{\mathrm{ret}}$. For $v>1$ its front reaches $x^1=vct$ outside the metric cone. Smooth compact source bumps also give nonzero response at suitable metric-spacelike points by convolution. A response-faithful same-$g$ cone-contained carrier cannot realize this branch with (I.13q.2) and $A>0$. That rejection uses the independently retained cone identification; preferred-frame, disformal, multifield, higher-derivative and nonlocal repairs are different classes.

At $n>1$, $A=A_{\mathrm{crit}}(n)$ of (I.13c.5.2), $h'(y_*)=h''(y_*)=0$ and $h^{(3)}(y_*)>0$ at $y_*=[(n-1)/n]^{-1/n}$. The sign follows by twice differentiating $h'=1+A[1-e^{-u}(1+nu)]$ at its nondegenerate minimum. A finite $k'$ would make $k'(h(y_*))h'(y_*)=1$ impossible. Inversion of the nonzero cubic term gives a cube-root cusp in $k-y_*$ and a $|x-h(y_*)|^{4/3}$ leading nonaffine term in $F$. Thus (I.13q.2) is not $C^2$ at $X_*=a^2h(y_*)^2$. The accepted $C^1$ static endpoint remains; no assertion is made about every weaker-solution theory. Above criticality the static obstruction is Theorem I.13c.5(5).

**IV. Smooth timelike extensions and explicit source moduli.** On the strict branch put $b_0=1+A$. Since $ye^{-y^{-n}}$ is smooth and flat at zero, extend $h(y)=b_0y$ to negative $y$ near zero. Smooth inversion gives $k(x)=x/b_0$ plus a flat remainder. Integrate and compose with $\sqrt X$: every derivative of that remainder is a finite sum of flat derivatives times inverse powers of $X$, which flatness dominates. Hence $P_+(X)=-X/(2b_0)$ plus a smooth flat remainder at $0+$. Therefore
$$
P_0(X)=\begin{cases}P_+(X),&X\ge0,\\-X/(2b_0),&X\le0\end{cases}
\tag{I.13q.9}
$$
is $C^\infty$. For $A>0$ no real-analytic $P$ near zero can give the exact static branch: its jet is exactly $-X/(2b_0)$, while $h(y)<b_0y$ gives $k(x)>x/b_0$ and $P_+(X)<-X/(2b_0)$ for every $X>0$. The analytic identity theorem contradicts that strict inequality. Smoothness suffices; analyticity is not imposed as a physical requirement.

Define the literal smooth bump and family
$$
\mathcal B(z)=\begin{cases}\exp[-1/((z-1)(2-z))],&1<z<2,\\0,&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}
\qquad P_\epsilon(X)=P_0(X)+\epsilon a^2\mathcal B(-X/a^2).
\tag{I.13q.10}
$$
All members have identical complete static action, derivatives, equations, stress and $P(0)=0$ on $X\ge0$. Their difference is supported strictly in $-2a^2<X<-a^2$, not in a vacuum counterterm or a retuning of $G,a,A,n$. Every
$$
|\epsilon|\le[512(1+A)]^{-1}
\tag{I.13q.11}
$$
preserves positive timelike energy and regular positive-energy principal response throughout $X<0$. To verify it, put $t=(z-1)(2-z)\le1/4$, $u=1/t\ge4$. Then $|\mathcal B|<1$, $|\mathcal B'|\le u^2e^{-u}<1$, and
$$
|\mathcal B''|\le e^{-u}(u^4+2u^3+2u^2)\le416e^{-4}<26.
$$
Here $u^je^{-u}$ decreases for $u\ge4$, $j\le4$, and $e^4>16$. The principal quantities $-P_X$ and $-(P_X+2XP_{XX})$ have base $1/(2b_0)$, with perturbations at most $|\epsilon|$ and $105|\epsilon|$. Equation (I.13q.11) keeps each positive, the second above $1/(4b_0)$. In the timelike rest frame,
$$
\rho_\Phi=(2XP_X-P)/(4\pi G),\qquad p_\Phi=P/(4\pi G).
\tag{I.13q.12}
$$
The base density is $-X/(8\pi Gb_0)$, at least $a^2/(8\pi Gb_0)$ on the bump support; its perturbation is at most $5|\epsilon|a^2/(4\pi G)$. Equation (I.13q.11) preserves positivity; outside the bump it is unchanged. These bounds establish the stated classical scalar stress and principal-response conditions. At $X=-3a^2/2$, $\mathcal B=e^{-4}$ and $\mathcal B'=0$, giving the exact distinct homogeneous projections
$$
\delta p_\Phi=\epsilon a^2e^{-4}/(4\pi G),\qquad
\delta\rho_\Phi=-\epsilon a^2e^{-4}/(4\pi G).
\tag{I.13q.13}
$$
A constant timelike gradient solves each vacuum scalar equation on the fixed flat test and has conserved constant stress. Flat space with that stress is not asserted an Einstein solution. The source projections already differ before a metric solution is chosen: full static data, including the vacuum constant, do not select one homogeneous scalar source. ∎

<a id="theorem-i13r-convex-scalar-addition-boundary-lensing-and-a-sharp-multifield-cone-bound"></a>**Theorem I.13r (Convex Scalar-Addition Boundary, Lensing and a Sharp Multifield Cone Bound).** Consider a finite collection of local first-gradient scalars on an ordinary Einstein metric with $\lambda>0$, tensor coefficient $G_E=\lambda G$ and actual matter metric $\widetilde g_{\mu\nu}=e^{2q\cdot\phi/c^2}g_{\mu\nu}$, with constant real charges $q_i$. Retain the actual matter action and source normalization. At leading weak-static order, under the finite scalar-energy/potential scaling in which scalar backreaction enters at the next order,
$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{phys}}=U+q\cdot\phi,\quad\Psi_{\mathrm{phys}}=U-q\cdot\phi,\quad
\Delta U=4\pi\lambda G\rho_b,\qquad\Phi_{\mathrm{phys}}+\Psi_{\mathrm{phys}}=2U.
\tag{I.13r.1}
$$
Thus an independently added scalar does not obtain the lapse-clock lensing result by relabeling its potential. Use the fixed acceleration normalization $a_0>0$ of the source (the registered member has $a_0=c^2\sqrt\Lambda/8$) and the same $\nu,h$ of the static law. The following convex-force and characteristic statements use the genuine dark branch $A>0,n>1$ with strict $m_A=\min h'>0$. Theorem I.13o supplies the separate preferred-clock lapse action; the following classification concerns the stated finite scalar class.

**Proof. I. Matter coupling and the Newtonian double count.** The actual $S_m[\widetilde g,\psi]$ and scalar equations conserve the complete tensor by their diffeomorphism identity. Expansion of the conformal factor gives (I.13r.1); null geodesics are conformally invariant, fixing leading lensing to $2U$. Scalar stress remains in the exact action with its stated higher-order backreaction. Adding the full unit-coupling static scalar response of Theorem I.13q to a $\lambda=1$ tensor gives
$$
g_{\mathrm{phys}}=g_N+g_N\nu(g_N/a_0)
=[2+A(1-e^{-(a_0/g_N)^n})]g_N,
\tag{I.13r.2}
$$
with local Newtonian limit $2G$. More generally a same-shape sum $\lambda g_N+w g_N\nu(y)$ matches the original high- and low-acceleration endpoints only if $\lambda+w=1$ and $\lambda+(1+A)w=1+A$. At $A>0$, $w=1$, $\lambda=0$. The endpoint equations classify the stated fixed-shape sum.

**II. Arbitrarily coupled finite convex scalars.** Let the static scalar energy multiplied by $4\pi G$ be a differentiable convex rotationally invariant function $E$ of all scalar spatial gradients, including cross-couplings. On radial fields put $v_i=\partial_r\phi_i$ and $e(v)=E(v_1n,\ldots,v_Nn)$. The common normalized matter flux and scalar force are
$$
\nabla e(v)=q s,\quad s=g_N=GM_b(r)/r^2,\qquad\delta g=q\cdot v.
\tag{I.13r.3}
$$
For a sheet use $s=2\pi G\Sigma_b$. If $s_2>s_1>0$, convex gradient monotonicity gives
$$
0\le[\nabla e(v_2)-\nabla e(v_1)]\cdot(v_2-v_1)
=(s_2-s_1)[\delta g(s_2)-\delta g(s_1)].
\tag{I.13r.4}
$$
Thus every such increment is nondecreasing, even if the inverse is not differentiable. On a regular strictly convex branch $H=D^2e>0$, $\delta g'(s)=q^{\mathsf T}H^{-1}q\ge0$. At the original $\lambda=1$ calibration the required increment is $As[1-e^{-(a_0/s)^n}]$, whose derivative is $A[1-(1+nu)e^{-u}]$, $u=(a_0/s)^n$. It is negative for $0<u<u_c$, where $e^{u_c}=1+nu_c$; the unique positive root is proved in Theorem I.13p. No finite number of these convex scalar forces, however coupled and nonlinear, realizes that full increment at the same ordinary Einstein $G$. The class is nonempty, containing canonical attractive scalars. The monotonicity argument covers the stated nonlinear convex scalar class.

**III. Exact static boundary under altered tensor calibration.** Allow $\lambda\ge0$ in this static comparison and put $r_\lambda(y)=h(y)-\lambda y$. Its minimum derivative gives
$$
m_A=1+A[1-ne^{-(n-1)/n}]>0.
\tag{I.13r.5}
$$
Convexity requires $\lambda\le m_A$. Conversely, on the stated $A>0,n>1$ strict branch, $0\le\lambda\le m_A<1$ makes $r_\lambda$ strictly increasing and unbounded, with only one zero derivative at equality. Its inverse $j_\lambda$ supplies
$$
F_\lambda(x)=\int_0^xj_\lambda(t)dt,\qquad
E_\lambda(v)=a_0^2F_\lambda(|v|/a_0).
\tag{I.13r.6}
$$
Its flux equation gives $|v|=a_0r_\lambda(y)$ and $\lambda g_N+|v|=a_0h(y)$ exactly. At $\lambda<m_A$ the Hessian is regular and positive; at equality its inverse derivative diverges at the minimizing point, giving a convex $C^1$ static endpoint rather than a regular $C^2$ principal theory. This inverse statement is not extended to the degenerate $A=0,\lambda=1$ case. For $A=7,n=3/2$, $m_A=8-(21/2)e^{-1/3}\approx0.476421238975$. The compatible tensor coefficient is less than half $G$, and the leading lensing coefficient is $\lambda$ by (I.13r.1). This does not authorize changing an independently retained metric calibration or fitting lensing after the static match.

**IV. Sharp multifield characteristic comparison.** For a Lorentz-invariant first-gradient action $P(X_{ij})$, $X_{ij}=g^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\phi_i\partial_\nu\phi_j$, at a collinear spacelike background define $K=-2P_X$ using the symmetric-matrix derivative. The flux is $Kv=qs$, the longitudinal static Hessian is $H=D^2e$, and the quadratic principal action, up to a positive factor, is
$$
\tfrac12\dot\phi^{\mathsf T}K\dot\phi/c^2
-\tfrac12(\partial_\parallel\phi)^{\mathsf T}H(\partial_\parallel\phi)
-\tfrac12\sum_\perp(\partial_\perp\phi)^{\mathsf T}K(\partial_\perp\phi).
\tag{I.13r.7}
$$
Assume exactly the positive time/spatial quadratic-energy conditions $K,H>0$. For $C=c_{\max}^2/c^2=\lambda_{\max}(K^{-1/2}HK^{-1/2})$, $H\le CK$ and $H^{-1}\ge C^{-1}K^{-1}$. Equations (I.13r.3)–(I.13r.4) imply
$$
\delta g'(s)=q^{\mathsf T}H^{-1}q\ge C^{-1}q^{\mathsf T}K^{-1}q
=C^{-1}\delta g(s)/s,\qquad
\frac{c_{\max}^2}{c^2}\ge\frac{\nu(y)-\lambda}{h'(y)-\lambda}>1,
\tag{I.13r.8}
$$
where $h'-\lambda>0$. The strict sign follows from $\nu-h'=Anue^{-u}>0$. The single-scalar construction (I.13r.6) saturates the ratio, so it is sharp. Adding finitely many convex Lorentz scalars cannot remove the wider cone with that same response and constant conformal coupling. The wider cone retains hyperbolicity and time-retarded response; physical rejection uses an independently retained same-metric containment premise. Preferred-frame fields, nonminimal curvature, disformal metrics, higher derivatives and nonlocality are outside the theorem. ∎

<a id="theorem-i13s-a-positive-radiation-source-realizing-the-initial-capacity-weighted-proper-separation-response"></a>**Theorem I.13s (A positive radiation source realizing the initial capacity-weighted proper-separation response).**
Keep the same $G>0$, $\Lambda>0$, physical proper-time unit and minimal clock action as I.13o. Let $N_{\rm cmp}=2$ and $M_{\rm sp}=8$. For any finite positive atomic law
$$
\mu=\sum_{j=1}^r\pi_j\delta_{t_j},\quad\pi_j>0,\quad\sum_j\pi_j=1,
\quad t_j\in(0,1)^d,\quad
m(q)=\sum_j\pi_j\prod_{l=1}^d t_{jl}^{q_l},\quad q\in\mathbb N^d,
\tag{I.13s.1}
$$
there is a positive homogeneous null-stream release-slice preparation and a retained three-qubit instrument whose actual metric-generated initial differential proper-separation acceleration has operating derivative
$$
g_{\rm rad}(q)=\frac{C(q)}{\ln2}\,\frac14\frac34\frac1{\sqrt3}
\,c^2\sqrt{\Lambda/3},\qquad
C(q)=N_{\rm cmp}\ln2\,m(q).
\tag{I.13s.2}
$$
The density equality, homogeneous ruler, source-to-initial-data assignment, ideal classical clocks and retained source records specified below are premises. The physical output is the signed difference of two initial proper-separation accelerations differentiated in an independently normalized source parameter. It is an initial response on this source class. Each outcome has its own conserved positive source and Einstein evolution. Its homogeneous geodesic clock embeds it in the same varied-clock action; a mean stress is not evolved in place of individual outcomes.

##### Part I. Conserved positive source, exact metric and observable

Use the three-torus of coordinate side $L$ and
$$
ds^2=-c^2dt^2+\sum_i a_i(t)^2(dx^i)^2,\quad
V=L^3a_xa_ya_z,\quad H_i=\dot a_i/a_i.
$$
The source is a finite collection of **labels** for spatially homogeneous collisionless null streams along $\pm x,\pm y,\pm z$, including positive isotropic tagged null streams used for the ruler, and optional comoving pressureless controls. Every opposite pair has equal density. If $K_i>0$ is its conserved comoving momentum weight and $E_d\ge0$ is control rest energy, then
$$
E(a)=E_d+\sum_iK_i/a_i,\quad\rho=E/V,\quad
p_i=K_i/(a_iV),\qquad
\dot\rho+\sum_iH_i(\rho+p_i)=0.
\tag{I.13s.3}
$$
Here $\rho$ is energy density. These are the Routh data of minimally coupled massless worldlines with null Hamiltonian $c\sqrt{\sum_i p_i^2/a_i^2}$; on an axis ray it is $c|p_i|/a_i$. Lapse variation of $-NE(a)$ gives $E$ and directional variation gives $p_i=-(a_i/V)\partial_{a_i}E$. Homogeneity preserves the axis-ray class exactly. All stream labels remain retained even when their summed stress agrees. The displayed conservation follows by differentiation.
The exact Einstein equations are
$$
H_xH_y+H_yH_z+H_zH_x=\Lambda c^2+8\pi G\rho/c^2,
$$
$$
\dot H_i+H_i\sum_jH_j=\Lambda c^2+\frac{4\pi G}{c^2}
\left(\rho-\sum_jp_j+2p_i\right).
\tag{I.13s.4}
$$
Conservation preserves the constraint. Choose $a_i(0)=1$ and all $H_i(0)=H_*$, with $3H_*^2=\Lambda c^2+8\pi G\rho_*/c^2$, the same for every outcome since its total energy is the same. Thus outcome-dependent second derivatives, rather than different initial metrics, carry the response.
Put
$$
R_\Lambda=\sqrt{3/\Lambda},\quad\rho_v=\Lambda c^4/(8\pi G),\quad
D_i(t)=R_\Lambda a_i(t),\quad
\mathcal A_{xy}=\tfrac12[\ddot D_x(0)-\ddot D_y(0)].
$$
Mark comoving observers at $\pm R_\Lambda/2$ on each axis and take $L>2R_\Lambda$. These curves are timelike geodesics and $D_i$ is their actual shortest homogeneous spatial separation on a sufficiently small registered window. Subtracting (I.13s.4), using equal initial $H_i$, gives
$$
\mathcal A_{xy}=\frac{4\pi G R_\Lambda}{c^2}(p_x-p_y)
=\frac{8\pi G R_\Lambda}{c^2}P,\qquad P=(p_x-p_y)/2.
\tag{I.13s.5}
$$
A ruler of initial length $\ell$ yields $\ell/R_\Lambda$ times this value. This finite homogeneous distance identity also agrees with the corresponding initial electric-curvature/geodesic-deviation component; it does not require extending a local small-distance expansion to $R_\Lambda$.

For these sources $0\le\sum_i p_i\le\rho$. At $H_i=0$ the forcing in (I.13s.4) is positive. At an index attaining $H_{\max}$, the constraint gives
$$
\dot H_i\le\Lambda c^2+8\pi G\rho/c^2-H_i\sum_jH_j
=H_jH_k-H_i^2\le0.
$$
Consequently $0<H_i\le H_*$ and $1\le a_i\le e^{H_*t}$; the smooth ODE remains regular for every finite future time. Take an auxiliary isotropic density $\rho_{\rm aux}=\rho_d+\rho_{\rm tag}\le\rho_v/2$, with $\rho_{\rm tag}>0$. Since $\rho_*=N_{\rm cmp}\rho_v+\rho_{\rm aux}$, we have $H_*\le\sqrt{7/2}\,c/R_\Lambda<2c/R_\Lambda$. A marker signal traverses at least $c(1-e^{-H_*T})/H_*$ in comoving distance. Every record emitted at $t_e$ arrives at the center by
$$
T_{\rm arr}(t_e)=\frac{-\ln[e^{-H_*t_e}-H_*R_\Lambda/(2c)]}{H_*},
\qquad t_e<\frac{\ln[2c/(H_*R_\Lambda)]}{H_*}.
\tag{I.13s.6}
$$
These are causal records carrying proper timestamps, not simultaneous remote measurements.

##### Part II. The finite ruler and its errors

The meter admits synchronized comoving proper clocks at release and nondemolition reads of degenerate finite labels transported by the counted tagged null streams. Its ideal clock accuracy is an apparatus input. A segment of coordinate length $R_\Lambda/J$ with transit time $\Delta$ satisfies
$$
R_\Lambda/J=\int_t^{t+\Delta}c/a_i(v)\,dv,
\quad
\frac{c(1-e^{-H_*\Delta})}{H_*}\le a_i(t)R_\Lambda/J\le c\Delta.
$$
Thus $Jc\Delta$ estimates $D_i(t)$ with geometric error at most $JcH_*\Delta^2/2$. For stencil times $s,2s$, let starting-time error be at most $\epsilon_t<s$, each transit timestamp error at most $\epsilon_t$, and $T_*=2s+\epsilon_t$. If $H_*R_\Lambda e^{H_*T_*}/(cJ)\le1/2$, then
$$
\Delta\le\Delta_*:=\frac{2R_\Lambda e^{H_*T_*}}{cJ},\qquad
\epsilon_D=\frac{2H_*R_\Lambda^2e^{2H_*T_*}}{cJ}
+[2Jc+R_\Lambda H_*e^{H_*T_*}]\epsilon_t.
\tag{I.13s.7}
$$
Use the registered exact $D_i(0)=R_\Lambda$. Choose the last local reading $T_{\rm obs}=T_*+\Delta_*$ below (I.13s.6)’s threshold; first choose small $s$, then large finite $J$, then small positive $\epsilon_t$. Finitely many passages and finite labels suffice at each frozen precision. Homogeneity is the premise that converts segment transit data to the full separation; no such inference is claimed for arbitrary sources. The clock accuracy and label measurement remain admitted resources rather than a new quantum-clock bound.

##### Part III. Independently normalized equality preparation

Each comparison copy has total initial source radiation density $\rho_v$, split equally among eight channel labels and then three packets per channel. A packet has density $\rho_{\rm packet}=\rho_v/(3M_{\rm sp})$, independently of the environmental latent law. A sign $\sigma=\pm1$ selects nonnegative opposite-stream weights with pressures
$$
(p_x,p_y,p_z)_{\rm packet}=\frac{\rho_{\rm packet}}3
(1+\sigma,1-\sigma,1),\qquad P_{\rm packet}=\rho_{\rm packet}\sigma/3.
\tag{I.13s.8}
$$
It uses $2/3$ of the energy along $x$ or $y$, and $1/3$ along $z$, and changes no packet energy. By (I.13s.5),
$$
\frac{8\pi G R_\Lambda}{c^2}\frac{\rho_v}{3}=\frac{c^2}{R_\Lambda}.
\tag{I.13s.9}
$$
The equality density is an actual scope condition. In an isotropic precursor, $\dot\rho_{\rm copy}=-4H\rho_{\rm copy}$ and $H\ge c/R_\Lambda$ imply a unique transverse crossing from above $\rho_v$. With no dust and a fixed tag-to-copy radiation ratio $\beta$, the Friedmann quadrature is $(N_{\rm cmp}+\beta)\rho_{\rm copy}/\rho_v=\operatorname{csch}^2(2ct/R_\Lambda)$ after choosing the radiation big-bang origin. This follows on putting $y=a^2$ in the Friedmann equation and integrating $\dot y=2(c/R_\Lambda)\sqrt{y^2+\mathrm{const}}$. Dust changes the crossing time without changing existence or uniqueness. This precursor establishes the attainable density relation; the actual response premise is its explicitly prepared constrained release slice, not an unproved switching history from that precursor.

##### Part IV. Retained finite instrument and common frame

Sample the latent symbol $J$ in (I.13s.1) independently of a message bit. For exposure $q_l$, perform the finitely many conditional survival tests with probability $t_{Jl}$, live iff all survive. Deliver the bit on live and a message-independent erasure symbol otherwise. Retain $J$ and the live flag. Each comparison copy is independently prepared before the common downstream frame projection. All exposure records are owned.
For each channel/copy use a three-qubit source register and an independent uniform eight-valued active label $A_{\rm sel}$. Use **one shared uniform four-valued frame label** $B$ across every channel, both comparison copies and the ruler. It is independent of the latent/tests/message. Two of eight active labels are admitted; $B=0$ is the clock slot, while $B=1,2,3$ are spatial slots. The full-tangent reference has the same unit-QFI source family in every flag block. On live, active and spatial blocks drive
$$
|\psi(\theta)\rangle=\exp\!\left[-\frac{i\theta}{2\sqrt3}(Y_1+Y_2+Y_3)\right]|000\rangle.
\tag{I.13s.10}
$$
Otherwise leave $|000\rangle$ fixed. Since $Y_1+Y_2+Y_3$ has mean zero and variance3 on this state, the generator divided by $\sqrt3$ has variance1 and the pure SLD QFI for $\theta$ is 1. Measuring $X_i$ gives independent signs
$$
\Pr(\sigma_i=+1\mid\theta)=\frac{1+\sin(\theta/\sqrt3)}2,
\quad |\theta|\le\pi\sqrt3/4.
\tag{I.13s.11}
$$
Their classical Fisher information sums to 1 throughout this interval. Disabled blocks give independent unbiased signs. This exact one-parameter readout does not assert losslessness on arbitrary three-qubit inputs. Flag-controlled pulses implement the tangent projections without a hidden discarded $\theta$-dependent output; a reset alternative would have to retain ownership of its environment.
Choose $O_B$ to be the identity and two cyclic axis rotations for the spatial slots. In any one outcome rotate **every** packet and the observer axes by the same $O_B$. Then
$$
T_B=O_B\operatorname{diag}(p_x,p_y,p_z)O_B^{\mathsf T},\quad
P_B=\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}
[O_B\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,0)O_B^{\mathsf T}T_B]=P.
\tag{I.13s.12}
$$
The metric is rotated by the same tensor rule. This proves tensor addition before projection. Condition on $B$ and all retained latent, live and active flags. Given these flags, different channel/copy register outcomes are independent and their conditional scores have mean zero. The flag law is $\theta$-independent, so averaging over the flags preserves zero cross-score inner products and adds their conditional Fisher informations, even when flags are shared within a copy. The four equally weighted $B$ blocks form a direct sum; deleting block0 has norm ratio $3/4$. The active projection retains fraction $2/8=1/4$. Each channel’s32 active/frame score blocks have projection ranks8,24 and joint rank 6; those ranks multiply by the number of channel/copy registers even though the frame is shared. Independence of duplicate frame labels is not required.
For the 24-mode source ledger per comparison copy, the vectors $Y_{c,k}|0\cdots0\rangle$, $c=1,\ldots,8$, $k=1,2,3$, are orthonormal. The normalized channel vector is their three-term sum divided by $\sqrt3$; the eight channel vectors are mutually orthogonal. Thus the selected response-mode count is 24 and $M_{\rm sp}=24/3=8$, not the total tensor-product Hilbert dimension. The equal physical energy shares in Part III are part of this ledger.

Given a classical outcome record $\omega=(J,\mathrm{live},A_{\rm sel},B,\sigma)$, an admitted positive normalized measure-and-prepare primitive assigns precisely (I.13s.8), the counted isotropic auxiliary weights, and the constrained metric datum in Part I. Each outcome has total energy $N_{\rm cmp}\rho_vL^3+\rho_{\rm aux}L^3$, fixed matter action and unique future solution. Choose a monotone pulse from 0 to the selected setting, so its total parameter variation is $|\theta|$. The continuous setting is a classical control of the bounded Hamiltonian $\hbar\dot\theta(Y_1+Y_2+Y_3)/(2\sqrt3)$ with integrated norm at most $\sqrt3\hbar|\theta|/2$ per driven register. The source-state assignment is a release-slice input; an earlier actuator history, microscopic optical-switch synthesis and later disposal/reset are not inferred. At release all retained null-stream and control stress is counted. Labels may have scalar free Hamiltonians; that fact does not remove their positive carrier energy or their preparation resources.

##### Part V. Exact capacity, response, and finite precision

Conditional mutual information per copy is at most $m(q)\ln2$, attained by a uniform bit. Auxiliary controls and signs are independent of the message and cannot enlarge its capacity. Summing two independent copies gives $C(q)$ in (I.13s.2), for the fixed binary alphabet, waveform and clock. Before active/spatial projection, sign QFI is $N_{\rm cmp}m(q)$ per channel; afterward it is $N_{\rm cmp}m(q)(1/4)(3/4)$, and eight channel contributions add. The separate amplitude derivative $1/\sqrt3$ comes from the sine law in (I.13s.11), not by mistaking an amplitude for a QFI factor.
Averaging packet pressures and then using the outcome-by-outcome affine initial identity (I.13s.5) gives
$$
\mathbb E P_{\rm total}=\frac{N_{\rm cmp}\rho_v}{3}m(q)\frac14\frac34
\sin(\theta/\sqrt3),
$$
$$
\mathbb E\mathcal A_{xy}(q,\theta)=N_{\rm cmp}m(q)\frac14\frac34
\frac{c^2}{R_\Lambda}\sin(\theta/\sqrt3).
\tag{I.13s.13}
$$
Differentiation at 0 proves (I.13s.2). The literal finite retained diagonal operator
$$
O_{\mathcal A}(\omega)=\frac{c^2/R_\Lambda}{3M_{\rm sp}}
\sum_{\mathrm{copy},\mathrm{channel},k}\sigma_{\mathrm{copy},\mathrm{channel},k}
\tag{I.13s.14}
$$
equals each individual outcome’s initial metric acceleration, independently of $q,\theta$. Its spectrum lies in $[-N_{\rm cmp}c^2/R_\Lambda,N_{\rm cmp}c^2/R_\Lambda]$. Dead/disabled blocks retain positive energy but have zero derivative; live admitted blocks have the same sine response. Equality is outcome-by-outcome, hence preserves the retained release readout and its noise law. It does not identify subsequent mean-metric histories.
For symmetric angle step $u>0$, $D_u=g_{\rm rad}\operatorname{sinc}(u/\sqrt3)$ and
$$
|D_u-g_{\rm rad}|\le |g_{\rm rad}|u^2/18.
\tag{I.13s.15}
$$
With $n$ independent preparations at each angle, Hoeffding gives, simultaneously with probability at least $1-\delta$,
$$
|\widehat D_u-D_u|\le\frac{N_{\rm cmp}c^2}{uR_\Lambda}
\sqrt{\frac{2\ln(4/\delta)}n}.
\tag{I.13s.16}
$$
The forward time stencil $[D_i(2s)-2D_i(s)+D_i(0)]/s^2$ has error at most $B_3s$, where $B_3=40R_\Lambda H_*^3e^{2H_*s}$. To prove it, write $A_i=\Lambda c^2+(4\pi G/c^2)(\rho_d+2p_i)$: $|\dot H_i|\le3H_*^2$, conservation gives $|\dot A_i|\le12H_*^3$, and then $|\ddot H_i|\le30H_*^3$. Apply $D_i'''=R_\Lambda a_i(H_i^3+3H_i\dot H_i+\ddot H_i)$ and the triangular stencil kernel. The distance errors of (I.13s.7) add $4\epsilon_D/s^2$ to the half-difference, so the slope adds at most
$$
[40R_\Lambda H_*^3e^{2H_*s}s+4\epsilon_D/s^2]/u.
\tag{I.13s.17}
$$
Choose $u$, then causal $s$, then $J,\epsilon_t,n$ to meet any prescribed positive formal tolerance; each choice is finite and keeps the admitted clock-precision parameter explicit.
A $b$-bit midpoint setting on $[-\theta_{\max},\theta_{\max}]$, $\theta_{\max}=\pi\sqrt3/4$, uses $2^b$ pulse blocks and error at most $\theta_{\max}/2^b$. Since the sine response is Lipschitz with constant at most $N_{\rm cmp}(1/4)(3/4)c^2/(\sqrt3R_\Lambda)$, it yields the corresponding acceleration bound, divided by $u$ for a symmetric slope. For a registered latent alignment,
$$
|m(q)-\widetilde m(q)|\le\|\pi-\widetilde\pi\|_1
+\sum_lq_l\max_j|t_{jl}-\widetilde t_{jl}|.
\tag{I.13s.18}
$$
This follows by product telescoping and $|x^n-y^n|\le n|x-y|$ on $[0,1]$. It gives the response error after multiplication by (I.13s.2)’s coefficient, without claiming a latent permutation recovery from that bound alone.

##### Part VI. Fully populated example and same-action scope

Take $\pi=(1/3,2/3)$, $t_1=(1/4,3/4)$, $t_2=(3/4,1/4)$. Then
$$
m(0,0)=1,\quad m(1,0)=7/12,\quad m(0,1)=5/12,
\quad m(2,1)=7/64,\quad m(1,2)=5/64.
\tag{I.13s.19}
$$
In reference units $c=R_\Lambda=1$, $\Lambda=3$, $8\pi G=3$, let $L=4$, $\rho_d=\rho_{\rm tag}=1/8$. Then $\rho_v=1$, $\rho_*=9/4$, $H_*^2=13/4$, total source radiation energy128, auxiliary energy16(eight dust and eight tag), and total retained energy144 for every source outcome. The initial metric is $a_i=1,H_i=\sqrt{13}/2$. The response at $q=0$ is $3/(8\sqrt3)$; other displayed responses multiply it by (I.13s.19). In physical units, at $m(0)=1$,
$$
g_{\rm rad}(0)=\frac{3}{8\sqrt3}c^2\sqrt{\Lambda/3}
=\frac{c^2\sqrt\Lambda}{8}=g_0.
\tag{I.13s.20}
$$
This uses the registered equality slice, radius and unit-QFI parameter. Replacing the density or ruler multiplies the result by its actual density/radius ratio. Replacing the source parameter changes its derivative normalization. All environmental dependence is in the preparation channel, while the same physical $G$ in the action remains fixed. This bulk capacity is not substituted into a boundary-cell formula for $G$.
The homogeneous unit-lapse clock has $a_\mu=0$; varying the clock action first and then selecting this solution leaves only Einstein+$\Lambda$. The positive worldline stress and all counted tag/control carriers therefore solve the same action as I.13o. The result is the stated initial proper-separation response on a finite release-preparation/instrument class. Later-time dark-response, galaxy, lensing or other source-class identifications require their own owning projections, such as I.13t–v. The finite positive law (I.13s.1) is a supplied input of this theorem. Theorem H.4.7c gives its complete finite-exposure inverse classification over all finite latent ranks, and Construction H.4.7d derives the target-clean structural capacity map and composes it with this unchanged initial-response source.

<a id="theorem-i13t-a-normalized-finite-c-circular-source-its-prepared-evolution-and-complete-finite-optical-paths"></a>**Theorem I.13t (A normalized finite-$c$ circular source, its prepared evolution and complete finite optical paths).**
Use the varied-clock action of Theorem I.13o on the spatial-clock benchmark $A=7$, $n=3/2$, $\beta_\chi=1$ of Remark I.13c.8b, with the minimal couplings $b=\ell=0$ of Theorem I.13p. Set $g_0=c^2\sqrt\Lambda/8$, $a=g_0/c^2$ and $\kappa=8\pi G/c^4$. Define
$$
\nu(y)=8-7e^{-y^{-3/2}},\quad h(y)=y\nu(y),\quad k=h^{-1},\quad
F(x)=\int_0^xk(v)\,dv,\quad J(y)=\int_0^yh(v)\,dv,\quad
P(y)=F(h(y))=yh(y)-J(y).
\tag{I.13t.1}
$$
All functions take their continuous limiting values at zero. The gravitational density is $f(z)=\Lambda+2a^2F(z/a)-z^2$. For a prepared positive particle **rest mass** $M$, put $L_0=\sqrt{GM/g_0}$, $\varepsilon=g_0L_0/c^2$, $s=r/L_0$ and $s_0=10^{-4}$. Suppose
$$
0<\varepsilon\le(4\,000\,000)^{-1},\qquad 0\le s\le10.
\tag{I.13t.2}
$$
There is a uniquely normalized positive continuum of circular massive worldlines, a regular finite-$c$ core and a unique positive exterior metric, normalized by the outer proper clock $N(10L_0)=1$. Its acceleration obeys the uniform same-source bound
$$
\left|\frac{g_{\rm exact}(s)}{g_{\rm NR}(s)}-1\right|\le112000\varepsilon,
\quad g_{\rm exact}=g_0h(Q/s^2),\quad g_{\rm NR}=g_0h(s^{-2}),
\qquad s_0\le s\le10.
\tag{I.13t.3}
$$
For the complete finite source/receiver paths defined in Part V, the measured deflection has error less than $7\,000\,000\varepsilon^2$ radians relative to its stated finite-endpoint nonrelativistic reference. These are actual equilibrium preparations with their nonzero clock stress and boundary traction. Their finite evolution is unique within this invariant prepared class. No formation history or stability of arbitrary perturbations is a premise of this result.

##### Part I. Exact stationary equations and positive core

For $t=y^{-3/2}$, direct differentiation and monotonicity give
$$
0<8-\tfrac{21}{2}e^{-1/3}\le h'(y)=8-7e^{-t}(1+3t/2)\le\nu(y)\le8,
\quad y\le h(y)\le8y,
$$
$$
\tfrac12y^2\le J(y)\le4y^2,\quad0\le P(y)\le4y^2,
\quad2P(y)\le yh(y),\quad
\min(1,Q)\le\frac{h(Qy)}{h(y)}\le\max(1,Q).
\tag{I.13t.4}
$$
The inequality $2P\le yh$ follows from the decreasing function $\nu$: $J(y)\ge\nu(y)y^2/2$.
Write the metric and aligned clock as
$$
ds^2=-N(r)^2c^2dt^2+\frac{dr^2}{u(r)^2}+r^2d\Omega^2,
\quad z=uN'/N>0,\quad T=t.
\tag{I.13t.5}
$$
Here $u(r)$ is a radial metric coefficient. Energy density $e$ and pressures $p_r,p_t$ have units J m$^{-3}$. The metric equations and matter conservation equation are
$$
\begin{aligned}
&(u^2-1)/r^2+2uz/r+f-zf_z=\kappa p_r,\\
&(u^2-1)/r^2+2uu'/r+f-zf_z-(2u/r^2)(r^2\chi z)'=-\kappa e,\\
&uz'+z^2+uz/r+uu'/r+f=\kappa p_t,\\
&p_r'=-(e+p_r)z/u+2(p_t-p_r)/r,
\qquad \chi=\frac{k(z/a)}{z/a}-1.
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.13t.6}
$$
The stationary clock current is zero. Thus its varied equation, as well as the displayed metric equations, must be used. To check boundary terms independently, put $A_r=1/u$. The radial gravitational densities before and after integration by parts satisfy
$$
\mathcal L_0=2NA_r-2N/A_r+4rNA_r'/A_r^2-2Nr^2A_rf,
$$
$$
\mathcal L=2NA_r+2N/A_r+4rN'/A_r-2Nr^2A_rf,

<a id="theorem-i13v-a-positive-two-cohort-collision-with-a-regular-geodesic-clock-and-finite-opticalcurrent-centroids"></a>**Theorem I.13v (A positive two-cohort collision with a regular geodesic clock and finite optical/current centroids).**
The same minimal clock action of I.13o admits a genuinely time-dependent, spherical, positive massive Vlasov source on a finite domain. Two separately conserved colors overlap at positive density and completely reverse radial support order. Its actual normal clock is regular on the full used spacetime region. A complete finite null/Jacobi experiment has strictly positive optical and baryonic weights and exactly zero centroid difference by symmetry. The result uses the explicitly permitted $A_{\rm PM}=q=0$ endpoint of I.7, with nonzero ordinary metric lensing. It makes no inference of a generic off-axis offset or a finite-luminosity photon-backreaction realization.

##### Part I. Exact normalized preparation and the varied source

Fix independent exact nominal inputs $R=10^{23}$ m, $c=2.998\cdot10^8$ m s$^{-1}$, $G=6.67430\cdot10^{-11}$ SI, $\Lambda=1.1\cdot10^{-52}$ m$^{-2}$, $\zeta=\Lambda R^2=1.1\cdot10^{-6}$, $\eta=10^{-10}$, and neutral constituent mass $m_0=10^{-27}$ kg. Let $x=r/R$, $\tau=ct/R$ and
$$
ds^2=R^2[-e^{2\mu}d\tau^2+e^{2\lambda}dx^2+x^2d\Omega^2],
\quad 0\le\tau\le8,\quad0\le x\le12.
\tag{I.13v.1}
$$
In the local static orthonormal frame write $U=(E,v)$, $w=v_{\rm radial}$, $L=x^2|v_{\rm tangential}|^2$, $E=\sqrt{1+w^2+L/x^2}$. Thus $w$ is radial momentum divided by $m_0c$; $L$ is physical angular momentum squared divided by $m_0^2c^2R^2$ and is conserved. If $F_N$ is number per physical proper spatial volume per $d^3v$, put $f=(Gm_0R^2/c^2)F_N$, $\kappa_p=Gm_0/(c^2R)$, so $R^3F_N=f/\kappa_p$.
Define
$$
B(s)=\begin{cases}e^{-s^2/(1-s^2)},&|s|<1,\\0,&|s|\ge1,\end{cases}
\quad a=1/50,\ b=1/1000,\ h=\frac9{20\,000\,000},\ L_c=\frac{11}{20\,000\,000},
$$
$$
\begin{aligned}
g_A&=B((x-1.02)/a)B((w-.02)/b)B((L-L_c)/h),\\
g_B&=B((x-1.10)/a)B((w+.02)/b)B((L-L_c)/h),\\
Z&=4\pi^2\int_0^{12}\int_{\mathbb R}\int_0^\infty E(g_A+g_B)\,dL\,dw\,dx,
\quad \alpha=\eta/Z,\quad f_a(0)=\alpha g_a.
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.13v.2}
$$
The supports are respectively $[1,1.04]$, $[1.08,1.12]$ in $x$, $[.019,.021]$, $[-.021,-.019]$ in $w$, and $[10^{-7},10^{-6}]$ in $L$. All bump derivatives vanish at the boundaries. The Cartesian mass-shell distribution is smooth because it vanishes near $x=0,L=0$. The positive finite fixed initial label measure is
$$
d\nu=\kappa_p^{-1}e^{\lambda_0}f_0\,d^3x\,d^3v.
\tag{I.13v.3}
$$
Here $d^3x$ is dimensionless Cartesian spatial volume. Vary the common metric and each labeled worldline in $-m_0c\int d\nu\int ds$. Geodesic variation gives transport, and metric variation gives, in an orthonormal frame,
$$
T^{\hat a\hat b}=m_0c^2\int F_N\,U^{\hat a}U^{\hat b}/E\,d^3v.
\tag{I.13v.4}
$$
The two colors are passive labels of the same positive massive action. No independent force, static density prescription or test-matter approximation is used. This source satisfies the dominant and null energy conditions.

##### Part II. Full constrained Einstein–Vlasov system and normalization

Define dimensionless moments
$$
\rho=\frac\pi{x^2}\int Ef\,dw\,dL,\quad p=\frac\pi{x^2}\int\frac{w^2}{E}f\,dw\,dL,
\quad j=\frac\pi{x^2}\int wf\,dw\,dL,
$$
$$
p_T=\frac\pi{2x^4}\int\frac L E f\,dw\,dL,\quad
\bar n=\frac\pi{x^2}\int f\,dw\,dL,
\quad m=4\pi\int_0^xs^2\rho\,ds,
\quad H=1-2m/x-\zeta x^2/3,\quad\lambda=-\tfrac12\ln H.
\tag{I.13v.5}
$$
Energy density and pressures are $c^4/(GR^2)$ times these moments; proper rest density is $c^2\bar n/(GR^2)$, distinct from mass-equivalent energy density $c^2\rho/(GR^2)$. The exact equations are
$$
\begin{aligned}
&H(2x\lambda_x-1)+1-\zeta x^2=8\pi x^2\rho,\\
&H(2x\mu_x+1)-1+\zeta x^2=8\pi x^2p,\\
&\mu_x=H^{-1}(m/x^2+4\pi xp-\zeta x/3),\qquad
\lambda_\tau=-4\pi x e^{\lambda+\mu}j.
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.13v.6}
$$
Fix $\mu(\tau,12)=\tfrac12\ln(1-2\eta/12-\zeta12^2/3)$. For $A=e^{\mu-\lambda}$, the characteristics obey
$$
X'=AW/E,\quad
W'=-\lambda_\tau W-A\mu_xE+AL/(X^3E),\quad L'=0,\quad f_a'=0.
\tag{I.13v.7}
$$
The source moment identities give $\mu_x+\lambda_x=4\pi xH^{-1}(\rho+p)$ and $m_\tau=-4\pi x^2Aj$. The two $(\rho+p)j$ terms cancel in this energy identity, so $m(\tau,12)=\eta$ while matter stays interior. Differentiating $H$ recovers the stated momentum equation; stress conservation and the contracted Bianchi identity give the angular Einstein equation. For $f=0,m=M$, the result is exactly $H=1-2M/x-\zeta x^2/3$, $\mu=\tfrac12\ln H$, fixing the $\Lambda$ signs. These are the time-dependent spherically symmetric Einstein–Vlasov conventions of Andréasson(2007,§2), with the cosmological constraints of Andréasson–Fajman–Thaller(2015); the quantitative domain below is proved directly.
Let $I=\int_{-1}^1B$. On $|s|\le1/2$, $B\ge2/3$; on $1/2\le|s|\le2/3$, $B\ge1/5$, giving
$$
11/15\le I\le2,\quad1\le E_0<1.000222,\quad
8\pi^2abh(11/15)^3\le Z\le64\pi^2abh(1.000222),\quad .017<\alpha<.4.
\tag{I.13v.8}
$$
The supports are initially phase-disjoint; a one-to-one phase flow preserves $\|f\|_\infty=\alpha$, not $2\alpha$. Its divergence law is
$$
\partial_\tau(e^\lambda f)+\partial_x(e^\lambda Awf/E)
+\partial_w(e^\lambda W'f)=0.
$$
Thus, separately for each color,
$$
N_a=4\pi^2\kappa_p^{-1}\int e^\lambda f_a\,dx\,dw\,dL,
\quad M_{{\rm rest},a}=m_0N_a
\tag{I.13v.9}
$$
are conserved. The exterior mass parameter is independently $M_{\rm ext}=\eta c^2R/G$; it is not an ADM mass at de Sitter infinity. Since $e^{\lambda_0}<1.0000005$ on initial support,
$$
\frac{M_{\rm ext}}{1.000222}\le M_{{\rm rest},A}+M_{{\rm rest},B}
\le1.0000005M_{\rm ext},\quad
\frac{M_{\rm ext}}{2(1.000222)}\le M_{{\rm rest},a}\le\frac{1.0000005}2M_{\rm ext}.
\tag{I.13v.10}
$$
Equal unweighted phase volumes give the color bounds; the exact proper masses can differ through $e^{\lambda_0}$. Number measures are finite positive real continuum measures, not a claim of an integral finite discrete realization.

##### Part III. Explicit lifespan and smooth continuation

Start with the local smooth characteristic construction and bootstrap $.8\le X\le1.32$, $|W|\le.022$, $10^{-7}\le L\le10^{-6}$. Let $E_*=1.00025>\sqrt{1+.022^2+10^{-6}/.8^2}$. Integrating the full bounding velocity box with $f\le.4$ gives
$$
\rho<9\cdot10^{-8},\quad p<4.4\cdot10^{-11},\quad
|j|<2\cdot10^{-9},\quad p_T<7.1\cdot10^{-14}.
\tag{I.13v.11}
$$
For example $\rho\le\pi(.8)^{-2}(.044)10^{-6}(.4)E_*$, while $p\le.022^2\rho$, $|j|\le.022\rho$, $p_T\le10^{-6}\rho/(2\cdot.8^2)$.
The fixed mass, vacuum center and constraints imply throughout $x\le12$
$$
\begin{aligned}
&H\ge1-2\eta/.8-\zeta12^2/3>H_*=.999947,\\
&-1.26\cdot10^{-10}<\mu+\lambda\le0,\quad
0\le\lambda<2.651\cdot10^{-5},\quad |\mu|<2.652\cdot10^{-5},\\
&H_*(1-1.26\cdot10^{-10})<A\le1.
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.13v.12}
$$
Integrate $(\mu+\lambda)_x$ inward from the vacuum exterior, using $\int4\pi x(\rho+p)dx\le(1+.022^2)\eta/.8$. For $x<.8$, $m=\rho=p=j=0$ and $\mu=\tfrac12\ln(1-\zeta x^2/3)+C(\tau)$, a regular de Sitter center. Outside $x=1.32$, $m=\eta$ and $\mu=-\lambda=\tfrac12\ln H$, including an exterior collar of 12. No boundary inflow, shell or horizon is used.
On matter,
$$
|\mu_x|<4.9\cdot10^{-7},\quad|\lambda_\tau|<3.4\cdot10^{-8},
$$
$$
|W'|\le(4\pi\cdot1.32\cdot2\cdot10^{-9})(.022)
+\frac{[\eta/.8^2+4\pi(1.32)(4.4\cdot10^{-11})+\zeta1.32/3]E_*}{H_*}
+10^{-6}/.8^3<2.5\cdot10^{-6}.
\tag{I.13v.13}
$$
For $\tau\le8$, $|W-W_0|<.000020$, $|X-X_0|\le.022\tau$, and support improves to $.824\le X\le1.296$, $|W|\le.021020<.022$.
For completeness, derivative continuation is part of the proof. Given trial $f$, form its moments, integrate $m,\mu$, reconstruct $\lambda,\lambda_\tau$, solve (I.13v.7), and pull back $f_0$. On compact boxes away from $x=0,H=0$, this is the usual short-time $C^0$ contraction with local $C^1$ control; the compatibility identities in Part II give all Einstein equations.
The independent orthonormal curvature components are
$$
\begin{aligned}
R_{0101}&=4\pi(\rho-p+2p_T)-2m/x^3-\zeta/3,\\
R_{0202}=R_{0303}&=m/x^3+4\pi p-\zeta/3,\\
R_{1212}=R_{1313}&=4\pi\rho-m/x^3+\zeta/3,\\
R_{2323}&=2m/x^3+\zeta/3,\qquad R_{0212}=R_{0313}=-4\pi j.
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.13v.14}
$$
Physical components are these divided by $R^2$. The angular connection and Einstein Ricci equations give these identities; vacuum gives the stated Schwarzschild–de Sitter curvature. As $m=0$ below$.8$ and $m/x^3\le\eta/.8^3$ elsewhere, each component is below $1.6\cdot10^{-6}/R^2$ in absolute value, and the Euclidean Frobenius norm is below $2.56\cdot10^{-5}/R^2$ by the 256-component count. With $K_{ij}=-\tfrac12\mathcal L_nh_{ij}$, $K_{rr}=-e^{-\mu}\lambda_\tau/R$, angular entries 0, so $\|K\|<3.5\cdot10^{-8}/R$.
A geodesic variation obeys $D_s^2J=R(U,J)U$. In the smooth Cartesian orthonormal frame $e_0=e^{-\mu}\partial_\tau$, $e_i=[\delta_i^j+(e^{-\lambda}-1)n_in^j]\partial_{x^j}$, projector differentiation cancels apparent $\lambda_x$ terms in spatial commutators. Connection coefficients are bounded by twice the sum of $e^{-\lambda}|\mu_x|$, $e^{-\mu}|\lambda_\tau|$ and $|e^{-\lambda}-1|/x$, below $10^{-3}$ on occupied support. There is no $\mu_\tau$ term after orthonormalization. The Jacobi first-order system and its inverse therefore have bounded coefficients on proper-length intervals at most$8R$. The fixed-$\tau$ hitting map is transverse since $d\tau/d(s/R)=e^{-\mu}E\ge1$, and the slice second fundamental form is bounded. A loose eight-variable1-norm evolution bound 2 gives propagator/inverse at most$e^{16}$, with each frame conversion at most 100, hence phase-flow differential below $10^4e^{16}<10^{11}$. Since $|B'|\le8/e<3$, the scaled initial gradient is below$10^5$, and the transported derivative is below$10^{16}$. Differentiating the Jacobi system inductively uses curvature derivatives algebraic in already controlled derivatives of$f$ and reconstructed metric. Each highest new flow derivative solves a linear inhomogeneous finite-time ODE. Smooth initial data thus give finite derivatives of every order, allowing a local restart at a candidate endpoint. The strict support/$H$ improvements exclude any endpoint before 8. This proves a quantitative finite lifespan, not merely a local existence claim or numerical orbit result.

The full first-derivative metric bounds, useful independently, are $|\mu_x|,|\lambda_x|<4.41\cdot10^{-6}$, $|\lambda_\tau|<3.4\cdot10^{-8}$ and $|\mu_\tau|<2\cdot10^{-11}$. For the last, define
$$
k_3=\frac\pi{x^2}\int w^3E^{-2}f,\quad
p_4=\frac\pi{x^2}\int w^4E^{-3}f,\quad
\nu_1=\frac\pi{x^4}\int LwE^{-2}f,
\quad S=e^{\mu+\lambda},
$$
where every integral is $dw\,dL$. Integration by parts in the pressure moment gives
$$
p_\tau=-A(k_{3,x}+2k_3/x)-\lambda_\tau(3p-p_4)-2A\mu_xj+(2A/x)\nu_1.
$$
Differentiating the lapse integral and integrating the $k_{3,x}$ term once yields
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mu_\tau(x)={}&-\int_x^{12}2\lambda_\tau\mu_sds+4\pi\int_x^{12}Sjds-4\pi xS(x)k_3(x)\\
&-4\pi\int_x^{12}(sS_s-S)k_3ds
+4\pi\int_x^{12}sH^{-1}\lambda_\tau(3p-p_4)ds\\
&+8\pi\int_x^{12}sS\mu_sjds-8\pi\int_x^{12}S\nu_1ds.
\end{aligned}
\tag{I.13v.15}
$$
There is no outer normalization derivative. All integrals are over matter. Use $\int\rho ds\le\eta/(4\pi\cdot.8^2)$, $|k_3|\le.022^3\rho$, $p_4\le.022^2p$, $|\nu_1|\le(10^{-6}/.8^2)(.022)\rho$, and $sS_s\le4\pi(1.32)^2(\rho+p)/H_*$. The seven term bounds sum below $1.934\cdot10^{-11}$.

##### Part IV. Strict overlap and complete radial pass-through

The improved characteristic bounds give
$$
.018980\le W_A\le.021020,\quad -.021020\le W_B\le-.018980,
\quad X'_A>.01897,\quad X'_B<-.01897.
$$
At $\tau=4$, $\inf\operatorname{supp}_xf_A\ge1.07588$ and $\sup\operatorname{supp}_xf_B\le1.04412$, a positive gap$.03176R$. Every A particle initially inside every B particle has become exterior; separately conserved-number-weighted mean radii reverse their ordering. Vector centroids remain at 0 by spherical symmetry.
The positive-density assertion is quantitative. For each color, the current box
$$
|x-c_a(\tau)|\le.005,\quad|w-w_a|\le.0002,\quad |L-L_c|\le h/2,
\quad c_A=1.02+.02\tau,\quad c_B=1.10-.02\tau,\quad w_a=\pm.02
\tag{I.13v.16}
$$
backtracks to the interior of its initial occupied bump. Indeed $|Aw/E-w|\le.022(1-A_{\min})+(.022/2)(.022^2+10^{-6}/.8^2)$, and
$$
|X_0-[x-\tau w(\tau)]|\le(2.5\cdot10^{-6})\tau^2/2+\tau\sup|Aw/E-w|<.00014.
